author: alxgsv
body:
The brotli decoder has an out-of-bounds write, GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35 (critical). Every brotli from 1.0.3 up to 1.2.0 is affected, and it is fixed in 1.2.1. Every current pycurl wheel bundles an affected brotli:

| pycurl | bundled brotli (manylinux_2_28 x86_64 and aarch64) |
|---|---|
| 7.48.0 | `pycurl.libs/libbrotlidec-*.so.1.2.0` |
| 7.47.0, 7.46.0 | 1.2.0 |
| 7.45.7 | 1.1.0 |

libcurl decodes whatever `Content-Encoding` a server sends once `ACCEPT_ENCODING` is set, to any value. So an application that enables content decoding can reach the bundled decoder from a server-controlled response, even if it only asks for gzip.

vcpkg updated its brotli port to 1.2.1 on 2026-10-24 (microsoft/vcpkg#54566). The Linux wheel build clones vcpkg HEAD, so master already picks it up. I built this branch locally on 2026-10-25 with `CIBW_BUILD=cp314-manylinux_aarch64 cibuildwheel==4.3.4 --platform linux --archs aarch64`, using the unmodified `before-all`:

- vcpkg resolved `brotli:arm64-linux-dynamic@1.2.1` and `curl@8.23.0`.
- The repaired wheel contains `pycurl.libs/libbrotlidec-*.so.1.2.1`.
- `pycurl.version` reports `PycURL/7.48.0 libcurl/8.23.0 OpenSSL/3.6.5 zlib/1.3.1 brotli/1.2.1 ...`.
- The full test suite passed: 1064 passed, 16 skipped, including the new test.

Running the same test against the 7.48.0 wheel from PyPI fails: `assert (1, 2, 0) >= (1, 2, 1)`. Without `PYCURL_TEST_BUNDLED_LIBS`, it is skipped.

The Windows and macOS wheels use the vcpkg that ships on the GitHub runner image, and those images are not there yet:

| runner | image | vcpkg commit | brotli port |
|---|---|---|---|
| windows-2025 | 20261021.299 | a2f9862da6 (2026-10-21) | 1.2.0 |
| macos-15 (arm64) | 20260907.0337 | 04a9d8e521 (2026-09-04) | 1.2.0 |
| macos-15-intel | 20260824.0482 | 127402f1c7 (2026-08-22) | 1.2.0 |

This PR adds `tests/test_bundled_libs.py`, which reads the brotli version from `pycurl.version` and requires >= 1.2.1. It only runs when `PYCURL_TEST_BUNDLED_LIBS` is set. The wheel build now sets that through cibuildwheel's `test-environment`, so the check never runs for source or distro builds, where backported fixes keep the old version number. Because it reads the version string, the same test covers the Linux, macOS and Windows wheels. A Release run will fail on any platform whose vcpkg still resolves brotli 1.2.0, instead of publishing a vulnerable wheel.

Until the runner images pick up the new port, the Windows and macOS jobs need an up-to-date vcpkg (for example `git -C "$VCPKG_INSTALLATION_ROOT" pull` and re-bootstrap before `vcpkg install`) for this check to pass. I left that out because I could not test it on those runners.

Could you cut a 7.48.1 with the updated brotli once the wheels pass? Thanks!

author: jordanhoare
body:
Closes #91

## Summary

```diff
 mise install
   postinstall: mise run setup
     //backend:setup
     //frontend:setup
-    mise generate git-pre-commit --write   # hook -> mise run pre-commit -> prek run
+    prek install --force                   # hook -> prek hook-impl
```

```diff
 .pre-commit-config.yaml
   pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks
-    rev: v6.0.0
+    rev: 3e8a870… # v6.0.0
+  crate-ci/typos
+    rev: 7f9d081… # v1.51.1
+    typos [--force-exclude]               # reports only, no --write-changes
   local: gitleaks, ruff, biome, generate-client, shellcheck, actionlint, zizmor
```

- `--force` replaces mise's generated hook in an existing clone. Without it, prek keeps that hook as `pre-commit.legacy` and chains it, and it calls the `pre-commit` task this PR deletes.
- typos flags nothing on `main` today, so there is no `_typos.toml`.
- The prek shim records the absolute path of the prek that installed it, so it runs without mise activated. `docs/development.md` now notes that a clone shared by WSL and native Windows shares one hook, so run `mise run setup` on the side you commit from.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `.git/hooks/pre-commit` ran `exec mise run pre-commit`. `pre-commit-hooks` was pinned by tag.
  **After:** `mise run setup` writes a prek shim that points at `~/.local/share/mise/installs/prek/0.5.7/.../prek` and removes the legacy hook. A commit from `env -i PATH=~/.nix-profile/bin:/usr/bin:/bin` (mise on PATH, not activated) ran all 17 hooks, typos included.
- `mise run lint`: 17/17 passed. `lint:repo` in `ci` does not skip typos.
- `typos` on a file containing `recieve`: `error: recieve should be receive`.
- **Not verified:** native Windows Git Bash. Run `mise run setup` there and make a commit.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Reverting restores the mise task, and `mise run setup` then regenerates mise's hook.

**Blast Radius:** contributor-commits

An existing clone keeps the old hook until `mise install` or `mise run setup` runs again; until then its commits fail with a missing `pre-commit` task. A new misspelling in a commit now fails the hook.

- Reconstruct the exact first-attempt, main-only controller request from supplied waiting-run metadata; emit its canonical digest without issuing a permit or approval.

author: hhenson
body:
The resolver could find earlier dependency records, but enumerated histories in traversal order rather than following the conflict path. In `A -> P -> M -> X`, a conflict below M could therefore search the older records of an unrelated A branch before moving back to P.

Add a path-directed search that identifies the conflicting dataset, retains every parent link, probes the immediate consumer's revision zero, and uses the verified immediate-record bounds within that version. When it cannot match, move towards the subscribed parent, select an earlier record, and re-expand its selected path. Recheck all shared nodes after each change. Start with the leading side regardless of argument order.

Use the same zero/floor probes and count bounds when search reaches a subscribed root, following stored links across sparse data versions. Root pruning uses only the fixed peer's immutable immediate requirements, never its mutable descendant expansion. Retain the general enumeration fallback for joint choices and exact matches after omissions; committed update floors remain enforced.

For updates, skip upgrade preparation when the driving root is already at latest. Reuse committed at-latest trees whose intermediate choices are still latest. Keep root revisions fixed while allowing intermediate resolution and rechecking changed graphs. Older intermediate choices must be reconsidered even without a new notification, so they cannot hold back a waiting peer.

Add nine publication-and-notification regressions covering parent backtracking, subscribed-parent history, multiple paths, newest matching counts/all shared constraints, blocked-update catch-up, duplicate notifications, stable-tree reuse, and intermediate advancement below fixed roots. Preserve existing cut-selection assertions while updating read-order checks for zero/floor probes.

author: aliromman
body:
This enabling proof now gives a complete adverse repair test for the frozen PR4948 caller: **at least 104 additional paid field returns are required at every width f>=72**, even with feedback among new calls. The cheapest such repair fails the complete optimistic invoice for **every positive concave power tariff r^p, 0<p<=1**. A reusable error-versus-return theorem also rules out small-error repairs within the budget. The complete kappa calculation is unchanged.

[Repair proof and exact contract](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/45f7de73b168721cdf7ec8c1769b1b594493716a/research/clifford-pointwise-faithfulness/REPAIR.md), [repair receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/45f7de73b168721cdf7ec8c1769b1b594493716a/research/clifford-pointwise-faithfulness/REPAIR-RESULT.json), [complete optimistic invoice](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/45f7de73b168721cdf7ec8c1769b1b594493716a/research/clifford-pointwise-faithfulness/REPAIR-INVOICE.json), [pointwise tensor proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/45f7de73b168721cdf7ec8c1769b1b594493716a/research/clifford-pointwise-faithfulness/PROOF.md), [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/45f7de73b168721cdf7ec8c1769b1b594493716a/research/clifford-pointwise-faithfulness/SOURCES.json). Contribution head: `45f7de73b168721cdf7ec8c1769b1b594493716a`. Canonical base: `32890bc5de034ab8fc93ac88ead7279a6a416d04`, priority revision 7.

The underlying theorem applies to the full n-axis projective Clifford group. At every width f>=4n+4 its normalized tensor Gram matrix lies between I/9 and 17I/9. Coefficients, finite word choices and program length may depend on f. For one fixed Gaussian-dyadic scalar register program, four widths 4n+4 through 4n+7 decide equality at every positive width. The proof retains central phases raised to f. A separate stabilizer-map theorem includes rectangular maps and projections. These are sufficient bounds; the prior sharp one-axis window 5..8 remains stronger than the uniform window 8..11.

The paid-repair theorem combines this Gram estimate with the existing relative-history dimension method. Ordinary operations are scalar row combinations and the fixed columnwise monomial Clifford algebra. The entire retained history is granted at the start. Each new paid return is one field at the same 17-axis capacity and may be an arbitrary linear map using earlier new returns. Every original paid input expression, the original targets and the source-declared invoice stay fixed. All storage, COPY and owned CLEAR costs are granted zero. A primitive with several field returns must count its actual outputs; free outputs from a new supplier are not automatically charged as queries.

For the actual 104 independent source columns, the target cosets have grade 9 and are absent from the retained grades 0, 1 and 7. The quotient needs 104 full ordinary modules; one new return adds at most one. With q returns, the selected block error satisfies:

```text
2^(-17f) ||E||_HS^2 >= lambda_f (104-q)_+
||E||_op^2 >= lambda_f (1-q/104)_+
lambda_f = 1/9 for f>=72; lambda_f = 125/126 for f>=84.
```

The source invoice has only 96 units of rank-mass surplus. Adding the necessary 104 rank-one returns makes all nine exact concave-order hinges positive, including an eight-unit deficit at rank mass. At the reference tariff p=1-605457647/200000000000, exact interval arithmetic puts the original margin strictly between 36 and 37. Positive margin permits at most 36 additional returns; from width 84 every such approximate repair has squared operator norm error at least **2125/3276**. This reference calculation uses the pinned selected value as a tariff, not as a selected-caller replay. Histograms remain the frozen source declarations; no new physical word was recounted.

Changed original paid inputs, added free observations, native internal prefixes, larger capacity, noncolumnwise maps, nonlinear processing or changed targets need a new analysis. The result does not close active-feed constructions or the separate P104 repair work. It supplies no new caller, selected-frontier update or global lower bound.

Python 3.12 and the standard library suffice:

```sh
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/clifford-pointwise-faithfulness
python3.12 -I -W error -B research/clifford-pointwise-faithfulness/audit_mutations.py
```

All six registered normal/optimized checks pass. The repair verifier replays the unchanged author and independent source audits, including all 5,408 late words, and extracts the actual diagonal target and invoice through the retained loader. Further exact checks cover 576 group products, 18,432 phase covariance identities, 48 history prefixes and 12 physical least-squares cases. Controls include cached targets, wrong input versions, complementary singular targets that share one return, and small-width dependence. All twelve deliberate-defect checks fail at their intended diagnostic. The original complete stabilizer/Clifford censuses and native/projection residual checks also pass. See the [registered commands](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/45f7de73b168721cdf7ec8c1769b1b594493716a/research/clifford-pointwise-faithfulness/VERIFY.json), [mutation receipts](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/45f7de73b168721cdf7ec8c1769b1b594493716a/research/clifford-pointwise-faithfulness/MUTATIONS.json) and [research record](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/45f7de73b168721cdf7ec8c1769b1b594493716a/research/clifford-pointwise-faithfulness/RESEARCH-NOTES.md).

The committed-byte check and source-pinned package export pass. All six checks also pass in a fresh read-only 86-file export with Git absent from PATH; its bytes and inventory remain unchanged. The separate full-history preflight refuses the shared checkout's current shallow state; no full-history pass is claimed for this revision. The declared source base is the verified two-parent ancestor and all consumed bytes are in the published tree. The written universal proofs have author review and finite corroboration, not independent human acceptance or proof-kernel certification. No selected cold replay, physical emission, constructive full price, precision application or outer admission was run. Hosted status for this revision is reported separately when available.

Credit Dugongue for [PR #4948](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4948), source head `86e474038e05f99a76d41f71d81946ad2327e4a4`, and Chris R / Clear1nsight for [PR #4978](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/4978), its [retained passive audit](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/32890bc5de034ab8fc93ac88ead7279a6a416d04/research/passive-saved-query-ceiling/README.md), uniform-alphabet addendum and owned-reset clarification. Those principles are not claimed as new.

Ali Romman's [PR #5376](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5376) supplies the consumed native frontend and exact quadratic kernel, with its retained lineage notices. The [invoice comparator](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/32890bc5de034ab8fc93ac88ead7279a6a416d04/scripts/compare_recursive_invoices.py) credits classical concave order, mightyOil and predecessors. No behaviour change was found.

- **`0x8a210`: score 10 → MATCH.**

- **`0x2742f0`: score 17 → MATCH.** `difficulty` is declared in the `ai_team != NONE` block and set to 1 in an `else`, instead of being initialised to 1 at the top. The compiler then keeps 1 in `edx` for all three compares against 1, as retail does. The value is the same.

  - `0x245850` (14): retail sign-extends the plane index, and every retail caller of `0x14a300` does, which points to a `long` index in `bsp3d_get_plane`. Changing that in its six declarations keeps `0x14a300` matched but takes this function to 116, so it isn't changed. All 12 orders of one sum were tried. The note now sits directly above the `@retail` line, as it should.
  - `0x1e9ce0` (13): retail loads the field argument before the prologue pushes; every non-volatile spelling folds the load and scores 80–85.
  - `0x2732e0` (15): `ecx` and `edx` swap roles in the swarm loop, and the sibling `0x273200` (7) has exactly the same swap. A fast check reaches 15 only with its caller `0x2a5120` and `0xdc310` in it.

author: gebner
body:
Closes #13.

Adds RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 (RFC 8017 §8.2) for SHA-256/384/512: verification as requested in the issue, and signing.

## API

New exports in `dist/Hacl.h`. They use the `Hacl_RSAPSS_*` calling convention without the salt (big-endian modulus and exponent, explicit `modBits`):

```c
bool Hacl_RSAPKCS1_verify_sha256(uint32_t modBits, uint8_t *nb, size_t eLen, uint8_t *eb, uint8_t *sgnt, size_t mLen, uint8_t *msg);
bool Hacl_RSAPKCS1_sign_sha256  (uint32_t modBits, uint8_t *nb, size_t dLen, uint8_t *db, size_t mLen, uint8_t *msg, uint8_t *sgnt);
```
The `_sha384` and `_sha512` variants have the same signatures.

## Files

- **`spec/Spec.RSAPKCS1.fst`**: EMSA-PKCS1-v1_5 encoding (§9.2) with the DigestInfo prefixes (explicit NULL parameters only). It also defines total predicates `pkcs1_valid`, `pkcs1_signable` and `pkcs1_signed`, so postconditions can use them without side conditions on their arguments.
- **`code/rsapss/Hacl.RSAPKCS1.fst`**: builds on `Hacl.RSAPSS.rsa_exp`.
  - **Verify** builds the expected encoding and compares it with the recovered one, without parsing it. There is no padding scan and no DigestInfo parsing, so a forged signature has nothing to steer. Postcondition: `ok <==> 1 < n /\ n odd /\ s < n /\ pkcs1_valid ... (s^e mod n)`.
  - **Sign** encodes, then runs the constant-time `rsa_exp` with `d`. Unlike RSA-PSS signing, the postcondition says exactly when signing fails (`ok <==> pkcs1_signable ...`) as well as what it produces on success.
- **`spec/Spec.RSAPKCS1.Correctness.fst`**: for a valid key (`rsa_key n e d p q`, `pow2 (modBits-1) <= n`) with room for the encoding, signing succeeds and the signature verifies (`sign_succeeds`, `sign_verify`). `sign_then_verify` states this over the implementation's postconditions. Signing success is proved, not assumed as in `Spec.RSAPSS.Correctness`.
- **`tests/test_rsapkcs1.c`**: keys and signatures from the OpenSSL CLI. Moduli are 1025 to 4096 bits, including e = 3 and an empty message. Signing is checked byte for byte against OpenSSL. The rejection cases are:
  - flipped signature bits, a modified or extended message, the wrong hash
  - a signature equal to n or zero, an even modulus (both sign and verify)
  - a modulus too small for the encoding (both sign and verify)
  - five malformed encodings signed with the private key: DigestInfo without NULL, Bleichenbacher 2006 short padding with trailing garbage, block type 2, a non-0xff padding byte, and the wrong DigestInfo

Also updates the `Makefile` exports, `code/Hacl.fst` and the README algorithms table.

## Validation

Full `make` passes: lint, verify, extract, compile, stack and test. No admits or assumes.

author: jwa91
body:
Indexing goes over the whole collection in rounds, each with one tool: words first, for every file, with no model, then what text means, the text on screenshots and scans, what pictures show, what sound sounds like, and what's said. An exact search finds every file within seconds of choosing the folders, and meaning comes round by round. `indexing.memory_mb` is a ceiling on which rounds run side by side; memory pressure shrinks or stops it; on battery, words and new files go on.

The design is in `docs/design.md` (Indexing: Rounds, Tools and the budget, New files first, Memory pressure, Power, How far it is) and `docs/architecture.md` (the ingest path, the queues, the lanes).

## What changes

**Rounds.** `ingest/rounds.rs` says which rounds a file passes through after its words (pure, tested):

| Round | Tool, chip | Unit |
|---|---|---|
| words | none (readers, CPU) | files |
| text | the text model, GPU | passages |
| OCR | Vision's text recognition, Neural Engine | pictures |
| pictures | text model + vision encoder, GPU | pictures (a video: a frame looked at every 2 s) |
| sound | text model + audio encoder, GPU | seconds |
| speech | the speech helper, Neural Engine | seconds |

- What OCR and speech find goes into the keyword index at once, and its passages wait for the text round.
- Each round's queue goes cheapest first, new files first.
- A round works in items: a file, a batch of 16 passages, ten scanned pages, or five minutes of a video. A recording's sound is read in one go with a checkpoint every five minutes, where it stops when the plan needs its lane. A stopped file goes on from there.

**The plan.** `resources::Plan` (pure, tested): each tool declares its chip and what it holds (`Tool::chip`, `Tool::memory`, measured). Rounds with work are taken new files' first, then those whose tools are loaded, then in order (words, text, OCR, pictures, sound, speech). Each joins when it can run beside the ones before it and its tools fit in the budget; words and the first tool always run. The plan says which tools are loaded (`Plan::tools`), and the run lets go of the rest.
- A loaded tool works through its queue: on a small budget, the passages speech and OCR bring the text round wait for them to be done, instead of pushing them out every second or two.
- The text model stays while it fits beside what runs, counted in the budget, since the other rounds bring it passages; when it doesn't fit, it goes. It loads again in 0.2 s.
- Each lane that reads (words, and the GPU's pictures or sound) has a reader in the budget, and they share two to four in all.
- The GPU takes pictures or sound, one at a time; the text round's batches go first while passages wait.
- The Neural Engine takes OCR and speech together, measured below.
- A memory-pressure warning makes it one tool; critical stops the run and lets everything go (`adapters/macos/pressure.rs`, a `DispatchSource` memory-pressure source).
- `indexing.on_battery` is `words` (default: words and new files go on), `all` or `none`. Low Power Mode is `words` at most. Old files' work in hand stops at its next checkpoint, and the speech lane stops after the stretch it's on.
- A tool that isn't built yet (a Core ML text encoder on the Neural Engine) slots in by declaring its chip and memory.

**The queues are the index's.** A `work` row per file and round: state, amount, done, where the next item goes on (`resume`), new or not. A passage waiting for its vector says so (`segments.due`, with its `context`). The text round fills vectors of existing segments, so the engine now catches up by each partition's appended rows, not by segment id (`index/mapped.rs`). Schema 7: the index is made again.

**The run** (`ingest/schedule.rs`): lanes for words, media decoding, OCR and speech, and one thread for the GPU and the writer.
- The words, OCR and speech lanes need no GPU, so they're answered between any two picture or sound pieces and may run far ahead. When they were answered once a pass, words took 107 s instead of 9 on the demo, OCR was 6× slower beside sound, and speech ran at half speed.
- Text goes first on the GPU while passages wait.
- The speech lane streams: one file waits beside the one it's on, and the run stops a file by naming it.
- New files from FSEvents go first in every round.
- Per-round progress uses rates measured while each round ran (`ingest/progress.rs`).

**Protocol:** `IndexerStatus.rounds` (below). **CLI:** `sift-it status` shows the rounds; `sift-it read` shows each round's pieces.

**A config.json that can't be read** (`"on_battery": true` from before, or a typo made by hand):
- The error names the key and what it takes: `indexing.on_battery: true isn't "words", "all" or "none"` (`serde_path_to_error`, a small crate of dtolnay's).
- `sift-it config <key> <value>` sets it right: the value is checked against its key alone, set in the file as it is, then the file is read again, or the error names the next key that doesn't do.
- The daemon waits for the file to change instead of exiting (and launchd restarting it in a loop), with `state` `waiting` and `detail` saying why. `sift-it serve` starts with the defaults, so the app can still send `config`.

**Decoding from partway** (`adapters/macos/av.rs`, docs/audio-decoding.md).
- A read that starts partway now warms the decoder up on up to 3 s before, starting at a whole second.
- Before, the first second after a resume came out differently: a sound window there had a cosine of 0.988 with an uninterrupted read. Now it's bit-identical on MP3 and AAC (tested). Speech's resumed chunks gain from this too.
- In a VBR MP3, AVFoundation's seek itself lands ~0.2 s off. That's why sound is read in one go and seeks only after a stop.

## Measurements

Apple M5 MacBook Air (fanless, 24 GB), macOS 26.6.2, on the charger, dev builds, scratch `SIFT_IT_HOME`. Nothing else ran except an idle engine left over from another worktree, which the sampler leaves out.
- **Peaks:** `proc_pid_rusage` v6, lifetime max `phys_footprint` and neural footprint, sampled every 50 ms. "All at once" is the most the indexer, the helper and the engine held together.
- **Setup:** `sift-it index` on `sift-it-data/demo`, while the engine searched by meaning every 5 s.
- **Order:** main and the branch alternated at 4096 and auto, a minute's rest between runs.

**The demo folder** (628 files: 428 photos, 91 videos, 71 recordings, 38 documents and texts; 28 h of sound):

| `memory_mb` | | Every file found by words | Text by meaning | All done | Indexer | Helper | Engine | All at once |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2048 | main | 2,171 s | 2,179 s | 2,844 s | 1,018 MB¹ | 149 + 607 MB | 290 MB | – |
| | rounds | **5 s** | **93 s** | **2,037 s** | **756 MB** | 313 + 607 MB | 385 MB | 1,764 MB |
| 4096 | main | 2,130 s | 2,140 s | 2,164 s | 1,107 MB | 116 + 607 MB | 316 MB | 2,123 MB |
| | rounds² | **5 s** | **104 s** | 2,131 s | **822 MB** | 336 + 607 MB | 309 MB | **1,934 MB** |
| auto (6 GB) | main | 2,117 s | 2,127 s | 2,151 s | 1,072 MB | 104 + 607 MB | 309 MB | 2,041 MB |
| | rounds | **6 s** | **104 s** | 2,109 s | **767 MB** | 342 + 607 MB | 506 MB³ | **1,843 MB** |

¹ From `time -l`. The sampler started late in that run, so "all at once" is missing.
² Measured with this PR's first version. 2048 and auto were measured again after the review's fixes; there, the fixes found every file by its words 5 s sooner and as soon, text 8 s and 3 s sooner, and were all done 38 s and 26 s sooner, with the indexer peaking 28–41 MB higher.
³ The engine's code didn't change; it peaked at 309–385 MB in the other runs.

- **Before, a file was found only once all of it was read.** The cheapest went first, so the book and the long podcasts came last, and nearly everything was found only at the end.
- **All done is the GPU's work, the same either way.** At 2048 MB main wrote speech down after the reading; the rounds write it beside, which is 28% sooner.
- **The indexer holds less** because it ne

author: guimard
body:
Creating a password policy under a name already taken showed a toast, _The server refused: A password policy is named default: cn=default,ou=policies,dc=example,dc=com_, in English and with the other policy's DN, in the French interface too. Nothing was marked under Name.

ldap-rest answers that with a 409 that has no structured refusal code. On creating a policy, a conflict can only be about its name: a policy of that name exists, several do, or another administrator created it at the same time. So a 409 on create is now said under Name, in the interface's language: _A password policy is already named default_ / _Une politique de mot de passe s’appelle déjà default_. The field is marked `aria-invalid` and described by the message, and it takes the focus, as the form's own refusals do since #177. `PolicyForm.refuse()` shares that code with `read()`, and the next submit clears it.

Editing a policy keeps the toast: there is no Name field to say it under.

Tests: a console test with the server's 409, and a new e2e test, `POLICY-04`, against the seeded `default` policy.

The Mongolian string (`{name} нэртэй нууц үгийн бодлого аль хэдийн байна`) needs checking by the translator.

Closes #176

The screenshot's 'Choose a valid clip end' error came from validating an already rounded canonical end against the raw browser duration. A valid 9.991587-second end became 9.992, then failed renderer validation. Allow only one millisecond of boundary tolerance before clamping and canonical rounding; use integer milliseconds for the 200ms minimum trim. Repeated canonical validation is now stable while genuinely oversized trims still fail.

Add normalized title and timed-caption positions to the canonical edit and shared canvas renderer. Drag visible text within the actual letterboxed canvas content, or use horizontal/vertical position sliders with reset controls. Positions persist in drafts and exports; changes invalidate the paid edit quote, while default positions retain legacy identity. Pointer edits are disabled during playback/export and use frame-local coordinates.

Validation: 94 frontend tests passed. Added regressions for repeated fractional-boundary validation, exact 200ms trims, title dragging, timed-text sliders, position validation, default identity and actual renderer text coordinates. author: zebangcheng
body:
After a media run was accepted with HTTP 202, an asynchronous provider failure could turn the canvas node red without explaining the failure in its workbench. Only errors from the local save/run request were displayed.

## Reproduction

1. Run an image or video node and let the request be accepted.
2. Return a failed execution runtime afterward, for example a provider `429 SetLimitExceeded`, while the workflow projection still contains the queued attempt. On the base revision, the workbench has no failure alert.
3. Repeat with a Ready node retaining an earlier output after failed regeneration. Its latest failure is also hidden.
4. Queue another execution while projections still retain the previous failure; the previous alert must clear without suppressing a distinct current error.

The added component tests simulate these transitions without sending HTTP or provider requests. A real Seedream quota rejection was also checked manually in the running project.

## Fix

- Image/video workbenches select the current execution error across independently refreshed runtime and workflow projections, including failed regenerations that retain an output.
- Execution identity and timestamps prevent stale failures from leaking into newer queued/running attempts; distinct current errors remain visible.
- Local save conflicts/errors retain priority. Provider HTTP wrappers display a bounded, actionable summary instead of account identifiers, endpoints, or request payloads.
- Displaying an error adds no retry action or provider request.

## Regression validation

Verified final head `0da0c4ecc1543b6ce53524f57e085ef4b893ad80` against base `a395733f0fc3ad0cc78180571a3d54397b16e7df`.

- All 18 added regression scenarios were copied unchanged onto the base: **12 failed, 6 passed**. On this PR all 18 pass as part of **226/226 targeted tests** across four files.
- Coverage includes accepted-then-failed image/video runs, old Ready outputs, out-of-order projections, clearing inherited queued errors, preserving different current errors, sensitive-payload suppression, and no automatic retries.
- Type checking, focused ESLint (**0 errors/warnings**), production build, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Manual UI verification of the real `429 SetLimitExceeded` response showed a concise model-limit notice without the provider wrapper/payload.

From `apps/web`:

```sh
npx vitest run src/features/agent-canvas/workbench/AgentCanvasInlineWorkbench.test.tsx src/features/agent-canvas/workbench/useNodePromptAutosave.test.tsx src/features/agent-canvas/canvas/canvasGraphModel.test.ts src/features/agent-canvas/chat/actionableFailure.test.ts --maxWorkers=1
npm run typecheck
npx eslint src/features/agent-canvas/workbench/MediaPromptWorkbench.tsx src/features/agent-canvas/workbench/NodeWorkbenchError.tsx src/features/agent-canvas/workbench/AgentCanvasInlineWorkbench.test.tsx
npm run build
```

body:
## Phase D — Founder/operator-only Copy Trading UI cohort (default-DENY)

Makes the **read-only** Copy Trading monitoring UI visible **only to a founder/operator cohort**, default-DENY. Part of the continuous-SHADOW programme; monitoring/visibility only — grants **no** observation/replication/execution authority.

### Backend
- `trade_copier.flags`: `copier_ui_cohort_allowlist()` + `copier_ui_enabled_for(user)` — lowercased `COPIER_UI_COHORT_ALLOWLIST` (settings-then-env). **Pure allow-list, no global-flag path** (the legacy global `copier_ui_enabled()` is deliberately not consulted → no "global ON exposes everyone" footgun). Empty allow-list ⇒ everyone denied; anonymous/missing user ⇒ denied (fail-closed). Mirrors the `broker_intelligence` multi-mailbox cohort idiom.
- `trade_copier.views`: all three read-only views (`status` / `masters` / `overview`) now gate on `copier_ui_enabled_for(request.user)`. Non-cohort caller → `enabled:false`, no rows (approved unavailable response). Owner scoping + no-leak 404 preserved for cohort members. Every response carries the permanent banner **`SHADOW — EXECUTION OFF`** + `execution:"off"`.

### Frontend
- `getCopyTradingStatus()` client; `AccountManageContent` **hides the Copy Trading nav entry** unless the per-user status is enabled (fail-closed to hidden).
- `CopyTradingContent` renders the permanent **`SHADOW — EXECUTION OFF`** banner on every state (enabled / disabled / API-fail).

### Tests
- Cohort flag unit tests: default-deny, case-insensitive + trimmed, anonymous denied, **no global footgun** (global `COPIER_UI_ENABLED=True` does not open the per-user gate).
- API tests: cohort member sees dashboard; **non-cohort owner denied + no leak**; cohort non-owner → 404; banner on every response; `masters` cohort/non-cohort.
- Frontend: banner present in enabled + disabled/API-fail states.

### Safety
- No model/schema change. All copier **execution** flags remain OFF; nothing here can place/modify/close an order. Default config (empty allow-list) keeps the UI dark for everyone until `COPIER_UI_COHORT_ALLOWLIST` is set (founder-only, e.g. `support@guvfx.com`).

author: jbutlerdev
body:
## What

**`golang.org/x/net 0.58.0 → 0.60.0`** (root + `test/` modules) — clears **5 REACHABLE advisories** that appeared in the vuln DB since the day-2 baseline scan:

| Advisory | Issue |
|---|---|
| GO-2026-6617 | HTTP/2 HPACK encoder race → server crash |
| GO-2026-6612 / 6611 / 6610 | HTTP/2 + proxy issues |
| GO-2026-6603 | `x/net/html` form-parse infinite loop (DoS) |

**Reachability: first-party direct.** `tools/search.go` imports `golang.org/x/net/html` directly; govulncheck symbol traces run through `genai.NewClient`, `tools.RetrievePage`, `tools.SearchWeb` — not transitive-only.

Cascade (go get–mandated): `x/text 0.41→0.42`, `x/sys 0.47→0.48` (indirect). `test/go.sum` regenerated via `go mod tidy` (the x/net move left xanzy/ssh-agent's x/crypto entry stale — missing-go.sum would have broken builds).

## Verification (observed, go1.26.9 GOTOOLCHAIN=auto)

```
root  go build .        → rc=0
root  go vet .          → rc=0   (root pkg has no test files)
test/ go build ./...    → rc=0
test/ go vet ./...      → rc=0
govulncheck ./ (root):  BEFORE 14 findings → AFTER 9
```

## The 9 remaining (deliberate hold — documented, not hidden)

1. **crypto/x509 GO-2026-6809** (`Distrust compromised intermediate certs`) — fixed only in **go1.26.10 toolchain**. CI pins go 1.21 anyway (workflows lane = Jeremiah); toolchain bump is the same class as bifrost go1.26 → owner consent, not a code PR.
2. **8× `github.com/ollama/ollama`** (GO-2025-3557…4251: missing auth on model management, etc.) — **no fix exists**: advisory ranges are `introduced:0` with **no fixed event** (verified via vuln.go.dev JSON — bumping 0.32→0.40 changes nothing). Moreover genai imports **only `github.com/ollama/ollama/api` (client)**; the advisories target the ollama **server**, which is never compiled into genai binaries. Symbol-level reach is through `api.init`/errtype strings only. → accept-known-risk, monitor upstream.

## Notes
- 0 source/test files touched; lockfile-only (4 files: go.mod/go.sum ×2 modules).
- genai Dependabot board remains 0 open (alerts enabled here — this finding came from my build-based govulncheck sweep, one day ahead of what the board saw).

## 변경 요약
Blogger 실행이 게시용 시크릿 없이도 초록으로 끝나 초안만 쌓이던 문제(D-25)와 건너뜀이 조용하던 문제(D-26)를 고치고, `macat0722`를 영문 프로필 준비 전까지 정지한다(D-32, 운영자 결정 2026-10-25). 운영자 요청서 4번(발행 복구)의 두 번째 복구 PR이다.

**원인**: 게시 시크릿 4개가 비어 있는데도 실행은 초안을 저장하고 종료 코드 0으로 끝났다. 하루 상한·일시정지 같은 건너뜀도 로그 한 줄도 남기지 않아 "왜 아무것도 안 올라오지?"를 실행 로그에서 알 수 없었다. 검증 중에는 다른 블로그 이력 제목의 개행으로 로그에 `::error::` 줄을 만들 수 있는 경로도 발견했다.

**변경**
- 게시 대상인데 게시용 시크릿이 없으면 글을 만들기 전에 **종료 2(빨강) + `::error::`(시크릿 이름만)**. 이 점검은 상한·주제 선정·이력 읽기보다 앞선다.
- `PIPELINE_PAUSE`·`mode: off`·하루 상한 건너뜀에 `[SKIP]` 줄 + 요약 + `::notice::`. 주제 없음·게이트 탈락은 경고, LLM·주제 확장·게시 실패는 종료 1.
- `plan`: `--only`에 없는 key·다른 플랫폼 key는 종료 1(유효 key 안내). 워크플로 plan 단계가 실패하면 단계도 빨강(예전엔 `matrix=`가 빈 채 초록), 대상 0개는 notice + 요약, `ONLY_BLOG`는 env로만 받아 셸 주입 방지.
- 로그·요약 정화: `console.one_line()`·`md_cell()`(개행·CR·U+2028·`::`·`##[`·마크다운 링크/표/HTML 무력화), 게이트 중복 사유의 제목은 한 줄·100자(판정은 불변).
- `blogs.json`: `blogger_macat`을 `mode: off`로. 정지 중에도 매일 02:00 UTC 실행은 돌고 초록 + notice로 끝난다. 재개 절차는 HANDLER §3 P1(영문 프로필 → draft → 시험 → 시크릿 → auto, 각 단계 T3).
- 문서: ARCHITECTURE(Plan·Topic·§4-1 코드표·처리 순서), HANDLER, ENGINEERING_GUIDE R9·L3, SECURITY_GUARDRAILS G-L2, REQUEST_BRIEFING, DEFECT_REGISTER(D-25 해결·관측 필요, D-26 완화, D-48 신규), WORKLOG.

**알아야 할 효과**: 정지(mode off) 상태에서는 `--dry-run`도 막힌다(시험은 mode를 켠 사본에서). 정지로 워치독 이슈 #10(UNPUBLISHED)이 닫히지만 시크릿 미등록·영문 프로필 문제가 풀린 것은 아니다. `BLOGGER_PUBLISH=off` 수동 실행도 하루 상한을 쓴다(상한의 의미 유지는 T3 판단).

body:
## What was wrong

`world-safety.test.ts` "validates a save in a worker without blocking the main event loop" asserted that the validation promise was still pending after one `setImmediate`. A real worker thread can reply within that single loop turn on a fast run, so the assertion failed at random. It was a race with thread start-up, not a sign that validation blocked the main thread.

## What changes

- The test replaces `Worker` with a held fake for its duration (`save-validation.ts` reads `Worker` from the `worker_threads` module at call time, so no production change is needed). The fake records the script path and the data it was started with, and its reply is sent only when the test emits the worker's message.
- It checks that exactly one validation worker starts, running `save-validation-worker.js` with the save bytes, that the promise stays pending across ten loop turns, and that the result comes only from the worker's message, with the bytes unchanged.
- A new test checks a real worker's round trip (fields and bytes) with no timing assertion.

The property checked is the same: validation runs in the worker and the main thread gets the result only through its message. Only the timing dependence is removed.

## Checks

- `pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` in `apps/desktop`: pass.
- `pnpm run test:main` in `apps/desktop`: 169 pass, 0 fail.
- The new worker test run 20 times in a row: 20 of 20 pass.
- Mutation check: with validation changed to run on the main thread (no worker), the new test fails with an assertion error. The mutation was reverted before the commit.
- Not run: `apps/web` and sim checks; neither was changed.

author: pkdone
body:
One failed Homebrew app no longer stops the rest of setup, and the run log says which entry failed and how to install it. ## What changed - **Run log.** `install.sh`, `bootstrap.sh`, and `brewsync` each copy their output to `~/Library/Logs/dotfiles/` (`install-YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS.log`, and the same shape for `bootstrap` and `brewsync`). The path is printed at the end. Logs older than 30 days are removed. The log is the script's own output; the admin password is read from the terminal and is not written. A log path inside the repo checkout is refused. `.gitignore` also ignores `*.log` and `logs/`. - **Named failures.** After `brew bundle`, missing formulae and casks are listed one by one, with Homebrew's error line when there is one and the exact `brew install` command. The old "some entries did not install" line is gone. - **One retry.** Only the missing entries are tried again, once, after a short wait (2 seconds). `brewsync` uses the same path. - **Admin password.** If a Brewfile cask is a pkg installer (Karabiner-Elements is one), a terminal run asks with `sudo -v` once and keeps that timestamp fresh until the script exits. A non-interactive run skips the prompt and says those installers may fail. The scripts still refuse to run as root. - **Adopt existing apps.** When this Homebrew's `brew install --cask --help` includes `--adopt`, casks are installed with it (`HOMEBREW_CASK_OPTS` for `brew bundle`, and the flag on the retry). An app already in `/Applications` is taken over. `--force` is left alone, because it cannot be combined with `--adopt`. - **Checks before installing.** Setup stops, with a plain explanation, if github.com or formulae.brew.sh cannot be reached, the Xcode Command Line Tools are missing, or less than 10 GB is free. Serious `brew doctor` output is printed and setup continues. A harmless doctor note does not. - **Tests.** A stub `brew` covers a second install that changes nothing, and one failing cask that does not stop the others, is retried exactly once, and is named in the summary. ## Tests `./tests/run-all.sh --shellcheck all` — 37 passed, 0 failed (shellcheck of all 91 scripts included). `./tests/run-all.sh --mac-home` — 36 passed, 0 failed. `fish -n fish/functions/brewsync.fish` — ok.
  
--- > [!NOTE] > **Medium Risk** > Touches first-run bootstrap, sudo handling for pkg casks, and all Brewfile installs via new shared logic; mitigated by extensive stub tests and explicit exit codes. > > Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 46828a42f30aaf2e2b51a810c2825c601419ea48. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).

author: lefthandcold
body:
## What type of PR is this?

- [ ] API-change
- [x] BUG
- [ ] Improvement
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] Feature
- [x] Test and CI
- [ ] Code Refactoring

## Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

issue #31064

Related upstream fix: #30796. This PR adapts that fix to the exact production baseline, rather than upgrading to current `4.2-dev`.

## What this PR does / why we need it:

### Review target and scope

- **Base branch:** `4.2.1-prod-20261025`, created directly at `d2393868a7aaa6343518d80849fe4696aa3577e9` (original `v4.2.1` / current production source baseline).
- **Head:** `9ebefa5bc1bc0daa9fce761c39f099cc2204a077`, exactly one commit on that baseline.
- **Production code:** only `pkg/sql/colexec/merge/merge.go` and `types.go`, 19 added lines. The other two changed files are regression tests.
- This is **not cumulative** with other `v4.2.1-hotfix-*` releases and does not include unrelated later 4.2-dev changes.
- **Human review is requested. Release, tag publication and production rollout remain paused; this PR does not authorize or perform a deployment.**

### Root cause

`materialized.Source.Next` returns an independent caller-owned batch. The baseline's materialized Merge reader did not retain that returned copy for cleanup. Pass-through Projection borrows its vectors, and Source cleanup only owns Source's stored batches, so neither path reclaims the reader's returned copy.

For account-tracked vectors, terminal query cleanup can consequently leave nonzero live allocations. Allocation-account finalization detects the invariant failure and suspends the CN registry's admission. Subsequent requests can fail, including the internal SQL needed to authenticate new connections. This is not exhaustion of the configured query byte limit; some queries on existing connections can still succeed.

### Minimal ownership repair

- Retain at most one current returned batch per Merge reader.
- Clean it before advancing to the next batch and during Prepare/Reset/Free.
- Make Free release the source reader when Reset has not run, preserving idempotent teardown.
- Keep ordinary non-materialized Merge, planner decisions and account protection unchanged.
- Do not introduce `MaterializedSingleBatch`: that later feature is absent from this production baseline.
- No new batch copies, allocation algorithms, goroutines, locks, I/O, configuration, wire protocol, catalog schema or persistent format changes.

Reviewed ownership closure: Source -> Merge -> borrowed Projection / copying MergeOrder and pSpool -> pipeline Reset/Free -> account finalization. MergeOrder's early Clean is safe because Batch.Clean clears owned vectors; later serial cleanup is idempotent.

### Regression coverage

The existing materialized-reader test suite now leaves returned-copy cleanup to the production owner and checks advancement, EOF, producer errors, cancellation, early Reset/Free, repeated teardown, source/operator reuse, independent readers, and real Projection/account finalization. A new small authenticated SQL test reuses the package's existing serialized cluster fixture.

The SQL witness uses synthetic data, not customer schema/data: two shared CTEs and four scalar consumers, with a plan gate requiring four Sink Scans. Each same-instance round checks direct SQL, two binary prepared executions, two SQL PREPARE/EXECUTE executions, exact results `[1, 0.04, 2, 6]`, fresh independent authentication/table reads and verified teardown.

### Tested with

All results below are **local validation of the exact candidate**, not a claim that this PR's GitHub CI has passed.

- Original `d2393868` plus the same final Merge tests: fails for retained batch allocations / terminal account invariant, including cancellation. Candidate: passes.
- macOS/arm64, Go 1.26.4: owning Merge package normal + vet-all and race pass; six individually selected materialized-reader tests each pass 100 race repetitions.
- Direct consumer packages `materialized`, `projection`, and `mergeorder`: pass.
- Authenticated SQL regression: two same-instance rounds pass, including both prepared protocols and fresh authentication.
- Linux/amd64, official Ubuntu 22.04 / Go 1.26.4 builder: fresh native build, exact clean candidate executable build, owning Merge package and focused authenticated SQL regression pass.
- The final packaged Linux executable was also launched separately in a bounded, isolated, no-network test container: both rounds / all ten witness executions, new authentication and cleanup pass.
- `git diff --check`: pass. No product code or test assertion was weakened for this hotfix.

Representative reproducible commands, after building matching native dependencies with `make cgo`:

```sh
.agents/skills/mo-dev/scripts/mo-cgo-test -v -vet=all -count=1 -timeout=120s ./pkg/sql/colexec/merge
.agents/skills/mo-dev/scripts/mo-cgo-test -race -count=1 -timeout=120s ./pkg/sql/colexec/merge
.agents/skills/mo-dev/scripts/mo-cgo-test -v -count=1 -timeout=120s ./pkg/sql/internal/materialized ./pkg/sql/colexec/projection ./pkg/sql/colexec/mergeorder
.agents/skills/mo-dev/scripts/mo-cgo-test -v -count=1 -timeout=240s -run '^TestIssue31064SharedCTEJoinAllocation$' ./pkg/tests/issues
```

### Remaining release / rollout boundaries

- Intended later rollout scope is **CN-only**; TN, LogService and Proxy do not require this operator patch. Roll out in controlled batches and verify new authentication, not only `SELECT 1` on an existing connection.
- Local Linux mode was `GOAMD64=v3`, `GOEXPERIMENT=simd`, Ubuntu 22.04/glibc 2.35. The exact production runtime image and CPU flags were not verified; private image access was unavailable. Local executable success is not universal runtime-compatibility or rollout clearance.
- The original production DDL/data/physical plan was not available. The real synthetic SQL proves the defect and availability mechanism, but is not presented as an exact customer replay.
- Human review, PR CI and final image/digest verification remain separate gates. No Release, image publication or production change has occurred.

author: thomasmichon
body:
## Intent

Refs #8689; preserves #7743's fresh-Manager repair owner and #6820's sequencing boundaries.

On a measured slow Windows host, an explicit sharing failure consumed most of the native origin's 180-second budget before a retry could finish. Increasing the runtime-construction watchdog cannot affect that earlier phase. Keep the default and existing admission rules; make a longer, still finite recovery budget an explicit per-request choice.

## Changes

- Admit `WORKTREE_MANAGER_ENGINE_ACQUISITION_TIMEOUT_SEC` only as a positive finite duration no greater than 3,600 seconds. Absence retains 180 seconds; invalid input refuses submission without echoing the value.
- Capture the choice in the durable Manager invocation and restore it for the pinned executor. Consume the private Manager option before engine forwarding; do not extend the shared context-key contract. An absent choice clears a later worker's ambient setting. Sharing retries consume the same original deadline and remain limited to three attempts; timeouts are not replayed.
- Preserve source, marketplace, ledger, provenance, process containment, refusal precedence, dependency, health, cutover and rollback checks. Do not downgrade the update-driver schema or introduce a second installer.
- Keep admission independent of heavy installer imports and delay the full Manager command module until verified canonical execution.
- Document the knob and the fresh-Manager path for an older engine that cannot read the current queue.

## Validation

The new regressions first produced 13 failures and 2 passes. Final canonical contained run:

```text
python tools\run-plugin-tests.py worktree-manager --test-file tests\test_engine_acquisition_budget.py --test-file tests\test_engine_origin.py --test-file tests\test_engine_origin_process.py --test-file tests\test_update_driver_cli.py --allow-explicit-tiers
151 passed, 4 skipped in 173.58s; 187.38s including preparation/cleanup
```

Ruff `F,E9` passes. The existing install-contract gate passes for all 13 plugins. The four skips are explicit POSIX-only native cases on Windows, not waived Windows failures.

- Unit: unchanged default, positive-finite bounds, rejection before enqueue/acquisition, one shared deadline, refusal/no-replay controls, request capture and ambient restoration.
- Simple end-to-end: actual Windows child holding the payload directory survives refusal; release permits retry. Real queue/worker/participant processes preserve exit, serialization, provider identity and three distinct explicit/absent budgets despite a different worker ambient value. A separate child loads the unchanged actual Worktrees engine adapter and joins the Manager-owned request through real participant custody. Its strict existing context validator accepts the request, and no private Manager argument reaches the forwarded body.
- Fresh state: disposable native registration/payload and queue homes exercise first-touch admission without installed host state. A full new-machine installer is not requalified here: provisioning and construction logic are unchanged.
- Live rollout: retained after review and promoted-release verification, through the ordinary authorized updater. These source tests do not claim that an installed host is repaired.

The synthetic queue fixture now stubs only the canonical product body, not queue, worker, custody or context restoration. Its native caller window is 30 seconds, accounting for interpreter, observer, the production worker's existing 15-second startup allowance and participant launch. The three-request drain receives three such finite windows, with a bounded aggregate item deadline. This corrects fixture composition rather than extending production deadlines or removing assertions.

The review's shared-context finding was reproduced first: the real engine adapter returned `update request contains unsupported execution context`. Keeping the budget in Manager-owned serialized arguments fixes the whole handoff rather than adding a key that only simultaneously upgraded engines understand.

## Contract impact

This stays inside the existing update operation as optional owner-internal configuration. Public invocation, exit codes, durable request/runner format, shared context keys and driver schema are unchanged; unknown arguments still refuse. A private `--engine-acquisition-timeout` option serializes the choice only between the Manager and its same-generation pinned executor, which consumes it before the older engine boundary. It is not a prerequisite command or a new argument sent to an independently upgraded engine.

Existing requests omit the option and retain 180 seconds even if a later worker has an ambient override. The actual pinned Manager executor validates and enforces its captured value; a newer payload or package number alone is not support evidence. The real unchanged engine adapter regression covers the supported strict-context baseline without requiring that engine to acquire a new key or parser option.

An older Manager may retain its stricter default and must not be reported as honoring this optional recovery choice. Expand the released provider first, verify the selected fresh generation, then opt into a longer budget. No baseline operation is retired. Existing immutable-runner retention owns queued execution across rollback; incompatible older driver schemas remain explicitly refused, never rewritten.

## Performance impact

Validation is constant-work at submission/acquisition and adds no process, network request, scan or retry. Default upper bounds remain unchanged. An explicit longer budget changes the permitted wait, not admission or a claimed speedup. Native queue fixtures avoid unrelated catalog/model discovery while retaining real process boundaries; no production startup SLO is inferred from their timings.

## Documentation impact

The Manager README documents the changed configuration, shared deadline, unchanged refusal policy and older-client recovery path. This realizes the existing installer vision's bounded, attributable self-repair and the service-contract pattern's preference for configuration within the owning operation. No new architecture, service, scheduler or lifecycle owner is introduced; existing installation and cutover documentation remains accurate.

## 問題

- 問題が複数あるとき、「対応」の項目がどの問題への対応なのかが読み取れない
  - 「対応」の節が項目を並べるだけで、問題との結び付きを書く決まりが無いのが原因

## 対応

- 問題が2つ以上あるときの、問題のラベル（`A: `、`B: `…）と、「対応」の節のラベルごとの小見出し（`### A: <見出し>`）の追加
- 複数の問題に共通する対応の`### A・B: <見出し>`と、どの問題にも当たらない変更の`### その他の変更`の追加
- `check_message.mjs`への、ラベルの順番、小見出しが指すラベル、小見出しの無い問題、問題が1つのときのラベルの検査の追加
- `check_message.mjs`の、ラベルの`: `の後ろの空白の、全角文字との間の空白の検査からの除外
- `check_message.mjs`の節の判定の、`##`までの見出しへの限定（`###`の小見出しで「対応」の節が切れないように）
- `SKILL.md`、`assets/gitmessage`、`docs/design.md`への書き方と例の追記

author: xndcn
body:
## Why

`loop-block-test` failed on some CI runners with `a speculated MAC loop was not vectorized` (main 40154719793, and the rerun of op1emu/bcore#29). Once #29 started recording each runner's CPU, the pattern was clear: it fails only on **AMD EPYC 9V74 (Zen 4, AVX-512)**, and the same shard passes on EPYC 7763.

**The loops were vectorized. The test counted them twice.** LLVM 15 doesn't know Zen 4 and reports it as `znver3`, and the znver3 tuning has no preference for 256-bit vectors. So with AVX-512, LV picks VF 16, and from VF 16 up it also adds a **vectorized epilogue** (VF 8). Both loops carry `llvm.loop.isvectorized` and do vector work, so `count_module` counted 464 against 232 speculated loops.

## Offline reproduction (no AVX-512 machine needed)

I dumped the IR just before LV from all 305 modules of loop-block-test shard 1, then ran `opt-15` over them (forced LV + the passes after it + `default<O1/O2>`) with different `-mcpu`/`-mattr`, and counted with `count_module`'s rule:

| Tuning | Old count | New count |
|---|---|---|
| znver3 + Zen 4's AVX-512 features (the LLVM 15 view of Zen 4) | **464** | 232 |
| generic + AVX-512 (likely how LLVM 15 sees Zen 5) | **464** | 232 |
| alderlake / znver3 / skylake-avx512 / sapphirerapids / x86-64-v4 | 232 | 232 |

(The Intel tunings and x86-64-v4 prefer 256-bit vectors: VF 8, no epilogue.)

## What

- `SatReductionSpeculation` adds a distinct `!{!"bcore.speculated"}` to the speculative copy's loop ID. LV keeps it on every loop it builds from the copy (the main vector loop, the epilogue, the scalar remainder).
- `count_module` counts each such copy once; vector loops without the tag are counted as before.
- The foreground translation's copy of the loop counting in `Core` is replaced with `count_module`, as the worker already does.

**Codegen is unchanged:** for 40 modules (31 of them using zmm), compiled with and without the tag through opt + llc for both znver3+AVX-512 and alderlake, the assembly is byte-for-byte identical.

## Tests

Added `bcore-vectorize-count-test` (second commit; covers the dedup logic regardless of host CPU):
- `rules`: fixed IR containing copy A's main vector loop + epilogue (same tag), copy B (a different tag), scalar remainders, an untagged vector loop, and a loop with vector ops but no vectorized mark → counts 3.
- `pipeline`: a W32 MAC loop block (`tests/data/mac_loop_block.ll`: the module as `Compiler::optimize` receives it, reduced with llvm-reduce-15 to 473 lines) run through the real `Compiler::optimize` at O1/O2, **compiled only, never executed**, for znver3+Zen 4 AVX-512 and for x86-64-v3: 1 speculated loop, 2 / 1 vector loops, counted as vectorized once. The CPU and features are overridden via the new `Compiler::set_target_cpu`; registered on x86-64 hosts only.
- Negative checks: drop the dedup and both tests fail; stop `SatReductionSpeculation` from adding the tag and `pipeline` fails (`rules` writes its own tags).


- full configuration: all 19 tests pass locally (including the two new ones); the noprof build compiles and both new tests pass there
- O1 emu suite: 793/793
- loop-block shard 1 with the fix: 232 speculated, 232 vectorized

Not covered by this PR: whether VF 16 + epilogue on AVX-512 hosts is faster or slower for FIR than VF 8. I have no AVX-512 machine to measure on; correctness is unaffected either way.

author: hashimthearab
body:
Fixes the red `dev` test `mod-host local_files::observation::tests::same_size_replacements_and_missing_sources_do_not_reuse_old_bytes`. It fails only on "Rust tests (windows-latest)" (run 40152738687 at 8931b3979, left `old`, right `new`).

## Root cause

The culprit is d4836c0a0e, "Avoid rereading unchanged mod sources during reload polling". It added the observation cache and this test together, so the test has no earlier commit to bisect against.

Reload polling reuses cached bytes while the source's `Identity` is unchanged and the 2 s content deadline has not passed. On Unix the identity includes device, inode and ctime. On Windows it held only creation time, modification time and length. NTFS tunnels a replaced name's creation time onto the file renamed over it. So an editor's save-by-rename that kept the length and modification time looked identical, and the cached old bytes were reused. That is a real production bug: a Windows mod reload could miss a same-size edit for up to one revalidation window.

## Fix

- On Windows, `Identity` now records the volume serial and file index from `GetFileInformationByHandle`, plus `ChangeTime` from `FILE_BASIC_INFO` when the file system reports it. `ChangeTime` is the Windows counterpart of ctime.
- On every platform, the file number and the change time are now separate fields.
- Package observation uses the same `Identity`, so it gets the fix too.

## Tests

- New test `replacements_with_identical_stamps_are_reread_before_the_deadline` runs on every platform. It strips creation, modification and change times from the identity to simulate Windows tunneling, so only the file number can expose the replacement. To check it, I temporarily set the Unix file number to a constant, matching the old Windows identity, and ran it on Linux. It failed with the CI message (`left: [111, 108, 100]`, `right: [110, 101, 119]`), and so did the existing replacement test. With the fix, both pass.
- `cargo test -p mod-host` passes on the remote Linux builder (462 lib tests). `cargo clippy -p mod-host --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- I could not compile the Windows-only code on the remote builder because it has no MinGW toolchain for `ring`. The Windows CI job on this PR is the check for it.

## How to see it

Nothing visible changes.

author: dmitry-kov
body:
OPC part names are URIs, and an unreserved character (a letter, a digit, `-`,
`.`, `_`, `~`) must not be percent-escaped. Word for Mac 16.114.1 refuses a
package with an `Override` whose `PartName` escapes one, even when the
`Override` names a part the package lacks. No rule reported it; the
case-override check (#106) recorded it as a gap.

- **`PKG012` (ERROR)** reads each `Override` in `[Content_Types].xml` and
  reports, once per `Override`, the escapes Word refused: an unreserved
  character (upper- and lower-case hex), a slash, a backslash, the bytes of a
  non-ASCII character, and a `%` not followed by two hex digits.
- Escapes of other ASCII characters are not reported: Word opened the variants
  escaping a space, `%` and `#`.
- The finding names the escape; it belongs to `package.content-types`, and its
  baseline identity is file, code and the `Override`'s location.

**Evidence** (`evidence/docx-escaped-part-names/`): twelve variants of the
Word-saved `word-review.docx` with one `Override` added for an absent part,
built byte for byte by `research/escaped_part_names.py`, with Word's verdicts;
8 refused, 4 opened, and the control opened before and after. A first pass that
did not wait for Word to be idle mixed up its prompts and was discarded.

**Corpus.** Over 1,903 public Word files `PKG012` fires on none; in this
repository on the three escaped case-override variants Word refused, whose
record now lists it. The fix evidence counts the new files.

Full pytest: 2795 passed, 7 skipped; from a built sdist: 2767 passed, 35
skipped; producer evidence, revision text, frozen replay, comment stories,
fixture rebuilds and the baseline/SARIF round trip unchanged; ruff clean. 13 of
the 19 new tests fail on 0.8.3; the others are controls.

author: alex09x
body:
## Problem

Rust introduce-variable could rewrite text in literals/comments, capture an existing binding, reuse a value across rebinding or mutation, treat overloaded operators as pure, lose macro grouping, and move a guarded shift panic. Later review also found NFC identifier collisions and literal patterns rewritten into catch-all bindings.

## Change

Use the analyzer's Rust syntax tree and binding/type evidence to select executable occurrences and prove primitive operations and direct field access. Preserve patterns, strings, comments and grouping; refuse uncertain effects, macro captures and panic placement before writes. Compare identifier identity with NFC using the already-locked ICU normalizer. Compose replacements against original coordinates and check the source has not changed before application.

Integration testing also exposed an overly conservative panic-order check on a previously supported conditional product. An operation's own panic now follows its mandatory selected operand; earlier operands and conditional copies retain their independent checks. This restores the existing positive case without disabling the negative panic-order guards.

## Reproduce and verify

One scoped invocation on a Linux x86_64 build node:

```sh
prod-code exec -- cargo test -p prod-code-mcp \
  --test introduce_variable_preservation --test orchestration -- --exact \
  canonical_identifier_freshness executable_literals_preserve_patterns \
  macro_capture_proofs positive_controls review_followups \
  seven_public_review_regressions uncertainty_and_evaluation_boundaries \
  a_variable_is_introduced_for_every_occurrence --nocapture
```

Original before runs exercised all seven reported cases through public planning/apply, live rust-analyzer syntax/definition/hover and actual rustc/runtime checks. The pattern regression changed `f(1)` from 2 to 1; the repair retains the pattern and result for normal and forced apply. NFC collision fixtures changed `(3, 100)` into `(3, 3)` before repair and now refuse unchanged, while fresh/case-distinct/compatibility-distinct names remain supported.

The initial integration command passed seven new groups but failed the existing safe conditional-product expectation. After the complete panic-order repair, focused positive/negative checks passed. The final command above passed **7 groups plus 1 existing test**, with **61 unrelated tests filtered out**, exit 0.

## Measurements

Final test runtimes: 23.34s for the new target and 19.58s for the selected existing test; 47.6s command wall time including compilation. Twelve of sixteen source/test files match the worker exactly. Primary changes are the focused panic-order correction and runtime control, plus replacing two external hash-log helpers with complete-source logging.

## Checks (run on a build node, paste the result lines)

- Recorded candidate formatting reused for unchanged bytes; primary changed files formatted on the build node after the coherent repair.
- Final scoped Clippy for the library and both targets: exit 0 with 105 baseline warnings, none in changed files. Earlier strict lint failed and is not claimed green.
- Final compile/test gate: `7 passed; 0 failed` and `1 passed; 0 failed; 61 filtered out`.
- `git diff --check` passed. Independent aggregate review and primary review of the repair and integration failure are recorded.

Cargo.lock adds only a direct consumer edge to the existing `icu_normalizer 2.3.0`; no package/version/checksum changed. No dependency installation, unrelated compatibility suite or broad test run was performed.

The harness uses live rust-analyzer for syntax/identity/type queries and scripted clean diagnostic responses; actual original/transformed compiler and runtime comparisons establish tested semantics. Unproven grammar, binding or effects can explicitly refuse. No global grammar or live diagnostic completeness guarantee is claimed.

Closes #1300

author: mahdishariatzade
body:
On MSI Stealth 14 laptops (such as the Stealth 14 Studio A13VF), the keyboard features an ANSI-style layout with an extra physical key placed in the bottom row between AltGr and Right Ctrl, engraved with backslash and pipe ('\\' and '|').

Hardware emits scancode 0x56 for this key, which the kernel atkbd driver defaults to KEY_102ND (the ISO European key for '<' / '>').

Map scancode 0x56 to backslash (KEY_BACKSLASH) to match the physical keycap.

Verified on MSI Stealth 14 Studio A13VF (MS-14K1).

author: grinv
body:
## Суть

```text
Dockerfile
  builder: python:3.14-slim + uv 0.13.5 → uv sync --frozen --no-dev (UV_COMPILE_BYTECODE=1, cache mount)
  runtime: python:3.14-slim ← .venv, compileall app alembic, pip удалён, USER 10001; uv в образе нет
.dockerignore: **/__pycache__, **/*.pyc, tests, docs, openspec, scripts, *.md (корень)
docker-compose.yml
  migrate (alembic upgrade head, один раз) → api, worker: depends_on service_completed_successfully
  порты postgres / redis / rabbitmq / api — 127.0.0.1
  redis — profiles: ["redis"] (в app/ его никто не использует)
ci.yml: job image — hadolint, docker build, trivy HIGH,CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed
```

`.env.example`: `RABBITMQ_URL` — `guest:guest`, как у брокера compose. pip удалён из рантайма: trivy находил HIGH в его vendored-копиях msgpack, urllib3, setuptools, а приложению он не нужен. `--ignore-unfixed`: без него 46 HIGH/CRITICAL в пакетах Debian без исправления — CI был бы красным навсегда.

Change `docker-image-compose` (`skip_specs`) заархивирован: поведение сервиса не меняется.

## Проверено

Было: образ 373 МБ с uv; `import app.main` на read-only ФС — 2,21–2,26 с (байткод при каждом старте); `.pyc` из `app/` уезжали в образ; миграции — в команде API; порты на всех интерфейсах.
Стало: образ 360 МБ без uv; импорт — 1,05–1,08 с; `alembic --help`, `import app.main` / `app.worker` на `--read-only`, `uid=10001`. `docker compose up` с нуля: `migrate` отработал один раз с кодом 0, `/health` — `ok`, Redis не поднят. hadolint, trivy, zizmor — чисто; `pytest` — 1898 passed.

body:
**Scores change.** This adds the first new detection signal since 0.5.0. It was tuned on development data only and then scored **once** on the frozen 0.6 held-out set.

## The era bias, fixed first
- New `benchmark/modern-human.json`: 80 human passages from **before Nov 30, 2022** (pre-ChatGPT), each with its license and a permanent link: Stack Exchange 35, Wikinews 15, Wikipedia 20, Wikibooks 10.
- It confirms the bias: Stack Exchange answers use "you" as often as casual AI text (4.0 vs 3.8 per 100 words), so "you" and contractions are not usable signals.

## The new signal: vocabulary variety
- The measure is the share of distinct words in each 30-word window, averaged over the text, so it doesn't depend on text length. Human text averages about 0.85 and AI text about 0.90, so AI repeats words less.
- It applies to texts of 40 words or more. Above 0.93 it adds `round((v - 0.93) * 300)` points, at most 21.
- On the development sets, the parameters add no false alarms on modern human text:

| set | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| regression corpus | 16/60 AI, 61/62 human clean | **19/60**, 61/62 |
| 0.5 held-out (dev) | 3/34, 31/32 | **10/34**, 30/32 |
| modern human | 76/80 clean | 76/80 |

## One-shot held-out result (`heldout-0.6.json`, never seen during tuning)
| detector | AI caught | human clean |
| --- | --- | --- |
| released v0.6.0 | 2/35 | 30/35 |
| this PR | **5/35** | 30/35 |

The exact reports are committed in `benchmark/reports/`.

## Disclosed, not fixed
On fresh human text, even v0.6.0 flags 5 of 35 human samples, worse than the 31/32 published earlier. The cause is two existing rules:
- uniform rhythm, on a recipe and a press release;
- triads, in health advice. One triad match ("chronic, severe, or even") treats "even" as a list item, which looks like a bug.

Fixing them now would mean tuning on this held-out set, so they're documented for the next round, which will need a new frozen set.

## Other changes
- Results gain `metrics.vocabVariety` and `breakdown.structural.variety`; SCORING.md documents both.
- Updated the published figures in the README, the website, and `benchmark/README.md`, plus a changelog entry under Unreleased.
- `npm test` passes, 137/137, including a new variety test. Docs, bench floors, and `check:release` pass.

author: matkaise
body:
Brief §3: heavy calculations (history, TWR) run in a Web Worker (comlink), so the UI stays responsive.

## What changes
- **`src/lib/calculations/`**
  - `portfolioCalculations.ts`: pure functions on plain data (`computeMaxHistory`, `computeAnalysis`). `createHistoryInput` sends only the FX rates of the currencies involved (new `pickFxRates` in `domain/fx/rates.ts`, minor units such as GBp map to GBP). Copying the full ECB table to the worker took ~55 ms on the main thread; now it takes ~25 ms, mostly price histories.
  - `calculations.worker.ts`: `expose(calculations)` via comlink 4.4.2 (`new Worker(new URL(...), { type: 'module' })`, works with Turbopack in dev and build).
  - `calculationClient.ts`: `runCalculation(name, input)`. Without `Worker` (SSR, tests), or if the worker script fails or the input can't be cloned, it calculates synchronously on the main thread with the same result. An error inside a calculation is passed on as-is.
  - `useWorkerComputation(name, input)`: drops results of inputs that changed in the meantime and keeps the previous result while recalculating. `null` = nothing to compute.
- **AnalysisContent**: uses the worker instead of `setTimeout` + synchronous calculation. The cache (`isCacheFor`) stays. The worker returns the metrics with and without dividends, so the dividend toggle no longer triggers a recalculation or the "Analysedaten werden berechnet..." screen.
- **DashboardContent**: the MAX daily history also comes from the worker. While it recalculates, the previous history stays visible.
- Dev dependency `jsdom` 30.1.2, only for the hook test (`// @vitest-environment jsdom`).

## Tests
- Hook: synchronous fallback without Worker (result equals `computeAnalysis`), a late result of an old input is dropped (the test fails without the guard), the old result stays visible while recalculating, nothing happens after unmount, an error is not passed off with the old result.
- Calculations: equal to the previous direct calculation path; the FX subset gives identical results (incl. GBp and fee currency); results survive structured cloning.
- `npm run lint`, `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm test` (223 passed, 1 skipped as before) and `npm run build` are green locally.

## Measurements (production build, `next start`)
**"Demo ansehen":** the analysis page shows the same figures as before (volatility 6.7 %, Sharpe 1.95, max drawdown −10.0 % Apr. 2025, all monthly returns, sector/region shares). The demo calculation is small: even before this change, no long task over 50 ms came from it.

**Synthetic large portfolio** (local only, not part of the PR): demo + 20 well-known stocks, monthly buys since 2012, ~3,870 transactions, 5,400 daily points. Main-thread blocking was measured with a MessageChannel heartbeat (gaps > 50 ms). The `longtask` observer reports nothing while the browser pane is hidden. Same data before and after, page text identical.

| Action | before: blocked total / longest block | after: blocked total / longest block |
|---|---|---|
| Toggle dividends (analysis) | 651–703 ms / 228–251 ms (4 blocks) | 169–177 ms / 169–177 ms (1 block, render only) |
| Switch portfolio (dashboard + analysis recalculate) | 823–889 ms / 488–517 ms | 345–380 ms / 242–278 ms |
| Open project + price sync (25 s window) | 2,192 ms / 552 ms | 1,715–1,759 ms / 458–481 ms |
| Tab switch dashboard ↔ analysis (cached) | 225–232 ms | 205–221 ms (unchanged, rendering) |

In the worker: `computeMaxHistory` takes ~210–260 ms round trip, `computeAnalysis` ~350–490 ms. Before, that time blocked the main thread; now only sending the input does (~25–30 ms).

## Not in this PR (possible follow-ups)
- What still blocks is mostly rendering (Recharts with ~5,400 points, chart widths) and derivations that live in the components (`riskSeries`, MWR monthly map), each ~150–250 ms on large portfolios.
- Dashboard and analysis each calculate the same MAX history (once raw, once normalized). They could share one worker result.

author: skuzow
body:
## Summary

Links CRUD for signed-in users, plus edge-cached slug redirects and a Vitest suite.

Redirect path (`server/middleware/link-redirect.ts`):

```text
on(GET|HEAD /:slug)
  skip /api, /_*, multi-segment, invalid or reserved slug
  cached = edge cache (origin, slug)
  if cached miss          -> fall through (404 page)
  if cached hit           -> count click (GET only), 302
  url = D1 lookup
  if none                 -> store miss (15s), fall through
  count click (GET only), store redirect (60s), 302 no-store
```

Cache purge on every write that can change a slug's target:

```text
POST   /api/links        purge [slug]
PUT    /api/links/:id    purge [old slug, new slug]
DELETE /api/links/:id    purge [slug]
deleteUser.beforeDelete  purge [all user slugs]   (resolves TODO)
```

```diff
 app/
+├── components/links/     # Card, Grid, Toolbar, FormDialog, Empty, Skeleton
+├── composables/useLinks.ts, useLinkForm.ts
+├── middleware/guest.ts   # signed-in users leave /login for /links
+└── repository/           # client API modules ($api plugin)
 server/
+├── api/links/            # list, create, update, delete
+├── middleware/link-redirect.ts
+├── repositories/link.repository.ts
+├── utils/link-redirect-cache.ts
+└── testing/              # miniflare-backed test server + local D1
 shared/
+├── schemas/link.schema.ts   # slug + redirect URL rules, shared by form and API
+└── constants/link.constant.ts
```

Infra:

- Migrations squashed into `0000_init.sql` (auth tables + `links`).
- `wrangler.jsonc`: `db` binding now targets `skuz-link-pro`; `skuz-link-dev` moves to `previews` / `preview_database_id`. Migrate scripts target the `db` binding.
- CI gets a `test` job; Husky pre-commit runs tests.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `pnpm test` → no `test` script; no coverage of links, redirects or cache.
  **After:** `pnpm test` → `Test Files 12 passed (12) · Tests 136 passed (136)`

Covered behaviors include:

```text
redirect: GET counts click, HEAD redirects without counting
redirect: cache hit / miss / store / purge
redirect: any-case http(s) scheme accepted
api: create/rename/delete purge affected slugs; 409 on taken slug
auth: deleteUser purges redirects for the deleting request's origin
schema: reserved slugs rejected
search: query with leading slash matches
```

## Merge Danger

**Door:** one-way

The migration squash renames `0000_open_shinko_yamashiro` to `0000_init`. Any D1 that already applied the old file will see `0000_init` as new and fail on `CREATE TABLE account`. Reset `skuz-link-dev` (and `skuz-link-pro` if it was migrated) or rewrite its `d1_migrations` row before deploy. Code paths stay two-way.

**Blast Radius:** wide

- Deploys now bind to `skuz-link-pro`: run `pnpm db:migrate-pro` first, or every request touching D1 fails.
- Middleware intercepts every single-segment GET/HEAD path. A new top-level page must go in the reserved slug list, or a link can shadow it.
- `caches.default` is per-colo, so purges clear only the local colo. Other colos can serve a stale redirect for up to 60s, or a stale miss for up to 15s.
- Account deletion now reads and purges all of the user's links before delete.
