author: xyrolle
body:
## What was wrong or missing

- **The message chunks sat beside the bundler's chunk directory, not in it.** A client build put them in a sibling of the directory its chunks go to. Under Kit that is `_app/immutable/grai/`, still immutable. Under Astro (`_astro/`) and plain Vite (`assets/`) it is the site's root: `/grai/` and `/grai-<locale>/`. Hosts serve only the bundler's directory as immutable: `@astrojs/node` caches `/_astro/*` for a year and `/grai/*` not at all, so every visit would revalidate the message chunks.
- **A page with no module of messages never saw an edit in dev.** An edit reaches a page as a patch, which the dev module of messages applies. An Astro page draws its words on the server; one without an island loads no such module, and kept its old words until reloaded by hand.

## What changed

- The message chunks go to a `grai/` within the chunks' directory (`_astro/grai/`, `assets/grai/`, `_app/immutable/chunks/grai/`), and each locale's copies to `grai-<locale>/` beside it. They are at the same depth, so their relative imports resolve alike.
- `grai({ reloadOnEdit: true })`: in dev, an edit reloads the open pages instead of patching them. The server environments still take the patch, so a reloaded page renders without the app being evaluated again. On both paths the pages are now sent their update after the servers are sent theirs. It is off by default; the Astro adapter, coming next, sets it.

No hot path changes: build output paths and a dev-only option.

## How it was tested

- `test/vite.test.ts`:
  - a new test that a build puts the message chunks in `assets/grai/` and their copies in `assets/grai-<locale>/`. It failed before, with `grai/`, `grai-de/` and `grai-en/` at the root;
  - the import-map tests in Chromium, and `test/svelte.test.ts` and `bench/svelte-texts.mjs`, on the new paths;
  - a new test that with `reloadOnEdit` the pages are sent `full-reload` and no `grai:update`, and the server's render shows the edit. It failed before, with the pages sent `grai:update`.
- Gate: biome, both typechecks, the package build, and `test/vite.test.ts` with `test/svelte.test.ts`, in Chromium, under the shared heavy lock at a load of 14–16: 26 passed, against 24 on `main` (`9ece86a`) in the same window.

## For other PRs

- #11's per-locale delivery follow-up matches Kit's message chunks under `/immutable/grai/`; they are now under `/immutable/chunks/grai/`.
- #46 changes `src/vite-dev.ts`, `src/vite.ts` and `test/vite.test.ts` too. Whichever lands second is rebuilt on `main` by cherry-pick.

The day's restart count and the task's recent updates include it.

Stacked on #1402 (D1, the feed channel). This branch contains #1402's commits, so merge #1402 first. The diff of D3 alone against `claude/atlas-devui-chan` is 29 files, +6473/-1.

- **Actions from the map.**

- **Action log and undo.** The Alt+L panel lists each action with its result. Undo of a spawn runs the matching delete. Read-only overlay refreshes stay out of the log.

author: shaullavo
body:
## Quick summary

Listing a large directory used to rebuild and send the entire list for every small guest buffer. Directory reads now fetch only the records needed for that buffer, with cookies that continue to work when entries change.

Fixes #118.

## Implementation

- Add `FileSystem.readdirPage(handle, cookie, byteLength)` while retaining full-list `readdir` for host callers.
- Keep an original balanced live-entry index per directory, with monotonic unsigned 64-bit cookies and no per-descriptor snapshots or tombstones.
- Return Preview1 binary records through existing response transport, including exact partial headers and UTF-8 names. Large buffers and names use existing overflow replies, not a new 64 KiB semantic cap.
- Validate page bounds and cookies at the service boundary before dispatch. Preserve rights, mode, revocation, namespace traversal, and removed-open directory lifetime.
- Document live mutation and reload semantics in `docs/directory-pages.md`.

This branch originally started independently at `cc885cd`. It now merges landed link-count and truncate work from pinned main; its own changes remain limited to the granted enumeration work and required fixtures. No watcher draft is included.

## Evidence

Retained red commit `cfadb5f` reproduces the problem through a real Worker, service, client, and actual WASI `fd_readdir`. Its correctly paged consumer checks every complete record and retries partial records. Before the fix, the focused file reports 1 pass and 2 failures.

For 10,000 entries and 4 KiB guest buffers:

| Counter | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Enumeration calls | 87 | 87 |
| Full lists including probes | 90 | 0 |
| Materialized entries | 900,180 | 10,201 |
| Completed response bytes | 43,388,280 | 354,261 |

These are operation and completed-payload counters, not browser latency or network traffic. Post-fix tests count real index traversal and yielded entries, with a positive materialization bound to prevent bypass-green.

- `bun test tests/metadata-directory-contract-r173.test.ts tests/metadata-readdir-r173.test.ts`: 16 pass, 137 assertions.
- `bun test tests/host.test.ts tests/filesystem-{permissions,refcount,worker,review,publication}.test.ts tests/installer-symlinks*.test.ts tests/metadata-directory-contract-r173.test.ts tests/metadata-readdir-r173.test.ts`: 305 pass, 7,541 assertions across 20 files.
- Source and NodeNext TypeScript checks pass. Tooling TypeScript reports only the absent generated `dist/proc/directory.js` import; no build output was generated for this lane.
- Focused format, lint, duplicate scan, and `git diff --check` pass. Installed tools differ from pinned versions: oxfmt 0.70.0, oxlint 1.85.0, jscpd 5.4.2. This is not a full quality-gate claim.

Additional controls cover deletion, rename and replacement, symlinks through existing namespace edits, cookie exhaustion, unsigned boundaries, exact partial UTF-8 bytes, a 72,000-byte name through Worker binary overflow, cancellation, revocation, foreign handles, rights, removed-open directories, and balanced index cleanup. Full browser storage, consumer, size, and immutable integration gates remain with the coordinator.

## Integration note

The landed link-count fix and this branch share fixture paths. The composition keeps this branch's directory-capable WASI and Worker fixture superset; the service fixture is identical. No protocol, persistence format, read preparation, revision, resize, or watcher publication expansion is added by this PR.

## Style repair and pinned-main composition

The independent correctness review approved `4d4b0b3e28dd8c57c5b65cd7e9c5eff91b8e9171`. Its two production nesting notes are corrected by helper extraction. The AST audit also found an unbraced-control depth-four path in the shared WASI test fixture; that loop is extracted while descriptor disposal stays in the original finally. All added TypeScript now stays within three control levels, including unbraced controls.

Final head `42525cd6b7f6b139fd4e9016f35af8c176ed5671` normally merges exact main `4cf4ba4a21c27b207d7227ce5d17333b5bdd698e`. Conflicts combine count/index bookkeeping and keep the fixture superset. The shared metadata and truncate files match main exactly; all link-count updates remain present. No rebase or force push.

The canonical queue passed 33 focused directory/Wasm, link-count and pinned-truncate tests with 266 assertions, plus the one exact resident test with 7 assertions. Full source and NodeNext types, fixture types, scoped lint/format, AST depth and composition-preservation checks pass. Formatting required only a helper-signature wrap; only static checks were repeated afterward. No 305-test, browser/product, prepare, Rust or full-quality campaign was repeated. Prior counter measurements above remain the baseline evidence. Keeping draft for parent final checks and landing.

author: bosunski
body:
Operators can inspect and restore retained releases directly with `rook releases list`, `inspect` and `restore`, even while the daemon and control plane are unavailable. These native commands replace the Python recovery utility and do not load agent credentials or connect to the control plane.

Restore requires the service stopped, an exclusive local lock, the expected current release and explicit acknowledgement of every uncertain operation. It persists a mutation fence, verifies retained containers, images and readiness, then saves the binding and retires the predecessor. Existing opaque metadata is preserved. No rebuild, image pull, migration or database restoration occurs; reconciliation and fence removal remain explicit operator steps. See the [command reference](https://github.com/phpsandbox/rook/blob/bosun/offline-release-recovery/docs/host-execution.md#local-release-commands).

Builds on terminal-operation durability changes in #10 (merged).

Validation: full Go tests and race tests, vet, formatting, installer syntax and Linux AMD64/ARM64 builds pass. Native commands restored retained releases in both directions on an isolated host, reusing exact containers with unchanged migration/startup records and application data. Post-restore workflow checks and control-plane reconciliation passed. The minimum Go version is now 1.26.10 to include the certificate distrust fix; the vulnerability scan is clean. CI intentionally skipped.

author: bitcodepro
body:
From the audit of Kafka administration.

## Problems
1. **The `.DLT` topic always got 1 partition.** `CreateQueueAsync` made `<topic>.DLT` with `NumPartitions = 1`, but the topic exists to match Spring's dead-letter convention. By default Spring's `DeadLetterPublishingRecoverer` publishes to the **same partition number** as the failed record, and Spring documents that the DLT needs at least as many partitions as its source. Example: `orders` has 6 partitions and `orders.DLT` has 1. A record failing on partition 3 can't be dead-lettered, so the consumer retries it forever or stops.
2. **Consumer lag was understated when a partition's watermarks couldn't be read.** If a partition had no leader after retries, for example during a broker restart, the watermark loop set the count error and stopped. `Ends` then held only the partitions read before it. `WithConsumerLagAsync` counted every missing partition as lag 0 and still showed a precise number. Example: partitions 0-3 with partition 1 leaderless, a group committed at 100 everywhere, high watermarks at 1000. Expected lag is 3600 or "unknown"; the app showed 900.

## Change
1. **DLT partitions.** The topic setup moved into a new `TopicSpecifications(QueueDefinition)`. The DLT now gets the same partition count as its source (`Partitions ?? 1`). The existing handling of "DLT already exists" and "DLT refused" is unchanged.
   - When partitions are added to a topic, `GrowDeadLetterTopicsAsync` grows each existing `<topic><suffix>` DLT (using the profile's dead-letter suffixes) that has fewer partitions.
   - It never shrinks a DLT, and it never touches another topic's DLT.
   - If growing the DLT fails, the error says the topic grew but its DLT did not, so records failing on the new partitions can't be dead-lettered until it is fixed.
2. **Lag.** The watermark loop (`ReadTopicInfo`) keeps going past a partition it can't read, so every readable partition is still counted.
   - `LagOf` returns null when a group has committed on a partition whose end wasn't read.
   - `ConsumerGroupLag.Lag` is now `long?`. Null is shown as "lag unknown (a partition end could not be read)", or "some lag unknown" when other groups have a known lag. The row is highlighted instead of looking caught up.
   - `MaximumLag` counts only known lags.

## Tests
Each new test fails on main.
- `KafkaPartialWatermarkLagTests` uses a fake consumer whose `QueryWatermarkOffsets` throws LeaderNotAvailable for partition 1:
  - partitions 0 and 2 are still read;
  - a group committed on all three partitions gets a null lag;
  - a group committed only on the readable partitions gets 180.
  - A second test covers how an unknown lag is displayed.
- `KafkaDeadLetterPartitionsTests` checks `TopicSpecifications`: a 6-partition topic gets a 6-partition DLT, and no partition count gives 1.
- Integration test `The_dead_letter_topic_has_and_keeps_the_partitions_of_its_topic` creates a topic with 3 partitions and asserts the DLT has 3. It then grows the topic to 5 and asserts the DLT reaches 5. It ran against a Kafka container started as in CI, and all 14 Kafka integration tests passed.

## Full runs
- Windows: 3388 passed plus 93 UI.
- Linux: 3356 passed plus 93 UI.

author: nasyrov
body:
**Fixes #3353**

## Summary

A plugin author no longer lists locales. The build discovers the locales a plugin ships from the compiled `<locale>.mjs` files under its `catalogPath`. A published plugin ships `locales/*.mjs` and no `.po` files, and compile writes one `.mjs` per `.po`, as the issue comment decided.

```diff
 export interface PluginI18nSlot {
   readonly sourceLocale: string;
-  readonly locales: readonly string[];
   readonly catalogPath: string;
 }
 export const PLUGIN_I18N_SLOT = {
   sourceLocale: "en",
-  locales: ["en", "uk", "ar", "de", "zh-CN"],
   catalogPath: "./locales",
 };
```

```diff
 computeManifestAndRegistry(plugins, { ..., projectRoot })
   buildManifest(registry, {
     plugins,
+    pluginCatalogLocales: discoverPluginCatalogLocales(plugins, projectRoot),
   })
     projectPluginI18n
-      projectCatalogLocales(enabled, slot.locales, sourceLocale)
+      projectCatalogLocales(enabled, pluginCatalogLocales[id], sourceLocale)
 stagePluginCatalogs        # reads the compiled .mjs, not slot.locales
 collectPluginCatalogFiles  # reads the compiled .mjs, not slot.locales
```

- `discoverPluginCatalogLocales` lives in `packages/plumix/src/vite/plugin-catalog-resolve.ts`. It uses the same `resolveCatalogDir` lookup that staging uses.
- `plumix build` now fails on a missing compiled catalog only for the source locale. A declared locale with no `.mjs` can no longer happen.
- Two tests are gone because they only kept lists in step:
  - the `PLUGIN_I18N_SLOT.locales` vs Lingui locales check in `define.test.ts`;
  - "each plugin declares exactly the locales it ships" in `plugin-catalog-packaging.test.ts`.

  A test that `PLUGIN_I18N_SLOT.sourceLocale` matches core's Lingui source locale stays.
- Docs: `apps/docs/.../plugins/i18n.mdx` and `docs/architecture/i18n.md` no longer describe a declared `locales` list.

## Evidence

- **Before:** the new test in `packages/plumix/src/vite/manifest.test.ts` failed.
  ```
  fixture plugin: catalogPath = tmp dir with en.mjs, pt-BR.mjs; no locales
  site enables ["en", "pt-BR"]
  expect(pluginI18n.translated.catalogs["pt-BR"]).toBe(".../locales/pt-BR.mjs")
  - "pt-BR": "/_plumix/admin/plugins/translated/locales/pt-BR.mjs"
  + "pt-BR": "/_plumix/admin/plugins/translated/locales/en.mjs"
  ```
  The type test in `define.test.ts` (`// @ts-expect-error` on `locales: [...]`) failed with `TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive`.

  **After:** both pass.
  - Unit tests: core `src/plugin` 26 files, 484 tests; plumix `src/vite` 40 files, 280 tests.
  - Typecheck: `turbo run typecheck --filter @plumix/core --filter plumix` is clean.
- **First-party catalogs still serve:** I ran `plumix build` of `apps/demo` with `i18n: { locales: ["en", "de-AT", "uk"] }` added for that one build. It staged `dist/client/_plumix/admin/plugins/blog/locales/{en,de,uk}.mjs`, with `de` serving `de-AT`. Discovery from `apps/demo` returns `["ar","de","en","uk","zh-CN"]` for every first-party plugin.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

The change is code only, with no data or migrations, and a revert restores the field.

**Blast Radius:** consumers

- Third-party plugins that set `i18n.locales` get a type error until they delete it. The framework minor changeset tells them to.
- A plugin whose `catalogPath` holds extra `.mjs` files that are not catalogs would now have them served as locales. No first-party plugin has any: `locales/index/` is a subdirectory, and discovery reads only top-level files.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] The plugin `i18n` slot type has no `locales` field, and passing one is a type error.
- [x] The default slot locale list is deleted, along with the test that kept it in step with the shared Lingui locales.
- [x] The manifest build, given a fixture plugin with compiled `en.mjs` and `pt-BR.mjs` and a site enabling `pt-BR`, emits the `pt-BR` catalog with no declared locales.
- [x] Every first-party plugin's descriptor drops `locales` (they share `PLUGIN_I18N_SLOT`), and their catalogs still serve.
- [x] The plugin i18n docs and the i18n architecture page no longer mention a declared `locales` list.
- [x] A changeset (framework minor) says the field is removed and catalogs are discovered.

## Notes

- `pnpm test:mutation`: plumix had no surviving mutants. Core's Stryker first test run timed out in this sandbox (`Initial test run timed out!`), so the core changes have not been mutation-tested.
- `catalog-locales.test.ts` reported "11 skipped" with no failure when run alongside three other test files. It passes 11 of 11 when run alone. I didn't investigate further.
- `plumix build` of the demo prints a Rolldown bundler-timings notice. This change doesn't cause it, and I haven't checked whether `main` prints it too.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---

### Review

- Added direct unit tests for discoverPluginCatalogLocales (sorted top-level .mjs only, ignores .po files, a directory named like a catalog and nested catalogs, missing directory gives [], plugin with no i18n slot is omitted). Deleted the ticket-number and what-comment from computeManifestAndRegistry in manifest.ts. Made the manifest test clean up its temp directory with onTestFinished so a failed assertion no longer leaks it.
- Left `packages/plumix/src/vite/plugin-catalog-resolve.ts:179` — compiledCatalogLocales treats any top-level .mjs as a locale and does not validate the tag: Issue comment 2 pins discovery from compiled `<locale>.mjs` files under catalogPath, so I left it. A stray non-catalog .mjs would be served as a locale; the PR body lists this as a blast-radius risk. No first-party plugin has one.
- Left `packages/plumix/src/vite/plugin-catalog-resolve.ts:108` — Smell: the catalog directory is scanned three times per build (discoverPluginCatalogLocales, stagePluginCatalogs, collectPluginCatalogFiles): Possible Duplicated Code. stagePluginCatalogs could stage from manifest.pluginI18n instead of rescanning. Restructuring the staging contract is more than this ticket asks, and the scans are cheap build-time readdirs.
- Left `packages/core/src/plugin/build-manifest.ts:147` — Smell: Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>> for plugin id to shipped locales appears in several signatures: Possible Primitive Obsession or Data Clump. A named type adds an export that surface:check would need a reason for, and there are only a few occurrences.
- Left `packages/plumix/src/vite/plugin-catalog-packaging.test.ts:100` — No test now checks that each first-party plugin's locales/ holds compiled .mjs files: The deleted test checked declared locales against .po files. The remaining test checks the catalog directory is published. A check that i18n:compile output exists would need a build, which test:unit does not have; the PR body's demo build run is the evidence that first-party catalogs still serve.
- Left `apps/docs/src/content/docs/plugins/i18n.mdx:157` — Left the 'site-side half of the intersection' wording: It is still true: the build serves the intersection of the locales the plugin ships and the locales the site enables. It no longer mentions a declared locales list.

author: amatsuda
body:
The container-literal walk reads the writes of a name from a per-name index and keeps the argument a caller's layout hands a parameter.

## What happened

`container_literals` collects the container literals a value can evaluate to, following a variable's writes and a parameter's callers. The boxed-element widening (`widen_boxed_elem_sources`) asks it at every store it widens through, in every round, and the walk recurses through what it finds, to depth 4.

Two of its cases were paid in full at each ask:

- For an ivar, gvar, cvar or constant read it walked every write node of that kind in the program, comparing each one's name with the read's.
- For a method's parameter it took every call of the method's name, resolved its targets, and laid the call's arguments out over the parameters (`call_layout`) to read the one slot it needed.

On a Rails application the walk was 20% and 12% of two windows sampled inside the main fixpoint loop; within it, 63% of the samples were in the layouts and 23% in the name scan's compare (an inlined field lookup per write node).

## The fix

Two commits:

1. The writes of each name are listed once per node table, by write kind (`clw_first_named`, chained ascending, rebuilt when the table changes, as `cst_first` and the other such indexes are). The walk reads the list for the name it follows; the class filter and the recursion are unchanged, and so is the order the writes are visited in.
2. The argument index a call's layout hands a parameter is kept per (call, method, parameter) (`cla_layout_arg`). The layout is decided from the call's argument nodes and the method's parameter list alone (`arg_layout_untyped` asks no types), so the answer holds while the node table and the scopes do; the memo is reset when either moves.

## Measurements

Rails application (`--timing`, same machine, the runs alongside each other):

| | master | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| infer_param_types, 21 calls | 161.2 s | 95.3 s |
| infer_param_types_settle, 45 calls | 166.4 s | 121.1 s |
| analysis_fixpoint (31 rounds) | 1,880 s | 1,766 s |
| analysis_renarrow (2 rounds, inside the fixpoint) | 558 s | 490 s |
| an_method_backstops | 126 s | 94 s |
| analysis | 2,867 s | 2,692 s |

The application stops on the same deferred refusals, and its refusal output is identical line for line to master's. The Active Support sample's C is byte-identical to plain master's. 1,385 related corpus tests pass locally (the promote-lane one under `SPINEL_INT_OVERFLOW=promote`); the gate check passes.

author: lidge-jun
body:
Fixes #1636.

**Problem.** Stop interrupts a Codex root turn and every descendant turn GOAT knows of. A native subagent that registered (`subAgentActivity started`) before its first `turn/started` has no turn context yet, so it is missed. Codex reports that child's interruption as an `item/completed` on the stopped turn, which the adapter drops (the guard on `terminalizedNonCompletedNativeTurns` in the `item/completed` handler). The task stays `running`:

- the runtime-wide `hasPendingBackgroundWork` stays true;
- since #1634, the thread-scoped check stays true too, so `ProviderSessionManager` defers unloading that thread.

**Fix.** When Stop ends a turn (the turn is in `interruptingNativeTurns`), every registered subagent in that turn's lineage that is still `running` or `pending` and has no known active turn is marked `interrupted`. This uses `emitSubagentTaskUpdate`, the same update the dropped notification would have made. Only Stop qualifies. Codex also reports a turn that manual compaction replaced as `interrupted`, and a failed root is untouched, because native subagents keep working after a failed parent (`emitOrDeferRootTerminal`). Such a subagent is marked `endedByStop`, so if a later turn gives it work, its first real `turn/started` reopens the task. A first turn otherwise never reopens a task. A child whose late `turn/started` still arrives is interrupted by the existing late-subagent path, and a real new turn can still reopen it.

`CodexAdapterV2.ts` was at its 8615-line budget. The selection and the two subagent text helpers (`label`, `detail`) moved to a new `codexSubagents.ts`, which leaves the adapter at 8608 lines.

The subagent replay tests also pushed `CodexAdapterV2.computerUse.test.ts` over 1000 lines, so the file is split:

- the replay fixture moved unchanged to `CodexAdapterV2.attachment.testkit.ts`, with `preamble[4]!` narrowed instead of asserted;
- the #1571 and #1636 tests moved to `CodexAdapterV2.subagents.test.ts`.

**Test (written first).** "Stop ends a subagent that registered before its first turn started, so it stops counting as work (#1636)", in `CodexAdapterV2.subagents.test.ts`, replays the race the #1634 review found:

1. Turn 1 spawns a child.
2. Stop interrupts turn 1.
3. The child's `interrupted` arrives on the stopped turn.
4. Turn 2 completes.

On dev both thread-scoped and runtime-wide pending stay `true` (`expected true to be false`); with the fix both are `false`.

Two more tests cover review round 1's findings. Both fail on the first head of this PR, e5fca16108:

- "an interrupted turn without Stop leaves an initializing subagent counted": the turn ends interrupted with no Stop, and the child is still counted as work.
- "a subagent Stop ended before it began runs again when a later turn starts it": Stop, then a new parent turn, then the child's first turn runs and completes, and the task ends `completed`.

Verification: under Node 26, `vp test run` on the subagents, computer use and main Codex adapter suites passed 188/188. `vp run check:changed` passed.

Known limits (review round 2, P2, tracked in #1645): three Stop paths still leave an early child running:

- a Stop whose goal pause (`thread/goal/set`) is still in flight when the interrupted turn completes;
- Stop between goal turns;
- Stop after the root turn already completed.

None of these is worse than dev, where every such child stays running.

NOT RUN: a live Codex Stop while a spawned child is still initializing.

Done by claude-opus-5-5 in GOAT (Codex harness).

author: vincemakes
body:
## What

Slice 4 of the desktop app (`apps/desktop`, private workspace): the panels (Changes, Files, Terminal and tasks, Preview), the window laid out as one row of columns, and the context window taken from the `./config` door. Nothing outside `apps/desktop` changes; no new dependency.

## The panels

A big panel beside the rail: full height, half the Work's width by default, full screen on request, closable. Opened from the overflow menu, from a thumbnail in the stream, or from an output or task row in the rail.

- **Changes**: the files the latest run changed, as added and removed lines, from the edit and write calls on the log (works without git; a change a command made is not shown, and the panel says so).
- **Files**: the folder as a tree one level at a time; dependencies and dot folders are folded as "not listed"; a file previews as text, markdown or an image; files the run changed are marked.
- **Terminal and tasks**: a background task's log (only the end of a long one) and the latest run's foreground commands with the first lines they printed.
- **Preview**: a page on this computer in a sandboxed frame; a dev server's address is found in command output or typed.

## Safety

- The host's folder doors (`/desk/fs/tree`, `/desk/fs/file`, `/desk/task-log`) are GET only, behind the same token, Host and Origin guard. A path is relative to the folder's real path, resolved through every link, and must land inside the folder; a link out is shown as such and never followed; the kiso home and the policy's protected files are refused even inside the folder and through a link; folders the tree does not open are not read through; text is read to 256 KB, images to 2 MB; a file with a NUL byte is never read as text.
- The preview takes only `http` on `localhost` or `127.0.0.1`, no credentials, never this app's own port; the page's policy adds a frame source for those two hosts only.

## Layout

The sidebar, the stream, the panel and the rail are columns of one flex row: no column is positioned over another and none has a z-index, at any width. The stream gives way first (down to 320 px), then the panel takes the stream's place (its column 0 wide); the rail stays 244 px beside an open panel and only its overview key closes it. Buttons now opt out of the window-drag strip.

## Context window

Settings takes the window from `contextWindowOf` (the person's, else the registry's), so the rail's ring shows a percentage for known models and the compaction tiers know the window.

## Evidence

- `npm run check:full -w @vincemakes/kiso-desktop`: build, typecheck, gates and 22 proof runs, all exit 0. New proofs: `files` (16 safety checks on a folder with links out and in, a link to the credentials, a kiso home inside the folder, a binary, a big file, an image, dependencies, a dot folder), `panels` (5 accepted and 17 refused preview addresses, discovery, the changes derivation), `panels-ui` (Electron), `layout-ui` (Electron: six layouts at three widths with the sidebar closed and open: column order, no overlap, no positioning or z-index, the rail 244 px, the 320 rule, the panel taking the stream's place, full screen, the rail key; planting the wrong column order makes it fail). The Electron proofs stay out of the Dock and the focus, asserted.

## Size

`src/main` 1,649 / 2,500, `src/shared` 245 / 400, `src/renderer` 2,950 / 6,500 (S4 growth 629 of 2,000), `scripts/gates` 206 / 800, `scripts/proofs` 1,185 / 1,300 (raised from 1,000 by an owner ruling of 2026-10-25, noted in the gate and the README).

## For hosts

None. `apps/desktop` is private and not part of the root build, typecheck or check.

## Left for later

The cards the design draws in the stream after a change; the Changes panel lists the latest run only; dot files (not folders) are listed and previewable, a policy question not decided here.

author: go-while
body:
`wildmat` no longer reads past the end of a malformed pattern. Found by the area 2 (NNTP commands) review; the fix belongs to area 10.

## The bug

`DoMatch` (Rich Salz's wildmat, as in old INN) walked past the NUL of a malformed pattern:
- **A character class without its closing `]`** (`a[^`, `a[b`): the class loop stopped at the NUL, and the outer loop's `p++` stepped past it.
- **A `-` just before the end** (`[a-`): `*text <= *++p` read the NUL, and the loop condition read the byte after it.
- **A trailing backslash:** `p++` to the NUL, then the outer `p++` past it.

A client reached it with XPAT and `LIST ACTIVE <wildmat>`. The pattern is a `std::string`'s `c_str()`, so it read the byte after its end: a wrong match, or a crash at an allocation boundary. The file's own header said "foo[a-" could cause a segmentation violation.

## The fix

- **Malformed patterns:** an unterminated class and a trailing backslash end the match (no match).
- **Ranges:** a `-` is a range only when a character follows.
- **Well-formed patterns** match as before.

author: lvlie
body:
Adds support for Incus OCI application containers (`incus launch docker:…`, Incus 6.3+) and for containers managed by [incus-compose](https://github.com/lxc/incus-compose).

## Detection
- Instances that have `volatile.container.oci` or `image.type=oci` become devices of their own.
- The image reference comes from the copied image properties: `image.description` gives the registry and repository, `image.id` gives the tag or digest.
- incus-compose services are recognised by the `user.label.incus-compose.project` and `user.label.incus-compose.service` labels.

## Update check without pulling
- The agent fetches the manifest for the container's architecture and computes Incus's fingerprint: the SHA-256 of the layer digests, as in `client/oci_images.go`. It then compares that with `volatile.base_image`.
- Results are cached by manifest digest, so later checks only send a HEAD request until the tag moves.

## Upgrade
- **Plain OCI containers:** stop (forced after `guests.restart_timeout`, because many app containers ignore SIGTERM), rebuild from the registry through the Incus API, then start. Config, devices and volumes are kept. If the image is already current, nothing is rebuilt.
  - Incus refuses to rebuild an instance that has snapshots, so no snapshot is taken and there is no restore button. An instance with snapshots of its own is reported with a clear error instead of updated, and its snapshots are left alone.
- **incus-compose services:** `incus-compose up --detach --pull always --no-deps <service>` in the project directory. incus-compose recreates any instance whose image differs from the one it pulled, so a rebuild done behind its back would be undone by its next `up`.
  - It does not record where a project lives, so the agent searches `incus.compose_dirs` (default `/root`, plus its subdirectories) and matches compose files by project name.
  - If a project can't be found, its updates are still reported, but the install action and upgrade button are hidden and upgrade commands are rejected.
  - No snapshot and no restore button, because incus-compose recreates the instance.
- Upgrading the host and all guests (`upgrade_all`) includes app containers.

## Entities
- An *Image* update entity, *Updates available*, upgrade and result sensors, *Running*, *Platform*, and upgrade, restart and restore buttons.
- Nothing runs inside app containers, so they get no package, system, kernel or command entities.
- App image updates count in the host's image update totals.

## Also
- Incus architecture names (`x86_64`, `aarch64`) are mapped to OCI names (`amd64`, `arm64`) for registry lookups.
- incus-compose itself needs `core.https_address` set and an Incus OCI remote named after each registry; the README says so.
- `instance-updated` lifecycle events now trigger a resync, so config changes are picked up.

## Tests
- Unit tests:
  - parsing the image reference (tag, no tag, digest-pinned, registry with port, incus-compose labels);
  - the fingerprint against an in-memory OCI registry with a multi-arch index;
  - finding compose projects (`name:`, directory name, hidden directories);
  - the incus-compose command.
- Agent tests: plain app update and rebuild, the up-to-date case doing nothing, `upgrade_all`, an incus-compose service with and without a known project, and that no commands run inside app containers.
- End-to-end tests (Incus stable, where skopeo, umoci and incus-compose are installed): a BusyBox OCI container is launched, checked, made outdated by pointing `image.id` at a newer tag, then rebuilt (`image.id` updated, running, up to date). An incus-compose project is detected and upgraded through incus-compose. LTS 6.0 has no OCI support, so these tests are skipped there.

author: gunbai-bot[bot]
body:
## What

The seed now ends an unbraced match-arm body where the **arm grammar itself** reads the next arm. Before, a hand-written predicate spelled the pattern forms that could follow. Assigned by tidy-ant-251 (Manager 1); repro by sunny-bee-153.

## The defect (DESIGN 6b)

`v1.compiler.parse` `parse_match_arm_stmts` consumes statements of a body that opens with `let`/`return` until `looks_like_arm_start` says a new arm begins. That predicate recognised only `_`, an uppercase leaf (bare or braced) and a dotted path ending uppercase. A lowercase binder (`other =>`), a literal (`false =>`, `0 =>`, `none =>`) or a guarded arm was read as **one more statement**. With a nested match as the body's last statement, the outer arm was **re-parented into the inner match**:

```
A { n: n } => let m = n + 1
  match g(x: m) { A { n: _ } => A { n: m }  other => other }
other => other          <- taken by the inner match
```

The seed refused `non-exhaustive match: missing variant(s) B, C` on the outer match. Where the swallowed arm type-checks in its new home, nothing refuses at all.

**Earliest unjustified boundary:** the predicate. It answered a question the arm grammar already answers, and it had been widened once before for the dotted form. **Root generalization:** an arm starts exactly where `parse_match_arm` reads one, so `looks_like_arm_start` now runs `parse_pattern` and `parse_optional_guard` and asks for `=>`. An unmoved stream means no pattern. The hand-written helpers `arm_start_after_qualified_path`, `scan_for_fat_arrow_after_braces` and `peek_is_expected_at` are deleted. The stage0 mirror `v1_compiler_parse.rs` is regenerated from the edited source (`claim_executor --required-regen`). That regen also reports drift in `v1_compiler_infer*.rs` and `v1_std_core.rs`, which comes from main's emitter (clone elision), not this change, so it is left to heal.

**v2 is the authority and was never affected:** its arm body is the grammar's `match_arm_stmt_body`, each statement guarded by an arm-head predicate (`v2.extdeps.languages.dag`).

## Evidence (executed; each seed built from the tree measured)

| program | seed @ main 963e18 (sha256 `3a7458506284e616f841f4a8d1d7d8b99a304ccaaa9ee00f85cde6ccafab6998`) | seed @ this change (sha256 `5d3039c4109d726b6136a2ebe8d8ffeb22ea5251ad079758bdecfc1118062140`) |
|---|---|---|
| repro: binder arms, with `let` | **RED**: `non-exhaustive match: missing variant(s) B, C (probe.dag:10:3)` | compiled, 0 diagnostics |
| same, without `let` (positive) | compiled, 0 diagnostics | compiled, 0 diagnostics |
| keyword-literal arm (`false =>`), with `let` | **RED**: `expected expression, found FatArrow (probe.dag:17:11)` | compiled, 0 diagnostics |
| same, without `let` | compiled, 0 diagnostics | compiled, 0 diagnostics |

In the emitted Rust for the repro on the fixed seed, the inner match holds its own two arms, and `other => other` stays on the outer match.

**v2 cross-check** (`v2.test.claim.body_lowering.let_arm_body_ends_at_the_next_arm`, the keyword-literal program, so it needs no binder): `lab_a_let_body_ends_at_the_next_arm` PASS and `lab_the_same_arms_without_a_let_infer` PASS, executed through the seed interpreter. The binder repro itself also infers on v2 on the #15125 branch, with and without the `let` (measured, not enrolled here because it needs #15125's binder).

## Census

- **The shape on main:** a source scan of every unbraced `let`/`return` arm body followed by an arm the old predicate rejected finds **0 genuine sites**. Its 12 hits are all text inside string literals (fixture sources, emitted-Rust templates) or one-line compound forms. It is a scan, not a parse census.
- **Workarounds authored to avoid it:** sunny-bee-153's `v2.workflow.roster_import_sweep` `roster_sorted_disjoint_plan` (#15101), plus six helpers on their unpushed stacked branch (`roster_census_scoped`, `roster_census_planned`, `roster_supply_tail_edits`, `roster_missing_import_edit`, `roster_last_line`/`roster_indent_of`, `roster_supplied_report`). They can be inlined once this lands.

## Ledger

New RFM row `gunbc.recurring_failure_mode` `an_unbraced_arm_body_swallows_an_arm_its_predicate_does_not_spell`: found below the ladder, now at ceiling (structurally guaranteed), because the decision is the grammar itself. This is the seed-defect correction record: the seed is repaired, so no v2-vs-seed divergence remains to admit through `SeedDefectCorrection`.

author: aaron-sulbaran
body:
## D31: talk to your own Muse

`POST /api/chat { text, role? }` runs one model turn through the existing loop over **read-only tools**, so "remind me what that settle-up was for" and "why 16?" are answered from the same data the cards show.

- **Tools.** `get_plan`, `get_reel`, `get_wallet_and_history` (balance, allowance, every payment with reason, amount, status, date), `get_sharing` (what each side shares, what was removed and why), `explain_payment(paymentId)` (the breakdown lines and where each came from), plus the product's own `get_my_calendar` and `get_interests` (a private event's title is replaced by "a private event" before the model sees it). `where_to_do_that(action)` returns the product's line for a request chat cannot do.
- **Guard rails.** No tool sends a protocol message, moves money, decides a plan or changes a setting; a model that asks for one gets an error. "Pay Mochi $5" and "message Mochi's Muse" get: "I can't send money from chat. Tap Settle up on the plan: I'll prepare the payment with its breakdown, and you confirm it there." Side b gets a 403 (no chat there). 20 chat turns per room per hour (`MAX_CHAT_TURNS_PER_ROOM_PER_HOUR`) plus the app-wide hourly total: 429 `{paused, reason, text, budget}` with `Retry-After`. A model that is down gives 503 with the honest reason, a `turn_failed` row, nothing stored, and the slot back.
- **What it leaves.** `Room.chat` (last 40 lines, cleared by Reset), the answer's `proof` (model call plus `toolCalls`, counts and states only), and one Activity row `chat_asked` "You asked: ..." whose `messageId` is the answer's id.
- **Voice (D32).** Answers are one to three plain first-person sentences, no tool talk, so they read as a line in a thread as well as a chat bubble.

### Snapshot fields for Lane B

- `UiSnapshot.chat: UiChatMessage[]`: `{ id, from: "user" | "muse", text, at, replyTo?, proof? }`, in order (`proof` is the existing `ModelProof` with `toolCalls: {name, args, result}[]`). Text is renamed like the rest of the screen ("Michelle's Muse" when the simulated friend plays side b).
- `UiNote` kind `chat_asked` with `text` "You asked: ...", `answerId` (the Muse line's id in `chat`) and `toolCalls` (the tools used). `ActivityNote` has a minimal entry so it renders; Lane B owns the tools display.
- `POST /api/chat` response: `{ data: { question, answer, budget }, error: null }`; errors `{ data: null, error: { message } }` with 400, 403, 429 (also `paused`, `reason`, `text`, `budget`), 503. The composer should keep the text on 429 and 503.

### Flag

The snapshot is the same for both roles, so a real second phone could read side a's chat lines in the JSON (the screen draws them on side a only). Private calendar titles never reach the model, but the person's own questions and the Muse's answers do ride in `/api/state`. If that matters before a real second person joins, `/api/state?role=b` could drop `chat` (Lane B would pass `role` in `use-snapshot`).

### Checks

Fake model (`tests/chat.test.ts`, 18 tests): a plan question calls `get_plan` and the answer, the proof and the "You asked" row exist; follow-ups carry earlier lines; "why 16?" reads `explain_payment` lines with sources ("a sample receipt, not a real one", "my own estimate"); a pay request gets the settle-card line and nothing moves, prepares or sends, and the offered tool list has no `send_money`, `send_to_friend_agent`, `accept_payment`, `decline_payment`, `record_reel_details` or `read_receipt`; model down gives 503 with nothing stored; the route's 400, 403, 429 and 503; private titles masked; Michelle naming; Reset clears; 40-line cap.

Live, on the local JSON store with Muse Spark: seven questions answered in 1.4 to 3.4 s each from `get_plan`, `get_reel`, `get_wallet_and_history` plus `explain_payment` ($13 plate, $1 tax, $2 tip from the sample receipt), `get_sharing`; the pay and message requests got the card lines; wallets and payments unchanged.

Local gate: tsc, lint, `next build` clean; 798 passed, 8 skipped. `docs/TECH_SPEC.md` has a new "Chat with your Muse (D31)" section.

body:
## What and why

Two follow-ups to the docs site ([#137](https://github.com/hanzala-afzal-dev/laravel-dynamic-throttle/pull/137), ADR-0029).

**1. Security advisories in the site's toolchain.** After #137 merged, Dependabot flagged `docs/`, and its security update for `vite` failed. `npm audit` there reported 3 vulnerabilities, 1 of them high:

- `esbuild` ≤ 0.24.2, [GHSA-67mh-4wv8-2f99](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-67mh-4wv8-2f99): any website can send requests to the dev server and read the responses.
- `vite` ≤ 6.4.3, for example:
  - [GHSA-fx2h-pf6j-xcff](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-fx2h-pf6j-xcff) (high): `server.fs.deny` bypass on Windows;
  - [GHSA-rq7h-c2jc-7f22](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rq7h-c2jc-7f22): files outside `server.fs.allow`;
  - the `launch-editor` advisories.

All of them are in the **development server** (`npm run --prefix docs dev`). The published site is static files, and CI only runs `vitepress build`. They still matter for a contributor who previews the docs with a browser open.

VitePress 1.6.4, its latest release, depends on `vite ^5.4.14`, and no Vite 5 release fixes these. So `docs/package.json` now overrides Vite with **6.4.4**, released 2026-10-06, which fixes all of them and brings esbuild 0.25.12. After the override, `npm audit` reports 0 vulnerabilities. CONTRIBUTING says why the override exists and to remove it once VitePress brings a fixed Vite.

**2. The home page's GIF was a 404 in the dev server** (a bug from #137; the published build was fine). The home page's source is `docs/site/index.md`, and `rewrites` serves it as `index.md`. In the dev server, a relative image path then resolves from the new place, so `../../art/limit-change.gif` pointed outside the repository. Pages now import images through an `@art` Vite alias for the repository's `art/` folder, which resolves the same way in both modes. The hero's screenshot uses it too.

**Checked**, on both the dev server and the built site, in Chromium:

- the hero screenshot (2880 px) and the GIF (1050 × 560) load;
- search finds the runbook;
- no failed requests.

The build still passes its link check, with 51 pages, ADR-0029 included. Root `npm run lint` and the composer checks pass too.

## Checklist

- [x] Linked spec or issue (or: this is a one-sentence change). Follow-ups to #137 and ADR-0029.
- [ ] Tests were written first and committed separately from the implementation (ADR-0003). Not applicable: no PHP or dashboard code. I reproduced both problems first: the audit before the override, and the GIF's 404 in a browser.
- [x] `composer test`, `composer analyse`, `composer format:check` and `composer refactor:check` pass. No PHP changed; `composer test` and `composer analyse` ran (2,219 tests).
- [ ] `CHANGELOG.md` has an entry under **Unreleased** (for user-facing changes). Not user-facing: only the docs site's toolchain and dev server.

## Does this change the public API? (ADR-0017)

- [x] No
- [ ] Yes. What changes: config keys / contracts / events / Artisan commands / HTTP headers / facade / database schema
  - [ ] Breaking changes have an upgrade note
  - [ ] Schema changes ship as a **new** migration (published migrations are never edited)

author: jonny-reckless
body:
Resolves the plan's open question (`docs/audio/native-backends.md`): Windows Audio becomes one shared API instead of two.

**Behaviour**
- At the endpoint's **mix rate**: `IAudioClient3` at the driver's smallest period that holds the block (raw mode asked). If another program holds the engine, it falls back to the engine's period, as the low-latency mode did.
- At **another rate**, on a Windows before 10, or where the driver refuses the small period: the engine's period on a fresh client, the engine converting, as plain Windows Audio did.
- A duplex stream's input routes itself the same way. The capture side keeps the period it always had on the classic path (only the render side takes the engine's period there).
- The routing rule is `wasapi::SharedRouteOf` in `WasapiFormats.h`, tested by the audio suite on every platform.

**Migration**: `AudioSettings.h` reads `"Windows Audio (Low Latency Mode)"` as `"Windows Audio"`, and `ModeNamed` maps the old name to the shared mode, so asking for it by name still opens. A test covers both.

**Behaviour change for products on plain Windows Audio**: at the mix rate they now get small periods and raw mode where the driver offers them. IR Capture offers only plain Windows Audio (it filters out the other two names); it will get the small periods on its next toolkit pull.

**Verification.** On Linux: the formats and settings tests (new route and migration tests), all 12 suites, Doxygen, format. **Windows:** this CI's MSVC job is the first compile of the `WasapiDevice.cpp` change. The Windows Audio device tests need a machine with speakers and run on no CI runner: they still need running on the Legion (`set RECKLESS_AUDIO_REQUIRE=Windows Audio,Windows Audio (Exclusive Mode)`, as `docs/audio/device-tests.md` now says).

body: ## Why LQ1-059: a second effectuate for the same tenant, product, unit, level, and effective date inserted into `Price`'s unique key and returned 500. The customer-exclusive path has the same key. LQ1-060: the exclusive delta used the standard price snapshotted on the price-change document at creation. Two changes opened before either was effectuated both still said "old = 100", so the first move was added again. Standard 100 / exclusive 95, then 100→110 and 100→115, left the exclusive at 120 instead of 110. Price cuts over-reduced by the same amount. ## What Effectuate still upserts the same-day `Price` and `CustomerPrice` rows inside one tenant-scoped transaction. The exclusive delta is now `new standard − the standard price actually in effect`, read in that transaction before the write. If no standard row is in effect, it falls back to the document snapshot. A transaction advisory lock on `tenant + product + unit + level` (`pg_advisory_xact_lock`) makes two simultaneous effectuations see each other's committed standard price, so the deltas cannot stack. The request status is re-read under that lock. Money stays in cents (`toCents` / `centsToDecimal`). The effect audit still records the price on the row before overwrite and the new price. The customer-sync audit records each exclusive old and new price, and the returned delta is the actual movement. ## Verification `jest --runInBand` with `FUND_PG_URL` and `DATABASE_URL` on local Postgres: **19 suites, 179 passed, 0 failed** (previous head `0e0722e` was 175/0). 1. **OpenAI math results (#1002): license.** The old sentence said no license was stated, so no code would be copied. That was wrong. openai/math is Apache 2.0 (checked at commit `1581d4cb`), and so is complexitylib, so adaptation with attribution is permitted. The new text keeps the practice of reading the formalizations for the mathematics and writing proofs against complexitylib's definitions. Any adapted code keeps its Apache 2.0 attribution. body:
Зависит от #37 (ветка создана от `reports-csv-zyuzin`; после слияния #36 и #37 diff станет чистым).

## Что сделано
- `core/graph_state.py` — `GraphRegistry` в `app.state`: граф `nn_graph.pkl` загружается в фоне при старте и держится в RAM; статусы `not_loaded/loading/ready/failed`; чтение по снимку; `replace_graph()` под RLock (для обновления графа администратором в следующем PR; при ошибке остаётся старый граф).
- `services/routing_adapter.py` — `FastRoutingService(RoutingService)`: переопределён только `get_driver_recommendation` — индекс ближайших узлов (BallTree) строится один раз, узлы филиалов кэшируются, один проход Дейкстры от водителя с остановкой после всех филиалов. Формула и формат словаря прежние, `MapGenerator` работает без изменений; на тестовом графе результат совпадает с исходным `RoutingService`.
- `services/demand_adapter.py` — `PeriodKMeansAnalyzer(KMeansAnalyzer)`: тот же период для анализа и карты.
- Эндпоинты:
  - `GET /api/v1/recommendations/driver?lat=&lon=` (admin, manager, driver) — филиал, время в пути, очередь, маршрут `[[lat, lon], …]`, `elapsed_ms`; 503 + `Retry-After`, пока граф не готов; 422, если точка дальше 2 км от дорог графа;
  - `GET /api/v1/recommendations/driver/map` — HTML-карта маршрута;
  - `GET /api/v1/recommendations/branches?n_clusters=&date_from=&date_to=` (admin, manager, executive) — зоны спроса K-Means; 422, если заказов меньше `n_clusters`;
  - `GET /api/v1/recommendations/branches/map` — HTML-карта зон спроса;
  - `GET /api/v1/branches`, `PATCH /api/v1/branches/{id}/queue` (admin, manager) — очередь филиала влияет на рекомендацию.
- `/health/ready` учитывает граф, если `LOAD_GRAPH_ON_STARTUP=true`.
- Новые настройки: `GRAPH_DOWNLOAD_IF_MISSING`, `ROUTE_MAX_SNAP_DISTANCE_KM`.

## Производительность (реальный граф: 10 732 узла, 27 374 ребра)
| Точка | Исходный `RoutingService` | `FastRoutingService` |
|---|---|---|
| 56.327, 44.002 | 266 мс | 27 мс |
| 56.25, 43.87 | 196 мс | 17 мс |
| 56.36, 43.82 | 157 мс | 15 мс |
| 56.30, 43.95 | 147 мс | 16 мс |

Полный HTTP-ответ `/recommendations/driver` ≈ 27 мс (цель — до 1–2 с). Ответы обоих вариантов совпали во всех точках.

## Проверка
- `pytest -q` — 124 passed (27 новых, синтетический граф; OSM в тестах не скачивается).
- Живой прогон: PostgreSQL 16 (Docker) + реальный граф + uvicorn — все эндпоинты, смена очереди меняет рекомендацию.
- `ruff` — OK, кроме `backend/tests/test_ml_services.py` (см. #36).

## Для @gagashga / Ахметова
- ML-файлы `backend/app/ml/*` **не изменены**: оптимизация сделана подклассом в `backend/app/services/routing_adapter.py`.

## ⚠️ Нюансы, требующие решения
1. **Фон дорог на карте маршрута не рисуется.** `MapGenerator` вызывает `edges_gdf.explore()`, которому нужны `matplotlib` и `mapclassify` — их нет в `requirements.txt`. Исключение гасится внутри генератора, карта строится без серой сетки дорог. Предложение: пакеты не добавлять (тяжелее образ и HTML), а если фон нужен — рисовать его в `MapGenerator` через `folium.PolyLine` без `explore()`.
2. **Граф в Docker.** Если `data/nn_graph.pkl` нет, при первом старте граф скачивается из OSM (~80 с), всё это время API маршрутов отвечает 503; остановка контейнера во время скачивания ждёт завершения потока. Предложение для docker-compose: хранить `data/` в Docker volume (скачивание один раз, затем загрузка ≈ 0,3 с), на CI — `GRAPH_DOWNLOAD_IF_MISSING=false`.
3. `score` в ответе считается от округлённого `travel_time_minutes` (формат словаря ML не менялся) — значение приблизительное, на выбор филиала не влияет.

author: jdkent
body:
Registration always checks against an `Evidence`: the second, evidence-less path (#141 open question 2) is gone, with the code only it reached.

## What changed

- **One path by signature.** `Catalog` holds no evidence. The operations that check against PubMed and the registries take it as an argument:
  - `register`, `register_many`;
  - `invariants.violations` and `neighbourhood`, and `identity_plan.apply`;
  - `migrate_caches`, `register_manifest` (split from `resolve_manifest`, which only reads);
  - the four id-lookup services, whose constructor is `(settings, catalog, evidence)`.

  `Catalog.open(root)` and `Catalog(conn, root)` take none. The funnel report and the five offline scripts need no PubMed client, and no method can reach a missing evidence (the `None` branches, the `evidence` property and `CrossrefIDLookupService.can_run`'s catalog guard are deleted).
- **`pubmed_email` only where NCBI or the registries are asked:** `add`, `run --manifest`, `migrate` and `repair-identity`. Every other command, `status` included, opens the catalog with no email. The README list gained `repair-identity`. `_evidence(settings)` closes the PubMed and registry clients.
- **A second journal DOI that another record of the same batch takes is refused with a reason.** Before, it was dropped without a trace (store.py `_settle_second_dois`).
- **Tests.**
  - `pubmed` and `evidence` are fixtures in `tests/conftest.py`. A test that takes `evidence` gets a cassette, with every host except `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and `huggingface.co` going through VCR: a request to PMC's id converter or any other host is recorded or fails. The Hub is left out because docling's weights come from the cache CI fills in its own step.
  - `test_model_outage.py` and `test_prose_stages.py` also leave out `prose.test`, the in-process transport their prose client is played by.
  - The `checked` fixture and five identical per-file `catalog` fixtures are one `catalog` in `tests/catalog/conftest.py`. The duplicate `test_another_paper_s_doi_is_refused_with_evidence_too` is deleted.

## What the evidence-less path chose, and what the evidence-backed path does

1. A PMID beside other ids was added unchecked. Now it is refused when its PubMed record gives a DOI another article holds and the registry gives that DOI the record's paper, or cannot say.
2. A second journal DOI was always refused. Now it is added as an `alternative_doi` when the registries give both DOIs one work; otherwise refused as before.
3. `id_lookup` skipped itself and `violations` raised without evidence. Both always run.

## Differences found

About 4,100 tests give the same result with the evidence. The setups that changed:

- `test_a_swap_of_pmids_is_one_call`, the `cli/test_repair_identity.py` setup and `test_a_merge_drops_only_a_record_s_pmid_or_pmcid` registered a PMID with a DOI PubMed gives another paper. Old path: stored, which is the corrupt state the repair is for. New path: refused. They now plant the legacy rows directly, as `test_invariants._hold` does.
- CLI tests that ran `add` without `--no-enrich` had passed offline only because enrichment failed quietly; they now say `--no-enrich`.
- `upload_body.py`'s matcher treats an empty body as empty, since a cassette also holds GETs. `test_sync_then_upload.py` counts neurostore replays only, and its `vcr_config` scrubs responses like the root one.
- Deleted `test_violations_need_evidence` (it asserted the `ValueError` of the deleted branch) and replaced `test_a_command_that_only_reads_still_needs_the_email...` with two tests: `status` needs no email, `add` does.

No other existing assertion was weakened.

## Tests

On beast, fresh venv from `pyproject`, CI's flags (`--record-mode=none --block-network --allowed-hosts=127.0.0.1,localhost`, `-n 24`): 4306 passed, 4 skipped, with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` as in CI and the docling weights cached. At base (efbc106) the same run gave 4112 passed, 2 failed. `test_a_wiley_pdf_is_read_into_the_articles_pdf_text` passes alone on a cold cache with the network open, and on the warmed cache offline with the network blocked.

With the network unblocked and `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`, a socket probe over the whole suite saw 0 connections to anything but loopback.

Mutations, each run against the affected files and reverted:

- `any` to `all` over the DOIs an article holds: 1 failed.
- No refusal for a second DOI another record took: 1 failed.
- `status` requires the email: 1 failed.
- `run --manifest` resolves instead of registering: 1 failed.
- `add` skips the email check: 2 failed.
- CLI opens with no evidence: all CLI registrations failed (52).
- `_pubmed_evidence` returns `{}`: 9 failed.

body:
## What

Finishes the tilemap editor so a map can be placed and its tiles turned:

- **Placement**: `TileMap::x, y` (pixels). Saved in the optional `TPOS` chunk; the canvas preview, a Move button with X/Y fields in the Tilemaps section, and the `.tmj` `offsetx` / `offsety` follow it. Moving is one undo step.
- **Turned tiles**: the top three bits of a cell are Tiled's flip flags (`TILE_FLIP_X`, `TILE_FLIP_Y`, `TILE_TRANSPOSE`, the last only for square tiles). `tile_flipped` / `tile_rotated` compose them as 2x2 matrices; `tile_pixel` samples a turned tile for the canvas, the tilemap window and `tilemap_render`; `.tmj` tile ids carry the same bits (`firstgid` added to the number, not the flags).
- **UI**: Flip H, Flip V and Turn buttons in the tilemap window (Turn disabled for non-square tiles).

## File format

`.pxa` stays version 1. `TPOS` is optional and skipped by older readers; an origin out of range is ignored (the map stays at 0, 0). A cell with flip flags is outside what an older reader accepts, so it drops *all* tile data of such a file (tile data is all or nothing) but keeps the pixels. Noted in `docs/MILESTONES.md` (milestone 25).

## Not in this PR

Tilemaps are still a canvas preview only: not merged into PNG/GIF/sheet exports, and a map has no layer order.

## Testing

TDD: new tests in `test_tilemap`, `test_tilemap_ops`, `test_tilemap_pxa`, `test_tilemap_export`, `test_composite` and `ui_editor_tilemaps`. Full `ctest`: 96/96 passed locally (MinGW). clang-format passes; clang-tidy (full config) is clean on the changed sources.

author: alexwaumann
body:
GUI half of the bridge's sandbox round. The daemon half (preview floor, Host header, read-only marker, waits ending on request cancellation) is `cf/bridge-fix-floor`. Step note: `docs/notes/bridge-fix-frames.md`.

## What testing found, and what each became

1. **A frame that navigated itself to another grant's URL kept its thread's bridge** (every grant shares the pages origin; each `load` also re-sent `cf:ready`). Fixed with a **per-frame nonce**: `HtmlFrame` opens the page at `<grant>#cf=<128-bit hex>`, `bridge.js` reads it at start and sends it on every message, and the host accepts a message only when the window, the origin **and** the nonce all match. **`cf:ready` now answers only `cf:hello`**, never a bare load. A page reached by navigation has no fragment, so it gets no bridge: `cf.ready` rejects at once with `unavailable` and the script posts only its height and theme ack. A reload keeps the fragment. `cf:resize` / `cf:theme:ack` now need the frame's window and origin too. Their nonce is optional, because hand-written pages (which the skills and `view.inline`'s warning describe) post them without the script, but a wrong nonce is still dropped. New `cf:bye` on pagehide ends a document.
2. **A no-thread page could drive a thread page's `window.cf` through `parent.frames`.** Frames without an owning thread are back on the **opaque sandbox** (`HTML_PREVIEW_SANDBOX` without `allow-same-origin`). Frames with a thread use `THREAD_PAGE_SANDBOX` (same-origin). A change of owning thread reloads the frame. **Accepted residual (documented):** pages of the user's own threads still share one origin and can reach each other.
3. **Host limits.** A duplicate in-flight `cf:run` id is refused with `invalid`. Each document may have at most 32 runs in flight and 16 subscriptions; anything over is refused with `invalid`. `bridge.js` queues its own runs past 32, so a well-behaved page never hits the cap. Messages over 256 KiB are ignored (`bridge.js` refuses such a call locally with `invalid`). **`cf:cancel`, a new document, `cf:bye` and unmount abort the in-flight Connect call** (an AbortController, threaded through `invokeConfirmed` → `invokeCommand`), so daemon-side waits stop.

## Screenshots (built app, isolated home, Haiku 5.5 thread)

Inline bridge page, ready in its thread (dark):

![inline dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alexwaumann/code-foundry/d77678e7979f6c323cef9e663a95c72977e51212/bridge-fix-frames-inline-dark.png)

Panel copy of the page with its thread's bridge, plus a page whose five `thread.wait` calls (3 s timeout) all ended `timeout` at 3.0 s, followed by a 6 ms `thread.list`:

![panel dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alexwaumann/code-foundry/d77678e7979f6c323cef9e663a95c72977e51212/bridge-fix-frames-panel-dark.png)
![panel light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alexwaumann/code-foundry/d77678e7979f6c323cef9e663a95c72977e51212/bridge-fix-frames-panel-light.png)

A plain HTML file in a File tab of the same panel (the thread never showed it): it renders, `cf.ready` resolves with no thread, and its probe of the three sibling frames reads "blocked":

![plain dark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alexwaumann/code-foundry/d77678e7979f6c323cef9e663a95c72977e51212/bridge-fix-frames-plain-dark.png)
![plain light](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alexwaumann/code-foundry/d77678e7979f6c323cef9e663a95c72977e51212/bridge-fix-frames-plain-light.png)

## Tests

- Vitest: nonce helpers, size cap and bye parsing (`lib/bridge.test.ts`); host: ready only on hello, start-over and abort on hello/bye/script-less load, cancel and dispose aborting, duplicate ids, the caps (`stores/bridgeHost.test.ts`); `HtmlFrame.test.tsx` (new): sandbox per thread, nonce in src, window + origin + nonce checks, optional nonce for resize, opaque `"null"` origin, reload on thread change; bridge.js: nonce on every message, no bridge without one, bye, the 32-run queue, size refusals.
- Playwright (WebKit), bridge/inline-html/file-tabs: 35 passed, 1 skipped (`SHOTS` unset). New: a frame sent to another grant's copy of the page (or to itself without the fragment) gets no bridge; a reload keeps it; a no-thread File tab's probe of a thread card throws (and reads "reached" when `allow-same-origin` is put back); a duplicate id is refused and cancel/reload abort the mock's held `thread.wait`; the lightbox copy has its own nonce and its thread's bridge.
- `make check` green.

## Not done live

Synthetic clicks didn't reach the app during the live run because another app's system dialog was holding the screen. So the lightbox and the click-driven calls were checked only in e2e against the mock. The live run covered inline, panel, the no-thread File tab and the waits, using pages that run their checks on load.

Daemon restart: needed (the daemon serves `bridge.js`, and the new host requires its nonce).

author: potatoattack
body:
Updates the FFVII Rebirth sparse VM patch sets to **Mesa 26.2.5** and a separate **CachyOS kernel package 7.3.0-5**. The kernel recipe pins the [CachyOS `cachyos-7.3.0-4` source release](https://github.com/CachyOS/linux/releases/tag/cachyos-7.3.0-4), based on Linux 7.3, and produces `7.3.0-5-cachyos-sparse-vm`. The user reports `linux-cachyos 7.3.0-5-cachyos` from the v4 repository. CachyOS's [public recipe](https://github.com/CachyOS/linux-cachyos/blob/523baf9cc1e37b7f8079064447f1418702c45154/linux-cachyos/PKGBUILD) currently uses the same source tag with package release 4; the exact inputs of the installed v4 package were unavailable for comparison.

### Patch adaptation

- The Mesa 26.2.5 and Linux 7.3 refresh preserves the accepted sparse VM batching, synchronization, scalar fallback, ownership exclusions and per-VM protocol v1. It removes an obsolete MES self-test hunk and adapts upstream reset and guard-page cleanup changes.
- The newer CachyOS source release changes six files outside the sparse-VM patch targets. All 14 patched kernel files are byte identical after applying the unchanged nine-patch series to either source release.
- Source pins, checksums, package metadata, README and validation records now describe candidate `0.1.0-rc4`.

### Validation

- The official kernel archive SHA-256 and BLAKE2 match its release asset and CachyOS packaging metadata. All 11 kernel recipe inputs pass their BLAKE2 checksums.
- All nine kernel patches apply with zero fuzz to the exact `cachyos-7.3.0-4` archive. The application log matches rc3.
- All 11 affected AMDGPU C translation units compile with AMDGPU and HSA/SVM enabled. The recipe reports `7.3.0-5-cachyos-sparse-vm`; host regressions and four native-result validator tests pass.
- Mesa source and patches are unchanged from rc3. The prior complete RADV build/link, staging and native CPU self-tests remain recorded in the [rc3 validation](docs/validation-rc3.json).

See [rc4 validation](docs/validation.md), [machine-readable evidence](docs/validation-rc4.json), and [source provenance](docs/provenance.md).

### Outstanding validation

A full Arch `makepkg` kernel build with Clang/LTO, kernel/module link, installation and boot, DKMS/initramfs integration, native GPU tests and game validation remain pending. No live kernel or driver was installed and no new performance or stability claim is made. Historical rc2 gameplay results do not validate these refreshed binaries.

## Summary

On prod v0.2.15, `POST /v1/brands/:brandId/storyboard-runs/:runId/plan/draft` returns 503 "The storyboard draft could not be generated". Root cause: the draft calls OpenRouter with `LLM_DEFAULTS.background` (`google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite`), and `OpenRouterService.withRetentionPolicy` adds `provider: { zdr: true, data_collection: 'deny' }` to every request. That model has no ZDR endpoint, so OpenRouter answers HTTP 404 `No endpoints found matching your data policy (Zero data retention)` (`failed_routing_step: Filter by Data Policy`), which the service maps to the retryable 503.

The draft (and the brand-remix scene analysis, which has the identical call) now use `LLM_DEFAULTS.fastText` (`openai/gpt-5.6-luna`): Azure ZDR endpoints with `structured_outputs` and `response_format` support, already used in prod for vision scoring.

## Related issue

No-Issue: found from a prod 503 report; nothing filed.

## Scope

Model key only, in two call sites, plus one regression test. `LLM_DEFAULTS.background` itself is not changed: it feeds the content-quality scorer, whose model is pinned in `scoring-surface.lock.json` and gated by calibration. Other `background` callers (brand-policy-judge, content-quality-scorer, task decomposition) would hit the same 404 if they run through OpenRouter with ZDR; that needs its own change.

## Verification

- Prod CloudWatch `/ecs/genfeed-production/api`: `Storyboard plan draft failed` with `reason: provider_error`, preceded by the OpenRouter 404 above, at 2026-10-25 09:10:02Z and 09:10:17Z.
- OpenRouter public ZDR list (`/api/v1/endpoints/zdr`): 0 endpoints for `google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite`; 5 Azure endpoints for `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, all with `structured_outputs`.
- Added a spec asserting the draft calls `LLM_DEFAULTS.fastText`. Tests were not run locally; left to CI.

## Screenshots

Not applicable.

## AI involvement

Claude Code drafted the change and test; verified against prod logs and OpenRouter's public ZDR endpoint list.

author: club-paradiso
body:
Follow-up to #150. Fixes the two P2 findings Codex raised on that PR shortly before it merged.

## Fixes
1. **Auto-resume could loop** (`src/features/live/StartScreen.tsx`)
   - **Bug:** the launcher resumed any interrupted remote session while the phone looked connected. That included recogniser or configuration failures. `resume()` resets the supervisor's retry counter, so its bounded recovery became unbounded, and a non-retryable failure was retried every 300 ms.
   - **Fix:** auto-resume now applies only when the phone caused the interruption ("not connected" or "disconnected" faults), and only once a **new** remote stream has arrived since then.
2. **A lost answer stranded negotiation** (`src/remote-mic/receiver.ts`)
   - **Bug:** if the Mac's answer POST failed transiently, the offer was still marked handled, so the phone waited forever.
   - **Fix:** the receiver keeps the locally created answer and retries it on later polls until it is delivered, the offer goes stale, or the pairing expires.

## Tests
- New regression tests: `remote-auto-resume.test.ts`, plus "retries a lost answer instead of stranding the phone's offer" in `peer.integration.test.ts`. The answer-retry test fails without the fix.
- `npm run lint` ✅, `npm run typecheck` ✅, `npm test` ✅ (157 files / 1786 tests), `npm run build` ✅
- `npm run e2e:remote-mic`: 43/43 on two consecutive runs. `e2e:live-failure` ✅.

Still not verified on a physical iPhone Safari + MacBook.

author: mo7lish
body:
## What & why

React Doctor 0.9.18 can report an untouched enclosing React project as complete with zero analyzed/scanned files while reporting the changed nested project normally. The adapter rejected that valid scoped report as an execution failure.

Treat an empty project like an omitted project only after Git independently proves it owns no selected source. Apply this normalization to both changed and staged reports. Keep incomplete scans, skipped checks or reasons, missing counts, unexpected diagnostics, touched-but-unscanned files, failed scope proof, and full-scan coverage failures blocking.

## Scope accounting

- `external.py`: normalize verified empty projects before existing scoped project-set and completeness validation.
- `test_react_doctor_scope.py`: expand the nested-workspace regression across changed/staged modes and malformed or incomplete report cases.
- Four synchronized metadata files prepare unused patch version `8.129.3`: Standards and compatibility manifests, the local lock entry, and this central repository’s own bundle pin. No rule severity, baseline, platform consumer pin, tag, release, or rollout changes.

## One-way or two-way door

Two-way. A revert restores the previous scoped-report rejection. No persisted data changes.

## QA impact / blast radius

React Doctor report interpretation in scoped hooks and CI. Full scans keep their existing completeness rules.

Manual checks:
1. Run the native analyzer on a root React package and nested React package, changing only the nested component. Confirm the changed report contains root 0/0 and nested 1/1 counts.
2. Parse that report with the original adapter and confirm the zero-file execution error. Parse it with this patch and confirm acceptance.
3. Change root source too and leave its reported counts at zero. Confirm the adapter still rejects it.
4. Supply incomplete/skipped reports or unavailable Git proof. Confirm failure remains blocking.

## Test evidence

- Before: the new valid-empty-root regression fails in both changed and staged modes.
- After: 363 scope regressions passed. After fixture typing/style cleanup, all 40 nested-workspace cases passed again.
- Native React Doctor 0.9.18 reproduction: changed reports include a completed root with 0/0 files and nested app with 1/1. Original adapter rejects the actual JSON; patched adapter accepts it. Native staged reports omit the untouched root and remain supported.
- Ruff passed. Review-me found no remaining code questions after correcting fixture typing/mutation/complexity findings from normal hooks.
- All normal commit and commit-message hooks passed: version sync, file conventions, staged Standards, whole-repository Python/TypeScript dogfood, and all Python/TypeScript typechecks. All normal pre-push hooks passed for both commits, including the full static-verification scan and native tool attestation.
- Initial full `make verify` stopped at host native-tool attestation. Subsequently provisioned official Compose 5.6.1 and Terraform 1.17.0 using the repository-prescribed scoped mise backends. Checksums/provenance and unchanged Standards attestation passed; no global activation or container operations. Full `make verify` has not been rerun; normal mandatory commit/push gates and remote CI are reported separately.

## Publication boundary

Draft tooling correction plus required version metadata only. The initial CI release-causality gate correctly rejected retaining already-tagged version 8.129.2 after changing publishable code; the follow-up prepares 8.129.3 without publishing it. Consumer adoption requires a reviewed tooling merge, a valid published corrected bundle, and a separate pin update. This PR does not merge, release, or deploy anything.

body:
Clicking Animate always set the 3D view to the same width. The cause was the player bar under the view, which needed a minimum width of about 1100 px: fixed minimum widths for the slider (220), frame label (170) and fps label (110), plus the buttons. When the bar was shown, the splitter had to give the view that width, so it squeezed the model tree. The view also stayed that size after the player was closed.

Measured in a 1100 × 800 window, model tree / view widths:

| | before Animate | after Animate | after Close |
|---|---|---|---|
| dev | 179 / 780 | 70 / 889 | 70 / 889 |
| this PR | 179 / 780 | 179 / 780 | 179 / 780 |

The camera itself was never reset. Only the view width changed.

## Changes
- `AnimationBar` uses a horizontal size policy of Ignored, so it never sets the width of the view. Its labels (plot names, frame, measured fps) get small minimum widths and are cut when space is short.
- Test: showing the bar under a view in a splitter leaves the splitter sizes unchanged. It fails on dev (`[0, 2731]` instead of `[199, 697]` with a long plot name) and passes here.
- CHANGELOG entry under Fixed.
- Full test suite: 153 passed, 8 skipped.

When the bar is shown, the view still loses the bar's height (28 px), as before. The GIF export uses the view exactly as it appears on screen.
