author: simoninns
body:
## Summary

A batch of five issue fixes, a documentation sweep, and a nix flake update.

**#331: combine Y/C into a single composite output (CVBS Sink)**
- New `combine_yc` parameter on `cvbs_sink`, offered only for Y/C projects. When it is enabled, luma and chroma are summed sample by sample into one composite (Y+C) signal. The result is written as a single `.cvbs` with `signal_type` `composite` in the `.meta`, in place of the `.cvbsy`/`.cvbsc` pair.
- The chroma DC offset is removed before summing: 512 for CVBS Y/C sources, and the uint16 midpoint for TBC Y/C sources. Out-of-range sums are kept as headroom with `CVBS_U10_4FSC` and clamped by the other encodings.
- A combined Y/C export is one stream, so it can now be piped to stdout (`output_path=-`).
- Unit tests added in `cvbs_sink_stage_test` and `cvbs_sink_stage_deps_test`.

**#332: CX23880/1/2/3 (cx88) captures in the VBI Capture Source**
- New `cx2388x card dump, 8-bit` NTSC presets for WST and NABTS. The container is the bt8x8 NTSC one (28.636363 MHz, 2048-byte records with 1600 valid samples), but it has 12 records per field starting at lines 10/273, and no frame counter, so dropped frames can't be detected.
- Geometry was measured on the CBS ExtraVision reference capture: NABTS on lines 15–18, 36.2 % lock rate, offset fitted at 230.1 samples.
- There is no 625-line entry yet, because there is no PAL sample to check the container against.
- Tests added in `vbi_source_format_test`, `vbi_ntsc_source_test` and `nabts_sink_pipeline_test`.

**#348: Daphne VBI Sink wrote only the `1VBI` header**
- The sink now decodes the biphase code and white flag from its own input frames and writes the 10-byte per-field records, two per frame, in field order.
- Fields with no readable code get zeros. A frame the input can't supply still gets both records, so later offsets stay correct.
- The "current limitation" warning is removed from the docs, and tests are extended in `daphne_vbi_sink_stage_deps_test`.

**#247: FieldQualityObserver → FrameQualityObserver**
- The observer ran twice per frame and stored the same frame-level result once for each field. It is renamed `FrameQualityObserver` (version 2.0.0) and now stores one result per frame, keyed by the first field, the same way the other frame-level observers work.
- The observation service, the Video Parameter observer presenter and dialog, and the tests are updated to match.

**#318: user-facing plugin guide**
- New `docs/plugins.md` mkdocs page, linked from the site nav, the index, and the GUI and CLI user guides.

**Documentation sweep**
- Brought the technical docs (plugin SDK/architecture/author/publishing guides, disc mapping), the GUI docs, the plugin registry README and many stage `instructions.md` files back in line with the current behaviour.
- Fixed tooltips and help text that had drifted:
  - `--safe-core-plugins` now says it clears the registry permanently.
  - `mask_line` sample levels now list the NTSC/PAL-M values.
  - `TBC-locked` is renamed to `STANDARD_STABLE_LOCKED`.
  - The `efm_sink` zero-pad description is corrected.
  - The video sink 3D-blend tooltips no longer say "2D".
  - The `source_align` header comment is corrected.

**Nix flake**
- Updated `flake.lock`, and removed the `mkDecodeOrc` wrapper and the unused ffprobe `preCheck`.
- Fixed a GCC 15.3 `-O2` false-positive `-Wfree-nonheap-object` in `frame_content.cpp` (`robust_spread` now takes a const reference and copies the vector itself).

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] New feature
- [ ] Refactor
- [x] Documentation
- [x] Other (nix flake update / GCC 15 warning fix)

## Validation

- New and extended unit tests for the CVBS Sink (`combine_yc`), the VBI Source (cx2388x format and NTSC source), the NABTS sink pipeline, the Daphne VBI Sink deps, the core observation service, and the Video Parameter observation presenter.
- cx2388x presets checked against the issue #332 reference NTSC capture. That sample is gitignored, so its functional tests skip in CI.
- Stage docs updated in both `instructions.md` and the mkdocs user guide for `cvbs_sink`, `vbi_source` and `daphne_vbi_sink`, as required by AGENTS.md §9.1.
- Not validated: Windows/macOS packaging, and the Daphne `.vbi` output in Daphne itself.

## Checklist

- [ ] Build passes locally
- [x] Related docs were updated if needed
- [x] Linked issue (if applicable)

author: michellzappa
body:
Fixes bipe-chat/bipe#204. Spec and strings: bipe-chat/bipe-shared, branch of the same name (spec `soft-logout`); its generated files land here.

## What changes (iOS and Android)

- `AccountSession` sets a `ClientDelegate` (`Client.setDelegate`) and passes `didReceiveAuthError` to account-start.
- Soft logout (token expired, device still exists): the session pauses, a new client on the same store signs in with the hidden password and the same device ID (`Client.login`), and replaces the old session in place. Keys, history and the other accounts stay untouched.
- The server refuses the hidden password (`M_FORBIDDEN`), or there is none: only the refused saved session goes, and the PIN screen opens for that account (recovery flow with `softLogoutUserId`). A good PIN replaces the session.
- Network or local failure: nothing is deleted; it tries again on the next foreground.
- Device signed out from another device: sign-out with `alreadyLoggedOut` and a one-time toast "<nome> saiu deste celular"; never a quiet sign-in.
- Recovery-start row "beta" (old e-mail and password) shows only in developer builds (gate `flag:developer`: iOS `AppConfig.isDeveloperBuild`, Android `BuildConfig.DEBUG`).

Provenance: bipe-shared product/screens soft-logout, recovery-pin, recovery-start, sign-out; registries/onboarding.json (gate flag:developer); matrix-sdk-ffi ClientDelegate.didReceiveAuthError, Client.setDelegate, Client.login, Client.deviceId, Client.session, SyncService.stop; ADR 0057, 0086; bipe#204.

## Validation

- Local: `headers`, `strings`, `a11y`, `deny-list`, `licences`, `sdk-version` pass; `node --test tools/*.test.mjs` 62 pass.
- Generated files from the bipe-shared branch with `node tools/gen.mjs --app` (Node 24).
- Native builds: GitHub CI.
- No password, token or recovery token is logged: the log lines name only the step.

## Manual acceptance (MZ, on device)

1. Soft logout: on the homeserver, expire the access token of a tester account (or wait for the expiry). Open Bipe Next: the chats keep loading, no screen shows, and the history and keys are still there.
2. Refused password: change the account's hidden password on the server, then expire the token. The PIN screen opens for that account; a good PIN brings it back. The other accounts keep working throughout.
3. Offline: with the phone in airplane mode during step 1, nothing is removed; after the network comes back and the app returns to the foreground, it signs in again.
4. From another device, sign this phone out (Aparelhos conectados). The account leaves the phone and a toast names it once; it does not sign in again by itself.
5. A tester build shows no "beta" row in Entrar numa conta que já existe; a debug build does.

Default chosen: a refused hidden password removes only the saved SDK session (never the hidden password or the store), because recovery-start needs the session gone to offer the synced token, and the spec allows it. MZ can overrule.

## 変更内容

### 背景と目的

集結タイムライン計算は、1周目のパターンをTの小さい順に確定していました。このため1周目と2周目でパターンの順番が変わり（例: 1周目が②①③、2周目が①②③）、周期ウェーブタイマーで1周目を周期ごとにループさせると、待ち時間を破る指示になることがありました。実物のHTMLを決定的な乱数1000件で動かした事前検証では、165件でループが待ち時間を破りました。

あわせて、1つのブラウザタブの中で複数の計算機とタイマーを持てるようにし、周期ウェーブタイマーが集結タイムライン計算のどのタブの結果を使うかを選んで読み込めるようにします。

### 主な変更

- 集結タイムライン計算（`web/攻城タイムライン計算.html`）
  - 1周目を定義順（①②③…）に確定する（SIEGE-013）
  - 周期は、1周目を周期ずつずらして繰り返しても全員の`帰還 + パターン間バッファ`を守る最小値とする（SIEGE-017）。2周目は1周目の全時刻へ周期を足す（SIEGE-021）
  - メインが0人のときは計算せず「メイン役割のメンバーがいません」と表示する（SIEGE-033）
  - ページ内タブ（追加、名前の変更、削除、キーボード操作）。新しいタブは表示中のタブを複製する（SIEGE-050〜SIEGE-054）
  - 計算結果も保存し、計算した後に入力を変えると注意を表示する（SIEGE-040〜SIEGE-043）
- 周期ウェーブタイマー（`web/周期ウェーブタイマー.html`）
  - ページ内タブ。各タブは独立に計測し、表示していないタブも計測を続ける。計測中のタブには「▶」と経過時間を表示する（WAVE-060〜WAVE-066）
  - 計算元の選択と「読み込む」。計算元が計算し直された、結果を出せなかった、削除されたことを文字で表示する。この欄は画面幅900px以下でも表示する（WAVE-070〜WAVE-076）
- 保存キーを`siegeCalcTabs`と`waveTimerTabs`へ移した。旧キー（`siegeCalcState`、`waveTimerSettings`、`waveTimerPastedTimeline`）は読むだけで、最初のタブへ移す（SIEGE-042、WAVE-052）
- 実物のHTMLをNode.jsとjsdomで動かす検査`tests/web/`を、`tools/check_web.py`経由で品質ゲートへ加えた（ADR 0030）
  - 計算結果が満たす性質C1〜C9（`siege-timeline.md`に定義）を、計画の固定例3件と決定的な乱数1000件で検査する
  - Node.js 22.11.0（`.node-version`）とjsdom 25.0.1（`package.json`、`package-lock.json`）を、Dev Container（公式イメージから複写、`postCreateCommand`の`npm ci`）とCI（`actions/setup-node`、`npm ci`）へ入れた
- 要件定義書（`docs/requirements/web-tools/`）を先に更新した。COM-002のURLを実際の公開先へ直し、ADR 0026へ訂正の注記を加えた

### 利用者・開発者への影響

- 運用者: 集結タイムライン計算の`周期：`の値が変わります（例: 計画書の例1では7分40秒から11分30秒）。出力の書式は変えていません。既存の保存データは最初のタブへ移り、入力は失われません
- 開発者: 品質ゲートにNode.jsとjsdomが必要になりました
  - Dev Containerは`Dev Containers: Rebuild Container`で作り直してください
  - Containerを使わない環境は、`.node-version`の版のNode.jsを入れて`npm ci`を実行してください
  - Node.jsまたはjsdomがない場合、`python tools/check.py`は入れ方を示して失敗します

## 判断と影響

- 分類: `web/`の補助ツールの変更で、KvKチーム編成の必須条件、警告、目的関数には影響しません
- ADR: ADR 0030（ブラウザ用補助ツールの実物のHTMLをNode.jsとjsdomで検査する）を追加しました。ADR 0013に置き換えの注記を加えました。`dev`で0029が使われていたため0030にしています
- 利用者の決定（2026-10-25）: 両要件定義書の「6. 決定済みの事項」に記録しました
  - 計算できないときは前回の参考結果を残す（KI-SIEGE-02は直さない）
  - 新しいタブは表示中のタブを複製する
  - 計算後に入力を変えたら注意を表示する
  - 周期ウェーブタイマーのタブ名は「タイマー{番号}」とする
  - メンバー0人のタブもそのまま復元する
- 作成者の仮定（両要件定義書の「7. 作成者の仮定」。運用者が覆せます）
  - 計算できなかったときは、残した参考結果があればその入力と比べて注意を出し続け、なければ出さない（SIEGE-043）
  - タブのidに作った時刻と乱数を含め、周期ウェーブタイマーはidで計算元を見分ける（SIEGE-041、WAVE-073）。保存データだけが作り直されたときに誤表示しないため
  - 周期ウェーブタイマーの予定は、スタート時刻からの経過で毎回求める（表示していないタブも計測を続けるため）
  - 削除後は右隣、なければ左隣のタブを表示する。矢印キーは端から反対の端へ回り込む
- 既知のリスク
  - Windowsから共有した作業ツリー（9p）では`node_modules/`の読み込みが遅く、`web/`の検査に数十秒かかります
  - 計算元から読み込んだ見出しはエスケープされずに表示されます。既知の不具合KI-WAVE-11で、範囲外のため直していません
  - GitHub CLIのTOKENに、ADR 0008の上限を超える`write:org`のスコープがあります。利用者の判断で、今回はこのまま作成しました
- 見送り: なし

## 関連情報

- 要件定義書: `docs/requirements/web-tools/siege-timeline.md`、`docs/requirements/web-tools/wave-timer.md`、`docs/requirements/web-tools/README.md`
- 画面の画像はありません。ブラウザでのDesktop幅とMobile幅の確認（COM-053）は未実施です

- `python tools/check.py`: 成功（pytest 206件、ブラウザ用補助ツールの検査53件。乱数1000件は4ファイルへ分けて実行）
- `python -m pytest tests/test_repository_scope.py tests/test_team_master_repository.py -k "hidden_words or placeholder"`: 3件成功
- `$review-kvk-change`: 4観点（domain、architecture、test、requirements）で、初回のレビューと再レビュー5回を行いました。最終はMust、Shouldなし（承認候補）です。結果はこのPull Requestへコメントとして投稿します

  - 実際のブラウザでの表示の確認

author: bhushank2k
body:
## Purpose
Prepare a versioned Android update that can install over an existing Risk Tracker release APK without changing the application ID or clearing app data.

## Patch-only changes
- Keep `applicationId` as `com.risktracker.app`.
- Bump `versionCode` from 1 to 2 and `versionName` from 1.0 to 1.1.
- Add a manual GitHub Actions workflow that builds and verifies a signed release APK using repository Actions secrets.

## Critical install requirement
The APK must be signed with the exact same keystore/certificate as the APK already installed on the device. The workflow intentionally fails if signing secrets are missing. Configure `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_BASE64`, `ANDROID_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD`, `ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS`, and `ANDROID_KEY_PASSWORD` in repository Actions secrets using the existing release signing key. Do not use a newly generated key; Android will reject the update if certificates differ. Never commit the keystore.

## Artifact
Run **Actions → Signed in-place Android update → Run workflow** on this branch after adding the signing secrets. The workflow runs unit tests, builds `assembleRelease`, verifies the APK signature, and uploads `risk-tracker-release-update-v1.1`.

## Stacked PR
This patch is based on PR #51 and only adds build/version/signing support. Merge in the existing stack order before release. CI has not yet been confirmed for this commit.

Worker: eric-agent-3. Part of #807. Follows #836.

## Why
I read all 96 bars of Eric's Golden sheet: no p/mp/mf/f, no hairpins, no Ped. marks. The dynamics decision merged in
#836 assumed marks. Applied to this sheet, it leaves every note at mf (= `KEYS_VELOCITY`), which changes nothing Eric
hears.

## What changes (docs only)
- **`specs/decisions/golden-demo-dynamics.md`:** each bar's velocity comes from the recording's loudness in that bar,
  in dB, mapped linearly from the 10th percentile at p (49) to the 90th at f (96). The mark ladder stays for charts
  that have marks. The alternative is our own arrangement (louder choruses, voicing), which is Eric's call after he
  listens.
- **`specs/context/findings.md`:** the sheet has no marks, so the per-harmony pedal rule applies to bars 1–96 (dated,
  as Requirement 1 asks).
  - A new pedal starts on a new pitch-class set per half bar, on the left hand's first strike in a bar, or after a
    rest of a bar or more.
  - Down 60 ms after, up 20 ms before the next.
  - Result: 112 pairs, with a median of one bar.

The local charts and `pedal.json` are already written by the local spike tool. Its self-test covers the pedal rule
(including the lift at a rest) and the velocity map. No Golden data is in git or in this PR.

## Checks
No code changed. CI's ownership and markers checks apply.

author: hieult-dev
body:
## Summary
Makes a learner's *wrong choice* shape their review, not just the knowledge point they missed.

- Each active error type with an active parent point gets an evidence-only **child knowledge point** (`error_types.trap_knowledge_point_id`, migration V79). It is never a review unit, never mapped to questions or prerequisites, and hidden from topic-sequence and the author picker unless `includeErrorTraps=true`.
- Learning records `error_trap` evidence (weight 0.3, outside the practice cap, no milestone XP) when an answer touches a tagged distractor, and keeps child points out of band, skills, snapshots, daily quests, staff stats and badges (V36).
- The review unit stays the **parent** point. Its weakest child picks which practice set is handed out (`searchPracticeSets` takes `trapErrorCode` and ranks by trap-question count, from two up). A child that drops to `PRIORITY` while the parent has no review creates an optional `ERROR_PATTERN` review.
- Wrong answers return `error {code, name, fixHint}`; review details return `errorTrap` and `blocking`; the tree and report nest child points that have evidence under their parent. Starting a review from a child point is a 409.
- True/False/Not Given traps are derived from the correct answer (backfilled for existing rows, filled for new versions).
- Seeds 19 practice sets (V80, titles cleaned in V81) and approves the reviewed error taxonomy (V82) so each in-scope error code has two sets with two trap questions each.

Contracts under `docs/contracts/` are updated. Design and phase reports are in `plans/261024-1720-error-trap-sub-knowledge-points/`.

## Test plan
- [x] `mvn -pl services/content-service,services/learning-service -am test`: content 959 tests, learning 941, 0 failures
- [x] Ran content + learning on a local stack (compose Postgres, config-server, minted internal JWT): a wrong answer on the trap option returns `error`, writes `error_trap` evidence and a child profile, and the tree/report/basket/suggestions endpoints return 200 without leaking child points
- [x] That run found two bugs, both fixed with tests: learner-facing error names came back empty because every error code was still unreviewed (resolved by the examiner's approval, V82); the tree reported the child point's own code instead of the error code
- [ ] `ERROR_PATTERN` creation was only covered by Testcontainers tests (it needs a child at `PRIORITY`, which takes 3+ pieces of evidence over 2+ days)

## Notes for reviewers
- **An IELTS examiner has reviewed the seeded practice questions and the error taxonomy (requested by the owner); nothing is left as draft (V81, V82).** Approval also changes what grading and Assessment's error analysis accept (they now get the 28 codes instead of none), and lets new True/False/Not Given questions get their traps filled in at save time.
- Migrations are new only: content V79, V80, V81, V82; learning V36. No applied migration was edited.
- Frontend counterpart: IeltsPath-Platform/frontend (shows the error name and fix hint, the optional review and the nested traps).

author: ersinkoc
body:
# W3.47 — the task board is the daemon's file

The kernel still reached **16** modules. This slice takes **two** of those edges — the same family, and the
first slice in a while that takes two at once (like W3.43).

## The port is the contract's — and it is the HOST's port

```go
// kernel/contract/workboardapi/hoststore.go
type HostStore interface {
    Get(id string) (Task, bool)
    List(f Filter) []Task
    Create(spec CreateSpec, now time.Time) (Task, bool, error)
    Claim(id, agent, runID string, now time.Time) (Task, error)
    /* … the whole lifecycle: Heartbeat, Comment, Block, Fail, Unblock,
       SetRetryPolicy, Complete, Prove, Review, SetSeat, Archive, Link,
       AddDependency, BlockingDependencies, ReclaimStale, SweepStaleClaims */
}
```

**Twenty** verbs — and the width is not a copy of the store's method list. It is the **host's** width, and the
read port stays where it was:

- the **plugin** (the agent-facing `workboard` tool) keeps the **read side only** (`Store`, two verbs: `Get`,
  `List`) — a plugin that could claim, complete or archive a task would be driving another agent's work item;
- the **host** drives the whole lifecycle, so the host's port carries all twenty.

That is the same shape W3.45 gave the script-tool store (`Store` for the plugin, `HostStore` for the host) —
and the same rule: **a port's width is decided by the weakest holder of it.**

## Two rules moved with the port

- **`ErrNotFound`** — the host reports it, and the host may not name a module's error. The module keeps the
  name as an alias.
- **the retry rule** (`RetryDecisionFor`, `NormalizeRetryPolicy`) — pure, and it reads the task, so it travels
  with the task. The module delegates to it, so there is one rule.

## The store file is the daemon's

```go
// cmd/agezt/main_toolinvoker.go
if cfg.Workboard == nil {
    store, err := workboard.OpenStore(filepath.Join(cfg.BaseDir, "workboard"))
    if err != nil {
        return nil, err
    }
    cfg.Workboard = store
}
```

A store that cannot be opened is a **startup error** — the board is part of the daemon, not a convenience.

## A missing board is an answer, not a panic — in TWO layers

The board used to be opened by the kernel, so the field was **never nil**. Now a host may open a kernel without
a board, so two layers had to learn the rule: the **kernel** refuses every board operation, and the **app
layer** refuses the same way on all four surfaces (service, watch, dispatch, execution).

`ProveTask` used to answer **"not found"** when the board was missing, because the missing board and the
missing task looked the same from the inside. Now they are different: no board → *"not available"*; a board
without that task → `workboard: not found`.

## The proof

- **Ratchet: 53/13 → 51/13** (two edges).
- **8 mutations, 8 caught, 0 survived, 0 skipped, 0 build errors** — four of them gate-measured by archcheck.
- All gates green: `gofmt`, `go vet`, `archcheck`, `deadcodecheck`, `depscheck`, `sdkparity`,
  `structure-md`, `changelog-lint`, `docclaimscheck`, `staticcheck`, `go test ./... -count=1`.

Evidence: `architecture/185-w347-workboard-port-evidence.md`

author: taraskovalenko
body:
Every build was printing a few dozen `Stale file '.../GhNotch/.build/...' is located outside of the allowed root paths` warnings. SwiftPM keeps absolute paths in `.build`, and those still pointed at the old GhNotch folder. `build-app.sh` now writes the checkout path to `.build/.pitwall-root` and wipes `.build` when that path doesn't match, so a moved or renamed checkout gets one clean build and then stays quiet.

The build script also takes a few optional env vars:

- `VERSION` and `BUILD_NUMBER` get written into the bundle's `Info.plist`
- `ARCHS="arm64 x86_64"` gives a universal binary (I checked it with `lipo`)

## Releases

`.github/workflows/release.yml` runs when you push a `v*` tag. It runs `swift test`, builds the app with the tag as its version (minus the `v`) and the run number as its build number, zips it with `ditto` and publishes `Pitwall.zip` plus `Pitwall.zip.sha256` as a release with generated notes. It only builds for Apple silicon, same as the README says.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/TarasKovalenko/Pitwall/main/scripts/install.sh | bash
```

The script downloads the release, checks the SHA-256 and the code signature, quits Pitwall if it's running, and installs into `/Applications`. If that folder isn't writable it uses `~/Applications`. `PITWALL_VERSION` pins a version and `PITWALL_DIR` changes the folder. The build is ad-hoc signed and not notarized, so the script also clears the quarantine flag. Otherwise Gatekeeper won't open it.

README has new Install and Releasing sections.

## Testing

- Ran `build-app.sh` twice: the first run cleaned `.build`, the second had no stale warnings
- Built a universal binary with version stamping and checked the arch list and plist values
- Zipped the app, checked the checksum, unzipped it and ran `codesign --verify`, all locally

The workflow hasn't run yet. It's set to the `macos-26` runner, so if GitHub doesn't have that image, change it to `macos-15`. The download part of the install script will only work once the first release is up.

body:
Changelog entries can set an optional metaDescription in frontmatter. The entry page uses that text for the meta description, the Open Graph description, and the Twitter description.

When metaDescription is missing, an existing summary or description is used. Otherwise the description is built from the entry body: markdown, MDX components, images, and link syntax are removed, whitespace is collapsed, and the text is trimmed to about 155 characters at a word boundary with an ellipsis.

The October 16 and October 23, 2026 entries include meta descriptions.

author: rockodragon
body:
## The bug

Since #101 went live, every `/@handle` on thecreative.exchange shows an empty page, whether or not the handle exists. Nobody has claimed a handle yet, so no one has run into it.

`routes/slug.tsx` wraps the person's page in the `_app` layout's default export: `<AppLayout>{page}</AppLayout>`. The production build wraps each route module's default export in a component that passes only the route's own props (`params`, `loaderData`). In the built `_app` chunk that shows up as `lt=B0(function({children:a}){…})`. So `children` never arrives, and the shell renders an empty `<main>`. The handle lookup never even subscribes. Unit tests run without that build step, which is why they passed.

## The fix

- `_app.tsx` exports the shell as `AppShell({ children })`. The layout's default export is now `function AppLayout() { return <AppShell />; }`, so every other page renders exactly as before.
- `slug.tsx` uses `AppShell`.

author: qiao-obs
body:
## 问题（两个，都在测试基础设施里）

### 1. `test/md.test.mjs` 硬编码作者本机路径

```js
await import('file:///D:/dsh%20work/dsh-update-checker/client/client.js');
```

在别人机器上必然 `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`。而 `package.json` 的 `test` 脚本用 `&&` 串联 8 个文件：

```
node test/checker.test.mjs && node test/http.test.mjs && node test/integration.test.mjs
  && node test/md.test.mjs && node test/render-harness.mjs && node test/lifecycle.test.mjs
  && node test/reminder.test.mjs && node test/reminder-scheduler.test.mjs
```

`md` 一挂，后面的 `render-harness` / `lifecycle` / `reminder` / `reminder-scheduler` **四个文件从来没被执行过**。

### 2. `DSH_CORDIS_PATH` 的默认值是作者本机 checkout，且跳过被伪装成通过

`test/harness.mjs`、`test/lifecycle.test.mjs`、`test/reminder-scheduler.test.mjs` 三处：

```js
const CORDIS_URL = process.env.DSH_CORDIS_PATH
  || 'file:///D:/dsh%20work/_dsh_src/dsh/node_modules/@deepseek-ai/cordis/lib/index.js';
```

而 `harness.mjs` 上面那行的注释写的是 *"Machine-specific paths are overridable via env; defaults resolve portably"* —— 注释与实现相反。导入失败时：

```js
catch {
  console.log(`SKIP  cordis checkout not found at ${CORDIS_URL} (set DSH_CORDIS_PATH to run)`);
  process.exit(0);   // ← 退出码 0
}
```

**测试没跑，CI 却是绿的**，这是最坏的一种覆盖假象。

## 改动

- `md.test.mjs` 改用 `new URL('../client/client.js', import.meta.url)`；
- 新增 `test/cordis-path.mjs`：`resolveCordisUrl()` 依次尝试 `DSH_CORDIS_PATH` → `createRequire(import.meta.url).resolve('@deepseek-ai/cordis')` → `null`；
- 三个文件改用该 helper；解析不到时打印明确的 *"This is a skip, not a pass."*；导入失败时把真实的 `error.message` 打出来，而不是一律说 "not found"。

## 结果

本机（cordis 可从上层 `node_modules` 解析）：

```
npm test
  38 assertions passed
  19/19 passed
  24/24 passed
  23/23 passed
  5/5 passed        ← lifecycle，修复前从未执行
  57 assertions passed
  33/33 passed      ← reminder-scheduler，修复前从未执行
```

没有 cordis 的机器上会打印明确的 SKIP 说明，而不是伪装成通过。

## 未改动

`test/checker.test.mjs:35-37` 里还有 `D:/dsh work/...` 字面量，但那是 `parseSpec()` 的**入参**，只测路径解析、不碰文件系统，保留原样。

author: oktkas
body:
Adds **WebP** (animated, looping) as an output format next to GIF, so renders are small enough to embed in GitHub/GitLab READMEs.

> **Depends on #25** (transparent background). This branch is built on it, so until #25 merges the diff also shows that commit. Only the top commit (`feat: add animated WebP output`) is new here.

## Why
SpinRender GIFs are often 7–10 MB+. WebP has inter-frame compression, full colour and 8-bit alpha. GitHub and GitLab both show it inline with a plain `![](board.webp)`.

Measured on 120 real 800×800 frames:

| Background | GIF | WebP | Smaller by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Opaque | 9.5 MB | 2.6 MB | 3.6× |
| Transparent | 7.3 MB | 3.1 MB | 2.4× |

Transparent WebP also has smooth, anti-aliased edges. GIF transparency is 1-bit, so its edges look jagged.

## Changes
- `RenderEngine.assemble_webp` assembles the output in one ffmpeg pass: `libwebp_anim`, lossy quality 75 (libwebp's default), `compression_level 6`, `-loop 0`. Opaque output is composited onto the background colour with the same graph MP4/GIF use. Transparent output keeps alpha (`yuva420p`).
- If the ffmpeg build has no libwebp encoder, the user gets a clear error. Most builds include it.
- `get_output_path` and the output-settings placeholder use `.webp`.
- WebP is added to the Format dropdown and to the options in all 19 locale files. The Transparent checkbox already applies to every format except MP4, so it needed no changes.
- Added tests for opaque and transparent graphs, the missing-encoder error and the output extension. README and CHANGELOG are updated.

## Testing
- `pytest tests/unit`: 538 passed.
- Ran `assemble_gif` and `assemble_webp` on the real frames above to measure the sizes.

author: pierrunoyt
body:
### Related GitHub Issue

Closes: #2188

### Description

A parent task can have tool results that are not yet in its API history when it starts a subtask. Delegation saves them first. If that save failed and the retry save also failed, delegation continued. The parent was disposed. Later, the parent resumed from disk. Its history ended with a `tool_use` that had no `tool_result`. Providers reject this with a 400 error.

This PR makes delegation stop in that case. The behavior is a choice. Please confirm it.

- **Delegation** (`ClineProvider.delegateParentAndOpenChild`): The method flushes the pending results. If the flush fails, it retries the save and flushes once more. Saving the existing history does not add results that never reached it, so the second flush is needed. If the results are still not saved, the method throws before it disposes the parent or creates a child. The parent stays open with its pending results in memory. The user can try the same delegation again.
- **User-visible behavior**: `new_task` returns this error through its normal error handling: "Could not start the subtask: the parent task's pending tool results could not be saved to disk. The parent task stays open and nothing was delegated. Check disk space and permissions, then try again."
- **Flush** (`Task.flushPendingToolResultsToHistory`): A flush can append the results to history and then fail to save them. A second flush used to append the same results again. The task now remembers this state. A repeat flush only saves the history. This makes the retry safe. The state resets when the next API request starts.
- **Not changed**: Successful delegation. The send-time normalizer from #2113. A trailing `tool_use` can still have a result that is pending, so the normalizer must leave it alone.

Review points:

- The old code treated any flush error as non-fatal. Now every failure to persist the results stops delegation. This includes a flush that throws.
- The error message is plain English, like the warning it replaces. I did not add translations.

### Test Procedure

Unit tests:

- `src`: `npx vitest run __tests__/ClineProvider.delegation.spec.ts core/task/__tests__/Task.persistence.spec.ts`
- Delegation tests cover: the flush and the retry save both fail; the retry save succeeds but the results are still not in history; the flush throws. Each case rejects, and nothing is disposed, created, or written to history. Other tests cover a repeat flush that succeeds after the retry (delegation continues), and a first flush that succeeds (no retry).
- Persistence tests cover: a retry saves results that are already in history without a second copy; results that never reached history can still be added by a later flush.
- The failure cases and the no-duplicate case fail without the source change.

Other checks: `check-types` passes in `src`. ESLint passes with no new suppressions. The `core/webview`, `core/task`, `core/tools`, and `__tests__` suites pass.

### Pre-Submission Checklist

- [x] **Issue Linked**: This PR is linked to an approved GitHub Issue (see "Related GitHub Issue" above).
- [x] **Scope**: My changes are focused on the linked issue (one major feature/fix per PR).
- [x] **Self-Review**: I reviewed my own code with care.
- [x] **Writing Style**: The PR title and description use Simplified Technical English (ASD-STE100): short sentences, plain words, active voice, one idea per sentence, no contractions.
- [x] **Testing**: New and/or updated tests have been added to cover my changes (if applicable).
- [ ] **Visual Snapshot** (UI changes only): Not applicable. This PR has no UI change.
- [x] **Documentation Impact**: I checked if my changes need documentation updates (see "Documentation Updates" section below).
- [x] **Contribution Guidelines**: I read and agree to the [Contributor Guidelines](/CONTRIBUTING.md).

author: matthewjones372
body:
This is the third and last entry of spec 0152, `spec-0152-unbind`.

## What
After #617 and #618, nothing reads the run's ThreadLocals, so they are deleted along with everything that bound them:
- **`Boundaries.within`** and its ThreadLocal. This follows the spec's answer to Q1: delete it, don't deprecate it. `Pulling.pull` now calls `pulled(max)` directly.
- **`Releases`'** `within`, `around`, `here` and ThreadLocal.
- **`Resources`'** `around`, `here` and ThreadLocal. A restart's attempt is built under `ctx.within(attempt)` and nothing more.
- **`Turns`'** own ThreadLocal, with `taking()` and `here()`. `Turns.fork` keeps the clock binding the spec leaves alone: `clock.locally` and `Waiting.within`. Both live outside this module.
- **`Pulling.within`**. lark-stream-actors' `ActorFanin` feeders call `feed`, `startInners` and `fold` directly. Their pulls were built under the run's context, so there is nothing to bind. That also drops the `run` parameter from `Input`, `Outer` and `Folding`, and `ActorBoundaries.pulling`.
- **The spec**: entry 2 is ticked with #618. Entry 3's text now says `run.within` is removed, where it used to say it would be replaced by a call that takes the context.
- **KDoc** that described the old binding now names the `PullContext`.

`grep ThreadLocal stream/lark-stream-forks` finds nothing. The clock binding the done condition allows for is lark core's, not this module's.

## API note
`Boundaries.within` and `Pulling.within` were public, `@StreamSpi`. Nothing in the repo called `Boundaries.within`, and only `ActorFanin` called `Pulling.within`. Every module that depends on lark-stream-forks or lark-stream-actors still compiles: actor-projection, kafka, cluster and both benchmark modules.

| Module | Tests |
|---|---|
| `lark-stream-forks` | 70 |

## cron 模板化与安装器

- 5 个文件、6 条命令行：`yiban-{audit,backup-sentinel,cleanup,probe,sign}` 的 `/opt/yiban-auto-sign` 改为 `@YIBAN_APP_DIR@`。

3. **突变证据（全部真跑）**：

- `:1005` 的可复制命令改为从值表渲染：`B="http://127.0.0.1:$(sed -n 's/^YIBAN_WEB_PORT=//p' deploy/web.env)"`。

author: kobyldav
body:
### Root cause
The shared `boundedProviderGet()` used by NASA GIBS and FIRMS passes `redirect:'error'` to `fetch`. Cloudflare Workers' runtime can reject that mode with `TypeError` before sending a request, while Fedora/Node works. This produced `GIBS_TRANSPORT_ERROR` and failing FIRMS on production Pages Functions even though they run and secrets are configured.

### Fix
Switch to `redirect:'manual'` and retain explicit `!response.ok` rejection; no 3xx is followed, no URL with FIRMS MAP_KEY can be sent to a different host. Works in both Node and Workers. New regression tests emulate Cloudflare's behavior and assert 302 is refused.

### Integration
MyWeb includes a compatible, allowlisted NASA-only redirect shim on main for its currently pinned SDK commit; after tests pass, package pin can be updated separately. This PR does **not** imply live upstream verification.

author: lexoliu
body:
## Summary

`ScrollController` only held the most recent requested target, so an app could not read where the viewport actually is or whether it has reached an edge. This adds a read-only `ScrollController::position() -> Computed<Option<ScrollPosition>>` carrying the measured offset, viewport size, content size, and `at_start` / `at_end` flags computed on the scroll axis only. Short content reports both.

The value only changes when a backend reports real layout or scroll geometry; `scroll_to` and other requests never write it. It stays `None` until the first real layout and keeps its last value across unmounts.

- `waterui-backend-core`: `ScrollHandle` carries a `ScrollPositionReport` (binding plus logical geometry). Geometry and binding rebind together, so an edge change is reported even when the offset doesn't move. Reports are written outside the internal borrow; offset watchers run first and the newest position is taken afterwards, so a watcher that scrolls can't be overwritten by a stale value. `rebind(None)` disconnects the sink, so the semantic (unbounded) pass never writes fake geometry.
- Hydrolysis: ScrollView and List report logical geometry from before the safe-area extension.
- Apple: ScrollView and List report from scroll and layout callbacks: UIKit uses the inset-adjusted offset/viewport, AppKit the clip bounds and document frame. The AppKit list observes its own `NSScrollView`. The new UIKit table handler slots are cleared through `HandlerTeardown`.

Fixes #1259

## Verification

- `cargo nextest run -p waterui-backend-core -p waterui-layout --lib -E 'test(scroll)'`: 52 passed (new cases: position-only sinks, wheel/glide/animated/user moves, geometry-only edge changes, clamping rebind, disconnect via `rebind(None)`, reentrant offset watcher).
- `cargo nextest run -p hydrolysis --test scroll --test list -E 'test(scroll_position)'`: 4 passed (pending request vs applied offset, content growth clearing `at_end`, observer mutating the list collection).
- `cargo clippy -D warnings` for the layout, backend-core, hydrolysis, and waterui-apple libs (macOS and `aarch64-apple-ios`): clean.

## Notes for reviewers

The new public API is in `components/foundation/layout/src/collections/scroll.rs`. It is read-only and doesn't change layout semantics; the maintainer approved it, hence the `layout-decision` label. Apple behaviour is covered by compilation only for now; there is no native harness for list scroll position yet.

author: pin4sf
body:
Design note only: `docs/proposals/ONE_WALDO_ACROSS_SURFACES_2026-10-25.md`. It has no runtime code, migrations, deploys or secrets. It designs four owner rulings of 25 Oct, as corrected about 10:20Z: Telegram is internal only, and row 2 is closed. Source pin: `beta-mvp` `296aee94`; the branch also merges the later tip `2c4672c9`, and the note accounts for #1458's per-chat compaction summary. Every claim is tagged [verified], [inference] or [proposed], with file:line.

## What it decides

1. **One timeline.**
   - **Today:** the app already shows iMessage rows, labelled `imessage`. I confirmed this with an uncommitted probe plus a failing control. What's missing is the model's window, which walks only the turn's own chain. WhatsApp and internal Telegram write the legacy `conv:*` store, and console rows are stamped `app`.
   - **Design:**
     - one main chain `owner:<principal>`, read and written by every user surface;
     - the delivery binding split from the history chain, with each `conversationRef` reader classified;
     - a forward-only cutover behind `WALDO_ONE_TIMELINE`;
     - no new store.
   - **Blocker:** the iMessage cutover waits on #1463's data-agreement answer, or needs a host-set health marker.
   - **ADR:** under `CLAUDE.md:18`, the bodies need no ADR. ADR-0077 (Supabase graph) does conflict with the OwnerDO store, so the note drafts an amendment's decision text.
2. **One approval rule.** It is enforced once, in the desk's `decide`.
   - An approve that reaches other people needs a step-up proof from the last 2 h:
     - console: `verified_at`;
     - app: the session's `created_at`, per #1541.
   - Chat surfaces bring no proof, so they fail closed with the existing app link. This also covers cards presented before the change.
   - Every one of the 7 kinds is classified by who it reaches.
   - `step_up_required` is returned only to app builds that declare the new contract revision.
3. **iMessage numbered replies.**
   - Cards go through the iMessage final outbox and arm when the delivery result arrives.
   - One armed card per chat: the latest outbound message.
   - An exact `1` or `2` decides before any model turn. Anything else goes to the model.
   - Tapbacks and edits are never admitted.
   - The note covers expiry, replay and digest binding.
4. **One capability list.**
   - Today three tables disagree, and the one the model reads is a literal at `telegram-turn.ts:16`.
   - The design is a directional V2 table in contracts and a runtime resolver intersected with live facts (transcriber, iMessage probe flags). The presentation, prompt, desk and delivery read only the resolver, and a conformance guard enforces that.

## Owner questions (§2.6)

- **Q1:** ungate `message_send`? It reaches only the owner's own chat today.
- **Q2:** the audience of `browser_submit`, `mcp_call` and `tainted_action`. The default is fail-closed: they count as reaching other people.

## PR split (§6)

| PR | Scope | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| A | Capability table V2 and resolver | Ark, #1449 |
| B | Desk audience predicate and step-up proof | Ansh, #1479; builds #1541's approval part |
| C | iMessage numbered replies | Ansh, #1479 |
| D | Timeline cutover | Ark, #1449; the iMessage part waits on #1463 |
| E | App labels and the step-up retry | waldo-app #138 |
| Brain | ADR-0077 amendment | owner and gate |

`approvals.ts` and `owner-do.ts` have one writer at a time. Proposed order: A → B → C → D.

## Verification at head `8d49bfab` (contains `beta-mvp` `2c4672c9`)

- `git diff --check`: PASS.
- `npx -y pnpm@10.34.4 verify:guards`: exit 1, from pgTAP only.
  - The `node --test` part: PASS, 153/153.
  - `run-all` stops at `guard-pgtap`, which is UNAVAILABLE on macOS (no `/etc/os-release` or `dpkg`). The 25 other guards were run one by one, including those that sort after pgTAP: all PASS.
- An uncommitted probe (§1.1) at `296aee94` passed. Its control mutation failed as expected. The file was deleted.
- The full `verify` wall was NOT RUN; this change is docs only. CI is the arbiter for pgTAP.

author: a11ign-workers[bot]
body:
https://linear.app/a11ign/issue/A11-253/one-standard-dependabotyml-for-every-repository-weekly-grouped-patch

Refs A11-253

Partial: step 1 of 2. Step 2 regenerates the nine consumer repositories (a11ign, agent-org, control, lab, documents, screenreader-fleet, screenreader-worker, announcement-emulator, a11ign.github.io) once this release is on the registry (`npm view @a11ign/toolchain version`): each bumps toolchain, adds its extras file, regenerates `.github/dependabot.yml`, adds the drift check, and lists what changed in its config. control also gains the test that every `layers.*.package` of `deploy-pins.json` is in `FROZEN`. The ticket's "each repository's file is generated" and "existing configs are replaced" lines are therefore met here for toolchain only.

Worked against the ticket as updated 2026-10-25T10:18:03.491Z

## What changed

`dependabot-config` (a new export and bin of `@a11ign/toolchain`) is the one template for `.github/dependabot.yml`.

- `dependabot-config --write [--root <dir>]` writes the file from the tree. `--check` exits 1, printing the diff and the `--write` command, when the committed file (or its absence) differs from that output; exit 2 when the tree or the extras cannot be read.
- Every ecosystem is weekly, Monday 05:23 UTC, with one `<ecosystem>-minor-and-patch` group (patterns `*`, update-types minor and patch), so a major is its own pull request. Also `commit-message.prefix: deps`, `cooldown.default-days: 7`, `open-pull-requests-limit: 10`, and no `labels:`.
- Ecosystems come from the tree: npm at `/` with a root `package.json`, pip per directory with a `requirements*.txt` or `pyproject.toml` (several directories are one entry using `directories:`), github-actions with a workflow `.yml`/`.yaml`.
- The npm `ignore` is `FROZEN` (`src/dependabot-frozen.ts`, exported as `./dependabot-frozen`: `@a11ign/screenreader-worker`, `@a11ign/screenreader-fleet`, `@guidepup/guidepup`, `@guidepup/setup`, each with its reason), then the workspace's own packages and the root's, then `.github/dependabot-extra.json`. Each is written with its reason on the line above. The extras schema accepts only an ignore (name and one-line reason), npm `directories` and an npm `versioning-strategy`, so no repository can opt out of the schedule, groups or freeze.
- Conventions for A11-254 and A11-255 are exported (`DEPENDABOT_GROUP_SUFFIX`, `DEPENDABOT_COMMIT_PREFIX`, `dependabotGroupName`) and written up in the README's "Dependency updates" section.
- toolchain's own `.github/dependabot.yml` is regenerated (was daily and ungrouped; now weekly, grouped, with the frozen and workspace ignores and a 7-day cooldown) and `scripts/dependabot-config.test.ts` checks it from source.

## Proof of each acceptance line

| Line | Proven by |
| --- | --- |
| Weekly at one fixed time, per ecosystem | `src/dependabot-config.test.ts` "every ecosystem of every repository is weekly at the one fixed time" (four real repository trees) |
| Patch and minor grouped, one per ecosystem; majors apart | "patch and minor are ONE group per ecosystem, and a major matches no group" (exact `groups` equality) |
| pip where present | "a11ign's two Python directories are ONE pip entry", "npm is at the root ... pip for each requirements or pyproject directory" |
| Frozen packages never proposed | "every FROZEN name is in the npm ignore of every repository that has npm, and the list has the four the policy names"; "each ignore is written with its reason" |
| List from one place | `FROZEN` is the only place the four names appear (the test imports it). Control's test that ties it to `deploy-pins.json` is step 2 |
| Commit-message and label conventions | "the conventions A11-254 and A11-255 read are constants, and the file is written from them", "no entry sets `labels`" |
| A check fails on drift | "--check passes on what --write made, and fails with the diff and the fix when the file is edited by hand", "--check fails when the file is missing, and when a frozen ignore is deleted", "--check fails when the workspace gains a package" |
| Existing per-repository configs replaced, PR lists what changed | toolchain's here (`scripts/dependabot-config.test.ts`); the other repositories are step 2 |
| After merge: next weekly run opens grouped PRs, none for frozen packages | Not provable before merge. It needs step 2 in each repository, then the chairman session reads the first Monday 05:23 UTC run. The acceptance block below proves the file that run reads |

The acceptance block in `.acceptance/` runs the tests, `--check` on this repository (exit 0), a hand edit (exit 1) and restoring it, and greps the four frozen names. Run on this branch: exit 0. `pnpm test`: `VERDICT pass: 438 tests in 37 files`; `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run typecheck` and `pnpm run pack-check` pass. The fixtures are tree listings of a11ign, agent-org, lab and a11ign.github.io at `origin/main` on 2026-10-25.

## Decisions made without a person

These come from the plan, which an unattended planning run wrote. Check each against the code.

1. The template and the generator live in `@a11ign/toolchain`, consumed by version (ADR 0045; `layout-check` is the precedent).
2. `FROZEN` lives in toolchain, with a test in control (step 2) tying it to `deploy-pins.json`, because reading control's manifest at generation time would need a checkout of control.
3. Frozen packages: `@a11ign/screenreader-worker`, `@a11ign/screenreader-fleet` (the manifest's `layers`), `@guidepup/guidepup`, `@guidepup/setup` (named by the ticket). Frozen names are ignored in every repository.
4. The schedule is Monday 05:23 UTC (the ticket asks for one fixed time and names none; off the hour, like `.github`'s `renovate.yml`). One place to change.
5. Groups use semver `update-types` `[minor, patch]`, one per ecosystem; a `0.x` minor is grouped.
6. Dependabot's default labels, no custom `labels:` (a missing custom label is silently dropped).
7. `cooldown: default-days: 7`, as agent-org has it.
8. The drift check is exact equality with the installed toolchain's output, run in each repository.
9. No ADR (ADR 0041 decision 4 is kept). Playwright is not frozen (A11-230).

Decisions I made while building (technical, not in the plan, or departing from it):

- **The generated header carries no toolchain version**, where the plan says "from `@a11ign/toolchain@<version>`". A version in the file would change it on every toolchain release, so the grouped toolchain bump would fail the check in every consumer and become a red group. Checked by "the file says it is generated ... and carries no toolchain version".
- Extras use `directories` (an array) for npm, also for a single directory (written as `directory:`). The plan says `directory` for announcement-emulator and `directories` for agent-org.
- pip directories skip paths under `fixtures`, `*.fixtures`, `venv` and `.venv`; a pip directory whose name YAML could misread is refused, not written. Only workflow `.yml`/`.yaml` files make a github-actions entry.
- The workspace ignore list is every workspace member's name plus the root's, from `pnpm-workspace.yaml` or `workspaces`. a11ign's workspace no longer holds `@a11ign/control`, so it is no longer ignored there (its old file did).
- agent-org's old `allow:` list (three packages) is not representable: every repository gets all packages, as the plan says.

## Outside the plan's paths

Outside-Region: src/layout-check.ts — `readLayoutTree` takes the names of extra files to read as text and `workspacePackageNames` is exported, so the generator reuses the layout check's workspace reading instead of copying it. One-argument `readLayoutTree(root)` is unchanged.
Outside-Region: src/layout-check.test.ts — the "every bin runs through its own symlink" test passes `--write --root <dir>` to `dependabot-config`, because every other bin takes a bare directory and this one needs a mode.

author: petertheone
body:
**Required merge order: #32 → #31 → #33.** #33 removes the gate exemption, which only works once #31 is in master. #31 needs #32's checker and keeps `PGACC_TOKEN_EQUIVALENCE_ALLOW_CRLF=1` in CI, so its CI against master and the master push after its merge still have the exemption.

Second of three stacked PRs. It is based on #32 (token-equivalence checker); #33 (enforcement) builds on it. The reformat is regenerated on the final master, with #28, #29 and #30 already merged.

Owner-approved one-time reformat: **PER Coding Style 3.0, whitespace rules only**. There is no enforcement in this PR: no CI format check and no hooks (see #33).

## Tool and rules
PHP-CS-Fixer **3.95.27** is pinned in `tests/style/composer.lock` and runs on the pinned `php:8.5-cli` image via `sh scripts/format.sh [--check]`. It has no PER-CS 3.1 set yet, so this uses `@PER-CS3x0`.

`.php-cs-fixer.dist.php` contains only the set's whitespace rules, each with the set's configuration:
- indentation: `indentation_type`, `statement_indentation`, `array_indentation`
- braces and layout: `braces_position`, `control_structure_continuation_position`, `single_line_empty_body`, `class_definition`, `function_declaration`, `method_argument_space`, `return_type_declaration`, `no_multiple_statements_per_line`
- spacing: `binary_operator_spaces`, `unary_operator_spaces`, `ternary_operator_spaces`, `concat_space`, `cast_spaces`, `compact_nullable_type_declaration`, `types_spaces`, `declare_equal_normalize`, `no_space_around_double_colon`, `no_spaces_after_function_name`, `spaces_inside_parentheses`, `switch_case_space`, `attribute_block_no_spaces`, `single_space_around_construct`
- blank lines: `blank_line_after_opening_tag`, `blank_line_after_namespace`, `blank_lines_before_namespace`, `blank_line_between_import_groups`, `single_line_after_imports`, `no_blank_lines_after_class_opening`, `no_extra_blank_lines`, `no_whitespace_in_blank_line`, `single_blank_line_at_eof`
- trailing whitespace and line endings: `no_trailing_whitespace`, `no_trailing_whitespace_in_comment`, `line_ending`

The set's token-changing rules are left out; the config lists them. `operator_linebreak` is also left out, because in `spendings.php` it would move an operator across a comment. One visible side effect: an unbraced `else` puts its statement on the same line (`else $x = 1;`).

## Proof
- `sh tests/coverage/token-equivalence.sh --allow-crlf-to-lf --check HEAD~1` passes for all 100 changed PHP files. It was rerun after #32's stricter rules (both short_open_tag settings, byte-exact doc comments, `__LINE__`), and no file is flagged.
- Without the flag, exactly the eight former CRLF files differ.
- `line_ending` cannot have changed a heredoc that matters: no heredoc had CRLF content, and every LF file is equivalent under the strict check.
- All 690 mutants are token-equivalent to the mutants the master targets produce on the old source.
- PHP 5 reference compare: 767 files, 346 identical, 351 accepted, 0 unaccepted, no stale entries.

## Line endings and the output change
All text files of ours are LF now (`* text=auto eol=lf`). Some files are `-text` and stay byte-exact:
- the fixtures;
- the PHP 5 recordings;
- the third-party `icons/`, `js/` and `jquery.fileupload.js`. `icons/readme.*` keep their original CRLF bytes.

The eight former CRLF pages now send LF in their HTML and SQL text. The CRLF that `index.php` appends after a CSV download is now LF too. That is a deliberate change of newline bytes only.

The PHP 5 reference cannot be re-recorded, so one allowlist entry, `RD-FORMAT-CRLF-TO-LF`, is a `transform`. It reads the reference with those CRLF as LF, but only in:
- `http/*.txt`: text/html bodies throughout, other text bodies only in their final CRLF, binary bodies never;
- `sql/*.sql`;
- `helpers/misc.txt`.

`db/` dumps are never touched, and the lane's recording is never changed. The transform affects 294 recordings; for 101 of them the newline change is the only difference.

CI sets `PGACC_TOKEN_EQUIVALENCE_ALLOW_CRLF=1` for this PR and its merge only; #33 removes it.

## Other changes
- `show-uncovered-functions.php`: line 74 is now 71.
- `ReceiptMigrationTest`: skips the blank line PER-CS adds after `<?php`.
- `http-page-views.php`: matches the dispatch list with the new spacing.
- Three HTTP tests now expect LF.
- The rest are docs.

## Blame
`.git-blame-ignore-revs` lists the reformat commit. Enable it locally with `git config blame.ignoreRevsFile .git-blame-ignore-revs`.

## Review tips
`git show 6a23034 -w --ignore-cr-at-eol` (or `git diff -w`). The reformat commit is mechanical; review the others normally.

## Local checks
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| token-equivalence over the reformat | 100/100 equivalent |
| `sh tests/static-analysis.sh` | 0 |
| `sh tests/mutation/run.sh 8.5 --self-test` | 0 |
| `sh tests/run.sh 8.5` with `PGACC_COVERAGE_BASE=origin/master` | 0; gate 0/0, every app file equivalent |
| `sh tests/reference/run.sh compare 8.5` | 0 |

CI is pending. No mutation runs.

## Regenerate (if master moves again)
1. Rebase onto #32.
2. Redo the formatter commit.
3. Apply the `.gitattributes` part, strip CR from the former CRLF files, then `git add --renormalize .`.
4. Run `sh scripts/format.sh` until it fixes 0 files.
5. Run `token-equivalence.sh --allow-crlf-to-lf --check HEAD~1`, then commit.
6. `git diff <old reformat> <old commit 4> | git apply --3way`.
7. Recheck that every mutant is token-equivalent, and that every search matches.
8. Redo the blame commit with the new hash.

author: rfoerthe
body:
## Why

The [Build and Tests run](https://github.com/rfoerthe/planning-poker/actions/runs/40182401421) warned that every action in the workflow still targets the deprecated Node 20 runtime and was being force-run on Node 24. Fixing that surfaced two adjacent problems: `.github/dependabot.yml` was still the unedited template, so no version updates ever ran, and the `pnpm` override list had drifted — twelve entries no longer bound anything while four advisory groups went uncovered.

## What changed

**`ci: bump actions to Node 24 runtimes`** — each action moved to its latest major, all of which declare `using: node24`: checkout v4 → v7, setup-node v3 → v7, pnpm/action-setup v4 → v6, cache v4 → v6, upload-artifact v4 → v7. No step inputs needed changing. `node-version: [22.x]` stays as it is; the warning was about the actions' own runtime, not the project's Node version.

**`chore: configure Dependabot ecosystems`** — replaces the template placeholder (`package-ecosystem: ""`, which is invalid) with the two ecosystems this repository has: `npm` for the root `package.json` and `github-actions` for the workflows, so a deprecated runtime shows up as a PR next time. Minor and patch bumps are grouped per ecosystem; majors still arrive individually.

**`fix(deps): upgrade Firebase CLI and prune stale overrides`** — `firebase-tools` 15.31.0 adopted `csv-parse ^7.0.2` and `stream-json ^3.6.0` upstream, which is the condition `patches/README.md` named for removing the pin, those two overrides and the compatibility patch together. 15.34.1 now resolves csv-parse 7.0.2 and stream-json 3.7.0 from its own ranges, so the pin, the patch and `patches/` are gone. Twelve overrides that no longer bound anything were dropped (undici 7/8, the MCP SDK, hono, ip-address, brace-expansion 1/2, source-map-js, proxy-addr, morgan, fast-uri, compression — resolving the tree without them produced identical versions). Four advisory groups the old list missed are now covered on the line their parents actually request: `undici@6 ^6.29.1` (5 advisories), `zod ^4.6.6`, `body-parser@1 ^1.20.9` / `body-parser@2 ^2.4.0`, `brace-expansion@5 ^5.0.12` (3 advisories). `basic-ftp` left the tree entirely because the CLI upgrade drops `proxy-agent`.

**`fix(deps): update vitest to 4.1.12`** — the last two advisories sat in `@vitest/mocker`, fixed in a release the existing `^4.1.11` range already allowed; only the lockfile held it back.

Net effect: the override list goes from 20 entries to 9, and `pnpm audit` from 17 advisories to none.

## For the reviewer

- The patch removal is covered by the offline CLI integration tests in `scripts/firebase-dependencies.test.mjs`, which exercise the *installed* CLI — auth import across the 1000-record batch boundary, CSV quoting, malformed-JSON rejection, database import, and the `__proto__` regression. All 15 pass against the unpatched 15.34.1, which is what makes dropping the patch safe.
- `@grpc/grpc-js` is the only override whose path reaches the shipped bundle (`@firebase/firestore` still asks for 1.9.x); its comment now says so. Everything else is dev-only, via `firebase-tools` or the lint/test toolchain.
- `pnpm update vitest` also raised the range in `package.json` to `^4.1.12` — pnpm's default on update, not a deliberate pin.
- No CHANGELOG entry: there is no `[Unreleased]` section and the previous dependency commit (d981b1b) didn't add one either. Happy to document this under 3.1.5 if you'd rather.
- Verified locally: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build`, and `pnpm test` (227 vitest + 15 node tests) all pass; `pnpm audit` reports no known vulnerabilities.

body:
ROADMAP S-54 (CireSnave, board 282 item 69, 2026-10-25: *"All of the formats matter...but they should be handled only abstractly in Fuel as the reading and writing of model files should be entirely within MLMF."*). New crate `mlmf-onnx`, format axis, no I/O.

- `encode_model(&OnnxModel) -> Result<Vec<u8>, EncodeError>`: writes a `ModelProto` from caller-supplied initializers (`raw_data`, already in its element type), `opset_import`s, producer strings, `metadata_props`, graph inputs/outputs. **Nodes are opaque**: pre-encoded `NodeProto` bytes appended unchanged. Choosing operators or building a graph from weights is not file work and stays out (the old root-crate exporter that did it, `src/formats/onnx_export.rs`, is not touched here; its fate is S-20/S-31).
- Not guessed: `ir_version` and every `opset_import` are required arguments; optional strings and `model_version` are absent when `None`. Refuses a wrong byte length, a duplicate initializer name, a dtype with no ONNX type, a dimension that overflows i64.
- **Evidence (independent implementation):** `tests/golden.onnx` is what the reference `onnx` 1.23.2 package serializes (`deterministic=True`) for a model with 5 initializers (F32, I64, F16, BF16, scalar U8), 2 opsets (one non-default domain), producer strings, model_version, doc_string, 2 metadata props (one non-ASCII), a node, symbolic-dim input/output; it passes `onnx.checker.check_model`; `tests/make_golden.py` regenerates it. The Rust writer's output is **byte-identical** (240 bytes). The first draft was NOT: it wrote `dims` packed and the reference writes it unpacked (3 bytes longer); the golden check caught it. Sabotage (BF16 type code 16 -> 15) fails the golden test; reverted.
- Local: workspace tests excl. root, `mlmf-core --no-default-features`, clippy -D warnings, doc, fmt, `--locked`. CI steps for the new crate added. Version 0.7.11 proposed (after #155's 0.7.10).
- Reading ONNX (initializers) is not part of this row; Fuel keeps its evaluator.

author: zr-jb
body:
Builds on #429; its commit drops out of this diff once #429 merges.

Each Firefox network E2E job ran three steps that only matter on a runner image without `certutil`:
- naming the image for a cache key;
- restoring a cache of `libnss3-tools` .debs;
- `command -v certutil || scripts/ci/apt-cached.sh certutil …`.

The ubuntu-26.04 image ships `/usr/bin/certutil`. Every Firefox network job checked found it and skipped the install: images 20261012.601 (run 39903764647), 20261021.618 (runs 40167915619 and 40168981078) and 20261023.163 (#429's run). As a result, #429's certutil cache step logged "Path(s) … do not exist, hence no cache is being saved".

- **CI:** the three steps are gone.
- **`apt-cached.sh`:** it loses its one-entry package-set switch and takes only the directory. Its header names what it installs: the target checks' cross compilers.
- **README:** it says the network jobs take the image's `certutil`.
- **If an image ever drops it:** `client/e2e/browsers.ts` fails the first network test at `Bun.spawnSync(["certutil", …])` with a clear error.
- **Cache:** the cross compilers' cache key hashes the script, so it starts cold once.

Proof: `mise run workflow-check` passes, and `bash -n` on the script is clean. This PR's run covers the Firefox network shards without the steps, and the Rust target checks with the narrowed script, which saves a fresh cache.

**Bundled at the coordinator's request:** setup-project now gives jdx/mise-action an explicit `cache_key`: `{{cache_key_prefix}}-{{platform}}-{{version}}-{{install_args_hash}}-p{{cache_period}}-<hash of mise.lock>`. Before, the key hashed every mise config file, `mise.toml` included, so each task edit wrote a fresh set of 7 toolchain caches on main, about 1 GB; three sets were written on 2026-10-25. The installed tools are fixed by `mise.lock` (installs run `--locked`), the selected tool list (`install_args_hash`), the mise version and the runner image (`platform`), so the key still changes whenever the cached tools would. The README says so. `mise run workflow-check` (including jactionlint's YAML and expression checks) and `pipeline-test` pass.

author: banchen21
body:
## 关联任务

降低 Actions 消耗：CI 只在打 tag 时自动运行。

## 改了什么

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` 的触发条件：

```yaml
on:
  push:
    tags: ["v*"]
  workflow_dispatch:
```

去掉 `pull_request` 与 `push.branches` 两个触发点，保留手动触发。

## 为什么

GitHub Actions 当前因账号付款/额度问题无法启动 job（`The job was not started because
recent account payments have failed or your spending limit needs to be increased`），
日常提交与 PR 触发 CI 只会持续累积无法执行的运行记录。发布流程本就以 tag 为界，
把 CI 也对齐到 tag，等额度恢复后再按需手动触发。

## 影响与风险

- **PR 不再有自动门禁**：合并前需要本地跑门禁（`pnpm gate` / `cargo check` 等），
  或到 Actions 页面手动 `Run workflow`。
- 未改动 `deploy.yml`，发布流程不受影响；打 `v*` tag 时 CI 与发布都会触发。
- 各仓 `master` 未配置「必需的 PR 检查」（已核对 `user_client`；其余私有仓读不到保护配置，
  若确有 required checks，PR 会因该检查永不产生结果而无法合并——需要时就地关闭该要求）。

## 验证

- 仅改 YAML 触发块，未动 job 内容。
- 触发块语法为 GitHub 官方支持的 `push.tags` + `workflow_dispatch` 组合。

## 审阅结论

待独立审阅。

author: patrykcieszynski
body:
## Behavior

C2 connects the C1 generator to ordinary equipment drops in authored Loot V2 regions. Solo and party both use KillRewardResolver.resolve_ordinary(). After ordinary items are selected, a separate per-instance affix RNG chooses quality/counts and resolved bonuses; the original item RNG stream, table probabilities, spawn attempts, Luck, item identities/amounts and party recipient draws remain unchanged.

The editable natural_affix_profile.tres has provisional alpha weights: normal 60 (0+0), magic 30 (1+1), rare 9 (2+2), legendary 1 (3+3). These are example tuning values for review, not finalized economy odds. Quality changes affix counts only; it does not restrict tiers. A two-affix item can roll any tier allowed by its base. Iron Sword's authored eligibility stays at 1; higher eligible tiers are covered by fixtures, not silently enabled for live bases.

Honed and Rhythmic extend the natural pool to three prefixes and three suffixes using C1 resources/rules. Their shared precision group name exercises the independent namespaces. Existing UI rarity presentation derives from affix count; there is no new persisted quality field, crafting UI, currency or mob rarity.

Materials/stacks/KU, event-specific grants, starters, NPC purchases and the legacy arena/Metin guaranteed reward retain their existing behavior. An invalid quality batch returns an error without partial awards or fallback rerolls.

## Custody and recovery

Affixes resolve before GroundLootSystem assigns a UID. Structural C1 validation is applied to versioned ground rolls; pickup never calls the generator or current quality profile. Existing reservation/expiry/capacity, PostgreSQL claim/receipt and Inventory reconciliation remain in charge. No SQL schema or network protocol change.

The existing PostgreSQL ground-runtime case now spawns a naturally generated six-affix sword, loses its successful completion, reads the receipt, and verifies the exact frozen UID/affixes survive recovery and replay. A second owner cannot acquire the same UID; item and claim tables each contain one row. It also demonstrates that subsequent profile edits do not reinterpret a frozen drop.

## Verification

- git diff --check: PASS.
- tests/run-smoke.ps1: PASS, 26 Godot cases and 99 Web UI tests, including new natural_affix_loot (0/2/4/6 counts, eligible top-tier access, materials/KU exclusions, immutable input and frozen ground UID).
- Production caller parity across deterministic kills: selected IDs/amounts, attempts/Luck and item RNG state equal unmodified LootResolver results. Affix RNG cannot perturb subsequent party draws.
- python tools/postgres/run_readiness.py --pg-bin Y:/Software/PostgreSQL/bin --suite ground-runtime: PASS, including six-affix unknown-completion recovery alongside existing rollback, races, capacity and session tests.
- tests/run-combat.ps1 -Scene party_network -MarkerPrefix PARTY: PASS server/client1/client2. First invocation used an incorrect wrapper marker; the scenario itself passed, and the corrected wrapper passed all roles.
- tests/metin_encounter.tscn: METIN_ENCOUNTER_OK, thresholds, reward-once, contributions and respawn lifecycle.
- tests/run-cef-export.ps1: PASS Windows client, Windows server, Ubuntu server packaging and existing client/server pack boot checks.
- Isolated editor import: no script/parse/extension-load errors. Existing headless certificate/resource-teardown warnings remain.

## Metin network follow-up

The baseline FIGHT timeout was traced to the test bypassing the derived combat-stat projection when overriding attack. PR #135 refreshes that projection and asserts the fixture boost before combat (four lines, test only). Metin network passes twice on the main-based fix branch and also passes with that same test temporarily applied to this C2 head (5077cdd9), server and both clients. This PR's original test was restored afterward. Integrate #135 to remove the fixture limitation; no combat/HP/timeout change is required.
No physical/native gameplay feel or final rarity balance claim. Current documentation updated in place; no per-commit report. Ready for review; do not merge automatically.

author: atbuy
body:
Running `carrier config` with no subcommand in a terminal now opens an interactive settings editor. Outside a terminal it prints its help, as before. `carrier config set` changes one setting from the command line.

## `carrier config`

- Every setting is in one scrolling list, grouped like the TOML file: Storage, Redaction, Notifications, Shell, Hints, Appearance. The selected setting's key, where it is set (default or which file), and a description show below the list.
- On/off settings toggle with enter or space. Settings with a fixed set of values show all of them (`● suggest  ○ follow  ○ off`); enter moves to the next one and ←/→ go either way. Durations, numbers, paths and colors are edited inline; colors also show a swatch. Lists (`ignore_commands`, `redaction.patterns`) open on their own screen to add, edit and delete items.
- `r` resets a setting to its default, `/` searches titles and keys, and `e` opens the file in `$EDITOR` and reloads it afterwards.
- Each change is saved right away and only the setting's lines change, so comments and the rest of the layout stay. The file is written to a temp file and renamed into place, keeps its permissions, and is written through a symlink rather than replacing it. A value that `config check` rejects is not saved, and its error is shown. When an include sets a value, the include is the file changed. On exit, carrier prints which settings were saved, and where.

## `carrier config set <key> <value>...`

- Saves the same way as the editor. Toggles accept true/false/on/off/yes/no, choices are checked against their values, and numbers must be whole numbers.
- For a list, the values replace it; `--add` and `--remove` change single items. `--reset` removes the setting from the file, so its default applies.
- Tab completes the keys (shown with their titles) and the values of toggles and choices.

## Under the hood

- `config.Settings` describes each setting (kind, choices, title, summary). A test fails if a config key is missing from it.
- New `config.Set`, `config.Reset`, `config.Source` and `config.ParseValue`, plus `RemoveValue`. `SetValue` now replaces arrays written over several lines and handles nested tables such as `[ui.theme]`. The load code reads through a function, so a change is checked before it is written.

Also updates the docs (configuration reference, commands, README) and the changelog.

author: shineshuai
body:
I did not test it in a real browser or with real WebRTC (no WebRTC in the sandbox). The MQTT client is only checked against my own fake broker. Before relying on it, run node tools/signal-probe.mjs from the locations you are. It tries the three brokers with the page’s own client.

Summary of the change
- Link join: the host’s invite is now a short link #j=<token>. The guest opens it, types a greeting, and taps Join. The host sees the greeting and taps Accept or Decline.
- Offer after approval: only after Accept does the host make its connection offer. Offer and answer travel through the brokers, then the WebRTC channel opens and the room is cleared.
- Greeting rule: the host can tick “Ask for a greeting”. The host refuses an empty greeting itself, whatever the guest’s page does.
- Brokers: test.mosquitto.org, broker.hivemq.com and broker.emqx.io are all used at once (SIGNAL_BROKERS in config.js). One working broker reachable from both sides is enough.
- Fallback: if no broker answers within 8 s, the host gets a button “Invite with a code instead”, which runs the old manual flow. Old #c= and #coop= links still work.
- Host waiting: an invite expires after 10 min. If the host’s page was asleep, the guest sees “page may be asleep”. The host receives the waiting request on wake-up (visibilitychange, online).
- Texts and CSS: changed in both languages. I reworded onlineSub, onlineBlurb and noConnection, which no longer mention a reply or “no server”.
- CSP: index.html lists the three wss:// origins. check-config.js reads them as text, so the trial stays removable with its folder.
- Tests: new files for crypto, the MQTT client, the multi-broker hub, the full handshake, and the screen in a fake page.
- Probe tool: tools/signal-probe.mjs, documented in tools/README.md.
- session.js: I dropped my fix because your new upload already contains it.

Security
I need to correct something from my earlier design. I said the per-guest key stops anyone else with the link from hijacking a guest. That was wrong: they could have answered first with their own offer, with the host never involved. Now the link holds the secret plus a fingerprint (a short hash) of the host’s public key. The guest checks the key in the host’s reply against it, so only the real host can answer a guest.

Someone who has the link can still:
- ask to join (the host decides);
- send junk messages, which are ignored or cause a false “declined”;
- see that a room exists.

They cannot read the greeting, the offer or the answer, and they cannot impersonate the host or the guest. The brokers see only ciphertext.

Limits
- Leftover messages: if a page dies without closing, its encrypted retained messages stay on the brokers until the brokers drop them.
- Host accepted, guest gone: after 30 s the host sees an error and must start a new invite.
- No TURN relay: pairs that STUN cannot connect still fail, as before.

author: midhunvijayvs

Before: the ERP kept most data in a Google Drive file. Website customers and online orders were separate lists, and products existed only as a fixed list on the website, so "Create invoice from this order" could not match products.

After: everything lives in Firebase. There is one Products & Materials list that the website reads, with photos, publish/unpublish, website display order, and stock status that updates automatically. There is one customer list (online and offline), and customers added in the ERP get an ovalfarm.in login with a temporary password. There is one order list with an online/offline column, status tabs and a New Order button. Every invoice is made from an order and fills in from it.

How: Firestore is now the only store (`js/store.js` and `js/firebase.js`); the Drive sync, merge and the related tests are removed. Staff can see published products, but cost prices stay private: the site reads a public `catalog` copy that the ERP keeps in sync (`js/catalog.js`). Customer logins are created with a second Firebase app instance, and the free Firebase set-password email is sent. Order prices include GST, so invoice lines use price ÷ (1 + GST) and the totals match. The products that were on the website are seeded automatically the first time an admin signs in. Rules: `firebase/firestore.rules` and the new `firebase/storage.rules`. Tests: 80 rules tests, a demo-mode end-to-end test, and a new emulator end-to-end test covering the ERP and the website together (`tests/firebase.e2e.mjs`). author: juninmd
body:
## Problema

Em `digest()` (src/digest.ts), o bloco de eventos de fora de Franca enviava o cabeçalho "🗺️ Fora de Franca" e, se o envio falhava, seguia postando os eventos mesmo assim. O próprio comentário no código diz que evento de fora sem cabeçalho "pareceria rolê de Franca". Com a falha, o evento era marcado como postado, então a próxima rodada não o reenviava com o cabeçalho.

## Correção

Um flag `cabecalhoOk` controla o envio de `postaDia` e `postaLancamento`. Se o cabeçalho não saiu, os eventos não são marcados e saem na próxima rodada, com o cabeçalho. O bloco de agenda da região (`agenda:fora`) não muda: já se identifica pelo próprio título.

## Verificação

- Teste vermelho antes da correção: `evento de fora não sai se o cabeçalho de fora falhou` (`posted_today` = 1, esperado 0).
- Depois: `test/digest.test.ts` 7/7; `bun test` 136 pass, 0 fail; `bunx tsc --noEmit` sem erro.
- Biome: `digest.ts` com as mesmas 8 linhas de variation selector de emoji pré-existentes; o trecho alterado está formatado. `digest.test.ts` sem diferença.
- Dados sintéticos (evento "Show Longe" em Ribeirão Preto, Telegram simulado).

Fora desta PR: o cabeçalho continua sendo enviado a cada rodada com evento de fora novo, como já era; não mudei esse comportamento.

author: less82
body:
## 무엇
미리보기 f894b77 실관측: 총괄 PC «시뮬» 탭에서 시뮬 목록 items=[]·DB 슬롯 IDLE 인데 머리줄 STOP 이 보임. 작성자 보고로 **폰 총괄도 같은 꼴** → 이 PR 범위를 폰 총괄까지 넓힘(조정 지시).

## 원인(코드 확인)
- 서버: 시뮬 슬롯은 고정 로봇 행. IDLE 이 되면 `owner_user_id=None` 으로 비우고 행은 `/robots?scope=all` 에 그대로 남는다(`simulation.py` 끝내기·띄우기 실패 정리). **서버 동작은 설계대로** — 서버 수정 없음.
- 웹: `App.tsx` 총괄 STOP 후보가 `sim=true` 만 봐서 담당 없는 IDLE 슬롯도 후보로 셌다(PC). 1차 고침 뒤에도 폰은 `phone ||` 로 담당 판정을 건너뛰었다.

## 고침(웹 `App.tsx` 한 곳, PC·폰 같은 함수 `mayStop` 하나)
- 총괄 STOP 후보 = 시뮬이고 **담당이 나**인 로봇만 — PC·폰 공통(STARTING·ACTIVE·STOPPING 동안 서버 담당 = 띄운 사람). 목록 갱신 전 «띄우는 중»은 기존 `sim.live()`(toSim) 경로가 그대로 덮는다.
- 운영 관리자(PC·폰): 판정 그대로(머리줄 STOP 항상, #94). 폰 조종·명령 경로·«시뮬 정지»·Space(#96·#98) 변경 0.

## 커밋
- `5203b1f` PC 총괄: 내가 띄운 시뮬만
- `5f443be` 폰 총괄도 같은 판정(`mayStop` 에서 `phone ||` 제거)

## 시험(실제 실행)
- PC 재현 `simtab.test.tsx`: 총괄 + IDLE 슬롯(담당 없음)만 / 남이 띄운 시뮬만 → STOP·Space 고르기 없음. 고치기 전 2건 실패 → 고친 뒤 통과.
- 폰 재현 `drive.test.tsx` «폰 총괄 + IDLE 시뮬 슬롯만 …»: 폰 총괄 + 실기 1 + IDLE 슬롯 1(대상 경로) / IDLE 슬롯 + 남이 띄운 시뮬(고르기 경로) → STOP·Space 없음, 내 시뮬 떠 있음 → STOP 있음, 폰 운영자(박OO) → STOP 있음·Space 로 r7 정지. **고치기 전 실패(STOP 남음) → 고친 뒤 통과** 확인.
- `drive.test.tsx` 총괄 SIM 고정값의 담당을 `''`(=IDLE 슬롯 모양) → 총괄 본인으로(떠 있는 시뮬을 뜻하던 시험).
- 기존 시험이 덮는 것: 띄우는 중 STOP(#96 P1 누름·Space), 떠 있음 STOP(#94), 마지막 시뮬 끝내기 뒤 STOP 0(#96 P2), 운영자 STOP 그대로.
- 집중 drive·simtab·simkeys·shell 221/221, `tsc --noEmit` 통과, web 전체 17파일 659/659(MemAvailable ≥ 2.5GB 조건으로 1회).
- 화면(로컬 `runs/admin-idle-stop/`, 저장소 밖): PC 총괄 «시뮬» 탭 + IDLE 슬롯 → STOP 없음, 폰(390×844) 총괄 «로봇 연결» + 실기 1 + IDLE 슬롯 → 머리줄 STOP 없음. 둘 다 로컬 QA 진입점(커밋 안 함, 서버 없음 — 연결 끊김 띠가 보이는 것은 그 때문).

## 넓힘 3 — 끝낸 시뮬 슬롯을 로봇 목록에서 빼기(`a73da0c`)
- 근거: ADR-003 §7 ③ «끝내기 → 로봇 빠짐». 미리보기 e0fed19 실관측 — 끝낸 뒤 PC 로봇 탭에 IDLE 시뮬 슬롯 행(sim=true, 담당 없음) 1개가 남음. 서버가 슬롯 행을 남기는 것은 설계 → 웹에서만 처리.
- 고침: `fake.ts` 에 뿌리 판정 하나 `idleSim = sim && 담당 없음`. `App.tsx` 의 공용 `pool`(PC 로봇 목록·폰 «내 로봇»·기록·시나리오 고르기 — 모두 이 값)에서 뺀다. STOP 판정 `mayStop` 도 같은 `idleSim` 을 쓴다(목록과 STOP 후보가 같은 판정). **담당 없는 실기 로봇은 그대로 보임.** 지도 탭(`maps.tsx`)은 로봇 표시가 없어 해당 없음.
- 시험(실제 실행): PC `simtab.test.tsx` «총괄 로봇 탭: IDLE 시뮬 슬롯…» — [실기(담당 있음), 실기(담당 없음), IDLE 슬롯, 내 시뮬] → 목록 `Go2-7, Go2-9, 시뮬-1`. 폰 `drive.test.tsx` «폰 총괄 «내 로봇»…» — [실기, IDLE 슬롯, 내 시뮬] → 카드 `시뮬 로봇 1` 만. **둘 다 고치기 전 실패(슬롯이 목록에 남음) → 고친 뒤 통과.** 집중 drive·simtab 175/175, `tsc --noEmit` 통과, web 전체 17파일 661/661(MemAvailable ≥ 2.5GB 조건으로 1회).
- 화면(로컬 `runs/admin-idle-stop/pc-fleet-idle-slot-hidden.png`, 저장소 밖): 총괄 PC 로봇 탭 + 위 4대 → 끝낸 슬롯 행 없음, 담당 없는 실기·내 시뮬 보임. 로컬 QA 진입점(커밋 안 함, 서버 없음 — 연결 끊김 띠는 그 때문).
- 남은 권고(이번에 안 고침): 관제 요약 칸 «전체» 수(`robots_total`)는 서버 대시보드 값이라 IDLE 슬롯을 셀 수 있음. 설정 탭 로봇 관리 표(`settings.tsx`, 서버 목록 직접)는 등록 관리 화면이라 그대로 둠.

## 미검증
- 실서버·미리보기·실폰 재현은 하지 않음.
- FAST 규칙상 STOP 판정 변경 → 두 모델 검토 각 1회 대상.

## 되돌림
`git revert a73da0c 5f443be 5203b1f`
