author: alonsoquezadar
body:
## Summary

The live demo now runs on the shape of a real CEN day (14 Aug 2026), and Jimmy, the monitor, reads the grid every simulated hour. Jury attacks are still resolved live, now by the faster decider. Spec and accepted deviations: `docs/real-day-contract.md`.

```diff
 LiveSession (backend/live/engine.py)
-  scenario = demo_scenario.json                    # synthetic day
+  scenario = scenario_path()                       # GRIDPILOT_SCENARIO: real-day (default) | synthetic
+                                                   #   real_day_scenario.json, built by scripts/build_real_day_scenario.py
   _clock_loop (1 Hz)
-    every 3 sim hours: one of 5 canned sentences
+    every sim hour + when severity rises: monitor.assess()      # metrics from the solution, by code
+      background call, never awaited by the clock: GRIDPILOT_MODEL_MONITOR (gemini-3.5-flash-lite, ~0.7 s)
+      failed / late answer -> note worded by code from the grid now, labelled timeout | error | stale
   disrupt()
-    decider: gemini-4-argon, medium thinking (7-20 s, often > 12 s timeout)
+    decider: gemini-3.8-flash, low thinking (~4.3 s); options still from HiGHS + independent validator
```

What is real and what is not:

| Field | Provenance |
|---|---|
| Hourly system demand | derived: sum of measured bus withdrawals, SIP `demanda-real-estimada` 2026-08-14 |
| Solar / wind hourly shape per zone | derived: real capacity factor shape, amplitude normalised to scenario capacity |
| Zone shares of demand | assumption: bus→zone map covers 78.2 % of energy (< 99 %), so synthetic shares |
| Topology, line limits, capacities, costs, households_per_mw | synthetic, unchanged |

The screen shows "Día real CEN · 14-ago-2026 · perfil escalado" and labels the AI as "Gemini"; every answer's badge names the model that produced it.

## Evidence

- **Before:** the hourly note was canned text with no model call. The public backend served the synthetic day. 108 of the 111 offline incident files still held answers from the earlier synthetic recording.
  **After:**
  - Tests: `pytest`: 303 passed, 1 xfailed (bus-map coverage below 99 %, declared). `npm run build` passes.
  - Gates (`tests/test_real_day_scenario.py`): the baseline has no unserved energy; L2 is at 100 % from 10:00 to 16:00 with midday solar curtailment; the Centro peak falls at 20:00; the outages of `gas_centro` at 18:00 and `L3` at 19:00 each leave unserved load and get 2 validated options.
  - Live smoke through HTTP and SSE:
    - Monitor notes come from `gemini-3.5-flash-lite`, `ok`, in 0.6–1.0 s.
    - Jimmy turns to alert 0.8 s after a jury attack.
    - The largest gap between 1 Hz clock ticks is 1.03 s.
  - Re-recorded with real Gemini:
    - `demo-stream.jsonl` holds 11 monitor notes, all `ok`, and decisions by `gemini-4-argon`, `ok`.
    - All 111 library files were answered by `gemini-4-argon`, `ok`, on the real day.
  - Decider benchmark on the real day, 2 incidents each:

    | Decider | Latency | Options |
    |---|---|---|
    | `gemini-3.8-flash`, low | 4.3 s / 4.2 s | valid |
    | `gemini-4-argon`, medium | 11.8 s / 20.2 s | valid |

  - Independent review (Codex `gpt-6-astra`): no blockers. Five should-fix items were fixed in `4f40b0e`. One remains open: a timed-out model call keeps its worker thread until the HTTP timeouts end.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

`GRIDPILOT_SCENARIO=synthetic` brings back the old day, and `GRIDPILOT_MODEL_DECIDER=gemini-4-argon` with `GRIDPILOT_DECIDER_THINKING=medium` brings back the old decider. Neither needs a code change. The data commits replace recordings, and git history keeps the previous ones.

**Blast Radius:** demo

- Every live session, the offline fallback (`demo-stream.jsonl`, `frontend/public/incidents/`) and the agent panel change.
- The native v2 API (`backend/main.py`) is untouched.
- Anyone presenting must say "the shape of a real CEN day, scaled to our 5-node network", not "real data".

body:
A VK phone response that failed schema validation left registration locked. Support direct-link entry without a catalogue listing: retrieve a signed phone when available, prefill unsupported responses only as editable contacts, and allow manual contact entry with administrator approval. Unverified contacts never become identity proof, discover/link existing accounts, or reserve another user's number; Telegram and browser VK ID keep their existing requirements.

Validate calendar dates from 1900 through today on client and server, including profile and application edits. Guard duplicate submissions and stale directory responses, reject invalid cells and blank fields, offer VK entry from web login and a fresh launch link for expired native credentials. Remove submitted validation values from browser diagnostics. Upgrade development-only filelock to 4.2.4 for three newly reported vulnerabilities. No database migration or secret rotation is required.

Validation: 629 local tests passed across the complete run and rerun of 33 tests whose fixtures were initially blocked by Windows TEMP permissions; one Windows symlink test skipped. Eight native DOM scenarios passed, including unsupported phone proof, manual registration, invalid dates and account linking. An isolated real-browser flow reached pending approval; mobile content stayed within the viewport. GitHub runs the full Linux suite, CodeQL, Bandit and dependency audit.

author: snapotter-hq
body:
Single-file `registerSvgToRasterRoute` (`apps/api/src/routes/tools/svg-to-raster.ts`) reads only `file` and `settings` from the multipart stream. Only `/batch` reads and validates `clientJobId`. The base `/api/v1/tools/image/svg-to-raster` entry in `apps/api/src/openapi.yaml` omitted `clientJobId`, but its two conversion presets (`/api/v1/tools/image/svg-to-png` and `/api/v1/tools/image/svg-to-jpg`) still listed the field in `openapi.yaml` and all 20 translated specs, so callers sending `clientJobId` never received progress frames on that channel and never hit the #1691 `400` validation gate on a malformed value.

## What changed

author: clement-salin
body:
## Pourquoi

L'étape finale du `Dockerfile` lance `node dist-server/main.js`. npm et yarn n'y servent à rien, mais leurs composants internes (`brace-expansion`, `pacote`, `sigstore`, `picomatch`, `ip-address`…) portaient **10 failles HIGH** relevées par Trivy sur l'image en production.

## Ce qui change

- `Dockerfile`, étape d'exécution : `apk upgrade` puis suppression de npm, npx et yarn.
- Rien d'autre : le code, les dépendances et le `package-lock.json` ne bougent pas.

## Vérifié

- Image construite pour `linux/amd64`, scannée avec Trivy : **10 failles HIGH → 0**.
- `npm audit` : 0 faille. Typecheck et 133 tests : OK.
- Déjà déployée à la main sur le VPS le 25/10 (site en 200, base intacte, 23 enregistrements) ; l'ancienne image est gardée sous `languages:previous`.

## À savoir avant de fusionner

La fusion déclenche le déploiement par la CI. Elle utilisera pour la première fois le script `receive-deploy.sh` durci, installé sur le VPS le 25/10 : si le format de l'archive de la CI surprenait ce script, le déploiement s'arrêterait avec « Archive refusée » (aucune coupure, l'image en ligne resterait la même). À surveiller dans le journal du workflow.

Sans cette PR, le prochain déploiement par la CI reconstruirait l'image avec npm et ses 10 failles.

body:
Part of #9: core options for the libretro core.

## Options

| Option | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Render Scale (`hakux_render_scale`) | 1x to 4x | 1x |
| Screen Format (`hakux_screen_format`) | Normal (4:3), Widescreen (16:9), Letterbox | Normal |
| Language (`hakux_language`) | Auto (RetroArch's), or one of the Xbox's nine | Auto |
| Video Region (`hakux_video_region`) | Auto (the game's), NTSC-M, NTSC-J, PAL | Auto |

- The core reads these once, before the console boots. A change during the game takes effect when the game starts next, and RetroArch shows a message saying so.
- Widescreen makes RetroArch show a 4:3-sized frame at 16:9, through "core provided" aspect.
- PAL60 is now always set, as RetroArch runs at 59.94 Hz: European games that offer 60 Hz use it. NTSC games ignore it. 480p, 720p and 1080i stay off, as before.
- FXAA and the picture's shape stay with RetroArch: its shaders and its aspect setting. SGSR is not offered. `LIBRETRO_SPEC.md` section 10 records this.

## Changes

- `native/libretro/options.c` (new) declares the options: v2 where the frontend has it, and the legacy variables otherwise.
- `native/kernel/ex.c` gains `nc_kernel_set_av_region`; the EEPROM log line now includes the AV region. The Android app and the standalone don't call it, so they behave as before.
- `native/libretro/video.c` reports a 16:9 aspect for widescreen.
- The test harness supports the v2 options, a mid-run change and RetroArch's language. `check.py` checks:
  - the defaults with auto language;
  - every option set;
  - an unknown value falling back to its default;
  - the mid-game message.
- The README, Linux README, changelog (Unreleased), spec and handoff notes are updated.

## Testing

- Container: 5/5 CTest groups pass, including the new options checks.
- Nova, Burnout 3 through `runemu.sh`:
  - At 2x, widescreen and French, the console got video flags `00410000`, AV region NTSC-M (auto) and language 4. The game rendered at 1280x960 and was shown at 16:9, at full speed: 59.9 new frames per second, with RetroArch's `retro_run` taking 1.9 ms.
  - On the defaults, the console settings and frames were as before (1x, 4:3, English, NTSC-M, 59.9 fps), apart from the PAL60 flag.
  - RetroArch saved all four `hakux_*` keys to its core options file at quit.
- On the panel, the owner saw Burnout 3 draw in widescreen.
- Not checked: whether its text turned French. The logs only show the language the console reported to the game.

author: 0ssol1620-byte
body:
Security dependency bump, lockfile-only: **next 16.3.8 → 16.4.1** in `apps/web`.

## Why
Two CRITICAL Next.js advisories were published on 2026-10-22:
- GHSA-673q-mjm6-r5xr — unauthenticated remote code execution in `use cache` functions returning typed arrays; affects next 16.0.0–16.4.0, patched in 16.4.1.
- GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw — unauthenticated remote code execution in the Image Optimization API (upstream `sharp` memory bug on glibc Linux); affects next ≤ 15.5.27 and 16.0.0–16.4.0; the workaround is sharp ≥ 0.35.5. This tree already resolves sharp 0.35.5, so only the first advisory was open here.

The Security workflow on trunk has reported `next 16.3.8` under these advisories (Trivy, web image) on every run since 2026-10-19T17:10Z, including the scheduled main run and the Dependabot runs. Dependabot PR #106 (16.3.6 → 16.3.8) is superseded by this bump.

## What changed
- `apps/web/package.json`: `"next": "16.4.1"` (was `16.3.8`). `eslint-config-next` stays at 16.3.8: it has no peer dependency on `next` (peers are eslint and typescript only).
- `pnpm-lock.yaml`: produced by `pnpm update next@16.4.1 --lockfile-only --ignore-scripts` from `apps/web` in a clean worktree with no `node_modules` (nothing was installed). Besides `next@16.4.1` and its `@next/*` platform packages, the resolver refreshed a few floating transitive ranges within their declared semver (rollup 4.62.3 → 4.65.0, esbuild 0.28.2 added, picomatch 4.0.5 → 4.0.7, caniuse-lite, nanoid 3.3.18 → 3.3.20, style-mod, legacy-javascript, baseline-browser-mapping). No source file changed.

## What to check
- CI workflow (frozen install, typecheck, vitest, python-core): must be green at the merged head.
- Security workflow: the `next` CRITICAL rows on the web image should disappear; the remaining dependency-audit failures (pillow 12.3.0, pypdf 6.19.0, certifi, …) are pre-existing and have their own Dependabot PRs (#124, #128, #123). They are not fixed here.

## Founder veto
None: no copy, no claim, no pricing, legal or consent wording changed.

## Founder hands
- Core v2 production is the Vercel project `tavonel-product-core-v2`, which is **not git-linked**: merging this to trunk deploys nothing. The production deployment (`dpl_ARpeXMfVcWmjfje6DNDCAwAGyV35`, 2026-09-30) is redeployed only by the founder's CLI deploy of the merged trunk (FH-06). That deploy is what removes the exposure in production.
- The Foundation site (tavonel.com, next 15.5.24 + sharp 0.35.4) is affected by GHSA-2464-fhr4-w9xw and is handled in a separate Foundation PR (next 15.5.28).

**Fixed:** The standalone `vmrxd` v0.1.2 could sometimes get stuck at height 1 with 0 peers despite successful temporary seed handshakes. Keep existing VMRX mainnet bootstrap candidates as persistent priority connections **only** for normal online mainnet first launch without operator-supplied peer flags. No genesis/reward/PoW/difficulty changes, no Monero seeds, no new address format, and no changes to explicit priority/exclusive peer flags, offline mode, testnet or stagenet.

### Evidence
- [Original failing Windows seed-only first boot](https://github.com/ati1993de/vmrx-core/actions/runs/40184857431): 0 peers and height 1 for 5 minutes.
- [Original passing Windows seed-only first boot](https://github.com/ati1993de/vmrx-core/actions/runs/40185038433): 2 peers, height 1221, all 6 canonical historical chain hashes valid.
- [Candidate's standalone first boot](https://github.com/ati1993de/vmrx-core/actions/runs/40185617859): passed.

### Final v0.1.3 release gates
- Native rebuilt `vmrxd.exe` and `vmrxd` both self-identify as **VMRX Core v0.1.3**.
- Windows CI: correct genesis, exact 200,000 VMRX founder-premine block 1, six fixed historical hashes and live P2P mainnet full-sync, official embedded Windows logo, required DLL dependencies, **two independent default bootstrap / fresh-database tests**.
- Linux CI: freshly compiled binary, real P2P full sync and six fixed hashes; produce new v0.1.3 archive (not stale v0.1.2 executable).
- Release publishing workflow hard-gates on **two green exact-source-SHA GitHub Actions runs**, verifies CI artifacts and SHA256SUMS, publishes official tag v0.1.3 only once, never modifies v0.1.2.
- No Windrose production upgrade, no GUI bundle update; Node & Miner v0.1.2 still includes the older official Core v0.1.2 until separately rebuilt and verified.

**DO NOT MERGE until final dual-platform CI is green.** Wallet seed recovery and spend remain unverified; v0.1.3 is a non-consensus P2P maintenance release.

author: fabiencouprie
body:
La base d'empreintes surveillait **72 composants isolés**, nourris d'un son d'essai. Un défaut né de la **rencontre** de deux composants lui était invisible — et c'est exactement ce qui est arrivé cette semaine : « Étaler sur le clavier » rendait **cent trente cents** de faux avec tous les nœuds annonçant « Terminé » et quatre gardes au vert. L'aperçu de la banque avait changé de son, et personne ne l'écoutait.

```bash
npm run test:empreintes-exemples
EXEMPLE=un-son-projete-en-microtonal npm run test:empreintes-exemples
ECRIRE_EMPREINTES_EXEMPLES=1 npm run test:empreintes-exemples
```

# Ce qu'il surveille

**Tout nœud qui produit de l'audio expose son aperçu en WAV**, et pas seulement « Sortie audio ». Relevé en ouvrant l'exemple microtonal : **cinq lecteurs**, là où j'en attendais deux. Cela referme le trou des huit exemples sur dix-neuf dont l'audio n'atteint aucun nœud de sortie.

| | |
|---|---|
| exemples surveillés | **13**, pour **62 empreintes** |
| variable, donc hors surveillance | 1 — `paulstretch` et un réseau DDSP |
| hors de portée | 5 — ils attendent un fichier de l'utilisateur, règle **mécanique** qui lit le graphe |
| défauts connus écartés | **0** |

# Il mesure son propre bruit avant de surveiller

Un premier jet comparait à la neuvième décimale : relancé sans qu'une ligne ait changé, il annonçait **quinze écarts**. Deux espèces qu'il fallait séparer plutôt que noyer sous une précision choisie au hasard — le bruit flottant (`0,051016711` contre `0,051016712`) et la vraie variabilité, `paulstretch` à 5 %, un réseau DDSP à 2 %.

L'établissement joue donc chaque exemple **trois fois**, avec une marge : pour être surveillé à un pour cent, un exemple doit se reproduire à un demi.

## Le seuil de crête raconte sa propre leçon

Je l'avais desserré à 5 % pour un exemple dont la crête sautait. Cet exemple a été écarté depuis, pour un défaut qui lui est propre. **La raison de desserrer avait disparu, le desserrage était resté.**

Mesuré en replantant le défaut des cent trente cents :

```
etale / ecoute-banque   (0,004 % d'efficace, 6,529 % de crête, 0,017 demi-ton de couleur)
```

À 5 %, le garde attrapait son défaut fondateur **avec un point et demi de marge, par chance de seuil**. À 1 %, avec un facteur six.

## Et le centroïde a été ajouté pour une raison fausse

Je le croyais capable de suivre la hauteur là où le niveau n'en dit rien. Mesuré : il bouge de **dix-sept millièmes de demi-ton** sur ce défaut, six fois moins que son seuil. Un centroïde est une brillance *globale*, pas une hauteur, et l'aperçu est une cloche au spectre large.

**Il reste, et le fichier écrit que ma raison était fausse** : il voit un filtre déplacé ou un rééchantillonnage, que le niveau ne voit pas.

# Le lecteur de WAV est sorti du navigateur

Il vivait dans le `page.evaluate` qui s'en sert, donc **hors d'atteinte de tout cas**. Or un analyseur qui ne lirait qu'une partie des données rendrait un chiffre **stable et insensible** — un faux vert parfait, qui ne tomberait jamais.

`audio/empreinte-wav.ts` porte **onze cas** ; défaut planté sur un lecteur paresseux, **quatre tombent**. Il lit les trois profondeurs, dont les vingt-quatre bits qui sont le défaut de l'application, et parcourt les morceaux au lieu de sauter à un décalage fixe : un WAV d'Attic porte un `LIST`/`INFO` avant ses données.

**Deux attentes fixes remplacées par des conditions.** Un run est fini quand plus aucun nœud n'est en attente ni en cours, non après trente-huit secondes. Et les aperçus se posent *après* le statut, pas tous ensemble : une attente d'une seconde et demie relevait six lecteurs sur `canon-de-proportions` à une passe et huit à la suivante.

# Le défaut qu'il a trouvé, et qui est réparé ici même

« Boîte à groove » **déclarait sa graine et ne l'honorait pas** : `0.172357839` puis `0.170609203` sur deux passes du banc, pendant que son message annonçait « graine 4242 ».

**La cause, instrumentée plutôt que devinée** : **441 001 appels à `Math.random` pendant un seul rendu**, tous dans Tone — 441 000 pour remplir le tampon de bruit blanc, un pour choisir le **décalage de départ** de la frappe dans ce tampon. Deux voix sur onze ; Tone n'expose aucune graine.

**Deux de mes conclusions étaient fausses en chemin.** Mon relevé des voix cherchait `"noise"` quand le dépôt écrit `"bruit"`, et ma sonde directe annonçait zéro appel parce que les deux frappes que je lui avais données n'étaient pas des voix à bruit. J'ai failli livrer un correctif dont je ne savais pas expliquer l'effet.

**Après réparation** : graine 4242 rend `0.171573496` **trois fois sur trois**, graine 7 rend `0.154415729`.

## L'exception est déclarée et tenue, non tolérée

`hasard-couverture.test.ts` interdit de remplacer `Math.random`, et sa raison est écrite : un générateur l'avait fait **sans restaurer**, et toute l'application tirait ensuite sur lui.

Une quatrième catégorie porte l'unique entrée, avec les deux voies écartées et pourquoi, et vient avec **deux gardes neufs** :

- une **exigence structurelle** — un fichier déclaré borné restaure dans un `finally` ;
- `audio/hasard-borne.test.ts`, qui éprouve la restauration **après une exception**, le chemin exact par lequel la faute d'origine était arrivée.

Défaut planté, restauration déplacée hors du filet : **les deux tombent**.

Le son de Tone est conservé à l'identique. Réécrire les deux voix avec notre propre bruit respectait le garde sans exception, mais déplaçait toutes les empreintes d'un rendu contenant une batterie, pour un changement que personne n'entend.

# Vérification

`npx tsc -b` propre. Passe unitaire verte : **618 fichiers, 9 455 cas**. Tables régénérées.

Défaut des cent trente cents replanté : le garde tombe sur les deux nœuds qui portent l'aperçu de la banque. Base rétablie après réparation : `groove-etire-et-tourne` y revient, **stable**.

body:
## O que muda

**1. Os 10 corvos conversam de verdade.** Novo comando `dotcrow civ conversar` (e `/civ` dentro do modo terminal). Cada um dos 10 corvos fala com **o próprio modelo** (metade `gpt-5-nano`, metade `claude-haiku-5-5`), do jeito da sua personalidade e especialidade, respondendo ao que os outros disseram.
- Uma fala a cada 20 s (`--intervalo`), com tema livre ou `--tema`.
- O dono escreve no meio e o bando responde; chamar um corvo pelo nome faz ele responder (com ou sem acento).
- Enter vazio pede a próxima fala na hora; `pare` ou Ctrl+C encerra e mostra quantas chamadas foram feitas.
- Todos falam: quem está há mais tempo calado fala antes, e dois corvos não ficam só um respondendo ao outro.
- Se o modelo de um corvo falhar ou recusar, ele fala com o modelo do outro provedor. Sem chave de um provedor, o corvo usa um modelo que tem chave (com aviso).
- O bando agora fica salvo (`civilizacao.json`) e é sempre o mesmo. `dotcrow civ modelo <corvo> <provedor:modelo>` troca o modelo de um corvo; `dotcrow civ nova` faz outra Gênese.

**2. Recusa da Anthropic não para mais a tarefa.** Quando o Claude devolve `stop_reason: refusal` (filtro de segurança da Anthropic), o DotCrow mostrava "pedido inválido: o modelo recusou este pedido" e parava tudo. Agora isso vira `ProviderError::Refused`: o roteador passa para o próximo provedor da fila (ex.: OpenAI), sem castigo para o Claude. Vale também para recusa da OpenAI e bloqueio do Gemini, e para recusa no meio do streaming.

## Por quê

No Termux, os corvos não conversavam entre si (só existia o desenho da Gênese) e várias tarefas paravam com "pedido recusado por anthropic".

## Como testar

```bash
cargo test --workspace
dotcrow civ
dotcrow civ conversar --tema música
dotcrow civ modelo Nyx anthropic:claude-haiku-5-5
```

No modo terminal: `/civ` (ou `/civ música`), escreva para falar com o bando, `pare` encerra.

## Checklist

- [x] `cargo fmt --all`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` e `cargo test` passam (174 testes)
- [ ] Commits assinados com `git commit -s` (feitos pela interface web)
- [x] Testes novos cobrem o comportamento novo (vez de falar, nomes sem acento, bando salvo, troca de modelo, recusa → próximo provedor)
- [x] Documentação atualizada (README)
- [x] Nenhuma chave, senha ou dado pessoal no código, nos testes ou nos logs

author: fratercem-design
body:
## What

In `public/sw.js`, `staleWhileRevalidate()` called `event.waitUntil(...)`, but `event` is only in scope inside the `fetch` listener. When an image was already in the cache and younger than 7 days, that line threw `ReferenceError: event is not defined`. The promise given to `respondWith()` then rejected, and the browser treated the image request as a network error.

The worker is only registered from the live-notifications subscribe form (`src/components/live/subscribe-form.tsx`), so the people affected are visitors who turned on stream alerts. For them, cached images failed to load on repeat visits.

## Change

- The fetch event is now passed into `staleWhileRevalidate`, which uses it for `waitUntil`.
- `CACHE_VERSION` goes from `v3` to `v4`, so installed workers drop their old caches. This also clears out any card art cached from before the text-free repaint in #368.

`cacheFirst` and `networkFirst` don't use `event` and are unchanged.

## Verified

I ran both versions of the worker in a Node `vm` sandbox with stubbed `caches` and `fetch`, sending a request for an already-cached image:
- old: `FAILED: event is not defined`
- new: serves the cached image, then the background fetch replaces it in the cache

`node --check` and `eslint public/sw.js` both pass.

author: yukikotani231
body:
Before: Bastio programs and libraries could be built for x86-64, AArch64 and the C backend only; nothing ran in a browser or Node.js.

After: `bastioc1 --arch wasm32 -o prog.wasm file.bastio` writes a WebAssembly module from the IR (`stage1/wasm.bastio`). Hosted programs and `export fn` libraries build; a module imports `bastio.print` and `bastio.putc` and exports `memory`, `bst_alloc`, `bst_free`, `main` and every `export fn`.

What changed:
- Each IR register is an `i64` local; control flow is one `loop` with a `br_table` over label segments; frames, string literals and a size-class allocator live in one linear memory. Results of more than two words go through an extra last parameter (the caller's frame slot).
- The AArch64 pass pipeline is factored into `a64_passes` and shared (no behaviour change there).
- `ROADMAP.md` gets a "Beyond systems programming" section (wasm, HTTP) and the Scope line is updated; `docs/ir.md` and `docs/trusted-base.md` describe the backend.
- CI: `tests/wasm.sh` (every `tests/pass` and `bench` program the backend covers, run under Node.js, compared with the C backend's output and exit status) and `tests/wasm_lib.sh` (the lines, base64 and utf8 example libraries called from JavaScript).

How it was checked: `tests/wasm.sh` reports 233 programs identical to the C backend, 31 skipped (device, kernel, lock and host-call operations), 0 failed. `tests/ci.sh` passes except the local-only comparison against a stale `../bastios` checkout.

Trusted base: the module's only unchecked code is its runtime (allocator, free, `Vec` growth), about 280 lines of Bastio that emit wasm; `--trusted-base` does not count it yet. stage0 is untouched.

What is left: host calls (arguments, files, stdin), a typed JavaScript shell for `Bytes` and structs, and a browser demo.

author: abdullah-a8
body:
## Summary

pq's timing tests failed now and then on a loaded machine, so I stress-tested them. With 4 copies of `tests/clipboard.rs` running in parallel, 4 of 16 runs failed across three tests:
- `a_clipboard_read_whose_output_stays_open_does_not_hold_the_helper`
- `a_clipboard_tool_left_serving_the_selection_does_not_hold_pq_output_open`
- `a_copy_that_lands_late_and_hangs_is_still_cleared`

In each case pq kept its bounds. For example, the clear helper ends within its 1 s delay plus the 5 s clipboard-command limit. The tests' wall-clock margins of 3–10 s were too tight once the machine was loaded, and on their own they reached 13 s of a 15 s budget.

- **Shared timing constants:** what a fake stalls, hangs or lingers for is one constant, `STALL` (30 s). Each test allows `PATIENCE` (15 s) where it used 3–10 s. A run that finishes within that still shows pq didn't wait for the fake. Waits for something that should happen promptly return as soon as it does, so passing tests aren't slower.
- **Fake pass-cli:** it now waits in 0.1 s steps. When pq kills a stalled call (a version check or a slow vault), no 30 s `sleep` is left behind holding pipes open. The version test `a_stalled_version_check_does_not_hold_up_a_vault_error` once took the stall's full 30 s. Sol's review found no race in pq behind that: aborting the check kills `pass-cli`, and the test passed 64 more runs at eight-way concurrency in 1.2–1.7 s. Such an orphan is the one way left for the harness to wait that long, so it's removed. The single 30 s run itself stays unexplained.

Real pq isn't affected: `pass-cli` is one process, which pq's kill-on-drop stops.

## Test plan

- [x] Stress after the change, 4–6 test binaries in parallel: `clipboard` 16/16 and 24/24, `version` 16/16, `session` 16/16. Before it, `clipboard` passed 12/16.
- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked`
- [ ] CI green

author: architect-moaaz
body:
Fourth Wave 0 PR, part 1 of the security hardening. Stacked on #7 (merge order #4 → #5 → #6 → #7 → this). Part 2 (staff logins with roles plus an audit trail, replacing `ADMIN_TOKEN`) follows as its own PR.

## Fixes
| Gap | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| **Session cookie** | `gc_uid` held the raw user id, so anyone with the id was that user. Logout only cleared the cookie. | `gc_session` holds a random token, and Redis maps its hash to the account. Logout deletes the key, so a replayed cookie is dead. Seller sessions use the same mechanism. |
| **Signup phone** | Anyone could sign up with any number and get a session. | Shoppers and sellers must enter the phone code before the account or store exists. A proven existing shopper number simply signs back in. |
| **Deal checkout** | Anyone with a deal id could set the delivery address. | Only the deal's shopper can (WhatsApp deals still use the private link). The delivery name shows only to them. |
| **Simulated payments** | `/api/checkout` and the checkout `simulate` action marked deals paid for free. | Removed, along with their buttons. Demo payments still go through the mock gateway until the production-cleanup PR. |
| **Rate limits** | None. | Code calls: 5/hour per number, 20/hour per IP. Code checks: 30 per 10 min per IP. Negotiations: 20/hour per shopper, 40 per IP. Haggles: 30 per 10 min per deal. Beacons: 120/min per IP. A Redis error lets requests through rather than locking everyone out. |

## Heads-up at deploy
- **Everyone is logged out once.** Old `gc_uid` cookies are ignored and cleared, and seller sessions moved to a new key. Shoppers and sellers log back in with a phone code.
- **Signup now needs Vobiz** to place the code call in production, as phone login already does.

## Also in this stack
Two CI fixes went into #5, and the stack is rebased on them:
- `next typegen` runs before `tsc`. A fresh checkout failed on `PageProps`.
- The Turborepo `build` task now waits for `typecheck`. Both write `.next/types`, and running them in parallel failed about one run in four.

## Tests
- **`security.test.ts`:**
  - session tokens don't contain the account id, and an ended session can't be replayed
  - the legacy cookie is ignored
  - signup only creates an account after the correct code, and a wrong code is rejected
  - an existing number signs back in
  - seller signup needs the code
  - checkout and the delivery name are owner-only
  - the simulate action is gone
  - rate limits return 429 with `Retry-After`, and the sixth code call per number is blocked
- **Totals:** core 17, db 2, web 51. Typecheck, lint and build pass, three clean runs in a row.
- **Browser test on the dev server (in-memory store):** demo item, name, number and consent → "Verify and find my deal" with the code from the server console → signed in, and the pending negotiation resumed. The cookie is httpOnly, logout clears it, `/api/checkout` returns 404, and there were no server errors.

body:
Closes [#700](https://github.com/grabartley/minecraft-dogs-unleashed/issues/700)

Fixes from the pre-release playtest.

## Costumes

- Every costume suit sheet now leaves the eye band of the head's front cell clear. Before, the hood rim covered the outer white of each eye on the husky, dachshund, beagle, golden retriever and dire wolf.
- The shiba inu's cheek cubes took the head's front cell, face opening and all, so they showed white squares. A new optional rig profile key, `suit_slots`, lets a bone take another slot's cells in a costume suit only. The shiba's cheeks take the neck's cells, which are solid cloth. Every other sheet (mud, harness, grey muzzle) and growth scaling and fitting still treat them as head. `ProjectedOverlays.suitTextureOf` and `SlotRegions.suitRegionsOf` carry the suit path, and `DogCostumeSuitLayer` uses it.
- The `dog-art` suit script follows `overlay_slots` so its renders match the game.

## Advancements

- Mush! is now Sleigh All Day. Its id stays `mush` so saved progress is kept.
- Sleigh All Day, Full Team and Show Dog now show progress: 100 to 1000 blocks, one to six dogs, and one to three tricks. Each keeps its old criterion name as the last step, and every step also accepts it, so progress saved under the old criterion still counts.
- The tab icon is the Dog Treat. Three advancements now use a mod item as their icon where one fits: Best Friend (food bowl), The Whole Pack (dog house) and Bad Hair Day (dog fur). The rest keep a vanilla item because it is what the player uses for that advancement.

## Docs

The PRD gains COSTUME-10, ADV-11 and ADV-12 and the new title. ADR 0006, the `add-dog-breed` skill and the `dog-art` skill describe `suit_slots` and the eye band rule. ADR 0006 also drops a stale line that said no overlay effect was registered yet.

## Tests

- `OverlayProjectorTest` projects every costume onto every rig and fails if a pupil or the texel either side of it is painted. It fails on the old creeper sheet for five rigs and passes now.
- `RigProfileTest`, `SlotRegionsTest` and `ProjectedOverlaysTest` cover `suit_slots`, including that other sheets keep the cheeks on the head. `DogTrickTest` checks Show Dog's steps.
- `SledGameTest` checks that three hitched dogs show Full Team at 3/6. `SledTravelledCriterionTest` and `SledTeamCriterionTest` check each advancement's steps.
- Suit projections register under their own texture id, so a sheet used as both a suit and an overlay can never swap textures.
- Unit, client and all 1180 gametests pass locally.

`DogCostumeSuitLayer` only changed which projection it asks for. It has no logic of its own to test outside a running client, so it relies on `ProjectedOverlaysTest` and the gametests.

author: thorstarlord
body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in, read-only bridge from the Campaign working context to reviewed, source-pinned architectural knowledge (PATH-1/T17). `campaign working-context` can attach one unmodified `context-for` result for one repository file, bound to a Campaign target. Without the new options the output is unchanged.

## Interface

```sh
sensemaking-skills campaign working-context --workspace WS --json \
  --knowledge-db INDEX.sqlite \
  --knowledge-repository ThorStarlord/sensemaking-skills \
  --knowledge-ref EXACT_INDEXED_SHA \
  --knowledge-repo ACTIVE_CHECKOUT \
  --knowledge-path src/sensemaking_skills/campaigns/execution.py
```

- The four `--knowledge-*` identity and index options are all-or-nothing. `--target-alias` is accepted only with them, and exactly one `--knowledge-path` is accepted in this release.
- The knowledge checkout's repository identity is derived with the same function target snapshots use. A public wrapper `repository_identity()` exposes it; `_identity()` is unchanged. The identity must match the Campaign target. `--knowledge-repository` is a caller-declared label and is not verified.

## Behaviour

- `reviewed_knowledge` is added only when requested. It contains the source identity (indexed ref, observed checkout HEAD, cleanliness), the target binding, `applicability` (`HISTORICAL`, `ALIGNED_TO_INDEXED_REVISION` or `NOT_ASSESSED`), the unmodified `context-for` envelope, `caveats`, and `semantic_truth_established: false` and `action_authorized: false`.
- Failures are explicit and never fall back to the unaugmented view. Usage errors exit 2. No bound target, identity mismatch, unindexed revision, invalid path, or non-Git checkout exits 4 with `CAMPAIGN_WORKSPACE_ERROR`.
- The Campaign payload is unchanged. Retrieved records do not select a responsibility or grant authority.

## Reviewed knowledge

Added to `.sensemaking/knowledge/architecture.json`: `component:campaign-working-context`, `component:campaign-knowledge-context`, `rule:campaign-knowledge-grants-no-authority`, and their relations. `knowledge-proposal-check` validates the file (49 claims, `SEMANTIC_KNOWLEDGE_PROPOSAL_VALID`). Before this change, the Campaign working-context code had no recorded owner.

## Verification

Construction-first policy: no unit or synthetic evidence tests were written or run.

- Static: `py_compile` and `ruff check --select E4,E7,E9,F` on the changed Campaign modules. Output is ASCII-only.
- Validators: docs currentness, strategic state, contract authority, repository structure, error boundaries and product boundary all passed.
- Manual CLI runs against a disposable Campaign bound to a worktree of `origin/main`, with a separately built index: the aligned happy path; a historical knowledge checkout; a dirty knowledge checkout; an identity mismatch; an unindexed revision; an invalid glob path; a missing target; partial options; `--target-alias` alone; two paths; a missing database; and a non-Git checkout. The default output and the Campaign part of the happy-path payload matched.

These are manual runs of the real CLI, not test results. CI runs on this PR; the owner's construction direction is to merge without waiting for it.

## Not established

Runtime correctness beyond the manual runs above, independent-agent usefulness, real-user benefit, and multi-file context (T18) are not established by this PR.

author: sebasssti4n
body:
## Summary

T4-4 creates `packages/agents`, where the brains of beings will live (ADR 0023), with the same
purity controls as the engine, and the navigation a brain plans with: Dijkstra and A* over the
window of its senses.

- **Package and controls.** `@open-origin/agents` imports only `@open-origin/engine`. It shares the
  engine's denied globals and GritQL plugins, with no exception file (no `Math`, `Map`, `JSON`, or key
  enumeration at all), and has its own import rule, purity scan, module-state rule, and tsconfig in
  the root `typecheck` chain.
- **Navigation.** `dijkstra(grid, start)`, `pathTo`, `aStar(grid, start, goal, bounds)`, and
  `octileMs`, over the senses' `edgeMs` contract: exact integer durations, a deterministic binary
  heap over typed arrays ordered by (g, index) and (f, h, index), each cell expanded once, every
  invalid input an `EngineError` with all its issues.

Written by a delegated writer in an isolated worktree, in parallel with T4-2 and T4-3 (independent
units with disjoint surfaces); the docs were integrated inline.

## Verification

- **`bun run check`:** exits 0 with 1,924 tests in 67 files.
- **Tests:** three independent oracles (an O(V²) Dijkstra, uniform-cost BFS, and every simple walk
  on 4 × 4 windows), 1,000 seeded random windows, admissibility and consistency of the heuristic on
  each, pinned ties and edges, every validation error.
- **Phase B:** 12 deliberate defects detected by the writer, 2 equivalent; 21 more killed by the
  verifier.

## 概要
Issue #57（2〜4人の可変人数）と #105（人数に応じた分担）をまとめて実装します。人数と分担は切り離せないので、1本にしています。

ユーザー判断（2026-10-25）：
- 人数は、P1がReadyを押した時点の**接続人数で自動**に決める（2〜4人）
- 分担は**操作定義から自動**で振り分ける。Minecraftは実機で確かめた3人だけ従来の専用画面を使い、2人・4人は定義から作った画面にする

決定の記録：`docs/decisions/2026-10-25-variable-players.md`

## 変更点
**ホスト（Rust）**
- 枠をP1〜P4にした（5台目は `full`・4004）。P1を含む2人以上でReadyできる。`required` は最低人数2だけを受け付ける
- Readyの時点の接続者を `game.participants` として、分担（`game.assigned`、枠名で配る）とともに終了まで固定する。再開で組み直さない
  - 参加者が切れたら一時停止し、戻るまで再開できない（自動復帰も同じ）。人数を変えるときは終了→準備→Ready
  - Readyの後に来た人の入力は送らず、その人が切れても止めない
- `game.fixedControls`：Minecraftを3人（P1〜P3）で遊ぶときだけ真。それ以外は `act:<操作ID>` だけを受け付ける
- 分担の案（`game.profile.assignment`）を、接続中の枠名で配る（P3が空いてP4がいる場合など）

**画面**
- PC：参加者4枠、分担の確認は人数分の列と「n人で、操作を分担！」。4人目は赤のキャラクター。定義から作る分担の説明文は3行で切る
- スマホ：参加者表示を4人分に、Readyボタンを「Ready・n人で操作を始める」に。後から来た人には「次の開始から参加します」

**分担の結果（Minecraft）**
| 人数 | P1 | P2 | P3 | P4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2 | 移動 | 視点・攻撃・使う・持ち物 | — | — |
| 3 | 移動・ホスト（専用画面） | 視点（専用画面） | アクション（専用画面） | — |
| 4 | 移動 | 視点 | 攻撃・使う | 持ち物 |

- `cargo build --release --locked`、`cargo test --release --locked`：ホスト31件＋プローブ3件成功

  - 2人・4人のMinecraftの分担と `act:` の送信、固定の操作名は送らない
  - 後から来た人の入力を送らず、その切断で止めない
  - 参加者が切れたら再開不可、戻ると再開可

author: angeles725
body:
## Summary
Makes the mnav class signal cheap in `nh find` for Spanish questions. mnav writes a flat posting view next to its ranker cache, and nh reads that view instead of decoding the 12 MB gob and scanning 50,746 haystacks per term.

**Where the time went (profiled):**
- The gob load took 70–78 ms: 34 ms to decode and 12 ms to build the names map.
- Ranking one question took 43–60 ms: about 31 ms of `strings.Contains` per term and about 19 ms of cold tf memo.

**What changes:**
- **The view.** `.mnav-cache/class-postings.bin` holds names, lengths, priors, the documents sorted by name (binary search, no names map) and a sorted term table of (doc ascending, tf) postings.
- **Term domain.** The build lists, per document, every term that can score, and keeps a posting only if `tf>0 && strings.Contains(haystack, t)`. That is exactly what today's scan finds, so a query term absent from the table provably has zero hits.
- **Integrity.** The header holds magic, version, payload length and a CRC-32. Offsets are bounds-checked, the file is written as temp + fsync + rename, and any mismatch reads as "no view", so nh uses the gob ranker.
- **Shared scoring.** Both rankers use `rankAll`'s scoring tail; only the scan differs.
- **No format bump.** `cacheFormat` stays at 2. mnav's `Cached()` and `Open()` write the view on a gob hit when it is missing. nh uses the new read-only `ReadView()`/`ReadCached()` and never writes.

## Evidence
- **Ranks identical.** `TestClassSignalViewMatchesGobReal` (opt-in, real data) gives the same full class list and scores, compared with `==`, on 200/200 golden questions. The golden top 5 is identical on 200/200 rows on 4.14 and on 4.15, and the floors are unchanged at 122/183 and 116/178.
- **Hermetic tests:**
  - query cases: multi-term, Spanish glossary, identifier token, no-hit term, a term that scores without being a substring, and a haystack substring absent from the table;
  - failure cases that fall back with identical results: truncated, header only, flipped payload byte, flipped key, wrong magic, wrong version, empty, stale stamp, missing.
- **Latency.** `nh find`, 50 Spanish rows × 3 runs:

  | | p50 | p95 |
  |---|---|---|
  | before | 553 ms | 1643 ms |
  | after | 408 ms | 1292 ms |
  | signal off | 404–420 ms | – |

## Test plan
- [x] `go test ./internal/nav/... ./internal/help/...`
- [x] real equivalence and golden checks on a scratch corpus copy
- [x] gofmt, staticcheck
- [x] RDD review acknowledged

author: jonasgrosch
body:
JPEG decoding was about 8% of Pagura's equal-weight cold time on the 80 bench jobs, roughly 1.7× hayro's zune-jpeg in the same units. This speeds up the native-plane decoder that painting uses. Output stays byte-identical.

## Changes
1. **Sample storage only where used.** `Frame::parse` allocated and zeroed full-size sample storage that native planes replaced immediately. That zeroing was about 4% of JPEG decoding on the bench scans.
2. **Vectorized blocks.**
   - **Transform:** the certified f32 IDCT ran mostly scalar. Its row-group loop kept runtime offsets, and overflow checks kept that index arithmetic checked. Coefficients are now scattered column by column during entropy decoding, so both passes are plain 8-lane networks with one transpose between them. Every lane keeps the network's operations and order, so the f32 values, the certificates and the f64 refinements are unchanged.
   - **Byte bounds:** they convert in one flat loop, and the refine mask is built with word operations.
   - **AC codes:** when the table lookup already holds the magnitude (code and magnitude fit in 12 bits), the coefficient is decoded straight from that entry. Before, it went through a token and magnitude arithmetic that did nothing for these codes.
   - **Bookkeeping:** a block's storage offsets are computed only for blocks that are actually stored.
3. **Planar YCbCr in exact integer lanes.**
   - **Arithmetic:** Table 13 rounding is exact in the byte domain: luma plus each chroma pair's rounded offset, with the reference's binary64 order only at green half ties. Rows convert that way in integer lanes; the leftover samples of a run convert as one padded group.
   - **Shared offsets:** the ordinary decoder's `transform::rgb` now shares `deferred::offset`, so its exhaustive test of every byte triple covers it.
   - **`floor_byte`:** it now serves only the transform bounds; AArch64 uses the shorter saturating `u32` form.

## Timing
M3 Pro, under the bench lock. Each variant is rotated per job, forward then reverse, keeping the best of the two runs. Base is `render/one-pass` 051cb5b71; ratios are geomeans. The machine stayed busy (load 5–20). The 62 jobs without JPEG run unchanged code and came out at 0.991× cold and 0.997× warm, so treat ±1–2% per category as noise.

| jobs | n | cold ÷ base | warm ÷ base | cold ÷ hayro, base → this PR | warm ÷ hayro, base → this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| image-heavy | 20 | 0.903 | 0.958 | 1.073 → 0.968 | 0.638 → 0.611 |
| mixed | 20 | 0.988 | 0.993 | 1.801 → 1.779 | 1.502 → 1.491 |
| text-heavy | 20 | 0.990 | 0.988 | 1.508 → 1.493 | 1.297 → 1.282 |
| vector-heavy | 20 | 0.985 | 1.001 | 1.689 → 1.663 | 1.632 → 1.634 |
| JPEG pages | 18 | 0.883 | 0.945 | 1.106 → 0.976 | 0.661 → 0.625 |
| **all 80** | 80 | **0.966** | **0.985** | **1.489 → 1.438** | **1.193 → 1.175** |

- **JPEG pages:** these are the 18 jobs on pages with a DCTDecode image. Besides image-heavy pages, they include 0045 p0 (text-heavy), 0266 p22 (vector-heavy) and 0418 p0 (mixed; a 512×389 image, unchanged within noise). The mixed row's movement is noise.
- **Noise correction:** counting only the JPEG jobs' gain gives 0.972 over 80 jobs. Instruction counts give 0.966 (below).
- **Per job:** cold 0.79–0.91× on the JPEG-heavy pages. Several now render faster than hayro: 0009 p1 72 dpi 0.81 → 0.67×, 0095 p1 150 dpi 0.78 → 0.65×, 0603 p0 72 dpi 1.00 → 0.80×. 0045 p0 improves 1.80 → 1.50× (72 dpi). The small JPEGs of 0266 and 0418 do not move.

## JPEG microbenchmark
Every DCTDecode image XObject on the 40 bench pages (18 images, mostly 2–11 MP scans), decoded as painting asks (`Layout::Native`), then every planar row converted to RGB. Timed under the lock as base, PR, PR, base, best per image:

| | base | this PR | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| decode | 62.2 ms | 47.0 ms | 0.754 |
| rows to RGB | 15.0 ms | 11.0 ms | 0.734 |
| both | 77.3 ms | 58.0 ms | 0.750 |

Per image, decode runs 0.66–0.82× on the scans and photos and 0.90–0.97× on 0266's 25-pixel thumbnails. Rows to RGB run 0.35–0.48× on 0045's photos and 0.79–0.96× on the scans, whose rows are mostly background fills.

## Instruction counts
- **Microbenchmark, native:** 1.35 G → 0.87 G per pass. Decode alone 1.07 G → 0.69 G.
- **Microbenchmark, WebAssembly** (wasmtime 49, SIMD128, overflow checks on as in `.cargo/config.toml`): 2.08 G → 1.67 G. Decode alone 1.56 G → 1.14 G; colour conversion about even.
- **Cold renders:** the 18 JPEG jobs take 0.857× the instructions (geomean); the other 62 jobs are unchanged, so 0.966 over 80 jobs. Per job (base → this PR):

| job | 72 dpi | 150 dpi |
|---|---|---|
| 0009 p0 | 330 M → 247 M (0.748) | 499 M → 416 M (0.833) |
| 0009 p1 | 237 M → 189 M (0.800) | 397 M → 350 M (0.882) |
| 0045 p0 | 238 M → 186 M (0.781) | 427 M → 375 M (0.878) |
| 0095 p0 | 193 M → 157 M (0.810) | 355 M → 318 M (0.896) |
| 0095 p1 | 163 M → 136 M (0.839) | 322 M → 295 M (0.918) |
| 0266 p22 | 0.997 | 0.998 |
| 0418 p0 | 0.985 | 0.991 |
| 0603 p0 | 442 M → 329 M (0.744) | 648 M → 536 M (0.827) |
| 0603 p1 | 441 M → 328 M (0.745) | 646 M → 535 M (0.829) |

## Byte identity
- **Decoded pixels:** identical for the 18 bench JPEGs and the 390 JPEGs on the 300-page catalogue sample (native planes, RGB rows and interleaved samples), natively and under wasmtime.
- **Renders:** identical, with the same failure sets as base, on the 80 bench jobs, all 1,246 fixture jobs (206 fail in both) and the 300 catalogue renders (12 fail in both).
- **Tests:** `pagura-image` tests pass (104), including the exhaustive Table 13 and transform certificate tests, plus a new test of rows for every chroma repeat and length 1–150 with half-tie pairs. Clippy is clean.

## Size
+355 / −290, net +65. The new 30-line row test replaces the removed 30-line `nearest_integer` test. The ~100 lines per point of 80-job gain allow roughly 340 lines here.

Tried and dropped: skipping availability checks far from a segment's end (about 1% of JPEG for 25 lines), and a widening multiply instead of the division in the colour offsets (−9% WebAssembly colour instructions, +3% native).

## Overlap
#152–#155 do not touch `pagura-image`.

author: ahmedmoh14314-code
body:
## What
WinTools now has a real window, and it speaks English and Arabic.

- **The window:** the old settings window becomes WinTools' own window, still a separate process, so WPF never loads into the resident host. It has five pages:
  - **Home:** whether WinTools is running (with a Start button), the trigger key, the four steps drawn (Drag, Press, Choose, Drop), and the families WinTools works with.
  - **How to use:** each step explained, then Convert, Tools and Actions, the keyboard, and "Show the welcome tour again".
  - **Features:** every command the wheel offers, grouped. It is built from the catalog, so it never lists what isn't there.
  - **Settings:** the existing settings, plus Language, Reset and the logs folder.
  - **About:** the version, the promise that originals are never changed, the third-party notices and the logs.
- **The first-run tour:** welcome, then how it works, then the choices (language, trigger, where new files go, start with Windows), then "WinTools is ready". It shows once and can be shown again from How to use. Choosing Arabic in the tour redraws it in Arabic at once.
- **Localization:** Core's `UiText` holds the English and Arabic tables (`Strings.en.json`, `Strings.ar.json`). A test keeps them complete and their placeholders equal. The language is a setting: Same as Windows, English or العربية.

author: umeranjum17
body:
## What

At 270 dp (33 columns) the phone-side history copy lost lines: #1051's own recipe
walked back through `MARK-1031 -> 1034` (2 lines) and `MARK-1158 -> 1171` /
`MARK-988 -> 1001` (12 lines each). This fixes the copy's own loss, the whole-screen
hole. Rows a Herdr frame never carried are a separate, still open problem, named
below and filed as its own follow-up.

Two changes:

- `patches/expo-libghostty+0.8.1.patch` (Android history mirror, `areaMoved`): a
  frame that moves more rows than the screen holds carries no row that lines up at
  a shift, so the copy can only say "the whole content area above the footer moved".
  It pushed that area only when *every* row above the footer had changed. On a
  33-column grid each line wraps, and a wrapped line's tail ("the rocks.") repeats
  down the screen, so one such tail sitting at the same row in both frames vetoed
  the push and a whole screen was dropped. The rule now weighs the area: when more
  rows above the fixed footer changed than held, that area moved off and is pushed.
- `.agents/skills/done-done-verify-pockit/features/terminalScrollLocalLab.sh`: the
  walk reader no longer reports `gap MARK-999 -> MARK-10080` when tesseract misreads
  `MARK-1000`; an id outside `MARK-1..LINES` is not one the pane printed. A row that
  is really missing still shows as a break, because nothing sits where it should be.

## Why

Captain's intent: at 270 dp scrolling back through a fullscreen Claude Code pane
must not lose lines, as it does not at 390/411 dp. Follow-up of #1040 and #1051.

## Intent

Fix the phone-side copy so no walked screen loses lines at 33 columns. Out of
scope: the 411 dp layout (checked for regression only), the PWA and iOS scrollback,
terminal styling.

## Live proof

Release APK built from the product head (`node perf/buildPrApk.mjs`, provenance
`revision 338c2845`, `dirty: false`; the later commit here touches only the verify
harness, which is not in the APK), owned 1080x2400 emulator started through the
memory gate, guarded Herdr lab from this checkout, canned `labStub.mjs` pane. The
brief's recipe per width:
`LINES=1200 STUB_LPS=100 WALK=30 DENSITY=<640|420> done-done run terminal-scroll-local`.

| run | 30 walked screens | Latest | whole screen ever lost? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 270 dp `20261025T131011Z-589e6dd7-77fedf` (this head, exit 0) | `MARK-1189` back to `MARK-999` | `MARK-1193..1200`, pill gone | no |
| 270 dp `20261025T130405Z-589e6dd7-8c2aca` (this head, exit 0) | `MARK-1189` back to `MARK-988` | `MARK-1193..1200`, pill gone | no |
| 270 dp `20261025T125033Z-338c2845-881c8f` | `MARK-1189` back to `MARK-976` | `MARK-1193..1200`, pill gone | no |
| 411 dp `20261025T124347Z-338c2845-40b700` | `MARK-1148` back to `MARK-609`, 36 rows a screen | `MARK-1166..1200`, pill gone | no (no regression) |

Before, the same recipe on main's APK (24 Oct run) lost a whole screen at a time:
`walk-04 1157..1180`, `walk-05 1151..1174`, `walk-28 982..1004`.

Frame replay of one real 33x28 capture (122 frames, MARK-1..1200 at 100 lines/s)
through the copy's own compare, ported from the patch: 44 rows dropped before
(four whole screens), 0 after, no repeated row.

## What this does and does not promise

Shipping claim, sealed at this head (`589e6dd`, run
`20261025T131011Z-589e6dd7-77fedf`, exit 0): copying across thirty walked screens
never loses a whole screen, and Latest returns to MARK-1200. That holds at 270 dp
and at 411 dp.

Not claimed: a walk can still lose two or three rows, and two of the four 270 dp
walks here do (2-3 rows of 1200 each, `walk-21` and `walk-25` skip one MARK row in
the sealed run). Those rows never reached the phone. The host side of that is filed
as its own follow-up, **mx-host-frame-rows1** (child of this task), not fixed here.

## What is still open

A Herdr frame that moves more rows than the screen holds leaves the phone without
the rows in between, and no copy can invent them. Measured twice at the same size:
the captured frame set never carried 12 of 1200 rows, and the 270 dp walks lose two
or three rows of 1200 - the same magnitude, against the 44 rows the copy itself used
to drop in one burst. Closing it means taking the missing rows from the pane's
scrollback (Herdr holds it) instead of inferring them from screens, or sending
frames small enough never to outrun a 33-column screen: a host and contract change,
the follow-up **mx-host-frame-rows1**, not this patch.

## Self-review of the shots (270 dp width; the terminal surface is always dark)

`walk-01.png`, `walk-10.png`, `walk-20.png`, `walk-30.png`, `after-latest.png`
(270 dp) and `walk-10.png`, `after-latest.png` (411 dp): no clipped or truncated
text, nothing overlapping, no ids or paths, agent name and every line plain. The
boxes before `auto mode on` are Claude's own status glyph missing from the terminal
font, unchanged here.

## Checks

outcome: Walking back through the 270 dp history of a Claude Code pane, each drag walks the view back and the screens overlap in consecutive MARK rows, and no whole screen is lost; proof.log logs any break in the numbers as a gap line, and Latest returns to the newest output (MARK-1200) with the pill gone, while two or three rows of a screen can still be missing because the drag outran the frame.
repro: the same drags back through the history on the previous build walk back with a break in the numbers of twelve rows at once, logged as a gap line, where this build keeps consecutive MARK rows - systematic-debugging used
proof: done-done-verify-pockit: `LINES=1200 STUB_LPS=100 WALK=30 DENSITY=640 done-done run terminal-scroll-local` on a 270 dp Android phone, release APK, owned emulator, private lab host: 30 drags back through the history, run 20261025T131011Z-589e6dd7-77fedf exit 0
evidence: evidence/20261025T131011Z-589e6dd7-77fedf/walk-01.png, evidence/20261025T131011Z-589e6dd7-77fedf/walk-10.png, evidence/20261025T131011Z-589e6dd7-77fedf/walk-20.png, evidence/20261025T131011Z-589e6dd7-77fedf/after-latest.png, evidence/20261025T131011Z-589e6dd7-77fedf/walk-21.png, evidence/20261025T131011Z-589e6dd7-77fedf/proof.log

author: kevinzhao
body:
## Problem
`restoredWorkflow` only backfilled `LastObservedAt` when it was 0. A Ref restored from a hand-edited `sessions.json` (or written before a clock step back) could carry a future `last_observed_at`; `Cleanup` uses the board's latest observation as the session's effective activity, so the idle TTL was held off until the wall clock passed that stamp.

## Change
`restoredWorkflow` treats a future `LastObservedAt` like a missing one and uses the restore time. One condition changed; the `Cleanup` side is untouched since live observations are stamped by the process clock.

## Tests
- New row in `TestRestoredWorkflow`: `last_observed_at = now+24h` is restored as now (the table already asserts `LastObservedAt == now` for kept rows).
- Mutation check: dropping the `> nowMs` clamp makes the row fail.
- `gofmt -l .` empty; `go test ./... -timeout 20m` green.

Closes #3657

Vale hits currently appear only as check annotations in the Files tab, which contributors overlook (see github.com/JabRef/user-documentation/pull/701). author: alessandroscrem
body:
## Obiettivo

Rimuovere dal percorso per-frame gli assert runtime sugli accessi alle risorse del `RenderContext`, mantenendo il RenderGraph responsabile della compilazione dell'ordine di esecuzione, delle dipendenze e dei lifetime delle risorse.

## Modifiche

- Rimossi da `RenderContext` i controlli runtime basati su `reads()` e `writes()`.
- Rimossa la chiamata a `begin_pass()` durante l'esecuzione dei pass.
- Rimossi `ResourceAccess` e i parametri/configurazioni usati esclusivamente da quei controlli.
- Mantenute le dichiarazioni `reads()` e `writes()` dei pass per compilare dipendenze e lifetime del RenderGraph.
- Mantenuto l'accesso dedicato al bind group `PbrMap`.
- Aggiornati i test di `MeshPass` per verificare il comportamento di clear/load degli attachment, senza dichiarare una copertura dei controlli runtime rimossi.

## Verifica

- CI: verificata dall'autore sull'ultima revisione.

## Nota architetturale

Le dichiarazioni `reads()` e `writes()` continuano a influenzare la compilazione del grafo, ma questa PR non verifica più a runtime che ogni pass acceda soltanto alle risorse dichiarate. Un eventuale contratto statico o controllo in fase di compilazione/test va progettato separatamente.

author: lucian406
body:
📋 Summary
A major update completing the migration of the UI to Jetpack Compose. Adds a multi-token management system, instant Network Kill-switch, RTL language support (Farsi), dynamic server pings, and a font size setting.

🔄 Dynamic Server Pings
    Added real-time server ping checking directly on the home screen.
    Pings update cyclically (every 5 minutes) using a single thread pool (instead of spawning ~40 threads per cycle).
    Ping is displayed in the server dropdown next to each server.
    Ping cycle is properly stopped via Future.cancel(true) — fixed thread leak.

🛡 Network Kill-switch (instant block on network change)
    Added a new setting under Additional settings → Kill-switch → "Block traffic on Wi-Fi/Cellular switch".
    When the network type changes (Wi-Fi ↔ cellular), traffic is instantly blocked, without any reconnect attempts.
    Independent of "Reconnect attempts count" — fires immediately.
    Block is released only via the Disconnect button (same as the regular Kill-switch).
    Added isNetworkChangeInProgress flag to hold the blocking TUN.
    Network Kill-switch check is moved before the "Reconnect on network change" check.
    Added a localized disconnect reason in the notification ("Network changed (Wi-Fi/Cellular)" instead of the technical reason:network_change_blocked).

🔑 Token Management (Multi-Token)
    Added a new "Token Management" section in Settings. Now you can add multiple different tokens (accounts) at the same time.
    Hide unused servers with a single tap — only servers from active tokens appear in the dropdown.
    Clear separation of logic:
        On first FPTN install or after pressing "Logout" (when the database is empty), you enter the token on the login screen.
        If you want to add a new token (another account) — use "Token Management → Add Token".
        If you are updating an existing token (renewing it) — use the "Update token" section.
        This prevents duplicates and confusion.

🌐 Improved Domain Management (TLD & IDN)
    Added an advanced mode in domain blocking and Split Tunneling. Now you can block or bypass entire domain zones (e.g., .ru or .cn), not just individual sites.
    Added IDN (Internationalized Domain Names) support. Domains in Cyrillic, Arabic, Chinese and other languages are automatically converted to Punycode and processed correctly.

🌍 RTL Language Support (Farsi fix)
    Fixed a bug where the country flag overlapped the text in dropdowns when using RTL languages (Farsi/Persian).
    Forced LayoutDirection.Ltr for ServerRow, ServerDropdown, LegacySpinner — flags and characters no longer overlap.
    Inverted the dropdown arrow for clearer visual perception.
    The outer text in the dropdown is now also displayed left-to-right.

🛠 Security and Stability Fixes
    Fixed a critical app crash when stopping the VPN (IllegalStateException: Cannot access database on the main thread) on newer Android versions (13+).
    Fixed a thread leak in the ping checker, improving overall performance and reducing battery drain.
    Added a database migration (v2 → v4) preserving all your servers and settings.
    Fixed a Migration didn't properly handle error by removing NOT NULL from the migration SQL query for TEXT fields.

✨ Accessibility Settings
    Added a "Font size" setting under Additional settings (0.85×, 1.0×, 1.1×, 1.2×). Applies instantly to the entire UI, including dialogs.
    Improved line spacing and text readability across all settings descriptions.

🎨 Minor UI/UX Improvements
    The app now remembers the last selected server even if no connection was made.
    The order of servers in the dropdown now strictly matches their order in the source token.
    Removed extra paddings on the home page when the speed chart is disabled.
    Inverted the dropdown arrow for clearer visual perception.
    Fixed a bug where the "Back" button on the home screen could open Settings (added a BackHandler).
    Improved error handling for invalid token input (universal catch (Exception e) for Base64/JSON).
    Added country flag aliases (Turkey, Türkiye, Россия, USA, etc.).

author: kingiust2002
body:
## Stage 3: panel security (stacked on #183: it uses the e2e setup from there)

Guide for the owner: `docs/OPERATOR_SECURITY.md`.

### What changes
1. **Real logout / session revocation.** Every login becomes a registered session (random id in the signed cookie, a row in `operator_sessions`). Logout, "end other sessions" and "end all sessions" end it **on the server**, so a copied cookie stops working. Before, logout only erased the cookie in the user's own browser and a copy stayed valid for up to 8 hours.
2. **Activity log** (`operator_audit_log`, pages `/operator/activity` and `/beauty/operator/activity`): action, table, record ids, counts, session id and a keyed hash of the network address. No names, phones, message texts, e-mail addresses or raw IPs (values that look like personal data are dropped by the writer even under allowed keys). With a **shared account** it says what and when, never "who". Every changing action in both panels is logged (a test lists them and fails on a new unlogged one); **deletions are logged first and refused when the log cannot be written**; a missing log table is not an error.
3. **Optional two-step login** (TOTP, RFC 6238) with single-use recovery codes, per panel, switched on by the owner with `scripts/operator-2fa.mjs` (writes the secret and the **hashes** of the recovery codes to `deploy/.env`; never the codes). Replay of a code is refused (last accepted time step in the database), recovery codes work once, a lost phone has a documented way back. The env preflight refuses half-configured states.

One shared login flow (`lib/operator/loginFlow.js`) for both panels; **Health and Beauty keep separate** cookies, secrets, credentials, second factors, session rows and log rows (tested both ways).

### Database: migration 30
Four private tables (RLS on, no policy, service role only), exactly like migration 28. One transaction, idempotent, self-checking, touches no existing table or row. Tested on PostgreSQL 16 (applies, second run is a no-op, anon denied, service role allowed). `npm run check:rls` now probes them too.

**Deploy order is forgiving:** code before migration = old behaviour (Settings says "run migration 30"); after migration everyone logs in once more.

### Tests
- `tests/panel-security.test.mjs` (19): RFC 6238 vectors, drift window, replay, recovery codes, registry (revoke, cache, expiry, missing table, broken database fails closed), log hygiene, migration and wiring guards.
- `tests/e2e/security.e2e.mjs` (7, real browser): the Beauty panel runs **with** two-step login, Health without; wrong password/code, replay, recovery code once; a copied cookie dead after logout; cookies without/with unknown session id refused; end other/all sessions from Settings without touching the other panel; log content and no customer data; delete refused while the log is broken and allowed when the table is missing.
- Negative control: with the server-side session check disabled, exactly the three session tests fail ("the copied cookie still works after logout", "no session id: the panel opened", "the other session survived"); restored, all pass.
- `npm run lint`, `npm test` 142, `npm run test:e2e` 57, `npm run build`: pass.

### Code ready / tested / deployed / confirmed
Code ready and tested locally (fake database + PostgreSQL 16 for the migration). **Not deployed; migration 30 not run; nothing confirmed on the live site.** Two-step login is OFF until the owner runs the script. Not merged.

author: devmello
body:
Closes #570 (helper part). The fix that makes the prompt appear on the owner's install is in apps/desktop (S11), described below.

**Cause, from tccd's own log on this Mac (the owner's 2026-10-25 04:46 attempts)**
- The helper inside `Psyche.app/Contents/Resources` is not its own TCC subject. tccd logs `AUTHREQ_PROMPTING … subject=Sub:{com.psyche.desktop}Resp:{…PsycheHelper.app…}`.
- It then refuses: `Refusing authorization request for service kTCCServiceReminders and subject Sub:{com.psyche.desktop} … without NSRemindersUsageDescription key`.
- For Calendar it logs: `requires entitlement com.apple.security.personal-information.calendars but it is missing`.
- Psyche.app's Info.plist has no Reminders, Calendars, Contacts or Apple Events strings. Its entitlements are only `allow-jit` and `audio-input`. So no prompt is shown, and no "Psyche (Helper)" row can ever appear.
- **Ruled out:** a stale denial. Every status the helper sees is `notDetermined`; I read this without prompting, through a probe build launched with `open -g -j`.
- **Ruled out:** the launch path and the main thread. The parent is launchd, and the request runs on the main actor with the run loop alive.
- **Control:** the same Apple Development build, launched from outside Psyche.app, shows the prompt normally.

**Needed in apps/desktop (S11; reported to the integrator)**
- Psyche.app's Info.plist: `NSRemindersUsageDescription` + `NSRemindersFullAccessUsageDescription`, `NSCalendarsUsageDescription` + `NSCalendarsFullAccessUsageDescription`, `NSContactsUsageDescription`, `NSAppleEventsUsageDescription`, `NSSpeechRecognitionUsageDescription`.
- Psyche.app's entitlements: `personal-information.calendars`, `personal-information.addressbook`, `automation.apple-events`.
- Prompts and rows will then read "Psyche" (which also suits #541).

**This PR (helper)**
- `TCCAttribution` (Core) finds the enclosing app and knows, per permission, which usage keys and hardened-runtime entitlement tccd requires of it. `HostAttribution` reads them from the host's Info.plist and signature.
- `permissions.request`, EventKit's first use and Automation's first ask now fail fast with `forbidden/prompt_refused_by_macos` when the host lacks something. The message names the host and the missing key or entitlement; details carry `attributedTo`, `missingUsageKeys` and `missingEntitlement`. S09 can show it as is.
- An EventKit denial that returns in under 1 s while the status is still `notDetermined` is reported the same way. The status can lag a real answer, so slow denials stay `denied`.
- `permissions.status` gains `attribution {app, path, hardenedRuntime, missing}`, for onboarding and doctor.
- Helper Info.plist adds the pre-14 `NSRemindersUsageDescription` / `NSCalendarsUsageDescription`.
- New diagnostic flag `--probe-permission <reminders|calendars|automation:<id>> <out.json> [--ask]`, launched via `open`. It records what the helper sees; without `--ask` it never prompts.

**Prompts on the owner's screen during this work**
- One announced Reminders prompt for a scratch build outside Psyche.app. It was answered Allow, so this Mac now has a `com.psyche.helper` Reminders record. The installed helper is unaffected, because its subject is Psyche.app.
- Unannounced: an attempt to simulate nesting with an unsigned stand-in `Host.app` (scratchpad only) made CoreServicesUIAgent treat it as damaged. It probably showed a "damaged app" dialog twice. The stand-in is deleted, and there was no further live nested testing.

**Verified:** unit tests for the attribution rules, the refusal message and the instant-denial rule. Full `swift test` passes (98 + 225). The strict-concurrency, warnings-as-errors build is clean.

## What
**Split payment**
- ชำระเงิน on a group bill with 2+ people asks: **จ่ายทั้งบิล** or **แยกจ่ายรายคน**.
- Tick one or more people, then press **ชำระ ฿…**. The normal checkout opens for just their drinks. It uses `checkoutItems()`, so discount, cash and change work as usual.
- Each payment is its own normal bill, labelled `บิลกลุ่ม: <name> · <people>`.
- The paid lines leave the group, which keeps a `paid` list shown as green **จ่ายแล้ว** lines. The chip shows **เหลือ ฿…**.
- The group closes by itself when the last person pays. Ticking everyone is the same as paying the whole bill.
- Every payment counts in ยอดขาย and the cash drawer the moment it's paid.

**Unpaid money can't disappear**
- Group bills are **no longer cleared at midnight**. One left from an earlier day shows **ค้างจากวันก่อน** on its chip.
- **ลบ** on a group bill that still has drinks needs a confirm and a **PIN**, and is written to the access log.
- **ปิดยอดประจำวัน** lists open group bills and asks first. It still closes only what was actually paid.

**Fix:** two group bills opened in the same millisecond no longer get the same id. This made a test flaky.

author: saimskywalker
body:
Refs #1

Repo: backend_pst, branch `fix-error-handling`

Two small changes:

1. `src/penilaian/penilaian.repository.js`
   The query in `deleteDataPenilaian` said `DELET FROM`, so it always failed. The `catch` below it was empty, so the error was lost and `DELETE /api/penilaian/:id` still replied "Data Penilaian Berhasil Dihapus" while the row stayed. The query is now `DELETE FROM` and the error goes through `handleError` like the other functions in the file.

2. `src/config/utils/errorHandler.js`
   `handleError` used to throw `error.message` (a string). In the controllers, `error.message` on that string is `undefined`, so database errors came back as `{}`. It now rethrows the `Error` object, and wraps anything that isn't an `Error` in one. Messages from the services (like "Data Pegawai Tidak Ada") don't change.

How I checked:
- `node --check` on every file in `src` and on `app.js`
- A small test for `handleError`: an `Error`, a string and a plain object all come out as an `Error` with a non-empty `message`, and an `Error` input is rethrown as the same object
- Not tested against a real database. To check by hand, call `DELETE /api/penilaian/:id` with an admin token and confirm the row is gone from `penilaian_pegawai`

author: tyc67
body:
Fixes #3834

Reviewer: tmt-lead (core paths: `rust/crates/tmt-adapters`, `ARCHITECTURE.md`).

## Cause

The leaked process in the native Ops composer scenarios is a Core `ps` probe (`/usr/bin/env LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC /bin/ps -A -o pid=,ppid=,comm=`), not the composer, an editor or a shell.

- CI run 40052279750 (10-24, head `5ff4e0f69`): the `CLI sandbox diagnostics` line names `/usr/bin/ps` with pgid = pid, ppid 1, and the session of the board's PTY owner.
- CI run 39131074673 (10-18, head `04b7c3f43`): the same failure shape. That build predates the #3870 diagnostics, so the process identity is not proven there.

The sequence:
1. The Ops board starts Core through `tmt_invoke` in a new process group. On a preempting reload, at board exit or at the 15 s Core deadline, it sends SIGKILL to that group and reaps it (`tmt-invoke/src/process.rs:183-203`).
2. Core's `UnixCommandRunner` started every command with `setpgid`, `ps` included (`tmt-adapters/src/process.rs`, `start_command_with_environment`). So an in-flight `ps` was in another group.
3. SIGKILL does not unwind, so `RunningCommand::drop` never ran. The `ps` was reparented to init and was still alive when `withSandbox` counted the processes in the sandbox (`typescript/test/support/cli-process.ts:704-708`, `863-868`).

The leak check is correct and is not changed.

The issue title says "suspend", but the failing case in run 40052279750 was `{"enhanced":true,"lifecycle":"quit","requestTransition":"newer"}`; the `suspend` case passed in that run. Any case can hit it when a Core read is in its `ps` window as the board cancels it.

## Why `setpgid` exists

It came with the bounded process adapter (#107, `743b63b9c`). A command that owns its group lets failure cleanup kill the command and everything it forked, also a descendant that holds the output pipes, and the Darwin zombie-group rule depends on it. `SupervisedProbeRunner` (#907) already keeps probes in a supervised worker's group for the reason this PR fixes.

`ps` (started through `env`, which execs it) never forks, so it needs no group of its own: a pid kill ends it on its own timeout, and the caller's group kill ends it when the caller is killed.

## Change

- `CommandRunner::execute_leaf` (`process.rs`): a new trait method for one program that never forks. The default calls `execute`, so scripted runners and `SupervisedProbeRunner` keep their behavior; `&R` forwards it.
- `UnixCommandRunner::execute_leaf` starts the program without `setpgid` (`start_command(request, false)`). The existing cleanup for a non-owned group signals only the pid.
- `query_ps` (`process/ps.rs`) calls `execute_leaf`. Every Core `ps` run goes through `query_ps` (ancestry, runtime observations, runtime evidence, the Codex caller and the Claude channel).
- All other commands keep their own group.
- `ARCHITECTURE.md` ("Tmux and process effects"): one sentence that a leaf probe such as `ps` stays in its caller's group.

No new runner type, no new dependency, and no change to `tmt-invoke`, Ops or the native tests.

## Question for tmt-lead: other probes

Other `UnixCommandRunner` commands still start in their own group, so a supervisor's group kill does not reach them either. This PR does not change them, because each can fork, and group ownership is what lets their cleanup reach their children:
- tmux client commands (`tmux/mod.rs`, through `Host<UnixCommandRunner>`): a command can start a server.
- External host drivers such as Herdr (`host/external.rs`): an approved driver executable can fork.
- Provider and driver checks, `/bin/sh -c` scripts, extension commands and hooks, `git`, workspace capture, and native upgrade steps.
- `process_info` reads native process data and starts no command.

Choices for those: keep them in their own group (now), a SIGTERM grace period in `tmt-invoke` before SIGKILL so Core can clean up, or `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` (Linux only). Which one, if any, is a Core design choice.

## Tests (red then green)

- `process::cleanup_policy_tests::a_leaf_probe_dies_with_its_callers_group`: the test starts the test binary again as a caller in a new process group (`process_group(0)`, like `tmt-invoke`). The caller starts `/bin/sh -c 'printf … > pid; exec /bin/sleep 30'` through `UnixCommandRunner::execute_leaf`; the probe publishes its pid and never forks. The test sends SIGKILL to the caller group it created, reaps the caller, and polls up to 2 s for ESRCH on the probe. On failure, it kills only the probe it started (it checks that the probe leads its own group first). Helper: the ignored `leaf_probe_caller_waits_on_its_probe`.
  - Red (`execute_leaf` on the old group path): "leaf probe 76262 outlived its caller's group"; the test then removed the probe (`ps -p 76262` found none).
  - Green: 1 passed, in 0.03 s.
- `process::ps::tests::ps_starts_as_a_leaf_probe_in_the_callers_group`: a runner whose `execute` panics; `query_ps` must use `execute_leaf`. Red with `query_ps` on `execute`: "ps must start through the leaf path (#3834)". Green: 1 passed.

Evidence: `/private/tmp/claude-501/t9/3834/red/` and `green/` (local).

The tests use only processes they start. No tmux, Herdr or store is used.

## Review

reviewer-18: **READY YES** on `0d7e24226`, with nothing blocking and nothing should-fix. Inspected: the cleanup path without a group (pid-only SIGKILL, the same path `SupervisedProbeRunner` uses), that `ps` is a leaf (fixed program, `env` execs, `ps` never forks, no parsed field depends on the group), terminal signals, both tests (red by mutation; green 10/10), and the unchanged callers and the architecture sentence.

Notes and disposition:
- N1. On macOS `/bin/ps` is setuid root. A same-user SIGKILL is still allowed (the real uid is the user's), as with the old group cleanup. No change.
- N2. The test's liveness poll treats an unreaped zombie as alive, so it could fail by mistake under a PID 1 that never reaps. CI runs cargo on runner VMs, whose init reaps, and its Docker jobs use `--init`. No change.
- N3. A future runner that wraps another and forwards only `execute` would lose the leaf behavior. There is none today. No change.
- N4. The failure-path `killpg(probe)` has a small pid-reuse window. It runs only in the red case, within 2 s. No change.
- N5. The new `ARCHITECTURE.md` line was longer than its neighbors. Fixed in the second commit (wrap only, no word changed).

## Checks

Checks on the rebased head `51f1d9083` (on origin/main `e7d624ac1`; commits `5674d9058` fix and `51f1d9083` wrap; the same results were first on `0d7e24226`; TMPDIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/t9, CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2, CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/private/tmp/claude-501/t9/target-builder-18; `TMUX`, `TMUX_PANE`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and `CODEX_HOME` unset; in `rust/`):
- `cargo +1.97.0 fmt --all --check`: pass
- `cargo +1.97.0 clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: pass
- `cargo +1.97.0 test --locked -p tmt-adapters --lib process::`: 44 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored (the two re-exec helpers)
- `cargo +1.97.0 test --locked -p tmt-invoke`: 18 passed, 0 failed, 3 ignored
- `cargo +1.97.0 test --locked -p tmt-cli --bin tmt`: 429 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo +1.95.0 test --locked -p tmt-cli --test architecture`: 88 passed
- (`typescript/`) `corepack pnpm docs:format:check`: pass

No full workspace run. CI is the full gate.
