body:
The merged 27-package release half published: 14 versions are live on npm and the publish stopped on `@byokit/record` with a 404 because that name no longer has a trusted-publisher relationship with our release workflow. Five of the versions waiting behind it are names we no longer ship: `@byokit/record`, `overlay`, `statusbar`, `browser` and `bubble` are deprecated here and already live as `@platform-kits/record` 0.2.1, `@platform-kits/overlay` 0.3.3, `@platform-kits/statusbar` 0.1.2 and `@platform-kits/browser` 0.1.1.

So this PR holds those five back from publishing, using the release tool's own mechanism: `private: true`. `scripts/release.ts` builds its publish pending set from `workspacePackages().filter((p) => !p.isPrivate)` — its own header says "`private: true` holds a package back" — so the five are never attempted again and the 404 cannot recur. Being private also exempts them from the decreased-version lint rule, so no guard, lint, test or workflow is weakened or touched.

What stays exactly as merged: every version and pin of the other 22 packages (the eight that still belong in `@byokit` — mcp 0.2.0, cloud 0.6.1, audio 0.3.1, dictation 0.6.1, infer 0.3.2, phone 0.1.6, push 0.1.1, signaling 0.1.1 — keep the versions they need to publish), both lockfiles, `release.yml`, `.github/`, and the deprecations. Nothing is unpublished and nothing is deprecated further.

Each held package gets one `## Unreleased` bullet naming its new home. The verify skill's feature map gained `features/release-private-hold.md` with how to drive and prove the hold, including the negative control that puts one held name back in the gate list.

After merge, the existing trusted release is re-run and publishes the eight that still belong here.

## Checks

outcome: a release publish no longer tries to publish @byokit/record, overlay, statusbar, browser or bubble, so the 404 on record's trusted publisher cannot recur, and the eight kits that still belong in @byokit publish as before

repro: npm run release -- publish --dry-run listed @byokit/record 0.2.2 and the other four absent names as pending before this change (13 pending on origin/main); it now lists only the eight publishing names - systematic-debugging used

proof: verify-byokit (features/release-private-hold.md): npm run release -- publish --dry-run on this branch, plus the negative control with private removed from packages/record (record 0.2.2 reappears in the gate list), both exit 0 on this head

Native transcripts need to identify the exact paid window requests that produced them without copying financial truth into a second store. Migration 43 extends the existing SQLite transcript owner with policy/quality identity and window links. Artifact replacement and canonical policy/source/run/request ownership checks share one transaction; local replacement clears the links. A read-only snapshot projects latency, quality observations and existing receipt/attempt history, keeping unknown usage and requested-broker versus actual-upstream identity distinct.

Focused modules separate validation, persistence and reads. Cross-owner tests cover authorization tampering, exclusions, foreign/VLM/undispatched requests, idempotent replacement, forced rollback, concurrent reads, late receipts and historical recipe inspection. Empty output stays distinct from rejection/review; historical inspection preserves recorded quality decisions while new writes enforce current rules. Existing local wire/cache identities remain compatible.

Local gate and guarded publication passed (10/10, all 818 core unit tests retained). Tests use synthetic audio/fake transports/real SQLite; no paid provider, private-media or model-download acceptance is claimed. Native VAD readiness, pilot/bulk orchestration, adapters and typed native recovery remain subsequent #119 work; production native execution stays disabled.

author: gingergraham
body:
## Summary

`aws-update` (`shell/aws.sh`) and `az-update` (`shell/azure.sh`) called `install-aws` / `install-azure` directly. Installer files are never sourced into the interactive shell; `wb tools` sources them transiently. So both wrappers failed with `command not found`. workbench-core v2.21.0's module-CI clean-shell check (core D94) now rejects any `register.shell` file that calls an `install-*` function.

- `aws-update` runs `wb tools install aws`; `az-update` runs `wb tools install azure`. That's the same installer, which already handles both fresh install and update. `wb tools` doesn't trigger the `wb` wrapper's shell reload, and the exit status passes through.
- README: the wrappers' descriptions are updated, and the reference to `wb tools update` (removed in core D43) now says `wb tools install|upgrade <name>`.

author: garyjob
body:
## Problem

`'Scored Chatlogs'` (spreadsheet `1Tbj7H5ur…`) stopped growing at **row 7224**. Row 7225 onward is completely empty, so `getLastRow()+1` was never blocked — the writer simply never appended again. Meanwhile `'Telegram Chat Logs'` kept filling to ~15k rows with **~1,500 rows still `Pending`**, some carrying a Col N hash from 20261013 and earlier.

That backlog is the diagnostic tell: `processTelegramChatLogs()` opens with an unconditional, cheap **backfill loop** that stamps Col J on any `Pending` row that already has a hash. On any successful run those ~1,500 rows would flip to a final state before the main loop starts. They did not. So the function is dying at its **first statements**, not timing out mid-loop — and because it has no `try/catch` and no error surface, it failed invisibly into an execution log.

Suspected trigger: `6285a5c (#505)` "stop .claspignore-ing the accessor", which changed the live project's pushed file set immediately before the last-ever run (repo file touched Sep 18; last appends 20260913).

## Change (3 files, no behaviour change on the happy path)

**New `pipeline_diagnostics.js`**

- `diagnoseScoringPipeline()` — one read-only call that names the cause instead of guessing between them:
  - Script Properties present/absent (presence only, **never values**)
  - `ScriptApp.getProjectTriggers()` — is anything actually scheduling `processTelegramChatLogs`?
  - can the executing identity `openByUrl` each of OUTPUT / TELEGRAM / EXISTING sheets, and does each expected tab exist
  - intake queue depth: total Pending, Pending-with-hash, Pending `[CONTRIBUTION EVENT]`
  - output tail: `lastRow` + trailing Col H status dates
  - a plain-language `verdict`, most specific cause first
- `logPipelineHealth_(fn, outcome, message, detail)` — appends every run outcome to a new **`Pipeline Health`** tab (auto-created). This is the fix for the actual root problem: the next silent death shows up in the sheet itself. Never throws.
- `installScoringTrigger(everyMinutes)` — idempotent installer for the time-driven trigger. **No such installer exists in the repo** (grep for `newTrigger` + `processTelegramChatLogs` returns nothing), which is consistent with a hand-created trigger being lost and never recreated.

**`telegram_webhook_listener.js`** — add `?exec=diagnose` route; list it in the ping endpoint catalog.

**`grok_scoring_for_telegram_and_whatsapp_logs.js`** — `processTelegramChatLogs` now writes a `Pipeline Health` row on both early returns (`XAI_API_KEY` missing, intake sheet not found) and on success with the processed/backfilled counts.

## Rebased off current `origin/main`

First attempt (#596) was opened against `fix/routing-guard-unnamed-ledger`, which was itself squash-merged as #595 and left stale. Rebased onto current `main` (`54301b0`).

Verified before rebuilding: `merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main <branch>` → **no** (stale base, correctly flagged). Both edited files are **byte-identical** between merge-base and `origin/main`, and `pipeline_diagnostics.js` does not exist on main — so the edits apply cleanly, no 3-way resolution needed.

Note for reviewers: `git diff origin/main..branch` (two-dot) shows apparent deletions of `SCHEDULE_TRIGGERS.md`, `SCHEMA.md`, `Triggers.template.gs` and `tdg_wix_dashboard.js`. **Those are an artifact of comparing against a stale base, not lost content** — all four are present on `origin/main` at this commit. The three-dot diff (`origin/main...branch`) is the correct view and contains only this PR's 3 files.

## Testing

- `node --check` clean on all files in the branch
- No new Script Properties required; no secret is ever read into the report
- `diagnoseScoringPipeline()` is entirely read-only (one `openByUrl` per sheet + `getDataRange`); the only write is `logPipelineHealth_`, and only when `ok === false`
- Deployment is separate: `clasp push` then a new version. Verify with `?exec=diagnose` **before** re-arming the trigger, since re-arming starts writing at scale.

## Not in this PR

- Re-arming the trigger + draining the ~1,500-row backlog (deliberate: it calls Grok once per row and stamps many `Full Provision Awarded` cells)
- Backfilling H–K on rows 7220–7224 (5 partial rows from a one-off backfill that wrote A–G + L but not H–K)
- The unrelated in-flight `process_movement_telegram_logs.js` edit from the old branch is **excluded** — not mine, left for its own PR

author: yschimke
body:
`notify.mobile_app_<device>` messages from Home Assistant now post as Android notifications, once the user allows notifications.

## Delivery
HA's FCM relay only serves the official companion apps, so this uses HA's **local push**:
- The `mobile_app` registration now sends `app_data.push_websocket_channel: true`. Installs registered before this re-register once, with the same device id.
- `LiveHaSession.pushNotifications(webhookId)` subscribes to `mobile_app/push_notification_channel` (`support_confirm: true`) on every connection, and confirms each message with `mobile_app/push_notification_confirm`.
- The channel delivers every message, in order. It uses an unbounded queue, not the latest-only flow edit sessions use, so a burst (a clear after its post) is never dropped.
- **Limitation:** messages only arrive while the app holds its HA connection, which today means while it's in the foreground. Delivery with the app closed needs a persistent-connection foreground service. That comes with a Play foreground-service declaration, so it's left for a follow-up.

## Posting (`notify/HaNotifications`)
- **Permission:** nothing posts, and nothing asks for permission, until the user turns on **Settings → Connection → Home Assistant notifications**, which requests `POST_NOTIFICATIONS`.
- **Dedupe:** the notification id comes from HA's `tag`, falling back to the message content. A re-sent tagged message replaces the first, and `clear_notification` removes it.
- **Bridging to the watch:**
  - Notifications carry bridge tag `ha` and use the same key as their dismissal id, so dismissing on either device dismisses both.
  - A Wear app that later posts its own copy can suppress the bridged one with `BridgingConfig`.
  - When a paired watch has the Wear app, the notification gets a watch-only **Open on watch** action. It uses `RemoteActivityHelper` and a new `terrazzo-wear://open` filter on `WearMainActivity`. Once the Wear app posts its own copy, this becomes a no-op.
- **Taps and buttons:**
  - `clickAction`/`url` opens a dashboard path in the app or a URL in the browser; otherwise the tap opens the entity's details, else the app.
  - HA action buttons fire `mobile_app_notification_action` (with `action` and `tag`), on the app's socket or a short-lived session. `uri` actions open the URI.

## Remote Compose card (`notify/NotificationCards`)
On API 36+, when the message sets `data.entity_id`, the expanded body is that entity's tile. It's captured the same way launcher widgets are and played by the platform's `RemoteViews.DrawInstructions` player.
- **Buttons:** each control in the RC document is a host action, made of an action id plus the encoded `HaAction`. `setOnClickPendingIntent(actionId, …)` binds each id. On tap, the player fires the PendingIntent with the action's `remotecompose_metadata`, and `HaNotificationActionReceiver` runs the toggle or service call on HA, or opens details.
- **Live updates:** the card follows its entity. Each live state change re-captures the cards whose entity changed and replaces those notifications with `setOnlyAlertOnce`. It only does this while a notification is still showing, so a dismissed one never comes back.

## Test notification
Settings → Connection → **Send a test notification**, shown once notifications are allowed, for live servers and the offline demo. The public demo HA can't send one: its gateway denies writes, and every guest shares one account, so a dashboard button there would notify every demo user's device.

The test goes through the real path:
- tagged, so a second test replaces the first
- a "Got it" action
- bridged to the watch
- a live card for one of the user's lights

On a live server its card is tracked like a pushed one. In the offline demo, the card's toggle flips the demo entity and redraws the card, and "Got it" only dismisses.

## Tests
- `HaPushNotificationTest` (ha-client): parsing, tag and content dedupe, `clear_notification`.
- `HaClientPushChannelTest` (ha-client): a burst to a slow collector arrives complete and in order. It fails on the old latest-only delivery.
- `HaNotificationsTest` (Robolectric): bridge tag and dismissal id, "Open on watch" only when the watch has the app, HA actions becoming buttons, refreshes not re-alerting.
- `TestNotificationTest`: every test notification shares one id.
- `NotificationCardTest` (instrumented, API 36 emulator in CI):
  - The card binds a toggle or service call for its entity, and the platform player draws it. Both passed on the emulator in the first run.
  - The notification posts with the card, bridged, then clears on `clear_notification`. That test now waits for the system server's asynchronous post and cancel.
  - The demo's test notification posts with its card and "Got it".
- Lint and ktfmt pass.

author: clementdelestre
body:
## Why

`GET /api/auth/users-public` is unauthenticated and lists every username (security audit 2026-10-25, finding 2).

## What

- New admin setting `users_public_mode`, in Settings > General (DB-backed, no env): `everyone` (default, today's behaviour), `lan`, `hidden`. The settings API rejects any other value.
- `lan`: the roster is returned only when the socket peer and **every** `X-Forwarded-For` entry are private, loopback or link-local (IPv6: loopback, unique-local, link-local). The engine gateway appends the peer to the chain, so a forged header or a public hop anywhere in the chain gives an empty list. This is stricter than the login limiter's "last entry" rule on purpose, since it is an access decision. A reverse proxy in front that does not set `X-Forwarded-For` makes every client look local; the setting hint says so.
- `hidden` and a refused `lan` caller get `[]`. Client: the picker goes straight to `/login` when the roster is empty and no session is stored on the device, and `/login` hides the "choose another user" button in that case. Quick Connect starts from a picked user, so it is unavailable for new devices when hidden.
- Apple TV already offers "Other user" with a typed username on an empty roster, no change.
- Specs, `.sqlx` cache and settings hint (six languages) updated.

## Existing installs

No migration: the key is absent, which means `everyone`, so nothing changes until an admin picks another mode.

## Tests

Integration tests for each mode, spoofed and multi-hop `X-Forwarded-For`, and settings validation.

Supersedes #2013 (rebuilt on main after #2011; both auth_routes test blocks kept).

- **Session check on the server** (`src/lib/auth/server.ts`, `server-only`): `getCurrentUser()` forwards only the HttpOnly `WORKLY_SESSION` cookie to `${BACKEND_URL}/api/auth/me` (runtime env, `no-store`, 5 s timeout). 200 → member, 401 → signed out, anything else throws. Cached per request.
- **`/[locale]/feed`**: no valid session → redirect to `/[locale]/login`; otherwise rendered with the real member. If the backend cannot answer, a localized error page with retry (`feed/error.tsx`, Next 16 `retry()`) instead of a misleading sign-in prompt.
- **`/[locale]/login`, `/[locale]/register`**: signed-in members go to the feed; if the backend errors, the form is still shown.
- **Real member**: profile card, header avatar and composer use `displayName`; the card shows the email and the "Work email verified" badge only when `emailVerified`. The sample profile numbers (connections, views, completion) are removed; posts, people, topics and jobs stay sample data.
- **Logout** (`components/auth/logout-button.tsx`): `POST /api/auth/logout` with the CSRF token (existing client: refresh + one retry), loading state; success → full page load of the login page (no signed-in page left in the client router cache); failure → alert, still signed in. The backend deletes the session and expires the cookie.
- No auth decision in Proxy (a cookie-presence redirect could loop with an expired cookie). `/feed`, `/login`, `/register` are now dynamic; all other pages stay static.

## Tests and CI
- New `e2e/mock-backend.mjs`: a test-only stand-in for the API (`/api/auth/me` by cookie value, `/logout` with the backend's CSRF rule, `/csrf`), started by Playwright on port 3101. `BACKEND_URL` points build and start to it; `frontend-ci.yml` gets `BACKEND_URL: http://localhost:3101` because the `/api` rewrite is fixed at build time. Frontend CI still needs no Java.
- New `e2e/auth-session.spec.ts` (21 per project): signed-out and expired sessions → login in the same language; real name/email/avatar, verified badge only when verified, no sample member; session cookie invisible to scripts and no storage; signed-in login/register → feed; backend errors (login form still shown; feed error page, retry recovers, axe light/dark); logout with `X-XSRF-TOKEN` → login, cookie gone, feed and back button end on login, language kept, loading state, server and network failures.
- Updated: feed spec runs signed in; login spec expects the server's session (HttpOnly) and CSRF cookies and no storage; the hreflang test now checks for hreflang/alternate only (dynamic pages send font-preload `Link` headers).
- Console guard option `expectServerError` (error-page tests only): ignores the 5xx document's "Failed to load resource" and React's production Server Components error report (#441). Nothing else.

## Notes
- Each feed/login/register view makes one server-to-backend `/me` call.
- Personal pages are `no-store`; make sure the production reverse proxy does not cache them.
- Still open: login rate limiting, email verification gate, full-stack E2E in CI (Stage 4).

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run lint`, `npx next typegen && npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] Production build (`/feed`, `/login`, `/register` dynamic; others static)
- [x] `npm run test:e2e`: **336 passed, 2 skipped** (desktop-only photo tests on mobile); same with the CI flow (build with `BACKEND_URL`, then `E2E_PREBUILT=1`)
- [x] `git diff --check`
- [x] Manual full stack (real backend + local Postgres, production frontend): signed-out feed → login; register → feed with the real name and email; signed-in login → feed; logout → login, cookie removed, feed and back button → login; login (EN) → `/en/feed`; no console errors. Throwaway account deleted
- [ ] Frontend CI passes on this PR

author: mrgnw
body:
Every model load compiled the `.mlpackage` with `MLModel.compileModel`, which writes a full `.mlmodelc` copy into `$TMPDIR`. Nothing deleted it, so each spatial-maker run left one copy on the internal disk: about 47 MB for V2 Small and 640 MB for the large models. After a day of benchmarking there were 55 leaked copies totalling 10 GB.

The fix deletes the compiled copy right after `MLModel(contentsOf:)` loads it.

Verified:
- A DA3 photo run and a V2 Small video run both complete with correct output.
- No `.mlmodelc` is left in `$TMPDIR` afterwards.
- `cargo test` passes.

This touches the same lines in `coreml_load_model` as #15 (VDA), so whichever merges second needs a small rebase.

body:
## Pourquoi

Clément : « Vérifie qu'il y a des conseils d'entretien pour le t-shirt, c'est important. Même dans l'email de commande. » Pour ce projet, l'entretien protège aussi le QR : s'il pâlit au lavage, il se lit de moins loin, et les traits fins de l'accroche s'abîment.

État des lieux :
- **la boutique** donnait l'entretien avant l'achat ;
- **l'email de commande** le donnait en une ligne grise, entre les liens et le récapitulatif, qu'on ne lit pas ;
- **rien** dans l'email « Il est en route », la page « Ma commande » ni la FAQ ;
- **le texte** n'avait pas tous les conseils de Printful : pas de nettoyage à sec, sèche-linge à basse température seulement ;
- **rien sur le premier lavage** : un t-shirt DTG neuf, surtout noir, peut sentir légèrement le vinaigre et garder des traces claires autour de l'impression. C'est l'apprêt, qui part au premier lavage. Sans le savoir, on y voit un défaut ;
- **l'étiquette d'origine** est détachable. Si on active l'étiquette du col imprimée, ses symboles d'entretien disparaissent sans doute.

## Ce qui change

Choix de Clément :
- **Le texte, complété selon Printful**, partout (boutique comprise) : « à l'envers, à 30 °C, cycle délicat, sans adoucissant ni javel ; séchage à l'air de préférence, sinon au sèche-linge à basse température ; jamais de fer sur l'impression, ni de nettoyage à sec. »
- **Email de commande** : un bloc « Entretien » titré, sous le récapitulatif, à la place de la ligne grise.
- **Email d'expédition** : le même bloc, et la note du premier lavage. C'est le moment où le t-shirt arrive.
- **« Ma commande »** : l'entretien et le premier lavage, sous « À réception ».
- **FAQ** : une entrée « Comment laver le t-shirt ? ». La réponse « C'est quel t-shirt ? » annonçait une impression DTF : elle dit maintenant DTG, la technique réelle (cf. #78).
- **`MISE_EN_PRODUCTION.md`**, étiquette du col : noter ce que Printful imprime à la place de l'étiquette d'origine, entretien compris.

## Tests

- Unitaires (1084, dont 2 nouveaux) :
  - le texte d'entretien et la note du premier lavage ;
  - l'email de commande : un bloc titré, plus de ligne grise, pas de premier lavage ;
  - l'email d'expédition : l'entretien et le premier lavage, profil activé ou non ;
  - « Ma commande » et la FAQ, qui nomme le DTG et plus le DTF.
- Types, lint et typographie : propres.
- E2E avec base, accessibilité et visuel (24/24) : boutique (la ligne « Entretien » est toujours là), FAQ et « Ma commande », sans écart d'accessibilité. Smoke : 17/17.

- Retain payload and receipts across final-write, log, unlink and fallback-clear failures. If both independent

independent reviewer separately executed six actual-runner probes: known/unread usage crossed with ordinary
cleanup, unlink failure and fallback-clear write failure, each followed by three fresh-load continuations.

The second CI run `40192946158` exposed another extraction consumer: unchanged workflow tests patch the

### [`v8.0.1`](https://redirect.github.com/actions/download-artifact/releases/tag/v8.0.1)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/actions/download-artifact/compare/v8.0.0...v8.0.1)

#### What's Changed

- Support for CJK characters in the artifact name by [@​danwkennedy](https://redirect.github.com/danwkennedy) in [#​471](https://redirect.github.com/actions/download-artifact/pull/471)

### [`v8.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/actions/download-artifact/releases/tag/v8.0.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/actions/download-artifact/compare/v7.0.0...v8.0.0)

#### v8 - What's new

> \[!IMPORTANT]
> actions/download-artifact\@​v8 has been migrated to an ESM module. This should be transparent to the caller but forks might need to make significant changes.

> \[!IMPORTANT]
> Hash mismatches will now error by default. Users can override this behavior with a setting change (see below).

##### Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in `actions/upload-artifact`, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the `Content-Type` header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. Callers wishing to download a zipped file as-is can also set the new `skip-decompress` parameter to `true`.

##### Enforced checks (breaking)

A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. Callers can now configure the behavior on mismatch with the `digest-mismatch` parameter. To be secure by default, we are now defaulting the behavior to `error` which will fail the workflow run.

##### ESM

To support new versions of the @​actions/\* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

#### What's Changed

- Don't attempt to un-zip non-zipped downloads by [@​danwkennedy](https://redirect.github.com/danwkennedy) in [#​460](https://redirect.github.com/actions/download-artifact/pull/460)
- Add a setting to specify what to do on hash mismatch and default it to `error` by [@​danwkennedy](https://redirect.github.com/danwkennedy) in [#​461](https://redirect.github.com/actions/download-artifact/pull/461)

**Full Changelog**: <https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/compare/v7...v8.0.0>

### [`v7.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/actions/download-artifact/releases/tag/v7.0.0)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/actions/download-artifact/compare/v6.0.0...v7.0.0)

#### v7 - What's new

> \[!IMPORTANT]

author: justin13888
body:
## Summary
- `crates/torrentd/src/check_queue/worker.rs` (`admit_adoption`): an adoption whose profile is still configured but has no engine (a VPN profile whose tunnel failed at boot resolves `Failed`) is now held the way a fenced or offline profile's is. It goes to the back of the queue and the tick moves on. Its `pool.db` row, owner record and registry claim stay in place, and it is admitted once the profile has an engine. The hold is logged once per profile per tick on the existing `verify held: profile is off the network` line, with `reason = "no_session"`. An item whose profile no `[[profile]]` declares any more is still dropped, with its records released, as before.
- Why: admission used to drop every such item through `release_dropped_claim`. So a transient tunnel failure at boot threw away that profile's whole persisted adoption queue, even though docs/import.md §7 says the queue survives a restart.
- `crates/torrentd/src/check_queue/admission_tests.rs`: adds `a_boot_holds_the_queued_adoptions_of_a_profile_without_a_session`. Three adoptions are queued through `enqueue_verify` with every profile up. The test then simulates a restart: a fresh in-memory queue, then `restore_verify_queue`. It boots with `p` live but no engine reachable, `f` failed, and `gone` unconfigured. Over two ticks, `p`'s and `f`'s items stay queued with their row, owner record and registry claim, and `gone`'s item is dropped with all three released. Once `p`'s engine appears, `p`'s item is admitted (one `AddTorrent`, in flight) and `f`'s is still held. It imports `owner_of` from the pool-service test helpers.
- `docs/import.md` §7: the held-items bullet now covers a configured profile with no session. The dropped-item bullet says "no longer configured" in place of "stopped".

## Validation
- `cargo test -p torrentd --bin torrentd check_queue`: 46 passed.
- The new test with `worker.rs` reverted to the base fails at `` `p` and `f` wait `` (the items were dropped), so the test detects the defect.
- `mise run fmt`: pass (after `mise run fmt-fix`)
- `cargo clippy -p torrentd --all-targets -- -D warnings`: pass. The full `mise run lint` feature matrix and `mise run test` are left to CI.
- `mise run lint-tracing`: pass
- `mise run commit-lint origin/master..HEAD`: no errors in 2 commits

## Risks and rollout
- A failed profile's items now stay queued for the life of the process, and each tick passes over them once. `torrentd_pool_verify_queue_depth` counts them until a restart brings the profile up, the same as for an offline profile.
- Coverage gap: the once-per-tick logging of the new `no_session` reason is not asserted. It shares the `held_logged` set and code path that `adoptions_held_for_a_fenced_profile_log_once_per_tick` covers.

## Issue
Closes #651

## Decisions taken
Issue 651 - fix(torrentd): boot drops the persisted adoption queue of a profile that failed to start

1. **Which profiles are held when there is no engine.** Taken: hold when `ProfileRegistry::resolve` answers `Active` or `Failed`, and drop only on `Unknown`. Rejected: holding `Failed` alone. An `Active` profile with no engine is not expected, but holding it costs nothing, and dropping it would release claims for a profile that is still configured. Rejected: also holding `Unknown`. Nothing would ever admit those items, because a profile that is no longer configured never gets an engine, so they would sit in the queue forever. Reverse: change `engine.is_none() && configured` in `admit_adoption` to match the arm wanted.
2. **Log line for the hold.** Taken: reuse `verify held: profile is off the network` with a new `reason` value, `no_session`, so one log query finds every held adoption. Rejected: a separate message. That would split the query, and docs §7 already names this line. Reverse: give the `no_session` arm its own `warn!`.
3. **When a failed profile's items are admitted.** Taken: no new retry. The registry's failed set is fixed at boot, so these items wait for the restart that brings the tunnel up. Keeping them is exactly what lets that restart admit them. Rejected: re-initialising a failed profile at runtime. That is outside this issue's manifest. Reverse: none needed; this adds no mechanism.

body: Adds an **experimental** hybrid refinement-scoring mode to Smart Farm, OFF by default. CPU workers remain authoritative for oss!idle simulation, fatigue, mods and PP. If WebGPU is available in the host Electron session, a WGSL compute shader scores half the refinement candidates while CPU JavaScript scores the other half; CPU always validates numerical parity, enforces eligibility and ranks final results. GPU adapter/pipeline failures, numerical mismatches, unsupported graphics drivers and timeouts safely fall back to full CPU without stopping scanning. User-visible `Benchmark GPU compatibility` measures CPU vs WebGPU including transfers on 16,384 candidate vectors (3 rounds), gives adapter identity and max error; toggle persists via existing settings export/import. No graphics flags are changed or enabled, GPU buffers/devices are destroyed each scan. **Not GPU acceleration for full gameplay simulation**; this prototype tests whether GPU compute can help ranking, and may be slower especially on Intel HD Graphics 520 Linux Gen9. All 24 automated suites passed with mocked GPU readback parity and fallback, npm ci, build 1.40 MB below game's 2 MB cap, `node --check`. Real WebGPU device test on user's installed oss!idle remains pending; benchmark will report availability at runtime.

author: lukerandall
body:
## What changes

`Row::in_default_text` reports whether the default text of a listing lists a row. Its default returns true, so every existing row type prints the same bytes.

```rust
pub trait Row {
    // ...
    fn in_default_text(&self) -> bool {
        true
    }
}
```

- The default text (no `--json`, `--long` or `--fields`) lists each row that reports a problem, and each other row for which the method returns true.
- `--long`, `--fields` and `--json` list every row. A list, a batch, a single row and a stream print every row.
- `Document::only_problems` becomes the strictest case of the rule: it leaves out every row that reports no problem, whatever the method returns. Its behaviour does not change.
- A row that reports a problem is always listed, so the problem note and exit 1 never count a row that the text hides (OUTPUT-3).
- When the default text lists no row, a listing with a summary prints the summary alone, and one without prints nothing on standard output, as under `only_problems`. A listing that holds no rows keeps ADR-0153's rule.
- The footer counts every row of the page, the empty note prints only for a listing that holds no rows, and the budget's cut line counts the printed rows against the total, as under `only_problems`.
- The help prints no `Rows:` line and does not offer `--long` without long columns, because `parse` cannot know before the handler runs whether the method will hide any row.

An adopter's cleanup command uses it so that a dry run lists every item and a real run lists only the items that carry their own next step:

```text
$ tidy clean
Removed 2 items.
PATH        REMOVED  STEP
cache/lock  false    stop the server
```

## API-1 ground

The ground is one adopter's request for an ordinary need. Any tool whose run handles many items can want its default text to show only the items that need the reader, while its JSON keeps every item (ADR-0122).

## Records

ADR-0157 records the decision and amends ADR-0138 and ADR-0153. The listings directory reached its limit of 5,000 words (DOCS-2), so ADR-0157 leads a new node, `listings/default-text/`, and ADR-0138 and ADR-0140 move under it. `docs/behaviour/output/listings/README.md`, the rustdoc and the changelog describe the behaviour.

author: tbxy-agent[bot]
body:
## What & why

Updates the cert-manager Helm chart constraint from `1.19.*` (staging currently deploys v1.19.6) to `1.21.*`, rolling in the 1.20 and 1.21 releases plus patches through v1.21.3. This brings ACME Renewal Information (ARI) support, Azure Private DNS, Gateway API and cainjector improvements, security hardening, and — in v1.21.3 — removal of trust in the compromised eMudhra root CA (`emSign ECC Root CA - G3`) and a fix for the ACME ARI renewal loop.

## Changes

- `k8s/infrastructure/cert-manager/helm/helmrelease.yaml`: version constraint `1.19.*` → `1.21.*`

## Breaking-change assessment (1.19 → 1.21)

Reviewed all documented breaking changes against our config ([1.19→1.20](https://cert-manager.io/docs/releases/upgrading/upgrading-1.19-1.20/), [1.20→1.21](https://cert-manager.io/docs/releases/upgrading/upgrading-1.20-1.21/)):

1. **`cert-manager-edit` RBAC restriction** (Challenge/Order permissions, GHSA-8rvj-mm4h-c258) — already shipped in v1.19.6, which we run; no change on upgrade.
2. **Chart no longer creates the default `tokenrequest` Role/RoleBinding** — only matters if an issuer uses `serviceAccountRef.name` pointing at the controller ServiceAccount (Vault Kubernetes auth, Route53). Our issuers (selfSigned bootstrap, internal CA, ACME http01 via Traefik) don't → not affected.
3. **Removed values `prometheus.servicemonitor.targetPort`, `prometheus.servicemonitor.path`, `prometheus.podmonitor.path`; metrics port renamed `tcp-prometheus-servicemonitor` → `http-metrics`** — our values only set `crds.enabled` and `prometheus.enabled`; both verified present in the 1.21.3 chart values (pulled `oci://quay.io/jetstack/charts/cert-manager:1.21.3`). No references to the old port name anywhere in the repo.
4. **Container UID/GID default change (1000/0 → 65532/65532)** in 1.20 — chart-managed defaults; no hostPath/fs permission dependencies → no action.

## Rollout

Flux reconciles the HelmRelease hourly; the upgrade can be triggered immediately with `flux reconcile helmrelease cert-manager -n burginfra-system`. With `crds.enabled: true` the chart refreshes the `cert-manager.io` CRDs, then performs rolling restarts of all three controllers (controller, cainjector, webhook). The `cert-manager.io/v1` API is unchanged between these versions, so no manual CRD or manifest migration is required. Issued certificates live in Secrets and are untouched by the restart.

## Testing

- `just check` — yamlfmt + kubeconform pass (430 resources, 0 invalid, 0 errors)
- `helm show values oci://quay.io/jetstack/charts/cert-manager --version 1.21.3` — existing values keys validated against the new chart schema
- Cluster (read-only): HelmRelease `cert-manager` in `burginfra-system` at chart v1.19.6 (revision 5); 6 `cert-manager.io` CRDs present

## Risks / rollback

- **Rollback:** revert this commit and let Flux reconcile (or force with `flux reconcile`) — Helm downgrades to `1.19.*` from release history; chart-managed CRDs are restored on rollback and, since the `cert-manager.io/v1` API is unchanged, that is safe.
- Webhook mutating/validating webhooks use `failurePolicy: Fail`; the deploy is a rolling update (maxUnavailable 0) so no downtime is expected, but if a webhook call lands during a restart window it fails fast and is retried by the requesting controller.
- First reconciliation after merge should be watched (e.g. `flux get helmrelease cert-manager -n burginfra-system --watch`) to confirm v1.21.3 deploys cleanly and Certificates reconcile.

Everything is added up per person and day in one table, `usage_daily`. Five report views are included: `usage_people`, `usage_by_day`, `usage_by_screen`, `usage_by_action` and `usage_ai`. `docs/USAGE_ANALYTICS.md` is a plain-language guide with queries you can copy.

## Privacy
Nothing anyone types is stored, and neither are file or document names, document ids or IPs. Access is service role only (RLS on, no policies). The rows are erased when an account is deleted, included in "Download my data", and dropped after 13 months by the daily privacy job. The logged-out demo is never recorded.

## Database
Needs migration `supabase/migrations/202610250001_usage_analytics.sql` (**not applied yet; it waits for Jonathan's go**). Until it is applied the app records nothing and behaves as before. I checked the migration and every view on a local Postgres 16 with sample rows.

## Checks
- `tests/usage/analytics.test.js`: 8 new tests, all pass
- Full suite: 1295 pass, 6 fail. These are the known template-studio failures that also fail on main.
- Lint: 0 errors. Build (`--webpack`): green.

author: kingmoonk
body:
## Summary
Collected data stopped reaching the workspace on 2026-10-24: one collected conversation contained U+2028 (line separator), which `json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False)` writes unescaped. `register` read shards with `str.splitlines()`, which splits on it, so `json.loads` raised on half a record. The manager loop swallows errors, and since groups register in sorted order, every later group (here: history) was stuck behind it too.

## Changes
- `studio_collect/register.py`: split shard files on `"\n"` only.
- `studio_collect/store.py`: the journal tail does the same.
- `tests/test_collect_hub.py`: a record with U+2028 registers as one record.

## Testing
- `tasks.py test tests.test_collect_hub tests.test_collect_qa tests.test_api_collect`: 44 OK; the new test fails on the old code.

## Limitations
- A failure in one group still blocks the groups after it, and the manager hides the error; that is tracked separately.

author: jcollier0120
body:
An urgent kit fix should reach the staff in minutes. Kit 2.136.1 (#430, entry "**Urgent fix:") merged at 03:44Z on 2026-10-25. Clerk 0.5.84, Manor 0.17.34 and the rest released at 14:10Z, with the 14:00Z build. It was held up in three places:

1. **The urgent build took no kit.** `kitRides` is false for `by: 'urgent'`, so the rollout never ran between builds.
2. **It closed while the kit was tried.** The Steward's urgent build closed with "the newest kit waits for the next build" while main's kit was still on trial, so it released nothing.
3. **The agents' entries weren't urgent.** Each agent's kit-bump entry had a plain bold line, so even after the rollout nothing would have built the agents between builds.

## What changes

- **`stages/urgent.ts`**: the urgent rule also reads `kit/CHANGELOG.md` and `kit/changes/`, so an urgent kit merged alone begins the Steward's urgent build.
- **`pipeline.ts`**:
  - `kitRides(..., { urgentKit })` lets an urgent build roll out a kit that is itself urgent. Signing builds still don't.
  - The new `kitStep` makes the Steward's urgent build wait for its kit's trial and whole suite instead of closing.
- **`steward.ts`**:
  - In the Steward's urgent build, `urgentKit` checks whether the newest kit brings an urgent kit.
  - If it does, the rollout reaches every employee, not only the build's.
  - The build then closes with `out.soon` set, so the next round (two minutes later) runs `urgentBetween` and begins each agent's urgent build.
- **`bump.ts` `kitBumpEntry`**:
  - A bump that brings an urgent kit writes `**Urgent fix: it carries the Steward's kit X, with an urgent fix to the parts every agent of the manor shares.**`.
  - A newer plain kit that brings it names the urgent kit or kits in brackets.
  - A later plain kit stays as before.
- **`rollout.ts` / `trialpass.ts`**: the bump reads the kit's whole changelog at `refs/tags/kit-v<kit>` (`releasedChangelog`), so it sees urgent kits never released on their own. The release body holds only the newest entry.
- `urgentIn` and the new `urgentKits` move to `kitfiles.ts`, which avoids a bump ↔ rollout import cycle.
- Help texts (page, CLI, settings) and `kit/spec/RELEASE-NOTES.md` say so. Kit 2.136.4 is a docs-only kit change.

## How long it takes now

- Merge to the agents' releases is about 15–30 minutes, plus up to one round interval (10 min) for the first round to notice the merge.
- That's the kit's trial and whole suite (~8 min), the kit and Steward releases, the rollout (~4 min), a 2-minute gap, then each agent's urgent build and release, sent to customers at once (`urgentNote`).
- Manor's install follows on its usual update check.

## Tests

- `test/urgent-kit.test.ts` runs whole rounds:
  - The Steward's urgent build with an urgent kit: the kit is released and rolled out to Other, whose entry `isUrgent`. The build closes with `soon`, and Other isn't released in it.
  - The next round begins Other's urgent build and releases it.
  - A later plain kit under the Steward's urgent fix is released but left to the next build.
- Unit tests:
  - `bump.test.ts`: urgent, several urgent kits, a later plain kit, a step back.
  - `pipeline.test.ts`: `kitRides` with `urgentKit`, `kitStep`.
  - `rollout.test.ts`: `urgentKits`, `urgentKit` against the rolled record.
- Full suite: 2024 passed, typecheck clean.

Yukon submission `291505c5-5dce-4448-a2d9-3042e521c3c9` against https://github.com/Layr-Labs/cudafast-nemotron35-lightning-30b-a3b-engine at `2f32264c091e9f3d0b468fc0b5664bc87acbce9a`.

Current best score: 2.40852225230848. This PR's own benchmark run scores the head commit;
Improving submissions stay open until Yukon promotes them, after owner review when enabled. Other results are closed.

---

**Submitter note**

Model: GPT 6 Astra
Harness: Codex

# Same-budget tile-prefix and exception-tail L2 prefetch for lossless compressed Mamba out projections, retaining original arithmetic and synchronization.

Effort: ultra. Implemented and reviewed with GPT 6 Astra in Codex.

## Objective and exact source provenance

The benchmark is native Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B NVFP4 on the official
DGX Spark CUDA track. The checkout HEAD is `2f32264c091e9f3d0b468fc0b5664bc87acbce9a`.
At the start of this experiment the promoted source was fc04335b, with official
score 2.40852225230848 and a further 75-basis-point promotion requirement.
The source is checked again immediately before the upload; this note does not
claim that a historical score or a local CPU result predicts our official score.

Before this delta we imported the complete public carrier
`b91cd8e6-5d46-4cc9-95b6-47e5d2e3b6bd`, source `4a9392a396d15249ae8e769c7f461a24bfba8bb8`.
Its official correctness passed and its complete score was
2.42055983841207; it was not promoted. All eleven differing files
were initially compared byte for byte with that commit. Our changes below were
then added. The inherited stack contains the promoted lossless fp8c/nvsc paths,
the earlier four-piece decode composition, grouped native MTP up/compact-down,
the existing shared-down launcher and the scoped single-token prefill-lite path.
Those inherited mechanisms and their original source credits remain intact.
Their whole measured result is evidence for the carrier, not an isolated benefit
claim for each inherited component or for our new change.

## New method: distribute a fixed cache-prefetch budget by consumer tile

The promoted fp8c representation is tile-major. A Mamba out projection has
84 output tiles, each consumed by a projection CTA. The inherited prefetch reads
one contiguous head of this compressed buffer. With the existing five-MiB Mamba
window and the next-router reservation, that head covers only a leading subset
of consumer tiles. The proposal distributes no more than the same projection
byte budget over all 84 tiles, so every CTA can find its initial compressed
chunks and exception bytes in cache. This is a scheduling/cache hypothesis,
not a change to the FP8 decoder, weights, MMA chain or numerical result.

Each verified out-projection tile contains a 384-byte header, 32 main chunks
of 3,584 bytes, and an exception tail with padding. Its exception tail starts
at byte 115,072. The original fp8c admission limits the encoded ratio to 93%
of the raw tensor, giving accepted aligned tile strides from 115,200 through
121,856. The producer now attaches versioned layout metadata only after its
existing native decoder has compared every encoded weight byte with the source.
The prefetch guard checks that metadata, the exact storage pointer, CUDA byte
dtype, contiguity, shape, stride, alignment and total storage size. Copies or
views without that exact producer marker keep the original prefetch.

For a valid tile layout, divide the available projection budget by 84, round
down to aligned units, reserve the entire exception tail and header, then use
the remaining allowance for a whole number of main chunks. At least six chunks
must fit, covering every supported initial ring depth; otherwise use the old
contiguous policy. The header/main prefix ends at or before the exception-tail
start. The two ranges therefore do not overlap, and their combined size across
all tiles never exceeds the previous projection budget. Prefetching only the
main prefix would be insufficient because an early compressed chunk can need
raw escape bytes from the tail; those bytes are deliberately included.

The native helper issues only the existing cp.async.bulk.prefetch.L2.global
cache hints. It performs no stores and does not produce a model tensor. It uses
the same one-CTA, 128-thread launch geometry, the same side-stream fork, the same
router reservation and the caller's existing join before the projection. Each
request is split into aligned pieces of at most 64 KiB, as required by the
existing instruction. Mamba in projections, attention prefetch, MoE prefetch,
the uncompressed fallback and calls above eight rows keep their original path.

The ABI addition is optional. A Python module or library without it keeps the
original contiguous prefetch. If the optional native code cannot compile, the
build retries with that addition disabled and preserves the original library
entry points. Once a supported production launch is selected, a launch error
propagates; it is not hidden by a second asynchronous launch. L2PF_FP8C_TILES=0
disables this policy, and the existing L2PF=0 still disables all prefetch.

Eight focused CPU tests pass. They exercise 1,431 exact range plans over all
53 legal aligned strides and 27 budget boundaries, including unsupported and
small budgets. They check total bytes, disjointness, address alignment, bounds,
six-chunk minimum and the native request-size limit. The actual Mamba dispatch
is checked for compressed-only small calls, raw/disabled/old-library fallbacks,
the ten-argument ABI, prefetch-before-convolution and join ordering, and launch
errors without duplicate submission. These are arithmetic and dispatch tests;
the new CUDA prefetch kernel has not executed locally.

The expected benefit is fewer cold consumer CTAs and a shorter final completion
tail. Costs may include more prefetch instructions, a different cache-replacement
pattern, earlier eviction of useful bytes, and contention with the shared router
range. Equal byte budgets do not prove equal elapsed time or cache-hit rates.
The official full-model result is needed; no speedup or occupancy is claimed.


## Actual local validation and its limits

Development and CPU verification used an x86 environment with Python 3.12,
CPU PyTorch and the repository's Rust adapter. There is no local DGX Spark,
no local GPU model execution, and no local full-model timing for this archive.
The model checkpoint and paid cloud compute were not provisioned for this work.
GPU compiler compatibility, full-model correctness, admitted-path engagement and
the paired score must be established by the official runner. No unsupported
local speedup is submitted as a claimed score.

| Check | Observed local result |
|---|---|
| Rust formatting | passed |
| Clippy, all targets, warnings denied | passed |
| Rust adapter tests | 88 passed |
| Release adapter build | passed |
| Resident Python suite | 78 total; 74 passed; 4 skipped |
| apk12 host fragment decoder | 352,256 register comparisons, zero mismatches |
| Changed Python source parsing | passed |
| Manifest lint | passed |
| Preflight-only | passed |
| Whole editable-surface static review | passed |
| Diff whitespace, source-path and byte-budget verification | passed |

The four skipped resident cases need an importable full vLLM runtime. The new
CPU tests exercise actual source guards/dispatch and controlled model/graph
doubles where appropriate. They do not execute CUDA kernels. The apk12 test
compiles its host decoder and verifies the carried packed-fragment addressing;
it does not time or validate the CUDA GEMM. Preflight-only checks configuration
and packaging, not GPU inference. Inherited GPU admissions are retained and
remain distinct from the CPU evidence above.

Reproduce the local checks with the documented repository commands:

```bash
cargo fmt --manifest-path harness/protocol-adapter/Cargo.toml -- --check
cargo clippy --manifest-path harness/protocol-adapter/Cargo.toml --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --manifest-pat

author: max-code-menace
body:
Préparation de la bascule d'Ubique : copier sa base vers Clever Cloud sans rien perdre, et le prouver. Rien ne change dans les écrans.

## Ce qui est ajouté
- **`cargo run -- base empreinte <fichier>`** : l'empreinte de toute la base. Pour chaque table, le nombre de lignes et une empreinte de leur contenu ; les tables de données organisation par organisation (lues par le compte ordinaire, sans droit spécial) ; puis les compteurs internes et la structure (règles par organisation, déclencheurs qui figent les factures, liens, index). Deux bases au contenu identique donnent le même fichier. Une table de données qui aurait perdu sa protection est signalée. Servira aussi à vérifier une restauration de sauvegarde (étape 7-4).
- **`scripts/transfert-vers-clever.ps1`** : chez Clever Cloud, le compte de la base est ordinaire et ne peut pas recharger d'un coup les lignes de toutes les organisations (protection forcée). Le script recrée la base en trois temps (structure, données, puis index, liens, déclencheurs et règles), lève la protection le temps du chargement et la remet, puis compare l'empreinte de la copie à celle de l'origine. Il refuse une base cible qui n'est pas vide.
- **Procédure du jour J** dans `docs/mise-en-ligne.md`.

## Essayé sur ce PC
Deux bases jetables (la vitrine dans une organisation, une deuxième organisation à côté ; sauvegarde de 731 Ko) : **transfert réussi, copie identique** sur 137 lignes d'empreinte (35 tables protégées sur 35, 37 règles, 7 déclencheurs, 104 liens, 147 index, 40 compteurs) ; refus d'une cible non vide vérifié. Bases d'essai supprimées ensuite.

**Limite** : sans le mot de passe du compte `postgres` sur ce PC, la sauvegarde d'essai a été faite par le compte ordinaire (protection levée quelques secondes sur la base d'origine). La vraie sauvegarde (par `postgres`, chez franc) garde la protection, ce que le script prend en charge. À refaire une fois chez franc avec la vraie sauvegarde, vers une base d'essai de Clever Cloud, avant le jour J.

`cargo build` sans avertissement, `cargo test` : 516 réussis, 0 échec.

author: rvdbreemen
body:
## What

TASK-097, ADR-036 (Accepted 2026-10-25 on Robert's yes).

The library (`myscribe.db`, media, models, work, the app's log) is now asked for apart from the program and the speech engine.

- **Windows installer.** A library page comes after the program folder and is prefilled with `%LOCALAPPDATA%\MyScribe`. A silent install takes `/LIBRARY=<folder>`. The page writes `"library_request"` into `MyScribe.location`, but only when that file does not exist and `%LOCALAPPDATA%\MyScribe\env` does not either. An update therefore keeps what is there. Uninstall deletes neither the library nor the pointer.
- **macOS and Linux.** The first start asks the same question, with the same default, before anything is downloaded.
- **`locate_library` in the launcher** settles the request before the download:
  - The default left as it was prefilled gives today's layout (`<home>/data`), and no `"data"` is written.
  - An empty or new folder becomes the library and is written as `"data"`.
  - A folder with other files gets a `MyScribe` subfolder.
  - A folder that holds `myscribe.db` or `scribe.db` (itself or its `data\`, as in a former home) is handed to the engine. The engine shows its numbers and adopts it only when chosen (ADR-019, amended for a new empty library only).
  - Anything else is refused with a sentence.
- **This round: Robert's answer to ADR-036's open question (2026-10-25).** A door without a window (at login, or from the console) whose request cannot be used no longer stops. It starts on `<home>\data` and says the folder asked for was not used. What happens to the request after that:
  - It stays in `MyScribe.location`.
  - While no setup sitting has ended, the next start with its window asks the question again with the refusal's sentence. That question also says the library already in `<home>\data` stays where it is. Closing the question keeps the default and drops the request.
  - A start without a window says the same thing again.
  - Once a sitting has ended, the request is dropped with the existing "is not used and nothing was moved" sentence.
- **The engine always goes to the per-user home.** `--home` and `MYSCRIBE_HOME` still put it elsewhere, and a request is not read under them.
- **Disk check.** It asks the home's volume for the environment and the library's volume for the weights and working room.
- **Merge with origin/main.** `myscribe.iss` `CurStepChanged` keeps both the library-request write and main's add-to-PATH task. The ADR indexes were regenerated with `adr-index`, and `--check` exits 0.

## Evidence

**This round (red first).** `tests/test_launcher_library_request.py` was changed before the code. The three headless refused-request tests (five cases) now expect a start on `<home>/data` with the request kept. Four tests were added for the next start.
- Red: `7 failed, 30 passed`.
- After the change: `37 passed`.
- The two guards that already passed on the red run were "closing the question drops the request" and "dropped once a sitting has ended".

**Real run of the changed door.** The task's earlier harness, `run8-097-harness.py`, was copied to `run9-097-harness.py` and run on scratch folders on port 4510.
- Setup: a pointer written byte for byte the way the installer's Pascal writes it, naming a `D\Data` that holds other files and a `MyScribe` subfolder that also holds other files.
- `main --headless` result:
  - It reported the refusal, then "MyScribe starts with its library in …\local\MyScribe\data: the library folder asked for, …\D\Data, was not used. The request stays in …\MyScribe.location …".
  - The real app started, and `/health data_dir` was `…\local\MyScribe\data` with `myscribe.db` in it.
  - `main exit = 0`, and the pointer afterwards still held `library_request`.
  - `D\` held the same four entries before and after.
- In round 8 the same scenario logged "MyScribe cannot start: … asks for a library folder it cannot use".
- Stand-ins: no sync (the env is a junction to the repo venv), `run_prove` skipped, and the headless door replaced by the window's `first_run` with a scripted ask so the real app starts.

**Earlier rounds' real runs (round 8, same harness, scratch folders, synthetic libraries).**

| Scenario | Pointer afterwards | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `empty` | `"data"` = the chosen folder | `myscribe.db` made there |
| `new` | `"data"` = `D\Data\MyScribe` | |
| `other-files` | `"data"` = `D\Data\MyScribe` | `taxes-2025.pdf` left beside it |
| `existing-db` | `"data"` = the chosen folder | engine logged "now uses the library at …\D\OldLibrary (3 recordings), migrated in place" |
| `former-home` | `"data"` = `D\Data\MyScribe\data` | engine logged "(2 recordings), migrated in place" |
| `default`, `default-twice` | `library_request` = the default home, no `"data"` | library in `<home>\data` |

**ISCC.** It compiled the installer script (`myscribe-097-compile-only.exe` in the round's scratch output).

**Test files run one at a time this round** (`.venv/Scripts/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider <file>`), all exit 0:

| File | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_launcher_library_request.py` | 37 passed |
| `test_installer_library_page.py` | 9 passed |
| `test_setup_library.py` | 23 passed |
| `test_launcher_library.py` | 12 passed |
| `test_launcher_sitting.py` | 80 passed |
| `test_env.py` | 43 passed, 8 skipped |
| `test_autostart.py` | 94 passed |
| `test_web_settings.py` | 71 passed |
| `test_uninstall_text.py` | 11 passed |
| `test_setup_plan.py` | 185 passed |
| `test_app.py` | 34 passed |
| `test_launcher.py` | 200 passed, 12 skipped |

In round 2, `test_launcher.py` had one failure, `test_a_window_holds_the_lock_only_while_its_myscribe_runs[failed]`, with Tk's "Can't find a usable tk.tcl" from `C:\Python312`. It did not recur in this round's run.

**ADRs.**
- `adr-lint --strict docs/adr`: "All linted ADRs pass", exit 0.
- `adr-index --check`: exit 0.
- ADR-036's open question is answered with Robert's recorded decision of 2026-10-25, then accepted with `adr accept … --changed-by "Robert van den Breemen (said yes in session 2026-10-25; recorded by Claude)"`.
- No other ADR gained a status_history entry on this branch. ADR-019 only gains a `related: ADR-036` link.

## Not verified

- **A real install on this laptop with the library on `D:\Data\MyScribe` (AC #7).** Not done. Every run used scratch folders, and Robert's install, `D:\Data\MyScribe` and port 4242 were not touched. Installing the release `.exe` in Windows Sandbox is still to do.
- **The installer page in a running installer.** It has not been clicked through. The `.iss` was checked by tests that read it and by an ISCC compile only.
- **macOS and Linux.** The first-start question is covered by tests only, with no run on either OS.
- **The windowed re-ask over a request a headless start kept.** Covered by unit tests only, with no real Tk dialog. In that path the person can move to a new folder away from a `<home>\data` library that a login start may already have filled. The question names that library and leaves it in place. This is recorded as a negative consequence in ADR-036.
- **The full suite.** Not run in one go. Only the files listed above were run.

https://claude.ai/code/session_012QTdQ595hwSHo8VjnWPR3R

## What was wrong
Tapping a subregion on the globe (Italy, Germany, Sweden, …) gave no popup, while the US and Canada worked. The tap handler asked MapLibre for the features under the finger in two layers at once: the hidden **Raised** 3D layer (fill-extrusion) and the flat fill. On the globe projection, a query that includes the fill-extrusion layer comes back empty for much of the eastern hemisphere once the map has moved, so nothing opened.

## Fix
`js/globe.js` now looks each layer up on its own. It tries the raised blocks first, but only while they're shown, then the flat fill. `globe.html` bumps `globe.js` to `?v=20261025`.

## Checked
I ran a headless Chromium test that fires taps at Tuscany, Bavaria, Uppsala, Lombardy, Skåne and Hesse from two camera positions, with Raised both on and off:
- The old two-layer lookup returned **0** features at every European point.
- The new lookup returns the region every time, and the popup opens (for example "Bavaria" and "Skåne", or the city pin when one sits under the tap).
- US points behave as before.

author: jordanhoare
body:
## Summary

Two commits on `docs/about.md` and `docs/internal/architecture.md`.

`0ebea4e` carries review fixes that missed the earlier merge: the application sends its own email and Supabase only mints the links, the public pages include the API routes they need, "identity-provider token" is the one term for that concept, native clients get their own native session, and the header test folds into one header model.

`136d62b` re-homes the design in RFC 10017 and names the password-grant trade-off:

```diff
 architecture.md
-  "not the IETF's BFF to the letter ... delivers the BFF's properties without a proxy layer"
+  section 7.1, single-domain browser-based application not using OAuth, is this shape
+  its threat analysis leaves one attack, the same one the BFF leaves
+  section 7.1 sits under "Discouraged and Deprecated Architecture Patterns"; its warning is against OAuth replacing session management
+  sign-in posts the password to Supabase's token endpoint: the ROPC shape, the 7.1 exemption, the redirect-flow cost, no logging of those bodies
-  "the only thing that holds a credential worth stealing"
+  "the only thing that holds a secret"
 about.md
-  "the protections of the backend-for-frontend arrangement ... without a proxy layer"
+  the single-domain shape section 7.1 describes, with the BFF's one remaining attack
```

RFC 10017 lines relied on:

- §7.1: "Too often, simple applications are made needlessly complex by using OAuth to replace the concept of session management."
- §7.1: "Instead of using access tokens, the application can rely on server-side cookie-based session state to keep track of the user's authentication status. The security guidelines to protect the session cookie are discussed in Section 6.1.3.2."
- §7.1.1: "Due to the lack of using OAuth, this architecture pattern is only vulnerable to the following attack scenario: proxying requests via the user's browser (Section 5.1.4)."
- §6.1.4.3 (BFF): "The only viable attack pattern is hijacking the client application in the user's browser"
- §7: "This section discusses a few alternative architecture patterns, which are not recommended for use in modern browser-based OAuth applications."

author: deeem2031
body:
On QWERTZ keyboards, "QWERTZ Single" binds E and F to `;` and `'`. On German keyboards these need Shift, so E and F can't be played. Other QWERTZ variants (Czech, Slovak, Hungarian and so on) put different characters on the keys right of "L" and on the number row.

- **QWERTZ Single:** the two keys right of "L" now use the characters of the current layout:

  | Layout | Keys |
  |---|---|
  | German, Austrian, Swiss German | ö ä |
  | Swiss French | é à |
  | Czech | ů § |
  | Slovak | ô § |
  | Hungarian | é á |
  | Polish | ł ą |
  | Croatian, Slovenian, Bosnian, Serbian Latin | č ć |
- **QWERTZ:** the Czech and Slovak number rows are supported (ě/ľ š ř/ť ž ý í é). On Hungarian keyboards, "ö" takes the place of "0".
- **Key labels:** these now use `g_unichar_to_utf8()` instead of `"%lc"`, which depends on the C locale and showed "?" for non-ASCII keys on Windows.
- **ydk (Windows):** `gdk_keymap_get_entries_for_keyval (NULL, ...)` passed the NULL keymap on to `update_keymap()` and crashed.

The layout is detected with `gdk_keymap_get_entries_for_keyval()` at group 0 and level 0. That's the same lookup `PianoKeyBindings::get_keycode()` uses.

**Testing**
- Built natively on Windows 10 (MSYS2 UCRT64, GCC 16). On a German layout, Ö and Ä play E and F, and the piano keys show Ö and Ä as labels.
- Checked the selection logic against the Windows layout tables (`kbd*.dll`) of all the layouts listed above. The chosen keys match the physical keys.
- Not tested on Linux or macOS.

author: diam0ndnex
body:
## Summary

This continues the SceneBox-to-CineNex streaming integration with a focused, independently reviewable playback scheduling batch:

- Extend the CI-applied XITRIX bridge with bounds-checked `setPieceDeadline` and `clearPieceDeadlineAt` methods backed by libtorrent's native piece-deadline API.
- Schedule the exact pieces needed for each AVPlayer byte-range read in playback order, with 80 ms increments capped at 60 seconds.
- Clear stale deadlines when the requested playback range moves, avoiding abandoned urgent pieces competing with current playback.
- Add a pure deadline planner and tests for ordering, empty ranges, invalid coordinates, and delay bounds.
- Update the native bridge and streaming architecture documentation.

CI must validate the wrapper patcher, compile the patched native wrapper for device and simulator, build CineNex, and run the full unit-test suite before this is considered complete.

body:
Les retours vers les classes et les unités sont incomplets, les sommaires de 5E4 affichent la Lesson C et les reprises de certains exercices effacent toute la page. Cette PR rétablit les parcours sur les 24 pages et utilise un moteur commun pour les 13 leçons, en conservant les URL existantes et les 50 exercices principaux.

Les banques restent dans chaque classe. Le moteur accepte les variantes de réponse repérées dans l’audit, distingue les formulations non reconnues des erreurs certaines, retire les doublons et sauvegarde les questions, saisies et tentatives dans le navigateur. Les champs disposent de libellés, de retours associés et de zones de statut ; chaque reprise reste limitée à l’exercice concerné.

Validation :

- 23 tests passent : navigation sous deux préfixes, banques, correction, interactions sur adaptateur DOM et sauvegarde.
- Un contrôle de présence de l’image d’Emma est ignoré dans la copie textuelle locale ; le fichier binaire existant est conservé et la CI vérifie sa présence dans un checkout complet.
- Chromium ne démarre pas dans cet environnement : le rendu visuel et le parcours dans un navigateur restent à vérifier.

Le workflow ajouté exécute les tests sans déployer le site.

I could tell you that this is the biggest release TREK has ever had. Read **Changed** before you update: TREK copies your database before it touches it and needs the free space for that copy.

##### Added (Highlights)

##### Tours

Tours is a new addon for planning trips you make under your own power, or on skis or a horse, with each tour saved as part of the trip: hikes, bike tours, runs, rides, paddle tours, city walks and ski or winter tours. It is on for every install until an admin turns it off, and it works on desktop, on the phone and offline. ([#​2586](https://redirect.github.com/liketrek/TREK/pull/2586), [#​2662](https://redirect.github.com/liketrek/TREK/pull/2662), [#​2684](https://redirect.github.com/liketrek/TREK/pull/2684), [#​2687](https://redirect.github.com/liketrek/TREK/pull/2687), [#​2691](https://redirect.github.com/liketrek/TREK/pull/2691), [#​2693](https://redirect.github.com/liketrek/TREK/pull/2693))

![A hike around the Tre Cime in the Dolomites: the huts of the trip as waypoints, the route on the topo map with its elevation profile, and its SAC grades along the way](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/liketrek/TREK/233227f9c3a2559dbb2f497784014e6d7e4e14a5/docs/media/tours-demo.webp)

[Watch it as a video](https://redirect.github.com/liketrek/TREK/releases/download/v5.0.0/trek-5-tours-demo.mp4)

**Planning**

- Draw a route on a topo map, drag its waypoints or reorder them in the sidebar, and undo every change. Each tour type comes with maps of its own, and OpenHikingMap is there for hikes.
- Each tour shows its elevation profile, distance, climb and a walking time worked out from the hiking rule. Breaks and extra time can be added, and the planned duration adjusted by hand.
- Hikes get a difficulty grade from T1 to T6, and the planner shows known SAC grades, surfaces and kinds of way along the route. Open the 3D terrain view and start a flyover coloured by grade.
- A hike can avoid steps or ferries, prefer footpaths and choose shorter over faster. **Other ways** compares alternatives for one section, and a round hike of a length you ask for can be suggested from a stop.
- Via ferratas appear on the map in 2D and 3D, can be added as fixed legs, and warn you when a route crosses one.
- A tour can run over several days in stages, each on a day of its own. Any tour can be reversed or led back to its start, and **Save as new tour** makes an independent copy.
- The search along a tour finds places near the line and puts the best known ones first with a star, ranked by how often their Wikipedia articles are read.
- On a day, a hike shows sunrise, sunset, the weather and any warnings. Give a tour a start time and TREK works out when it ends.

**Every kind of tour**

- Bike tours are planned for a profile (touring, road, gravel or mountain bike) on CyclOSM, with surfaces, kinds of way and, on a mountain bike, trail grades. They can also find e-bike charging points along the route.
- Runs are planned at your own pace and shown in your distance unit, and a trail run keeps to forest tracks and natural paths. Rides on horseback are put together from signposted horse routes, and a ride recorded as a GPX file can be kept exactly as it was ridden.
- Paddle tours for kayak, canoe and SUP are routed on the water, or drawn freely across a lake, with OpenSeaMap seamarks on top. They mark portages and locks, estimate time on the water, carrying and waiting, and show the wind at the start.
- For the regions an admin adds, a paddle tour shows weirs, locks, put-ins and boating rules from OpenStreetMap, with a checklist that asks you to decide on each obstacle and asks again when the data changes.
- City walks plan sights on foot, with a length of stay and an importance for each stop, checked against opening hours for the day. A walk can be filled from a theme (culture, parks, food or a bit of everything) or from a Google Maps walking link.
- On the day, you check off a city walk stop by stop, offline too, and see how much walking time is left. Between two walks on the same day, the day plan offers public transit.
- Ski and winter tours cover alpine skiing, snowboarding, cross-country, ski touring, snowshoeing and winter hiking, routed over runs, lifts and trails on a piste map. When a ski leg cannot be routed, the planner names the one change that would make it work.

**On the trip**

- The trip shows tour totals by type above the tour list, which can be filtered by source, routing limit and type. Each person can hide single tours from the trip map.
- A tour keeps the track it was actually done with and compares it with the plan, in its values and on the map. The Atlas adds up the tours you have done, by period and by type.
- A tour can point at the trip's packing list. Changes saved by someone else arrive live, and TREK asks before overwriting what you are editing.
- Whole tours can be kept in collections and taken from there, or from another trip, into any trip.

**Importing and sharing**

- GPX, KML and KMZ files import as tours with a preview first, and a GPX file can be dropped straight onto the map or a day. An imported track can be turned into an editable tour, and you can still go back to the recorded track.
- Every tour remembers where it came from: planned in TREK, a GPX file, or a wanderer trail. Once an admin allows it, each user can connect their own wanderer instance under Integrations and reimport trails that changed.
- A saved tour can be downloaded as a GPX file or shared through your device's share sheet. One **Add tour** menu plans, imports or takes over a tour.

**Admin, MCP and the assistant**

- Admins control Tours under Admin, Addons, with switches for wanderer trails and the piste router and a panel for the regions whose paddle water data is loaded.
- MCP can list a trip's tours, read a tour's whole saved plan, and prepare, save and undo changes to a city walk.
- The assistant plans and saves every tour type, including multi-day hikes in stages and round hikes of a length you choose. It edits saved tours, reads route files dropped on the chat, checks off city walk stops and works with wanderer trails. ([#​2698](https://redirect.github.com/liketrek/TREK/pull/2698))

##### TREK Studio

TREK Studio, the photo book designer in Journey, grew from a layout tool into a full design studio in 5.0.0. Typefaces, themes, stickers, templates, photo effects and the Travel tab are all new or rebuilt, and the assistant can now design a whole book with you.
