author: danielbuva
body:
The Android embedded Python has no os.link, so receipt-validated native continuation previously failed before compiling. Reuse now copies and checks persisted object size/hash when that API is absent, retaining hard links elsewhere and preserving the failed original output.

J1167 records representative compile timings; J1168 records the failed continuation and compatibility fix. No complete phone native library, new game APK or gameplay qualification is claimed. Validation: 48 focused owner-code tests; 498-prefix reuse, low-space/corrupt-copy/link-error refusals; Ruff and manual public provenance review. Fresh-clone pre-push and exact-head CI must pass before merge.

author: nomanmediamonitors
body:
## Purpose

Resolves every npm advisory that can be fixed without a semver-major upgrade, across all three applications. **Lockfile-only — no `package.json` manifest is touched.**

Issue #13 tracked "2 high + 1 moderate" in the backend. That is confirmed, and all three are in the **production** tree (`npm audit --omit=dev` keeps all three). Auditing the other two apps — which had not been audited before — surfaced **two further high-severity advisories** that were untracked.

Stacked on #14. Base is `fix/frontend-lockfile`, because the frontend bump sits on top of that lockfile repair. Once #14 merges, GitHub retargets this to `migration/hattech-fullstack-2026-10-24` automatically.

## Changes

| App | Package | Severity | Advisory | Prod-exploitable? | Bump |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `backend` | `body-parser` | **High** · CVSS 7.5 · CWE-248 | [GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828) | **Yes** | 1.20.8 → 1.20.9 |
| `backend` | `nodemailer` | **Moderate** · CVSS 6.5 · CWE-20/436 | [GHSA-8c8m-p3m8-cjg8](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8c8m-p3m8-cjg8), [GHSA-m943-m63m-w62w](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-m943-m63m-w62w), [GHSA-85x2-q946-cp5h](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-85x2-q946-cp5h) | **Yes** | 10.1.1 → 10.2.1 |
| `frontend` | `zod` | High | [GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5) | No — dev only | 4.4.3 → 4.6.7 |
| `dashboard` | `vite` | High | [GHSA-9jrq-w75r-8gcw](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9jrq-w75r-8gcw), [GHSA-rq7h-c2jc-7f22](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rq7h-c2jc-7f22) + 3 `launch-editor` advisories | No — dev only | 6.4.3 → 6.4.5 |

Also fills in six missing `inBundle` entries under `dashboard`'s `@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi` — see the lockfile-gap note below.

### Why each bump is safe

**`body-parser` needs no `express` change.** `express@4.22.3` declares `body-parser: ~1.20.5`, i.e. `>=1.20.5 <1.21.0`. The patched 1.20.9 satisfies that range, so this is a pure lockfile bump — no `overrides` entry and no express major upgrade. The vulnerability is a remote, unauthenticated, pre-auth DoS on any route that parses a request body.

**`nodemailer` matters more than "moderate" suggests.** These are not cosmetic parser bugs: a crafted address can cause delivery to a domain the header does not name. The backend sends mail driven by the public contact flow, so attacker-influenced address strings reach `addressparser` directly. Patched inside the existing `^10.1.1` range.

**`frontend` zod and `dashboard` vite are both dev-only**, each confirmed by `npm audit --omit=dev` returning 0 vulnerabilities:
- The frontend `zod` is transitive via `eslint-config-next → eslint-plugin-react-hooks` — lint tooling, absent from the production tree. It is a *different* instance from the backend's zod and needed no major bump.
- The `vite` advisories affect the dev server and the `launch-editor` error overlay. `vite build` emits static assets; the vulnerable paths never ship. Still worth patching — the `launch-editor` arbitrary-command-execution issues target developer machines.

Every added or changed integrity hash was verified against registry metadata: `body-parser@1.20.9`, `nodemailer@10.2.1`, plus `@emnapi/runtime@1.11.3` and `@emnapi/core@1.11.3` inherited from #14.

## Deliberately excluded: backend `zod`

`backend` keeps `zod@3.25.76` with [GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5) (**high**, CVSS 7.5, CWE-770 — memory exhaustion validating oversized constrained collections) **unpatched in this PR**.

The advisory range is `<4.6.6`, so **all of zod 3.x is vulnerable and no 3.x patch exists.** The only upgrade path is 3 → 4, a semver-major on a production dependency. `npm audit fix --force` would have done it silently; it was not run.

Costed against the actual source rather than estimated. zod appears in 6 files with a narrow API surface (`z.string` ×72, `z.object` ×12, `z.enum` ×8, `z.boolean` ×8, `z.infer` ×7, `z.array` ×6, plus single uses of `z.literal`, `z.union`, `z.preprocess`, `z.number`, `z.discriminatedUnion`). Breakage:

| Site | Change | Severity |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend/src/middleware/error.middleware.ts:16` — `err.errors.map(...)` | → `err.issues` (renamed in v4) | **Hard break — required** |
| `.email()` ×2, `.url()` ×5 | Deprecated for top-level `z.email()` / `z.url()`; still functional | Soft |
| `backend/src/types/community.types.ts:67` — `{ message: ... }` | `message` → `error`; `message` still accepted | Soft |

So the real cost is **one required line change plus ~8 optional deprecation cleanups** — considerably smaller than "breaking change" implies. Recommend doing it as its own small PR gated on `test:security`, rather than leaving a CVSS 7.5 memory-exhaustion vector in the request-validation layer of a payment backend. Flagging for a release-authority decision rather than bundling a major into an otherwise non-breaking PR.

## Verification

`node_modules` deleted before each install; all three apps installed with `--ignore-scripts`.

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm --prefix backend ci` | **exit 0** |
| `npm --prefix frontend ci` | **exit 0** |
| `npm --prefix dashboard ci` | **exit 0** |
| `npm --prefix backend run test:security` | **7/7 pass, 0 fail** |
| `npm --prefix backend run build` (`tsc`) | **exit 0** |
| `npm --prefix frontend run build -- --webpack` | **exit 0**, 36 routes |
| `npm --prefix dashboard run build` (`tsc -b && vite build`) | **exit 0**, 1838 modules |

All 7 security tests pass against the **patched** dependency tree — HTML escaping, NoSQL/object input rejection, fail-closed DB behaviour, JWT algorithm/claim/session pinning, unsigned-webhook rejection, immutable session updates, and paid-webhook idempotency with amount-tampering rejection.

**Resulting audit state:**

| App | All deps | Production only |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `backend` | 1 high (zod, deferred above) | 1 high (zod, deferred above) |
| `frontend` | **0** | **0** |
| `dashboard` | **0** | **0** |

## The esbuild install-script warning is not a vulnerability

Dispositioned as issue #13 asked. The `esbuild@0.28.2` message is npm 11's install-script approval **policy prompt**, which fires on any package declaring a lifecycle script regardless of whether an advisory exists. `npm audit` reports nothing for esbuild.

Stronger result: all three apps were installed with `--ignore-scripts` and everything still worked — including `backend test:security`, which runs under `tsx`, an esbuild consumer. **No install script needs approval anywhere in this repo to install, test or build it.** Recommend `--ignore-scripts` as a standing supply-chain control in CI, which makes the approval question moot rather than merely answered. Suggested for the CI scaffolding in #11.

## Lockfile gap in `dashboard`

The lockfile-only pass added six missing `inBundle` entries under `dashboard`'s `@tailwindcss/oxide-wasm32-wasi` (`@emnapi/core`, `@emnapi/runtime`, `@emnapi/wasi-threads`, `@napi-rs/wasm-runtime`, `@tybys/wasm-util`, `tslib`) — the *same* wasm subtree that broke the frontend in #14.

The dashboard's `npm ci` passes on npm 10 because only *bundled* nested entries were missing, which npm 10 tolerates; the frontend failed because *top-level hoisted* peer entries were missing, which it does not. **Whether npm 11 is equally tolerant is unverified.** Please run `npm --prefix dashboard ci` on Node 24 / npm 11 specifically before declaring CI green. This PR fills the entries in and should pre-empt it either way.

## Scope and safety

No production release. No DNS, domain, Stripe or MongoDB change. `main` untouched. No secrets, keys, URIs or `.env` contents appear in this PR or its commits.

## Caveat on verification

Everything above ran on **Windows / Node 20.13.1 / npm 10.5.2**, not Linux / Node 24 / npm 11. The lockfile diagnosis is platform-independent since the original failure reproduced there too, but "all 3 buil

author: jnnngs
body:
## Problem

The README told readers to copy a skill folder by hand, and no page a reader sees named an install command. The [plan](roadmap/plans/2026-10-25-skills-install.md) said a published command nobody has run is the failure to avoid, and the run was blocked in the sandbox until the owner allowed it.

## What the run showed

Run on 25 October with `HOME` and the working directory both empty (scratch directories, nothing touched in a real home or in this repository):

* `npx skills add eyupio/zoomies --list` finds **five** skills: the three that ship (`zoomies`, `zoomies-kennel`, `zoomies-optimise`) and `babysit` and `steward` from `.claude/skills`, which are for working on Zoomies and must not reach a user's agent. A bare `eyupio/zoomies` would offer them.
* So the command names the skills: `npx skills add eyupio/zoomies --skill zoomies --skill zoomies-kennel --skill zoomies-optimise`.
* Installing those three wrote them to `.agents/skills/<name>/`, linked each into `.claude/skills/<name>` (the link resolves), wrote `skills-lock.json`, and wrote a second copy under `agent/skills/` with the frontmatter description re-wrapped across lines (the installer's own re-serialisation, same words). The `.agents/skills` files match the repository byte for byte, `reference.md` and `mcp-reference.md` included.
* It installs into the current project. The global form was not run, so the docs do not claim it.

## Approach

* `README.md` and `docs/cli.md` carry the command once each, with the hand route beside it; `docs/ai-context.md` and the Kennel section link to it, and the `zoomies` skill's routing row says the person makes the install.
* `TestTheInstallDocsNameTheCommandAndEveryShippedSkill` holds the README and CLI page to the command, built from the skills actually under `skills/` (a skill added later with no word in the docs fails it), and fails if either page tells a user to install `babysit` or `steward`. Mutation-checked: shortening one `--skill` fails it.
* The owner approved naming the installer in the docs; `internal/provenance` accepts it.
* `ROADMAP.md`, the ZF-233 row in `roadmap/progress.md` and the plan record the run.

## Verification

* `go test -count=1 ./internal/docs/ ./internal/provenance/`
* The install and list runs above, against this repository's `main` as pushed at the time.
* Not run: `mkdocs build --strict` (mkdocs is not installed here, so CI's docs build is the check for the new anchors), a second agent's run of the Kennel skill, and the global install form.

## Impact

- [x] Docs, one test, roadmap records; no code, API or dependency change
- [x] The installer is a third-party tool; the hand route stays beside it so nobody depends on it

author: kotmatrosk1n
body:
## Summary

KM Companion now adapts Team and storage boxes to the space available at the current resolution and display scaling. All six Team Pokémon stay in one row, while storage pages show more than 30 Pokémon when space permits.

## What Changed

`getBoxPageLayout` in `app_workspace.js` derives storage rows and columns from each panel's measured width and height after workspace zoom. Box, Box 2, Compost, and Trash use the additional room on larger layouts while retaining a minimum capacity of 30 for Royal Sword and later generations, or 20 for Generations 1 and 2. Constrained panels select a grid shape that fits the minimum capacity instead of retaining fixed columns and rows.

`updateBoxPage` reserves space for pagination only when it is needed and keeps the previous page's first Pokémon visible when capacity changes. Each box observes its own dimensions so resizing, display scaling, and opening drawer tools refresh the layout. Pages continue to follow the displayed sort order, color updates retain the current page, and changed search matches return to the first page. Existing records and storage formats retain their current meaning.

`app-workspace.css` gives Team six equal columns and sizes its cards and artwork to the available width and height. Animated sprites and visible names remain available, with full details in hover text and accessible labels. Storage uses flexible grid tracks to fill its panel and retains static pixel sprites without visible names. Removing the inherited sprite size limits allows the artwork to follow the resized cards while preserving its proportions, selection, speed borders, and damage colors. Existing card nodes, drag and drop, and assignment actions remain in place.

`docs/app-workspace.md` describes the single Team row, adaptive storage capacity, display scaling, and page retention during resizing. The shared drawer continues to leave the current calculator matchup interactive, and the layout changes preserve profile separation, saved teams, and box contents.

author: stepanssmbatyan94
body:
## What changed

**Camera database** (`scripts/update_speed_cameras.mjs` → `data/speed-cameras.json`, served by `/api/speed-cameras`)
- Was: 185 OSM speed cameras, Yerevan only (20 outside the city), no red-light cameras.
- Now: 498 speed cameras across Armenia (about half outside Yerevan, 389 with a known course) and red-light cameras at 18 junctions.
- Sources: OpenStreetMap (`highway=speed_camera`, `enforcement=traffic_signals`) + SpeedCamOnLine.ru community base "Armenia" (public iGo + CityGuide exports). Dummies (МЛЖ) dropped; duplicates between and within sources merged; on a limit conflict the lower limit is kept and printed; cameras whose limit differs from the road's OSM maxspeed are printed for review.
- OSM `direction` is not trusted (21 of 60 shared cameras point the opposite way to the SpeedCamOnLine course), so OSM-only cameras warn both ways.
- A camera without a known limit is `limit: null`, no longer a default 60.

**Navigation**
- Route and free-driving camera warnings only fire when the travel direction is within 60° of the camera's course (unknown course → both ways).
- Red-light cameras: traffic-light marker with red rim, 🚦 badge, own voice prompt in ru/hy/en; they never set the speed limit.
- Free-driving warnings re-arm 600 m after a camera (before: once per session).
- Removed three hardcoded cameras at rough coordinates; a database arriving after the route is now projected onto it; markers drawn from the projected list (one route × cameras scan per route instead of two, with a bbox prefilter).
- Data credit (OpenStreetMap, SpeedCamOnLine.ru) in the tools menu. Cache busters: index v87, phone v59.

## Licence note
SpeedCamOnLine.ru requires attribution (added) and allows commercial use only with the owner's permission. `node scripts/update_speed_cameras.mjs --osm-only` rebuilds the file without it.

## Verification
- `npm run check` ✅
- `npm test` ✅ 60/60 (new tests for direction filtering, red-light/no-limit voice and limits, re-arm, late DB load, DB shape, API, Armenian clip mapping; the direction tests fail with the filter disabled)
- `npm run verify` ✅ 12/12
- Browser pane: Yerevan → Ashtarak route picks up 14 cameras incl. 2 red-light junctions, projection ≈2 ms; red-light marker and credit line render.

author: jaivial
body:
## Symptoms
- `cliproxy/claude-opus-5-5` (the first cliproxy model in `/model`) and 9 more fail with **`HTTP 401 Invalid API key`**, while `claude-sonnet-4-5-*` works.
- `mini-tui doctor` reports **api key: FAIL** even when runs work.
- Every task on `cliproxy/claude-*` ends **`GoalOracleUnavailable`** ("oracle returned invalid JSON" / "format error").

## Causes and fixes
1. **Key chosen by a stale model list.** `modelEnv` only matched models listed in the connection saved at `/connect` (19). The gateway now advertises 29; the 10 new ones got no key, hence 401. **Fix:** match by provider prefix. Also include every native connection's key (one env var each, no collisions) so `/model` and the fallback chain can switch to another provider mid-run. Only the matched connection may set the shared `openai/` slot.
2. **Doctor/picker used the built-in default key.** **Fix:** read the saved connection (an explicit env var still wins). The picker's `curl` takes the key on stdin, not argv (no key in `ps`).
3. **cli-proxy cloaking hides our system prompt from Claude.** Seen in the gateway's request log: the upstream `system` becomes Claude Code's and ours is moved into a `<system-reminder>` "that may or may not be relevant". The goal judge then answered like a coding assistant. **Fix:** the judge's instructions also travel in the user turn.

## Verified (live gateway)
- `doctor` all green. One-shot runs answer on `claude-opus-5-5`, `sonnet-5-5`, `haiku-5-5`, `fable-5-1`, `sonnet-4-5` (opus-5-5 was 401 before).
- Run on xiaomi with xiaomi down → falls back to `cliproxy/claude-opus-5-5` and answers (before: no key for the fallback).
- Tasks with the judge forced: opus-5-5 and sonnet-4-5 `Submitted` on the first verdict, haiku-5-5 after a retry (before: `GoalOracleUnavailable` 3/3), xiaomi unchanged.
- Tests: providers (stale list, mid-run switch, shared `openai/` slot), goal_oracle unit tests. Full `bun test`: no new failures. `cargo test`: only `tests/context.rs` fails, same as on `main`.

## Not in this PR
The cloaking still applies to the agent's main system prompt with Claude. Turning it off (CLIProxyAPI ≥ 8.0's `disable-claude-cloak-mode`) is a gateway change, done separately.

author: garaemon
body:
## Summary
- Add an "If the grant has no effect" section under **Grant Accessibility access**. It explains that macOS ties the grant to the bundle ID plus code signature, so an entry left by an earlier build with a different signature (e.g. unsigned, before the team ID was set) blocks the current build. Fix: `tccutil reset Accessibility com.garaemon.BisectWindow`, then grant again.
- In **Set up**, show how to look up the team ID from the Apple Development certificate, and note that the team ID belongs in `Signing.local.xcconfig` because `make generate` overwrites changes made in the Signing & Capabilities editor.

Docs only; no code changes.

author: kikobeats
body:
Replaces #2292. Its free-tier copy ("25 requests a day, no signup") went stale after #2362, its `/docs` link 404s, and its hero edits conflict with #2341/#2344. This PR keeps the one piece of #2292 that still holds: a next step after the FAQ.

## What changed

- **Homepage:** a final "Start now" section after the FAQ (`#get-started`). It links to free API key signup (`cta=home:footer-cta`), shows the free-tier perks from `helpers/free-tier`, and links to the MCP setup and getting started docs.
- **`patterns/CallToAction`:** the markdown, screenshot and PDF pages each had a 145-line copy of this block. The copies differed only in accent color, outcome copy and `cta` id. All three now render the shared pattern and pass a footer slot for language guides. Net change: -414 / +38 lines in the page files.

## Outcome

The homepage no longer ends without a call to action. Measure it with the `signup_click` events where `cta=home:footer-cta`.

## Testing

- New `test/integration/components/call-to-action-pattern.js`: all four callers use the pattern, each `cta` id is unique, the CTA comes after the FAQ, and every next-step link resolves to a docs page that exists. I checked that it fails when a link is pointed at `/docs`, the bug in #2292.
- `npm run test:unit`: 353 pass. `npm run test:integration`: 1048 pass, 1 fail. The failure is `skills-catalog.js > every skill is assigned a category`, which fails on master too and is unrelated to this change.
- `standard` passes.
- Checked in the dev server with agent-browser: the home CTA at 1440 and 390 wide, no horizontal overflow, and the /markdown, /screenshot and /pdf CTAs render the same as before (6.2s sweep running, language guides nav present).

author: mcrrobinson
body:
## Summary
Underdark T4: the drow and the Spider Houses faction (design 9, section 4). Hostile dark elves with poisoned hand crossbows, Darkness, Faerie Fire and Magic Missile, spider-calling priestesses and Spire elites. Spiders are their allies, and every drow you kill pleases the Sylvan Court.

![Drow lineup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mcrrobinson/dnd-mod/pr-screenshots/feat-drow/drow-lineup.png)

## What changed
- **Mobs** (`entity/drow/`): `DrowEntity` base plus Warrior (26 HP, hand crossbow at 6-14 blocks every 50 ticks, scimitar within 4), Mage (keeps 8-12 blocks off; Darkness, Faerie Fire, Magic Missile), Priestess (scourge + poison, Summon Spiders max 4, Healing Word, Dread WIS 13 -> Frightened 5 s) and Elite (Parry 25%, levitates to ledges). Each has a name and a skin variant. They have Sunlight Sensitivity (Overworld daylight: Weakness I and Slowness I, and their bolts fly wide) and Fey Ancestry (immune to Frightened). Drow and spiders never target or hurt each other. Drow also attack surface elves.
- **Drow Poison** (`DrowPoison`, `DrowSaves` in `MobSaveInfo`): CON DC 13 tagged `poison`. A failure gives 6 s of Drow Poison (Slowness II, Weakness I and a darkened screen edge) plus the Poisoned condition, and adds a stack. Three stacks within 10 s and you fall asleep: Incapacitated (key `drow_sleep`), Slowness VI and Mining Fatigue III for 3 s. Taking damage wakes you. A success gives half the duration and no stack.
- **Spells**: `DrowDarkness` (a radius-4 sphere for 8 s that gives non-drow the Blinded condition plus Darkness), `FaerieFire` (a Glowing outline and +2 damage per hit, through `FaerieFireDamageMixin`), and `magic/MagicMissiles`, the wand's darts moved into a shared helper that `WandOfMagicMissilesItem` now uses.
- **Spider alliance**: `SpiderTargetMixin` on `MobEntity.setTarget` drops drow targets for spiders and cave spiders, including revenge targets.
- **Faction** `dndclasses:drow` "The Spider Houses": starts at -700, Elves at -900. Hostile below Neutral (`DrowHostility`). Killing a priestess costs -120. Rivals: Sylvan Court -0.5 and Grey Clans -0.25. `sylvan_court.json` gains `enemy_kills` for drow, with an uncapped +30 per kill.
- **Data**: tags `faction/drow`, `underdark/thralls` (the Mind Flayer's thrall tag already includes it), structure tag `faction/drow` (optional outpost and spire), drow added to `condition_immune/frightened` and `lore/humanoid`, loot tables (Spidersilk 0-2, arrows 0-3, 5% Drow Poison Vial, and the priestess also has a 2% Rare magic item).
- **Spawns** via `#dndclasses:habitat/drow`: warrior 20 (2-4), mage 5, priestess 2, in the dark only. Natural spawns despawn. Drow spawned with `SpawnReason.STRUCTURE` are persistent.
- **Client** (`client/drow/DrowClient`): `RacialHumanoidRenderer` with elf ears and the `tools/drow_skins.py` skins. The bolt renders as an arrow. The poison vignette is 40%. Icons come from `tools/drow_icons.py`.
- **Small extra**: `/rep <player> <faction> reset` forgets a stored standing, so the devscript can check start values on the fixed `Dev` player.
- Docs: new `docs/mobs/drow.md`, rows in factions.md and creature-study.md, and a line in docs/README.md and the README.

## Integration notes (parallel Underdark tickets)
- To keep merges with T5 and T6 small, everything registers from one class, `Drow.register()`, with one line in `DnDClasses` and one in `DndClassesClient`. Items go into the creative tab through `ItemGroupEvents`, so nothing was added to `ModEntityTypes`, `ModItems`, `ModEffects` or `ModItemGroup`.
- **Spidersilk** (`dndclasses:spidersilk`) is registered here. T6 can craft with it and T5 can buy it.
- **T5 (Grey Clans)**: add `"dndclasses:drow": 15` to `duergar_clans.json` `enemy_kills`, plus the duergar in `underdark/thralls`. Until T5 lands, `drow.json` lists `duergar_clans` as a rival, which only logs a "[Factions] ... unknown rival" warning.
- **T9 (Matron Mother)**: `drow_matron` is already an optional member of `faction/drow`. Her `kill_member_overrides` entry (-400) has to come with her entity type, because an unknown type in that map makes the whole faction fail to load. I hit exactly that while testing this PR.
- **T7/T9 structures**: tag the structures into `tags/worldgen/structure/faction/drow.json` and spawn drow with `SpawnReason.STRUCTURE`.

## Known limitations
- The Drow Poison Vial is a plain splash potion with no save, for players or mobs.
- Faerie Fire adds +2 damage rather than attack advantage.
- The sleep uses Incapacitated, since there is no Unconscious condition. A negative Jump Boost wasn't used because vanilla turns it into fall damage on landing, which would wake the sleeper at once.

## Screenshots
| Close up | Asleep from drow poison | Inside the Darkness | Priestess with spiders, Dread failed |
|-|-|-|-|
| ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mcrrobinson/dnd-mod/pr-screenshots/feat-drow/drow-close.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mcrrobinson/dnd-mod/pr-screenshots/feat-drow/drow-asleep.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mcrrobinson/dnd-mod/pr-screenshots/feat-drow/drow-darkness.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mcrrobinson/dnd-mod/pr-screenshots/feat-drow/drow-priestess.png) |

## To verify
- [x] `./gradlew build` passes
- [x] A warrior's bolts call a CON 13 save (`[D20] Dev Drow poison 2 +4 = 6 vs DC 13 -> FAILURE`). Three failures give stacks 1/3, 2/3 and 3/3, then "falls asleep" (Incapacitated `drow_sleep` in the condition list), and `/damage` wakes you. A forced 20 gives Drow Poison for 60 ticks. (`devscripts/drow.txt`)
- [x] A mage's Darkness gives the player Blinded (`drow_darkness`), Darkness and Blindness. A NoAI drow beside the player has no conditions and no effects. Faerie Fire (effect + Glowing) and magic missiles were cast (`[MobAction]` in debug.log). A husk under Faerie Fire is at 14 health after a 4-damage hit, a plain husk at 16. (`drow.txt`)
- [x] A priestess summons 2, then 4, and stays at 4 spiders. A spider hit by a drow keeps targeting the player. Her spiders vanish when she dies. (`drow.txt`)
- [x] The Dread save shows on the save lane and a failure applies Frightened. `/dndcondition immune` on a drow reports immunity to frightened. (`drow.txt`)
- [x] Killing a drow gives "-60 The Spider Houses, +30 Sylvan Court" (Sylvan 0 -> 30). (`drow.txt`)
- [x] An Elf starts at -900 with the Spider Houses and no race at -700. (`drow.txt`)
- [x] In Overworld daylight a summoned drow gets Weakness and Slowness. (`drow.txt`)
- [ ] The drow look right: the skins, elf ears, and weapons in hand (crossbow, scimitar, the mage's focus, the priestess's chain)
- [ ] Drow Poison's darkened screen edge is noticeable but not overwhelming. It is hard to judge in night screenshots.
- [ ] Fight a mixed drow patrol in the Underdark (Fungal Forest or Faerzress Hollows) and judge how hard it feels: bolts every 2.5 s, the mage kiting, the priestess's spiders
- [ ] Natural spawns show up in the Underdark's drow biomes at a sensible rate

body:
The app changes route mixes cursor and limit rules, response JSON assembly, schema resolution, and feed reads. The response array also passes through JSON serialization twice.

This refactor keeps the effectful flow in the route: parse the request, resolve the target, read the page, capture the examined cursor, read the current tip, check event visibility, then render the reply. The new `app_routes/change_rules.rs` receives data only. It contains the cursor/limit rules and the reply transformation, with explicit imports and no host, clock, or storage access.

The request rule retains the default sequence, `v1-` prefix and 16-character hex checks, the same malformed-request and malformed-cursor errors, the default limit of 100, and the 1–500 clamp. Unknown request fields keep their current serde behavior. The target reaches the existing schema resolver unchanged.

The examined cursor is captured before access checks, so hidden events still advance pagination. The existing visibility helper, target handling, feed read, tip read, event order, response fields, gap flag, and error responses stay in place. The route retains visible events in the original vector. The reply rule moves the final JSON array into the envelope without a second copy of its values.

The diff covers two files: 97 additions and 62 deletions, a net 35 lines and one additional function. The cursor decoder is folded into the request parser. The new functions parse or transform data; no forwarding wrapper, trait, dependency container, or runtime service is added.

Local format, whitespace, changed-file size, changed-function size, and new-allow checks pass. The complete published tree matches the local source. Both publication commits use the public no-reply author, and the worktree is clean.

[Required code CI](https://github.com/EdgeVector/lastdb/actions/runs/40230073215) passes, including the Mini and full-workspace checks. The [standard comparison](https://github.com/EdgeVector/lastdb/actions/runs/40230073225) passes, including `benchmark-complete` and verified uploads. The branch starts at `1041cc244279e81f1b5b58edd53a3148032ddec9`; its head is `534a0d830d79b97fc94ec5fd9bac1dc692ba5a5a`. The workflow selects `f1cdede730fe2c8d9aedaac2fcfeb24ca8a10c7a` and its first parent as the measured candidate and baseline. The complete candidate tree matches the published source. The source, CI measurements, and upload verification passed review before the merge step. The automated code review remains active at this update; there are no posted review findings or inline threads. It is not a required merge check.

The standard workload measures ordinary reads, writes, concurrency, and resources. It has no separate timed app changes case. A passing run does not establish a latency improvement for this route. Cursor, access, and reply compatibility receive source review and compile checks.

Tests remain retired. No local build, benchmark, node, primary data change, deployment, or CI configuration change is part of this work. Raw output stays in CI summaries and artifacts.


The recipe uses 10,000 records, four fields, 1,024-byte bodies, 256 general/single-write samples, 32 batch-insert samples, and 128 batch-update samples. Two alternating pairs run on one four-CPU AMD EPYC 7763 runner, with default workers for both programs. Results are medians of per-run percentiles, not pooled requests.

| Case | Base P95 ms | Candidate P95 ms | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Cold read, 1 record | 2.066 | 2.084 | +0.9% |
| Cold read, 32 records | 25.298 | 25.117 | −0.7% |
| Warm read, 1 record | 0.590 | 0.561 | −5.0% |
| Warm read, 32 records | 4.934 | 4.759 | −3.6% |
| Concurrent-read workload, 1 client | 2.253 | 2.436 | +8.1% |
| Four concurrent read clients | 4.777 | 4.888 | +2.3% |
| Mixed reads, 16 clients | 9.952 | 9.257 | −7.0% |
| Mixed reads, 32 clients | 16.428 | 15.596 | −5.1% |
| Insert 128 records | 230.614 | 226.431 | −1.8% |
| Update 128 records | 305.342 | 305.936 | +0.2% |

No latency measure crosses an advisory limit, so no speed confirmation runs. The largest P95 rise across all cases is concurrent-read/1: +0.183 ms, +8.1%, with paired changes +5.4% and +10.8%. The largest P99 rise is the same case, +7.4%. This does not establish fixed latency or a speed improvement from the app changes refactor.

The resource pass flags insert memory growth: 17.289 → 34.627 MiB (+100.3%). That metric is growth during the workload, not total process memory. Its confirmation changes from 32.537 → 40.062 MiB (+23.1%), below the confirmation limit. No resource warning is confirmed and no new confirmation-only suspect appears. Initial final-idle memory changes range from +1.3% to +17.3%; the confirmation ranges from −8.4% to +0.9%. Initial peak changes range from −0.2% to +12.0%; confirmation peak changes range from −8.9% to −2.3%. Compacted file-length changes stay within 0.116%. No whole-process memory guarantee is claimed.

All 19,072 distinct timed requests report zero errors; mixed read/write submetrics are not counted twice. All 12 generated homes stop their daemons and are removed. The app changes route itself has no direct timed case in this recipe.

The downloaded archive independently matches SHA256 `d61877096eb989e9a70b3b3331110fd25c2fbb3d53b5bc256cd0e143cbaa369b` (artifact 12613146054, expiry November 8, 2026). Raw output stays in CI.

author: ludagoo
body:
On BCM4378 only, retry `assoc_info` after `-EBADE` (-52) and reclaim a flowring's tx pktids instead of waiting for a txstatus that does not arrive.

BCM4378/3 answers `assoc_info` with a firmware error while a connect or roam is still committing. fwil reports that as `-EBADE`. The same windows drop in-flight flowring frames without a txstatus, and `brcmf_msgbuf_delete_flowring()` then waits about 75 ms on the event worker, logs the timeout, and zeros `outstanding_tx` while those pktids stay allocated. This chip retries `assoc_info` up to eight times (175 ms of backoff) only after `-EBADE`, and reclaims that ring's tx pktids instead of waiting. Other chips keep the historical wait and do not retry.

Machine: MacBook Air M1 2020 (J313), PCI 14e4:4425 rev 03, firmware 18.20.383 loaded as `brcmfmac4378b1-pcie`. This has not been booted as a new kernel in this pass.

Host policy check of `sleep_roam.h` printed `ok`. The KUnit suite `brcmfmac-sleep-roam` was not run.

author: sminnee
body:
# `/security-test`: dynamic security testing with OWASP ZAP

A new skill, `shared/skills/security-test/`. It agrees a project's security requirements with the user, then scans the worktree's own dev environment with OWASP ZAP in Docker and triages the alerts.

## Commits

1. `target-guard.sh` refuses any target outside this worktree, with its test.
2. `/security-test` agrees the security requirements, then drives OWASP ZAP.
3. The guide, `CONTEXT.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` document it.

## Decisions

- **The skill owns two committed documents.** `docs/security/requirements.md` and `docs/security/dast-scope.md`. Templates fix their headings, so all projects share one shape.
- **One shared file with the plugins.** The `security-guidance` plugin reads `.claude/claude-security-guidance.md` on each diff review. The skill writes a summary of the requirements there, between `security-test` markers, at 4 KB or less. The plugin's budget is 8 KB in total, for the user, project and local files together.
- **It reads `claude-security`, never writes like it.** The skill uses the newest `CLAUDE-SECURITY-*` report only when its revision stamp matches `HEAD`. ZAP output goes to `security-reports/`, because `claude-security` reads each `CLAUDE-SECURITY-*` directory as its own report.
- **The local-only rule is a script, and its output is the target.** `target-guard.sh scheme://host:port` accepts only `DEV_HOST`, `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` or `host.docker.internal`, on a `*_PORT` of the worktree `.env` inside `PORT_BASE * 10 … + 9`. The range refuses shared-service ports and the `_main` ports, which a worktree `.env` can also list. It refuses any path. Step 5 passes the guard's output to `docker run`, not a URL typed again.
- **The container sees only the plan and the report directory.** The plan mounts read-only, the report directory read-write. The worktree root holds `.env` and `.git/`, so it is never mounted. The image is pinned to `zaproxy:2.17.0`.
- **ZAP runs from a committed Automation Framework plan.** Credentials come in as `ZAP_<ROLE>_USER/PASS` env var names; values never reach a committed file.

## What the real runs changed

`zap-plan.md` holds facts from five runs against `web-fake` (run locally; the log is not committed):

- `alertFilter` checks its URL regex before it substitutes `${ZAP_TARGET}`, so the plan fails.
- `sarif-json` appends `.json` to `report.sarif`.
- A Vite dev server's tooling paths must be excluded. Without them, `spiderAjax` found 13,641 URLs, and the active scan took 4:52 instead of 1:44.
- The tailnet `DEV_HOST` works from the container with valid TLS. No `--add-host` is needed with Docker Desktop.

## Install the plugins

User-wide, once:

```
/plugin install security-guidance@claude-plugins-official
/plugin install claude-security@claude-plugins-official
/reload-plugins
```

The `security-guidance` README says to set `ENABLE_STOP_REVIEW=0` when several agents share one worktree. Maelstrom runs several agents in one worktree, and nothing sets the variable for you. Set it in your shell profile if you want it.

## Seams under test

- **`target-guard.sh` command line**, in `shared/tests/test_security_target_guard.py`. The `.env` is built with `render_managed_section`, so a change to the `.env` format breaks the test, not only the skill. The cases cover each accepted host, prefix ports, a non-`_PORT` port, userinfo tricks, a missing `DEV_HOST`, and a missing `.env`. Two mutations (drop the port anchor, accept any host) turn it red.
- **The skill text** has no automated seam. The proof is the end-to-end dry run, run locally; the log is not committed. Not verified: a real login, `openapi` and `graphql` jobs, and a `claude-security` report as input.

body:
<!-- Outside contributions: typo, docs and small bug-fix PRs only for now.
     For anything larger, open an issue first. See CONTRIBUTING.md.
     PR title: Conventional Commits, same as commit subjects, e.g.
     feat(ui-kit): add brand chart palette -->

## What and why

The first plugin page to run in a sandboxed frame (release 0.7.0, D8). Two commits:

1. `feat(web): host plugin pages in isolated frames`. Page routes now match `<route>/*`; a frame is told the path under the page (`init.path`, then `route`) and gets it as the prop `path`; an in-realm page answers "not found" to anything under its route. A page frame paints `--wm-bg`, never scrolls itself, and grows to its content (240 to 20 000 px) so the window scrolls. The one host CSS rule written for plugin pages (tables scroll inside a card on a phone) is repeated in `frame.css`. Hostile suite gets a `pageframe` phase.
2. `feat(forecast): run in an isolated plugin frame`. One line out of `IN_REALM_PLUGIN_IDS` (the only edit to `bundled.ts`; the comment above the set still lists forecast and is left for whoever lands second, to keep the diff rebase-friendly). Forecast needed no code change: no SDK-root imports, and its only request is `GET /core/recurring-items/forecast?horizon=&accountId=`, allowed by its `recurring_items` and `accounts` read grants. Adds `browser-check/forecast.ts` (83 checks), opens the page in the eval-violation check, updates the e2e smoke spec (the heading is in the frame) and makes the runtime tests independent of which other plugins are ported.

What a reviewer would miss from the diff:

- **A keyboard trap found by the check and fixed (touches widget frames too).** The frame cancelled Tab at its last control and asked the host to move focus. A page frame is the last thing on the page, so there was no next control and focus stayed put for ever. `FrameApp` no longer cancels the key; the browser carries focus out (as in-realm), and the frame sends `focus-out` only if focus is still there 60 ms later. Verified natively in Chromium only; other engines fall back to the old behaviour.
- The Forecast table was clipped at 390 px inside the frame until the phone overflow rule was repeated in the frame stylesheet: host CSS does not reach a frame.
- Findings and the list of what pages need that widgets did not (host dialogs, viewport information, `path` in `PluginPageProps`, shared styles) are in the decision record (workspace ADR 0014, not in this repo) for the Budgets and Import CSV spike.
- Existing, not fixed: Escape on the open phone drawer leaves focus on `<body>` (the menu button is in a bar that is still `inert`), on core pages too.

Decisions made without being able to ask (all reversible):

- Grow with content rather than fill the content area; the 800 px widget clamp does not apply to pages.
- Page routes use `/*` for every plugin page, so Forecast now also renders at `/p/wickermoney.forecast/forecast/anything` (it ignores the rest).
- `path` is passed to page components as an untyped prop; `PluginPageProps` in the SDK is not changed (no `feat(plugin-sdk)` commit; listed as a P4 need).
- axe exclusions for frame documents: `landmark-one-main`, `region`, `page-has-heading-one`; on the host document `page-has-heading-one` (the `h1` is in the frame). Everything else runs.
- The DEVELOPMENT.md sentence listing the in-realm plugins is edited here; P3a edits the same sentence, so expect a trivial conflict in that line, in `bundled.ts` (one line each) and in the runtime tests' lists.

## Linked issue

None.

## How it was tested

Ran (Node 22.23, Chromium 153.0.8010.12 headless in a cloud container, PostgreSQL 16):

- `pnpm lint`: the whole-repo run found two `no-useless-escape` errors in my hostile-suite edit, fixed; the changed files lint clean afterwards (the whole-repo run was not repeated after the fix).
- `pnpm typecheck` (21 tasks, including e2e and the hostile tsconfig), `pnpm build`, `pnpm test`: all pass (web 784, api 918, plugin-sdk 459, forecast 30, others unchanged).
- `pnpm test:integration` for `src/plugins` only: 14 files, 421 tests pass. The full integration suite was not run.
- `browser-check/forecast.ts` (new): 83 checks, 0 failed (load, size at 1440, 1024 and 390 px, content change and resize, route and history, drawer, a11y with axe 4.10.2 in light and dark, canvas and flash, Tab order against the in-realm page).
- Hostile suite: `hostile/run.ts` 145 attacks and 27 checks, 0 failed (new `pageframe` phase: 4); `hostile/remote.ts` 15 checks; `hostile/evalViolations.ts` 15 checks (now includes the Forecast page frame and a canary). `browser-check/run.ts`: 42 of 42.
- Measured (median of 7, alternating, cold load of the page): in-realm on `origin/main` 748 ms to the chart, 955 MiB browser memory, 3 renderers; in a frame 761 ms, 1085 MiB, 4 renderers; scripts and styles 213.7 KiB gzip against 354.1 KiB.

Not run: Firefox, Safari/WebKit, a screen reader, a real phone; `pnpm test:e2e` (needs the compose stack; the spec file typechecks and its in-realm page list, read from `bundled.ts`, still has three entries); the full integration suite; `api test:hostile`. No screenshots attached (light and dark were compared by pixel in the check).

## Checklist

- [x] Commits use Conventional Commits and are signed off (`git commit -s`)
- [x] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm build` and `pnpm test` pass (CI runs these too)
- [ ] `pnpm test:integration` passes, if this touches data isolation, roles or migrations (not touched; plugins subset only)
- [x] Tests added or updated for behavior changes
- [ ] UI changes checked in light and dark mode (by pixel comparison and axe, not by eye)
- [x] New migrations are new files; no applied migration was edited (none)
- [x] Money stays `numeric(19,4)` / `string`, or the boundary change is called out above
- [x] Docs updated where behavior changed (`README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, or the docs site) (CHANGELOG, DEVELOPMENT.md, browser-check README; ROADMAP not touched)

## SDK, ui-kit and plugin contract impact

None to `plugin-sdk` or `ui-kit` (no commit touches them; protocol 1 unchanged). Plugin pages now also match addresses under their route.

## Related PRs

None in other repos. Merge after P3a (both edit `IN_REALM_PLUGIN_IDS`).

body:
## Summary
- **PHP 8.4:** `PageTitleService::getEntityCreateTitle()` and `getEntityTranslationCreateTitle()` declared `string $bundle = null`. PHP 8.4 deprecates implicitly nullable parameters ("Implicitly marking parameter $bundle as nullable is deprecated"), and raises it at compile time, so on every request that loads the service.
- Now `?string $bundle = null`: the same signature (reflection gives `?string`, optional, default `NULL` before and after), valid on every PHP version the module supports.

---
Found by `php -l` and a runtime deprecation collector on Drupal 11.4.11 / PHP 8.5.12; independently reviewed before pushing.

author: viewfromthebox
body:
## Description

The Table of Contents block lists every heading in the block tree it renders in. In a single-post template, that tree holds the template's own headings and its parts' headings as well as the post body. A TOC in a post sidebar therefore listed "Related posts", a newsletter heading and the footer's column headings after the post's own.

The block has a new `source` attribute ("Headings from" in its settings):

- `page` (default) lists every heading on the page, as before.
- `post-content` lists only the headings inside Post Content.

**Closes:** — (no issue filed; found while adding a TOC to the ArtisanPack UI theme's post sidebar)

## Type of Change

- [ ] Bug fix (fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (adds new functionality)
- [ ] Enhancement (improves existing functionality)
- [ ] Refactoring (code improvement, no behavior change)
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Security fix
- [ ] Breaking change (breaks backward compatibility)

## Related Issue

**Issue:** none

## Motivation and Context

A TOC in a sidebar next to the post is the common place for one, and it needs to list only the post's headings. Before this change, the only way to keep template headings out was to drop them, which isn't possible for the footer and related-posts sections.

## Changes Made

- `TocResolver` records whether each heading is inside Post Content: in its rendered `_resolvedContent` HTML, or nested in its inner blocks. A TOC with `source: post-content` keeps only those headings. Every heading still gets its anchor, as before.
- A page with no Post Content block keeps every heading under either setting. That covers a TOC inside a post body, where the body renders as its own tree.
- `_resolvedItems` rows keep their `{level, text, anchor}` shape. The internal flag is removed before stamping.
- Editor: a "Headings from" control, and the preview applies the same filter (`filterItemsBySource()`, `containsPostContent()` in `derive-items.ts`). In the site editor, Post Content is a placeholder, so a `post-content` TOC in a template previews a note that the headings appear on the published page.
- `block.json`: `source` attribute (`page` | `post-content`, default `page`).
- Docs (`docs/blocks/TOC.md`) and CHANGELOG under Unreleased.

The React and Vue renderers only read `_resolvedItems`, so they need no change.

## How Has This Been Tested?

**Testing Environment:**
- Operating System: macOS 27.0.1
- Browser (if applicable): Chromium headless shell (Playwright)
- PHP Version: 8.5.12
- Project Version: `release/1.x` (1.17.1)

**Tests Performed:**
1. Full suites: Pest 4152 passed (1 skipped), Vitest 5662 passed (1 todo). `npm run verify:parity` is OK. phpcs is clean on the changed PHP.
2. Dropped the patched `TocResolver` into a Keystone install using the ArtisanPack UI theme, with a `source: post-content` TOC in the single-post template. A post with 12 H2s listed exactly those 12. Without the change, the same TOC also listed "Related posts", "One good build email a week" and four footer headings.
3. A post with no headings renders the empty-state placeholder instead of falling back to the template's headings.

## Accessibility Tests Run

- [x] Keyboard navigation tested
- [ ] Screen reader tested
- [ ] Color contrast verified
- [x] ARIA labels checked

**Details:** No markup changes. The `<nav>` landmark, its label and the list structure are unchanged. The new control is a standard labelled `SelectControl` with help text.

## Tests Added

- [x] Unit tests added/updated
- [ ] Integration tests added/updated
- [x] All tests passing

**Test details:** `TocResolverTest` has seven new cases: post-content only, headings nested in post-content, an empty body, no Post Content block, `page` and `post-content` TOCs on one page, a subclass with 1.17 override signatures, and no state carried between trees on a reused resolver. `derive-items.test.ts` has four cases for the preview filter, and the existing row expectations include `inContent`.

## Documentation

- [x] Inline code documentation added
- [ ] README updated
- [ ] Wiki updated
- [x] API documentation updated

**Documentation details:** `docs/blocks/TOC.md` has a `source` row in the attributes table and a "Headings from Post Content only" section. There's a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased.

n/a: the frontend markup is unchanged; only which items are listed differs.

### Review notes

- **Security:** `source` is only compared against a constant and never output. TOC text and anchors are still escaped by the Blade partial. No new input reaches HTML.
- **Compatibility:** the protected `TocResolver` method signatures are unchanged from 1.17. Whether the walk is inside Post Content is resolver state, saved and restored around `resolveTree()`. A test loads a subclass that overrides all four stamping methods with their 1.17 signatures.

author: sjawhar-agent[bot]
body:
Follow-up to #16 ("ci: stop the Go, Dispatch and docs jobs a diff cannot reach"), merged as 516398da. A Claude code-reviewer of #16 found the defects below. This PR fixes each one on main. No required check changes, and no check that can catch a real defect is removed.

## Findings and dispositions

| # | Finding | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The `changes` job's `actions/setup-go` hashes `packages/daemon/go.sum` + `packages/envoy/go.sum`. That gives main's full module cache key, and Docs and release restore that key. A cold `go list -m all` fills only a few MB, so this short job could save first and take the key with a nearly empty cache. | **Fixed:** `cache: false` on that step, with a comment. I confirmed the key is shared: `gh api 'repos/theorem-labs/legion/actions/caches?key=setup-go'` lists `setup-go-Linux-x64-ubuntu24-go-1.27.1-12cfa6225453fe5a…` on `refs/heads/main`, 452,710,983 bytes. setup-go's hash of the two go.sum files, computed locally, is `12cfa6225453fe5a480b6a92909abca925e63bf597efebd0afae9fd13be349be`. These are the same key. |
| 2 | orchestration-lean uses the combined `actions/cache`, which saves in its post step at job end. Since #16, a newer push cancels a pull-request run (`cancel-in-progress`). A run that is cancelled after its ~105-minute Lean stage2 build saves nothing. | **Fixed:** the workflow restores with `actions/cache/restore` and saves with `actions/cache/save` (both v6.1.0, `55cc8345`). The save is the step directly after `Build Lean stage2` and runs on every miss, on any event. It uses the same path and the restore step's `cache-primary-key`. The concurrency group and the narrowed paths stay. `check-image-trigger-paths.sh` adds both split actions to `NON_BUILDING_ACTIONS`, next to `actions/cache`. |
| 3 | `envoy-infra-go` also ran when `workspace_versions` was true. But `packages/envoy/infra` has its own `go.work`, so the root workspace's build list never reaches it. | **Fixed:** removed that clause from the job's `if:`. Verified: `cd packages/envoy/infra && go env GOWORK` gives `packages/envoy/infra/go.work`. The job still runs on its `envoy` filter. |
| 5 | orchestration-lean's `go test` runs in workspace mode, so a version change in `go.work`, `packages/daemon/go.mod` or `packages/envoy/go.mod` moves what it compiles, but it started no run. | **Fixed:** added the three paths to both lists. Verified with `go list -m` in `packages/orchestration`: before the change, `golang.org/x/sys v0.49.0`. After a `replace` in `packages/daemon/go.mod`, and separately in `packages/envoy/go.mod`, it gives `golang.org/x/sys v0.49.0 => v0.48.0`. After a `replace` in `go.work`, it gives `golang.org/x/text v0.43.0 => v0.42.0`. `declindex/confine` imports `golang.org/x/sys/unix`. All edits were reverted after the test. |
| 6 | `docs/site/generators/legion-config.sh` renders `deploy/kubernetes/**` into the config reference page, but no Docs trigger named that directory. | **Fixed:** added `deploy/kubernetes/**` to both Docs lists. Verified: the generator has `source_dir=deploy/kubernetes`. |
| 8 | The comment "GitHub Actions reads no YAML anchor in a workflow file" may be false. | **Fixed:** deleted it from docs.yaml and orchestration-lean.yaml. The two lists stay written out. |
| 9 | (a) The `changes` checkout's fetch-depth comment said "the first parent … of a push to main". (b) `base=$(git rev-parse HEAD^1)` could fail the step instead of falling through to `moved=true`. | **Fixed:** (a) the comment now says "the parent of a pull request's merge commit; the event's own base for a push or merge group". (b) The line is now `base=$(git rev-parse HEAD^1 2> /dev/null) \|\| base=`, so a failure leaves `base` empty and the step reports `moved=true`. |

## Why every check stays and only waste goes

- **1** changes no check. The step still installs the same Go and still runs the build-list comparison. Only the cache save and restore stop, and that cache was the wrong one for this job.
- **2** keeps every completed build. Before this change, a cancelled run lost its build. Now the save runs as soon as the build finishes, so the build is kept even if a later push cancels the run. A full run does the same restore, build, save and test as before, on the same key.
- **3** removes a run that could find nothing new: envoy-infra-go compiles against its own workspace. A change to that workspace's files still starts it through the `envoy` filter.
- **5** and **6** add triggers. They make more runs, not fewer: they close gaps where a change could reach the checked output without starting the check.
- **8** and **9a** change comments only. **9b** makes a failure take the safe path, where every Go job runs.

## Verification

At this head, run locally:

- `.github/scripts/check-private-names.sh`: "check-private-names: no file or path names the private deployment repository or the company, … (4952 files in the repository)", exit 0
- `~/.cache/infra109/check-public.sh origin/main HEAD`: exit 0
- `.github/scripts/check-image-trigger-paths.sh`: "every image trigger covers every input its build reads (4 image build(s))", exit 0
- `.github/scripts/check-image-trigger-paths.test.sh`: "Results: 808 passed, 0 failed", exit 0
- `.github/scripts/check-action-pins.sh`: "every remote action across 16 files is pinned to a commit SHA", exit 0
- `.github/scripts/check-action-pins.test.sh`: "Results: 16 passed, 0 failed", exit 0
- The changed workflows parse with `yaml.safe_load`, and `actionlint` exits 0 on all three.

What CI cannot show at this head: the Lean save path runs only on a cache miss. Main's key `lean4-d71bb0c6…-stage2-Linux-X64` exists (962,518,425 bytes), so this PR's orchestration-lean run restores it and skips both the build and the save. The save step's inputs are the same `path` and the restore step's `cache-primary-key` output.

CI at 9b1fffe7: all 13 checks that ran passed. In [lean](https://github.com/theorem-labs/legion/actions/runs/40230076849/job/121279709319), `Restore Lean stage2` (now `actions/cache/restore`) logged "Cache restored from key: lean4-d71bb0c6d04adbb8e94adfdf8c0e3291bfeea831-stage2-Linux-X64", and the Lean tests passed on it. Cross-family review gate: APPROVE at this head, served by openai/gpt-6-astra (pull/19#issuecomment-6402779504).

author: belalaamer
body:
## What this changes

Two patient-facing auth screens that could each strand a patient, plus the portal's blocked
screen that sent them to a dead end. **Front-end only** — no migration, no Edge function, no
GRANT/REVOKE, no RLS, no Production write.

| ID | Class | Finding |
|---|---|---|
| P4 | **Bug Fix** | `/reset-password` accepted a 6-character password while the invitation generator and the portal's own change-password step required 8 — and `/patient-portal/login` refused anything under 8 without ever saying so. A patient who used their recovery link at 6–7 characters could not sign back in with the password they had just chosen. |
| P7 | **Bug Fix + Enhancement** | The "portal unavailable" card conflated *your account is not enabled* with *the request was refused*, and told both to "use your invitation link" — which is single-use and already consumed by anyone who can reach that screen. |

## P4 — one floor, closed from both ends

- `src/pages/auth/ResetPassword.tsx`: floor 6 → **8**, the requirement named in the toast
  («كلمة المرور يجب ألا تقل عن 8 أحرف») and repeated as a static hint under the field.
  `autoComplete="new-password"` on both inputs.
  Deliberately **no `minLength`**: a native constraint blocks the submit before the handler
  runs, so the localized message would never be seen — the browser tooltip is not
  Arabic-aware and not ours.
- `src/pages/patientPortal/PatientPortalLogin.tsx`: **removed** the client-side length gate. A
  login form cannot know what the account was created with; only the server decides whether
  credentials are valid. `login-by-identifier` already accepts ≥6, so this also un-blocks any
  patient account that was created under the old 6-character recovery floor.
- `src/pages/patientPortal/PatientPortal.tsx`: the change-password screen keeps its 8-character
  rule but now **states** it — its submit button is disabled under 8 characters, so a patient who
  typed 7 saw a dead button with no reason.

Nothing can now *create* a sub-8 patient password, and no client can *refuse* a password the
server would accept.

## P7 — the blocked screen states one truth

`src/pages/patientPortal/PatientPortal.tsx` gains a `blocked` state, set where the failure is
actually observed:

- `"failed"` (the RPC was refused / the snapshot call errored) → heading "The patient portal
  could not be loaded", a **Try again** button, and a toast that says to check the connection.
- `"inactive"` (`active: false`) → heading "Patient portal unavailable", copy stating the clinic
  has not enabled the account, and explicitly that the invitation link works once and cannot
  reopen an account. No retry button, because retrying cannot help.

The card also picks up `dir` for Arabic, which the neighbouring screens already had.

## Measured, not assumed

- `worker.ts:194` (invitation temp password) and `PatientPortal.tsx:181-182` (portal
  change-password) both already required 8 — recovery was the only way to make a shorter
  patient password.
- Staff paths were checked and left alone: `Auth.tsx:122` accepts ≥6 and
  `UserManagement.tsx:1136` sets ≥6, so staff has no lockout. Aligning the staff *policy* with
  8 is recorded as a separate enhancement (P4b), not smuggled into this PR.
- No existing spec asserted any string this batch replaces.

## Gates (local, on the final tree)

- `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.app.json` → **0**
- `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.node.json` → **0**
- `vite build` → **0**
- `vitest run --no-file-parallelism` → **97 files / 885 tests**, 883 passed. The 2 failures were in
  `src/pages/inventory/InventoryMutation.test.tsx` — a file this PR does not touch — and they are
  that file's own `waitFor` (testing-library default 1000 ms) expiring while the host sat at load
  average 700. Run alone at load 156 it is **23/23 green**. CI runs the same suite on a quiet
  runner and is the authoritative regression gate for this PR.

New specs: `src/pages/patientPortal/PatientPortalLogin.test.tsx` (2 tests), 2 added to
`PatientPortal.activation.test.tsx`, 1 added to `ResetPassword.test.tsx` (34 tests across the three
files, all green).

## Evidence tier

Built + typechecked + tested locally → **CI** on this PR. Not merged, not deployed, so nothing
here is reachable by a user yet.

body:
## Summary
- **Attribute discovery for `@EntityForm` plugins.** Drupal 11.2 deprecates plugin managers that only support annotations ("Not supporting attribute discovery in CustomEntityFormManager is deprecated in drupal:11.2.0"), and Drupal 12 throws an `InvalidArgumentException` for them.
- Adds an `EntityForm` attribute next to the annotation and passes both to `DefaultPluginManager` when core supports it (Drupal 10.2+, detected through `AttributeInterface`); older cores get only the annotation class, as before. Like the annotation, the attribute derives the plugin ID `<entity_type>.<bundle>.<operation>`.
- Existing `@EntityForm` plugins keep working; core now flags them as deprecated for Drupal 13, so projects can move to `#[EntityForm(...)]` at their own pace.
- The attribute class avoids promoted/readonly properties, so every file still parses on PHP 7.

## Verification
- Drupal 11.4.11 / PHP 8.5 with a site's 17 `@EntityForm` plugins: identical definitions and `getFormClass()` results, and the deprecation is gone.
- Fixture forms declared once with the attribute and once with the annotation resolve to the same `getFormClass()` results.
- A stub of the pre-10.2 `DefaultPluginManager` constructor receives exactly the old arguments (PHP 7.4, 8.1, 8.5).

---
Found by a runtime deprecation collector on Drupal 11.4.11 / PHP 8.5.12; independently reviewed before pushing.

author: jpreculeau
body:
### Problem
A window class the icon theme has no icon for is looked up again on each taskbar rebuild: four failing theme lookups and a parse of `icon-missing.svg`, about 2 ms per such window on a Raspberry Pi 5.

### Change
`create_pixbuf()` remembers a failed theme lookup for 30 s (the icon may get installed meanwhile) and drops what it remembers when the icon theme changes, like the pixbuf cache. The `icon-missing.svg` pixbuf is kept per size (also dropped on a theme change). A remembered failure still raises when there is no fallback (`LookupError` instead of GLib's error; every caller catches `Exception`). At most 256 failures are remembered, all forgotten at once beyond that, as window classes come from other programs.

**Behaviour change:** an icon installed while the panel runs may take up to 30 s to replace `icon-missing`.

### Tests
Measured on a Raspberry Pi 5 (Hyprland 0.56.2, Python 3.13). The existing test harnesses (keyboard layout, controls, compositor exec, module order, sway, threads/network, sensors, CSS, config editor, tray, JSON, playerctl) give the same results on master 7105ae88 and on this branch.

| | master | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| icon harness (no lookup for a remembered failure, theme change, retry delay, known icons, no fallback) | 5/8 cases | 8/8 |
| class without an icon, per call (median) | 1.82 ms | 0.04 ms |

author: ottramst
body:
Closes #48.

## Summary
- **Retries with backoff.** Requests that Vaultwarden rate limits (HTTP 429) are retried with exponential backoff and jitter: 1s, then 2s, 4s and so on, capped at 30s between retries. The total wait is capped by the new provider attribute **`max_retry_wait`**, in seconds. It defaults to 60, `0` disables retries, and it can also be set with `VAULTWARDEN_MAX_RETRY_WAIT`.
- **No `Retry-After` from Vaultwarden.** Vaultwarden sends neither `Retry-After` nor `X-RateLimit-*` headers, so the wait can't come from the response. Its limiters refill one request per configured period, so waits of a few seconds to tens of seconds are realistic.
- **Errors name the setting to raise.** When a request still fails, the error says which server setting to raise, based on the response body:
  - `Too many login requests`: `LOGIN_RATELIMIT_*`
  - an HTML page: `ADMIN_RATELIMIT_*`
  - otherwise: `UNAUTHENTICATED_RATELIMIT_*`
- **Fresh body per attempt.** The request body is rebuilt for every attempt, and waiting stops when the context is cancelled.

## Testing
- Unit tests (`internal/vaultwarden/client_test.go`, run with `-race`) against an `httptest` server:
  - retries, then succeeds, and the original body is re-sent on every attempt
  - gives up with the right hint for each of the three limiters
  - `0` disables retries
  - context cancellation stops the wait
  - other errors are not retried
- End-to-end against a real Vaultwarden 1.37.4 limited to one unauthenticated request per 2s: three prelogins in a row succeed after about 2.5s waits. With `max_retry_wait = 0`, the second and third fail immediately.
- Full acceptance suite passes on **1.37.4** and **1.36.0**. golangci-lint: 0 issues.

body:
## What
1. **Admin override on real-hosted events.** New `assertCanManage(user, organizer)` (owner or admin; in `DEMO_MODE` the admin override stops at events whose organizer is not `@gatherly.demo`) → 403 `FORBIDDEN`. Used for event edit/cancel (`events/routes.ts`) and removing an attendee (`POST /registrations/:id/cancel`). Viewing the attendee list stays allowed (emails masked). Test in `test/demo.test.ts`.
2. **Proxy hops.** Replit documents no client-IP header that clients cannot forge, so `TRUST_PROXY_HOPS=4` stays. `app.ts` logs one warning when a request's `X-Forwarded-For` is *shorter* than the hop count: that is the dangerous misconfiguration (a client could prepend entries and pick its IP). Longer chains are normal (clients may send their own header) and requests without the header (health probes) are ignored.
3. **Per-instance limits.** `rate-limit.ts` comment and `README.md` limitations row now match `docs/api.md`: per instance, so up to N× the limit with N instances until a shared store. The README change is a one-line accuracy fix in this code PR.
4. **Totals past the last page.** Sorted (non-`for_you`) feeds took `total` from `count(*) over ()` on the returned rows, so an empty page reported 0. An empty page past page 1 now asks page 1 (pageSize 1) for the count.
5. `config.ts` comment: Replit Autoscale = 4 hops, and why the count is measured.
6. **Helmet.** `hsts: false` (Replit's edge already sends HSTS; live had two headers with different max-age). SPA and docs CSPs allow `https://replit-cdn.com`, where Replit's injected "Made with Replit" pill loads from; it only injects an inline `<style>` (already allowed) and links.

## Verified (production build, `TRUST_PROXY_HOPS=4`, `DEMO_MODE=true`)
- Headers: no HSTS from the app; CSP `script-src 'self' https://replit-cdn.com` (docs: plus `'unsafe-inline'`).
- Replit pill script loaded on /events with no CSP violation; `/api/docs/` renders, no CSP messages.
- Real-hosted event as demo admin: attendees 200, edit/cancel/remove attendee 403.
- `?sort=soonest&page=999` → `total: 39` (was 0).

- Migration `20261029100000_hot_path_indexes`: follows x2 (followee/follower, created_at DESC, other id DESC), conversations(bid_id) partial, messages (conversation_id, created_at DESC, id DESC) replacing the shorter (conversation_id, created_at DESC), messages media partial (attachment, voice), comments (post_id, created_at DESC, id DESC), attorney_profiles directory (trust_level DESC, rating_avg DESC, username_lower), posts popular partial, and 21 FK indexes: comments.author_id, comment_likes.user_id, post_view_events.viewer_id, case_comments.author_id, client_reviews.attorney_id, contact_disclosures client_id/attorney_id/case_id, case_journal.actor_user_id, attorney_tasks.case_id, bid_drafts.case_id, stories.file_id, review_helpful_votes.user_id, client_review_helpful_votes.user_id, legal_answer_likes.user_id, call_participants.invited_by_id, channel_posts.author_id, channel_comments.author_id, channel_reactions.user_id, post_shares.user_id, case_comment_likes.user_id. Matching `@@index` lines in schema.prisma (partial ones stay raw SQL only, like messages_expiry_idx).
- Counter aggregator: new entities `story` (view_count, nightly recount from story_views), `case_promotion` (impressions/reach/clicks, global table), `channel` (post_count). The last two are excluded from the nightly recount (`recount: false`). Used by stories view, cases feed promotion impressions, promotion delivery (budget cap still checks DB + pending) and admin channel post restore/remove. Every service falls back to the old direct update when the aggregator is absent.
- Public directory: composite opaque keyset cursor (trust_level, rating_avg, username_lower) with an OR predicate; old plain-username cursors still resolve.
- Unread counters (chat list, badges): explicit `m.created_at >= lr.created_at` bound next to the row comparison.

## Verified
typecheck, lint:fast, related specs (public directory cursor, badge unread bound, promotion delivery via aggregator, COUNTERS hot rows, cases feed, stories, admin-media, promotions) pass. ERD regenerated (no change). Migration not run against a live DB here (Docker/Postgres off); CI migrate deploy and drift check cover it.

## Risks
- Migration uses plain `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS` in the migration transaction, not CONCURRENTLY: Prisma cannot run CONCURRENTLY in a multi-statement migration and the online-DDL runner (#347) is not on main. Short write lock on small tables; later big-table builds should use prisma/concurrent once #347 lands.
- Story/promotion/channel counters now lag the DB row by up to the flush interval (10 s); own-story view count and promotion budget check add the pending delta.
- Old messages index dropped in the same transaction as the new one is created.
