author: gilbn
body: Login sessions now live in Postgres instead of Litestar's in-memory store, so an update, a container restart or a host reboot no longer logs anyone out. Stacked on #341. ## What changes - **Session store.** Migration `a41d7e6c2b95` adds the `auth_sessions` table. The app's `sessions` store is a `SessionTableStore` (advanced-alchemy's `SQLAlchemyStore` with a namespace-scoped `delete_expired`) behind a `SessionStore` wrapper. The wrapper stores the SHA-256 of each session id, never the id itself, and gives up on a lookup after 5 seconds. - **Outages answer 503, never 401.** A session lookup that hits a database outage answers 503, so an open dashboard stays on its page instead of landing on `/login`. Until the database is ready at startup or during recovery, the store doesn't query at all, and `/auth/login` and the OIDC routes answer 503 before checking a password or contacting the provider. Only connectivity errors count as an outage. A programming error still answers 500 with a traceback, and the `service_unavailable` log line names the cause's type. - **`APP_SESSION_MAX_AGE_DAYS`.** Sets how long a login lasts, 7 days by default and 1 to 400 allowed. The expiry still counts from login. - **Expired sessions.** A successful login also sweeps expired rows, at most once every 10 minutes for the whole app. A failed sweep is logged and never fails the login. - **Auth changes end every session.** The head stores an argon2 fingerprint of the admin user and password, whether password login is on, and the OIDC issuer, client id, allow lists, groups claim and scopes. When the fingerprint changes, startup or recovery deletes every session and logs `sessions_revoked` with the reason. The hash never reaches a log or an error message. - **Login page.** A 503 on sign-in says the database is unavailable instead of "Invalid username or password". While `/health` reports the database down, the page says so under the form. The `/health` read is capped at 3 seconds. - **Log out.** A failed logout shows a toast and keeps you on the page, because the session is still live. It used to go to `/login` anyway. - **Docs.** The README and `docs/deployment.md` describe the new behaviour, and `docs/configuration.md` lists the new setting. ## Upgrading Updating to this release logs everyone out one last time, because the old sessions only lived in memory. Restarts after that keep them. ## Screenshots The login page while the database is down. A sign-in that hit a 503. A failed logout on a phone.

author: jocaldwell
body:
Phase 1b makes every personal price follow the user's USD/EUR and store/Lowest choice. Prices still come only from Scryfall's daily default-cards bulk data.

## Built

- Spec-first commit rewrites §4.4 and marks the §2 price-source entry built; follow-up docs cover search, structured results, Settings, architecture and operations.
- Schema v13 preserves existing USD quotes as TCGplayer rows and keys prices by `(oracle_id, store)`. Both stores reduce playable printings/finishes together, stage in batches of 500 and swap with the publication date atomically. The first post-migration refresh loads both stores even on the same publication date.
- Per-user `price_currency`/`price_store` settings, UI-only validated `setPriceSource`, readable `getPriceSource`, and explicit permission-matrix classifications.
- One actor-taking `priceResolver` supplies card/search results, deck totals/unpriced counts, sourcing, proposal rows and projected price deltas. Wire amounts are `cents` with currency/store/date metadata; EUR is never placed in a USD-labelled field.
- Settings controls, $/€ formatting, store/date labels on deck estimates/card panels/hover cards, and source-aware cache invalidation. Agents get compact per-card amounts plus one source/date line per price-bearing response (and start_session). Exports, ruling lists and memory writes have no source line. Search retains `usd`/`eur`; each uses that currency's chosen store or Lowest.

## Decisions and where recorded

Spec §4.4 records per-user key/value settings (absent = USD/lowest), currency-specific search fallback, no cross-currency fallback for missing prices, deterministic printing/finish ties, and the same-date refresh marker. Scryfall card-object, price-source FAQ and search-syntax documentation were verified and cited in code. Spec §10.3 records neutral price fields and signed proposal deltas; §11 records Settings and UI labels. Historical migration fixtures now reconstruct the old USD table; assertions remain strict. Tool-text changes are deliberate and pinned.

Main was fetched and this branch rebased immediately before opening: main is 3e1798d, highest schema v12, so this migration is v13 with no gap. Production runs it on deploy.

## Acceptance

- `npm run check`: **982 tests passed**, no failures; server/web typechecks and architecture/permission gates green. Gate passed before every commit and again after the final rebase.
- Online SQLite backup from the owner's live DB (read-only source) into this worktree's ignored `.dev/`; all migrations, refreshes and UI changes used copies.
- Real Scryfall refresh, publication `2026-10-25T21:05:44.018+00:00`: **33,327 TCGplayer-priced cards**, **33,092 Cardmarket-priced cards**. Full price table: 34,039/33,601 rows respectively, including IDs outside the card catalogue.
- Original and new capability results compared across **all 18 decks** in the backup: zero per-card USD, total or unpriced-count differences under USD/lowest. Every original USD quote is unchanged.
- Sampled peak JS heap **83.46 MiB**; Linux VmHWM **236.52 MiB RSS**, below Phase 0's recorded 246.21 MiB. Streamed reduction and bounded staging retained. This runner's inherited getrusage maxRSS was excluded from the comparison; OPERATIONS documents the measurement.
- User 2 saved EUR/Cardmarket through Settings on 5181/API 8791 (ignored harness using the existing actor seam). Seeded deck showed **€244.27 · Cardmarket · 2026-10-25**; card panel showed its matching EUR quote. Screenshots inspected at desktop/720 px; zero browser runtime errors. Current 390 px shell remains cramped pending 4a's phone view.
- Read live-data agent start_session/get_deck and `eur<=1` search transcript: Cardmarket/€ with date; user 1 still TCGplayer/$. Automated tests cover both users, missing EUR prices, search fallback, staged failure preservation, populated v12 migration/reopen, and projected cost matching actual approval for copies/parking/maybe promotion.

## Left out and Phase 4a handoff

Phase 4a has not merged, so there is no PublicDeckState to wire in this PR. It must build `price { total_cents, currency, store, unpriced, as_of, source: "Scryfall" }` using `priceResolver(db, viewer | null)` and the computed estimate: signed-in **viewer's** choice, anonymous **USD/lowest**, never the deck owner's preference. `getPriceSource` and `priceResolver` now directly accept null; null reads never inspect any user's settings. A null `setPriceSource` is refused with 401 before any write. Internal estimates now call the amount `cents`; map it to public `total_cents`. Recheck migration order when merging parallel phases.

No MTGJSON, exchange rates, vendor APIs, scraping, price history, collection/printing ownership, buy links, hosting changes or public-page/phone implementation. Acceptance databases, scripts, images and transcripts remain ignored. Owner merges; this PR is not merged.



## Round 1 review fixes

1. **Real MCP path:** HTTP and callTool now execute through the same runTool helper. Tool metadata opts price-bearing responses into the one source/date line, including structured proposal reads; start_session also includes it. Exports remain byte-for-byte unchanged, and ruling/memory tools have no footer. Official MCP client tests against createApp cover both protocol eras, source/date uniqueness, EUR amounts/structured facts, sourcing and clean export/ruling/memory results. A live-data HTTP transcript on the ignored acceptance copy was read too.
2. **Negated prices:** scalar minimum-price comparisons now require IS NOT NULL before comparing, so negation includes unpriced cards while direct != excludes them. USD/EUR tests cover negation, double negation, AND/OR and !=. All three review queries match the pre-phase backup by oracle ID and count (32,791 / 153 / 34). Spec §4.4 records the behavior.
3. **Refresh readiness:** scheduler start() and next() both check the shared price-store version marker. Missing/old markers queue/report an immediately due refresh even one hour after a successful run. Populated v12 migration tests cover missing, old and current markers; hourly failure retries remain.
4. **Required null viewer:** getPriceSource(db, null) returns USD/lowest and priceResolver(db, null) resolves TCGplayer/USD without reading any principal's settings, even when the owner uses EUR. setPriceSource(db, null, ...) raises 401 without writes. Direct tests and permission probes cover these paths. This is the exact resolver signature Phase 4a's anonymous search needs, documented in §4.4.
5. **Nits:** invalid stored pairs fall back together to USD/lowest; ReviewDelta shows store/date; CLI reuses the source formatter and says the date is unknown before refresh; SCHEMA explains why its historical bootstrap table runs before v13; settings price/budget changes share a transaction with rollback coverage; the permission matrix itself probes agent setter rejection.

Final rebase: current main 3e1798d still has schema v12; this branch remains v13. Phase 3/PR #7 has not merged yet. The http.ts execution change and jobs.ts readiness checks are deliberately small to preserve its structured-logging work on a later rebase. Owner merges.

| `actions/download-artifact` | v4 | **v7** | release |

This is the smallest step that clears the warning. Later majors bring further breaking changes; for example, checkout v6 moves the stored credentials, which the pages job's `git push` relies on. `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` is a Docker action and is unaffected.

## Checks

- **Test workflow:** runs on this PR and covers checkout and setup-python.
- **Release workflow:** runs only on a tag, or by hand as a dry run (Actions → release → Run workflow), which builds and uploads without publishing.
  - That dry run is the way to test `upload-artifact@v6` before the next tag.
  - `download-artifact@v7` sits in the publish job, which runs only on a tag.
- **Workflow files:** all three still parse as valid YAML.

ettom
body:
When using the integration without setting the charge completion time, charging may get continuously postponed if new prices arrive before charging is scheduled (and the price is on a downward trend over multiple days). Even if the actual price difference is a few cents. To express the idea that charging earlier at a (very) slightly higher cost is desirable, this PR adds an user-settable waiting cost parameter.

Personally, I almost never set the charging completion time and instead I've just set a relatively low price limit, below which charging is acceptable to me. It would often happen that the electricity price would be just very slightly cheaper some time in the future (e.g. a few cheap quarters during the next day), but then, in the meanwhile, I'd drive the car and the next day's few cheap quarters would no longer be enough to fully charge it. So it missed a lot of opportunities to charge at cheap (on an absolute level) prices. This solution to the problem has been working well for me for a few weeks.

author: popov95s
body:
Stacked on #42.

A batch of small surface fixes. Pillars filtered out by `--pillar` rendered as zero findings, `--summary` ignored `--pillar` and `--diff`, MCP clients got no totals or typed argument schemas, `init` said "running on defaults" over an existing config, and the embedding model was fetched at whatever revision the Hub served.

- **eyez model.** `src/eyez/model.rs` resolves `SENSEZ_EYEZ_MODEL_DIR` first, then a cached snapshot of a pinned revision (also one the Python `huggingface_hub` cache left without a ref), and otherwise downloads into `HF_HOME`. With `HF_HUB_OFFLINE` or `SENSEZ_OFFLINE` set and nothing cached it fails with a message naming the override. The first download prints one line on stderr with the model, size and target directory. `hf-hub` becomes a direct optional dependency of the `eyez` feature.
- **CLI.** `sensez eyez search [PATH] QUERY` and `sensez eyez reindex [PATH]` default the path to `.`. A bad `--fail-on` value explains the usual mix-up: if the value was meant as the PATH, put it before the flag. `--fail-on-new` without `--diff` notes that it implies diff scope.
- **`--summary`.** Renders from the same selected report as a normal scan, so `--pillar`, `--diff` and output globs apply, and a clean repo in diff mode gives an empty summary. The MCP `get_configuration_summary` tool gains `diff`.
- **Terminal report.** Diff mode prints a header saying only findings on changed lines are shown, and pillars left out by `--pillar` are omitted instead of shown as `0 of 0` (`ReportMeta.filtered_pillars`).
- **Excluding paths.** `--output-glob '!pattern'` drops matching clone occurrences from a group (the group stays while two remain) and other findings in matching files; `!` and `!!x` are rejected because they can never match. An `accept.duplication` path such as `"legacy-fork/"` drops that location from every clone group, matching whole path components, while an `a.ts + b.ts` label still hides the whole group (`src/brainz/suppression.rs`).
- **MCP.** `noze_sniff` returns per-pillar `meta.totals` counted before `limit`, and `meta.truncated`. `threshold` and `limit` schemas carry `minimum` and `default`, `triage_finding` enumerates `pillar` and `verdict`, and `explain` with an unknown term returns a tool error listing the known terms instead of `-32602`. `stop_hook_active` is accepted and ignored so older hooks still validate.
- **Config.** `cycles.include_type_only` (default true) can switch off the `info` cycles closed only by type imports.
- **`init`.** A created config and a kept one get different closing messages. JSON configs keep their key order (`serde_json` `preserve_order`) and end with a newline.
- A `Pillar` enum in `src/report/pillar.rs` replaces `brainz::Namespace`, `AnalysisReport::refresh_totals` replaces four copies of the totals recount, and `brainz::VERDICTS` is the one verdict list.

Regression baselines are updated for the MCP outputs (`totals`, `truncated`, tool schemas), the cache and diff scenarios, and the `init` snapshots.

Checked with `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-features --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --all-features` and `./regression/run.sh --target flask --target zod --ci`.

author: mihirsamdarshi
body:
Monitoring plan (rev 3) phases 1–3: everything that does not need the 64 GiB local-path disks. Loki, Alloy, UCG syslog, TrueNAS/graphite, GPU and blackbox are out of scope. One commit per phase.

## What's in it

**Phase 1: metrics (`observability` namespace, PodSecurity `privileged` for node-exporter)**
- kube-prometheus-stack **92.13.1** (operator 0.94.1, Prometheus 3.15.0) with `crds.enabled: true`. The cluster-wide `CreateReplace` patch replaces the 0.91 CRDs that bootstrap installed with kubectl.
- `bootstrap/helmfile/crds.yaml` (+ `.j2`): the `prometheus-operator-crds` release is replaced by `kube-prometheus-stack` with `inherit: default`. The chart version now comes from the Flux OCIRepository, which Renovate tracks. The kps `helmrelease.yaml` stays a single document because `values.yaml.gotmpl` loads it with `fromYaml`.
- Prometheus is pinned to talos-02 with a `local-path` PVC of 10Gi (nominal; local-path does not enforce it). The nodes now have 64 GiB disks (about 69 GB), so 8 GB of retention uses roughly 12 % of one disk; no sizing change was needed. Retention is 30 d / 8 GB (WAL included). Memory is 1Gi requested, 2.5Gi limit. No HTTPRoute.
- Cardinality design:
  - **Layer 1:** a default ScrapeClass `guardrails` applies to every ServiceMonitor and PodMonitor, including those of other releases. It drops histogram buckets except an allowlist (its own marker), and allowlists the `go_`, `workqueue_`, `cilium_`, `envoy_` and `certmanager_` families (mark → drop unmarked → labeldrop). Each scrape gets `sampleLimit` 5000, with an `enforcedSampleLimit` of 20000. Label limits are 30 labels and 1024 characters per value.
  - **Layer 2:** keep-lists for the apiserver, kubelet, cAdvisor, probes, etcd, controller-manager and scheduler. The cAdvisor list copies the chart defaults verbatim first, then keeps eth0 only and drops `id|name|uid`. kube-state-metrics has collectors and metric allowlists. node-exporter is limited to 14 collectors.
  - **Layer 3:** the bucket-dependent default rule groups are off, as are `etcdGRPCRequestsSlow` and `NodeMemoryHighUtilization`.
- etcd is scraped over plain HTTP on 2381. A Service selects the hostNetwork kube-apiserver pods (`component: kube-apiserver`), so no endpoints are hard-coded. The bearer token is not sent. No Talos change is needed.
- PrometheusRules:
  - `guardrails`: head series 60k/100k, churn, sample and label limit hits, duplicate timestamps, size retention, `LocalPathFilling` (30/15 % free), and `NodeMemoryHigh` (85/95 %).
  - `certificates`: cert-manager rules with **lifetime-relative** expiry thresholds. With W = expiration − renewalTime, the alert warns below 0.5·W and is critical below 0.2·W.
  - Both files have Flux substitution disabled, so `$labels` survives.
- A PodMonitor for the Flux controllers. CoreDNS gets a metrics Service and ServiceMonitor from its own chart (`prometheus.service/monitor`). Its Deployment renders identically, so the pods do not restart.

**Phase 2: Alertmanager (Discord only, no heartbeat)**
- Alertmanager is pinned to talos-02 next to Prometheus, with a 512Mi PVC. No HTTPRoute.
- `Watchdog`, `InfoInhibitor` and `severity=info` go to `null`. Everything else goes to Discord. Inhibit rules compare object identity.
- The webhook URL comes from `kube-prometheus-stack/app/alertmanager-discord.sops.yaml` via `webhook_url_file`. It currently holds the placeholder `REPLACE_ME`.

**Phase 3: Grafana (stateless) at `grafana.local.<zone>`**
- grafana-community chart 14.0.1 (Grafana 13.2.4). It has no PVC and runs `RollingUpdate`. It is kept off talos-01 and prefers talos-02.
- The admin login is the SOPS secret `grafana-admin`, with a random 32-character password that was never printed.
- Datasources are Prometheus (uid `prometheus`, default) and Alertmanager.
- Dashboards are loaded by the sidecar from every `grafana_dashboard` ConfigMap: kps (folder Kubernetes) and Cilium (General), plus these vendored files:
  - flux-operator v0.61.0 (Flux)
  - grafana.com 20842 rev 3 cert-manager, with the `cluster` variable's allValue set to `.*` (Network)
  - envoy-gateway v1.9.2 proxy-global and clusters (Network)
  - a new **Alerting health** dashboard: failed Discord sends, firing alerts, head series, limit hits and samples per job
- The only published UI is an HTTPRoute on `envoy-internal` / `https`.

`template/config/**` has `.j2` copies of everything except the two SOPS secrets. Dashboard JSON is copied verbatim. A re-render therefore cannot overwrite values set with sops.

### Small additions beyond the plan text
- kube-state-metrics: `sampleLimit` 10000 (one target for the whole cluster) and `kube_node_role`, which `KubeCPUOvercommit`/`KubeMemoryOvercommit` need.
- kubelet keeps `kubelet_evictions` (for `KubeNodeEviction`).
- etcd keeps the client and peer byte counters, for the etcd dashboard.
- node-exporter enables `bonding` (for `NodeBondingDegraded` on bond0).
- The Flux PodMonitor keeps `workqueue_adds_total`, `rest_client_requests_total` and `controller_runtime_max_concurrent_reconciles`, for the Flux dashboards.
- Chart bump 92.11.0 → 92.13.1 on rebase: the only default that affects our copied cAdvisor list is that 92.13.1 stops dropping `container_memory_swap`. We keep dropping it on purpose (comment in the HelmRelease). The chart also adds `scrapeClass` options and a `kubernetes.io/tls` admission secret type (fresh install, so no migration).
- Review fix: every metric used by a shipped dashboard or our alert rules now passes all relabel layers (checked with a script over dashboards and rule files). Added: Envoy cluster/http/tcp connection and byte counters, outlier-detection and degraded/excluded membership, the TLS certificate expiry gauge, and the `rq_time` buckets; Flux `controller_runtime_reconcile_time_seconds_bucket` and `workqueue_longest_running_processor_seconds` (scrape class and PodMonitor); `apiserver_longrunning_requests`; `go_memory_classes_total_bytes`; `certmanager_clock_time_seconds`. Estimated cost: about 1.5–2.5k series, well inside the 40k budget.
- The Flux K8s API dashboard loses its apiserver request and admission latency panels (buckets would add several thousand series per apiserver). Its stat tiles and two timeseries panels were removed and the rest re-flowed. The Flux performance dashboard now queries `container_memory_working_set_bytes`.
- Removed the dead kube-state-metrics `metricLabelsAllowlist` (`kube_pod_labels` is not kept).
- aix and darwin node dashboards are off. The envoy-gateway-global dashboard is skipped because the controller is not scraped.
- The Loki and Alloy guardrail rules and the Loki datasource will ship with Loki.

## Local tests
- `scripts/validate-kubernetes.sh`: pass after rebasing onto main (55fcb16a) and the chart bump. The earlier helm/promtool/amtool results below were measured on 92.11.0; the operator version did not change.
- `helmfile -f bootstrap/helmfile/crds.yaml template`: 31 CRDs. The 10 `monitoring.coreos.com` CRDs are annotated `operator.prometheus.io/version: 0.94.1`.
- `helm template` of kps, grafana and coredns with the HelmRelease values: renders. The CoreDNS Deployment is byte-identical before and after.
- `promtool check rules --lint=all` on all 31 rule files (29 rendered kps files plus ours): pass.
- `promtool test rules`: the certificate rules fire at 15 d (warning) and 6 d (critical) for a 90-day cert whose renewal is failing, and nothing fires for a healthy cert.
- `amtool check-config` and `amtool config routes test`: Watchdog, InfoInhibitor and info → `null`; warning and critical → `discord`.
- Alertmanager v0.34.1 run locally with the rendered config and a `REPLACE_ME` file: it starts and reports ready. A test alert's send fails with `unsupported protocol scheme` and is retried. The process stays up.
- Prometheus v3.15.0 run locally against fake targets with the exact rendered relabelings (ScrapeClass, then monitor): 106 sample series kept and 55 dropped, as designed. Other buckets are droppe

body:
## Objective

S21's integration of the owner's Calendar canvas (CAL1–CAL21):
- Month, Week and Agenda each get their own address, with Month as the default.
- The week runs Monday to Sunday.
- A source that did not answer shows a dash with its reason, never 0.
- What no read carries yet says "Not read here yet".

The building is in seven slot tasks.

Part of #2420 (D1205). The issue stays `tracking` until its slot tasks land, so this PR closes nothing.

## Implementation

- **Addresses:** `/calendar` (Month), `/calendar/week`, `/calendar/agenda`, all with `/calendar`'s guard.
  - The view switch is a `nav` labelled "Calendar views", made of links, with the open one `aria-current`.
  - "Show next 90 days" is a link to Agenda.
- **The view comes from the address** (`viewOf`). Each view asks `GET /api/calendar/events` for its own window (`windowFor`):
  - the calendar month;
  - Monday to Sunday;
  - today plus 90 days.
- **Kind chips** count through `chipCount`. A kind whose source did not answer shows "—" titled "This source did not answer, so its count is not known." The degraded banner no longer says the chips "read 0".
- **Kinds are grouped into the canvas's five families** (`FAMILIES`). The legend counts its kinds instead of "Six sources, six kinds".
- **"Not read here yet"** with a reason for deadlines, interview calls and a whole-calendar subscription (`cal-wait-*`).
- No Worker route, migration or `wrangler.toml` change.

**Departures from the canvas:** the page still draws one list grouped by day in every view. These come with parts 5–7:
- the grids, filter popover, drawers and dialogs;
- `/calendar/item/:kind/:id`;
- `/calendar/connected`;
- `?date=`.

## Files changed

- **New:** `frontend/src/pages/calendarViews.js` (views, windows, families, `chipCount`, waits).
- `frontend/src/pages/CalendarPage.jsx`: the view from the address, view links, chip dash, waits card.
- `frontend/src/App.jsx`: two routes.
- **Canvases:** `design/incoming/Calendar Page.dc.html` and `Calendar · Boards.dc.html`.
- **Docs:**
  - `D1205.md` and `CALENDAR_MAP_2026-10-25.md`;
  - the ROUTE_MAP Calendar row;
  - the incoming and audits READMEs.
- **Tests:**
  - new: `calendar_views_d1205`;
  - updated: three pins in `calendar_page_c1` move from the C1 canvas to this one.

## Testing

- `npm run build`, `npm run test:frontend` (9,574 pass, 0 fail) and `npm run test:guards` all returned EXIT=0.
- `calendar_views_d1205`: 7 tests. Eight of eight mutations are caught.
- CI runs the full drift suite.

## Risks

- Ships as a frontend build only.
- `/calendar` now opens on Month, the canvas default, where it used to open on Agenda.
- The week window changes from "today plus 7" to Monday–Sunday.
- Rollback is a revert.

## Dependencies

Slot tasks:
- Worker parts, ready now:
  - #3172 (scope, plan gate, Calendly sync, advisor lookup, error codes);
  - #3173 (item fields, cancelled and pending, reschedule, pickers);
  - #3174 (new kinds);
  - #3175 (whole-calendar feed, sync errors, disconnect; migration 610).
- Frontend parts, blocked:
  - #3176 (grids, filter and states, after #3172 and #3173);
  - #3177 (drawer and dialogs, after #3173);
  - #3178 (connected calendars, subscribe and phone, after #3175 and #3176).

S21 · Claude Code

S1 for the integration and the slot split.

author: xinshoutw
body:
Proposes `openspec/changes/tigersync-last-writer-wins/`: TigerSync settles conflicts per item and per field by a hybrid logical clock instead of arrival order, device-side guesses and the "Use Server / Use Local" prompts.

Part of #689.

## What it decides
- Every user edit carries a clock value per field; deletions and resets are stamped tombstones. The backend keeps the newer value under the user's sync lock, clamps stamps to server time plus five seconds, and merges equal content silently.
- Released apps keep today's behavior: their single edits are stamped on arrival and their bulk uploads count as oldest.
- Course membership becomes a user layer over the school roster, so a school upload never brings back what the user hid.
- iOS refreshes local state, then TigerSync, then the school fetches, which wait for TigerSync at most 3 seconds. School data only writes the base layer.
- The per-assignment conflict alert and the re-enable "Use Server / Use Local" prompt go away.
- The #689 fixes ship first; the iOS course work later replaces their heuristics.

## Order

body:
depends on #246 (łańcuch #245 → #246 → ten; gałąź oparta na `task/refill-18`; przy `dirty` po squash — rebase).

## Co
T-296 (P1, crash-free, reguła 1 KPI.md): błędy GDScript z urządzeń trafiają do analityki.
- Nowe `game/src/systems/error_reporter.gd` (`ErrorReporter extends RefCounted`): `ingest(file, line, rationale, error_type, code)` bezpieczne wątkowo (`Mutex`, tylko dopisanie do bufora ≤ 1000, bez `print`/`push_error`), WARNING pomijany; `flush(analytics) -> int` na wątku głównym: sygnatura `plik:linia komunikat` z ciągami cyfr → `N` (ta sama normalizacja co `tools/log_budget.py`), obcięta do 256 znaków, 1× na sygnaturę i ≤ `error_report_max_per_session` na sesję (nowy klucz `GameConfig` = 10, `RANGES` [0, 100], 0 = wyłączone), `track_error("error", sygnatura)`.
- Nowe `game/src/systems/error_logger.gd` (`ErrorLogger extends Logger`): `_log_error(function, file, line, code, rationale, editor_notify, error_type, script_backtraces)` — sygnatura sprawdzona przez `ClassDB.class_get_method_list("Logger")` w Godot 4.7.2 — tylko `ingest`. Uwaga: dla `push_error` silnik daje treść w `code`, `rationale` pusty — `ingest` bierze `code`, gdy `rationale` jest pusty (inaczej sygnatura = `variant_utility.cpp:N`).
- `App`: 1 logger na proces (`static var error_logger`, `OS.add_logger`), `flush(Analytics)` w `_process` i przy FOCUS_OUT/WM_CLOSE, `OS.remove_logger` w `_exit_tree` tylko u instancji-właściciela (wiele `App` w testach nie dubluje).
- `AnalyticsProvider.track_error(severity, message)` no-op, `FakeAnalyticsProvider` zapisuje `{"type": "error", "event_id": "error:<severity>", …}`, `Analytics.track_error` deleguje; `test_provider_contracts.gd` zielony bez zmian.
- Testy: nowa `test_error_reporter.gd` (7): ta sama sygnatura 3× → 1; 11 różnych przy limicie 10 → 10; limit 0 → 0; dwie liczby w komunikacie → 1 sygnatura; `ingest` z `WorkerThreadPool` → 0 przed `flush`, 1 po; WARNING pomijany; obcięcie do 256; integracyjny: `OS.add_logger` + prawdziwe `push_error("t296 probe 1")` → 1× `track_error` z `tN probe N` (wpis w `tools/log_budget_allow.txt`; `test_log_budget.py` liczy 4 wpisy).
- Docs: GDD → Analityka `error_reported`, Mechaniki PROPOZYCJA refill #18 → zrobione; `docs/RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md` — listy eventów, Data Safety „App info and performance (Diagnostics)” i Privacy Labels „Diagnostics → Crash Data” wypełnione (zbierane przez GA, cel Analytics, bez śledzenia); `docs/DASHBOARD.md` 15b „Błędy skryptu / DAU” (KPI-1, top-10 sygnatur); `docs/privacy/index.md`/`pl.md` — zdanie o danych diagnostycznych. BACKLOG: T-296 → `review`. LOG sesja #27. Higiena: brakujące `.uid` suit `test_ad_sdk_edge_cases.gd`/`test_exp005_comeback.gd` (T-258/T-284) dodane.

## Dlaczego
Po T-255 nowa sygnatura ERROR zatrzymuje `make test`, ale błąd GDScript na telefonie nie zabija procesu — nie trafia do crash-free konsoli sklepu, a psuje rundę/zapis. Od 1. tygodnia soft launchu sygnatury widoczne w GA obok crash-free (cel ≥ 99,5 %). Pytanie 28 w GDD: przyjęto (tylko sygnatura, ≤ 10/sesję, Diagnostics).

- Sygnatura po normalizacji to `tN probe N` (cyfry w „t296” też → `N`) — allowlista i asercja używają tej postaci.
- `ingest` ma 5. parametr `code` (patrz wyżej). `OS.remove_logger` w `_exit_tree` zamiast `NOTIFICATION_PREDELETE`.
- Fallback `GameConfig.get_value(...)` bez literału (strażnik `test_no_literal_fallbacks`).

## Jak przetestowano
`make check` zielone (lint OK, 822 gdUnit4 / 0 failures (+7), 94 tools, export-check OK, „log budget: OK (4 signatures, all allowed)”).

## Ryzyka / ZWERYFIKUJ
- Limity długości/częstości error events GA niepodane w dokumentacji (https://docs.gameanalytics.com/event-types/error-events) — własny limit 10/sesję i 256 znaków.

body:
## Qué cambia

Ataques y habilidades con efectos propios (barridos, estocadas, fogonazos, impactos, partículas y sacudida medida), puertas de un sentido rediseñadas que se abren al pasar, arco sostenido con la cuerda hacia el cuerpo y aviso de cuándo despiertan los monolitos.

## Cómo se probó

- [ ] `npm run typecheck`
- [ ] `npm test`
- [ ] `npm run build && npm run test:e2e`
- [ ] Probado en navegador (PC) y en móvil o emulación táctil

## Notas

- Nuevo `client/src/vfx.ts`, basado en técnicas de "game feel": estela corta y rápida, destello al impacto, pocas partículas con dirección y sacudida proporcional al peso del golpe.
- Golpes cuerpo a cuerpo: media luna del color del Foco con núcleo blanco y líneas de velocidad. Gemelas con dos medias lunas cruzadas; brasas (Llama), pétalos (Guadaña) y esquirlas (Daga). Martillo y Guadaña sacuden la pantalla; el Martillo agrieta el piso.
- Lanza: punta de luz con chispas. Disparos con fogonazo, estela que se afina y forma propia por tipo (flecha, bala, dagas, rubí, esfera lunar, fuego, lanza, hilo).
- Al acertar: destello en estrella, anillo y chispas; los golpes de 15 o más de daño sacuden un poco.
- Efecto propio para cada Nombre e Inscripción: embestidas, Paso sin Nombre, Temblor, Grieta, Lluvia, curaciones, Velo, Escuchar al Viento, Ráfaga y Siega.
- Las formas que marcan el área real se siguen dibujando.
- Puertas de un sentido: postes de piedra y hojas de madera con hierro, orientadas según el sentido del cruce, que se abren al acercarse alguien; una runa en el piso marca el sentido.
- Arco: el PNG se refleja para que la cuerda quede hacia el cuerpo.
- Monolitos: antes de la Primera Llamada se muestra cuánto falta para que despierten, y si descansan tras romperse, cuántos segundos les faltan.
- Revisado en Chromium (14 efectos y puertas en sus cuatro sentidos). Pendiente revisar en partida la intensidad de la sacudida y los FPS en celular con `?perf`.

author: fatherlinux
body:
## Trentina 3.0 — Phase 2: the transform return variant

Splits the overloaded `TransformResult` dataclass into the Trentina 3.0 public transform contract. Phase 0 (vocabulary) and Phase 1 (`core.dispose`) are already in production; this is the transform-registry half of the plan — the `str → Applied | Declined | Failed` contract that the Phase 4 `transform()` stage and the Phase 6 plugin ecosystem both consume.

### The problem
The three-way outcome — applied / declined-for-shape / failed — was carried by a `bool` (`applied`), a magic string (`details["declined"]`), and a frozenset (`policy.FAILED_DECLINES`) that **three separate call sites** matched against. Because the fail-closed signal lived in data rather than the type, a **filtering** transform could not be built safely: `compose.py` swallowed any processor error into a pass-through of the original, so a filter that raised would deliver exactly what it exists to remove (documented in `base.py`).

### The change
- **`TransformResult = Applied | Declined | Failed`.** `Applied` carries the rewritten content; `Declined` is a safe no-op (even a floor transform declining never refuses); `Failed` is the fail-closed signal — the **type** is what a floor refuses on. A filter now returns `Failed` and is pinned `required` to refuse instead of passing content through.
- **`TransformRecord`** is the composition's per-step accounting (name, cost, result, bytes), with one `row()` the composition and gateway sidecar share. `TransformRecord.of` measures bytes in one place; transforms no longer carry name/cost/bytes.
- The three `declined in FAILED_DECLINES` tests collapse to `isinstance(..., Failed)` / `first_failure(...)`; **`FAILED_DECLINES` is deleted.**
- Producers that returned a reclassifiable reason string (`html._convert`, `structured._parse_and_reduce`) now return the typed outcome themselves, so a shape decline can never be mistaken for a failure at the call site.

### Behaviour-preserving
Exactly the old `FAILED_DECLINES` members (`error`, `petit_error`, `worker_error`, `no_api_key`, `empty_summary`, `too_large`) are `Failed`; every other reason is `Declined`. The same inputs refuse at the floor as before; `unreadable_pdf` stays a decline (pass-through).

### Verification
- Full suite **8027 passed, 55 skipped** (no change from the Phase 1 baseline).
- ruff, mypy, Gourmand (0 violations), semgrep (0 findings), Gatehouse — all green.

### Sequencing note
Phase 2's stage types (`Arrived`/`Transformed`) are deferred to Phase 4 and `Kind.DOCUMENT` retirement to Phase 5 — each lands where its single constructor exists (the orchestrator; the matrix Face), rather than floating across ingress sites about to be deleted. Same lesson as the Phase 1 seal: a type that does no real work yet reads as over-abstraction.

author: mairh
body:
0.0.5 is the first release with a signed SHA256SUMS (#143). Checking it by hand, cosign 2.4.1 can't read the signature's bundle format at all ("bundle does not contain cert"), while 2.5.3 verifies it (and a changed byte fails it). The installer verifies whenever cosign is installed and refuses on failure, so anyone with a cosign older than 2.5 would have been refused every install.

Now the installer reads `cosign version`: 2.5 or newer verifies as before and fails closed; older is skipped with a line saying so (update cosign to check it), and the checksum is still checked, the same as with no cosign.

Tests: the stand-in cosign answers its version; 2.4.1 is skipped and said, 2.5.3 and 3.1.4 verify, a bad signature still refuses, no cosign checks the checksum only.

body: Fixes the survey's R20 ("it always scrolls back to the start whenever I open it again"). ## What was wrong - With **Sync position across tabs** on, returning to Edit jumped to the playhead's line whenever the playhead was past 0. A paused song near the start meant "back to the top", even after scrolling far down. - The saved anchor was unreliable: the leaving view kept rendering as the next mode while it faded out, and the unmount cleanup measured an already-detached list. Positions drifted by about 15 lines per switch. ## Fix - Each `LyricLinesView` pins the mode it was mounted for. - When its mode is left, it records its anchor, the playhead and the line selection; anchor measurement is skipped once detached. - On return, if neither the playhead nor the selection changed, the tab goes back to its own position. Otherwise it follows playback as before. - The restore always uses the precise centering pass. ## Verified - Browser, 120-line song: Edit parked at line 102 with the playhead on line 10 now returns to line 98 (was 10); moving the playhead in Time still makes Edit follow it. - 2 new `selection-scroll` tests; `tsc`, `biome`, 748 tests, locales, build.
